# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-WET-RCA1-75C-001`
**Module:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip — Wet Chemistry & Surface Preparation  
**Parent Process:** Pre-Oxidation RCA Clean and In-Situ HF Dip Surface Preparation  
**Task Title:** 5:1:1 $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}/\text{H}_2\text{O}_2/\text{DIW}$ Mixing Recipe Execution & 75°C Thermal Stability Profiling  
**Generation:** Gen 1 (mm) | **Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Process Overview & Safety Prerequisites
- **Purpose:** Formulate the baseline RCA-1 (Standard Clean 1 / SC-1) alkaline oxidation bath ($5:1:1\ \text{DIW}/\text{NH}_4\text{OH}/\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$), bring to $75^\circ\text{C}$, and verify thermal and chemical stability for organic solubilization and megasonic particle removal prior to 3.5 nm dry gate oxide growth.
- **PPE Requirements:** Full chemical apron, chemical-resistant fluoroelastomer/nitrile double gloves, face shield, and chemical splash goggles.
- **Environment:** Class 100 laminar-flow wet bench with dedicated alkaline exhaust.

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Execution Procedure

```
  +-------------------------------------------------------------+
  | Step 1: Charge Bath with UPW (5 parts)                      |
  |         - Fill quartz/PTFE tank with 18.2 MOhm-cm DIW       |
  +------------------------------+------------------------------+
                                 |
                                 v
  +-------------------------------------------------------------+
  | Step 2: Add 29% NH4OH (1 part) & Initiate Circulation       |
  |         - Slowly dispense 29% NH4OH; begin gentle mixing     |
  +------------------------------+------------------------------+
                                 |
                                 v
  +-------------------------------------------------------------+
  | Step 3: Heat Solution to Initial Operating Band (70°C)       |
  |         - Ramp bath temperature using quartz immersion      |
  +------------------------------+------------------------------+
                                 |
                                 v
  +-------------------------------------------------------------+
  | Step 4: Add 30% H2O2 (1 part) & Stabilize at 75°C           |
  |         - Add H2O2; adjust heater to 75°C +/- 2°C           |
  |         - Stabilize for 10-minute clean profile             |
  +------------------------------+------------------------------+
                                 |
                                 v
  +-------------------------------------------------------------+
  | Step 5: Megasonic Agitation & Thermal Profile Check         |
  |         - Engage 1 MHz megasonics; verify T = 75°C          |
  +-------------------------------------------------------------+
```

1. **Vessel Inspection & Pre-fill:**
   - Verify that the quartz or PTFE immersion bath is clean, drained, and free of residues.
   - Charge the tank with **5 parts Ultra-Pure Water (UPW / DIW)** (resistivity: $\ge 18.2\ \text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$).
2. **Alkaline Reagent Addition:**
   - Add **1 part Ammonium Hydroxide ($\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$, 29% concentration)** into the UPW while maintaining liquid circulation.
   - *Caution:* Never add concentrated chemicals without DIW ballast to prevent uncontrolled exothermic local heating and ammonia fuming.
3. **Pre-Heating Phase:**
   - Turn on bath inline immersion heaters and ramp the solution toward **$70^\circ\text{C}$**.
4. **Peroxide Addition & Final Temperature Stabilization:**
   - Once the bath reaches $70^\circ\text{C}$, carefully dispense **1 part Hydrogen Peroxide ($\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$, 30% concentration)** into the bath to complete the $5:1:1$ ratio.
   - Ramp and stabilize the bath temperature at the target **$75^\circ\text{C}$** (operating window: $70^\circ\text{C}$ to $75^\circ\text{C}$).
5. **Megasonic & Thermal Stability Profiling:**
   - Engage the megasonic transducer array at **1 MHz** frequency.
   - Log bath temperature continuously across a baseline **10-minute hold** to verify closed-loop thermal regulation at $75^\circ\text{C}$ under exothermic $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ decomposition and megasonic power dissipation.
6. **Rinse Readiness Check:**
   - Ensure the downstream Quick Dump Rinse (QDR) is charged with $18.2\ \text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ UPW and programmed for a minimum of 5 dump cycles.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Window | Engineering Units | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Volumetric Mixing Ratio** ($\text{DIW} : \text{NH}_4\text{OH} : \text{H}_2\text{O}_2$) | `5 : 1 : 1` | $\pm 2\%$ per component | Dimensionless (volumetric) | Automated chemical dispense flowmeter |
| **Bath Operating Temperature** | `75.0` | $70.0 - 75.0$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ | Dual PTFE-sheathed RTD / thermocouple sensors |
| **Megasonic Agitation Frequency** | `1.0` | $\pm 0.05$ | $\text{MHz}$ | Megasonic generator controller telemetry |
| **Process Immersion Window** | `10.0` | $\pm 0.5$ | $\text{minutes}$ | Automated wet bench recipe timer |
| **Cascade Dump Rinse Resistivity Endpoint** | `> 16.0` | Min $16.0$ (from $18.2$ source) | $\text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ | In-situ resistivity probe |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations
- **Source:** *RCA Standard Clean SC-1, SC-2, and Native Oxide HF Dip Engineering*
  - Reagent concentration and ratio: $5\text{ parts UPW} : 1\text{ part } 29\%\ \text{NH}_4\text{OH} : 1\text{ part } 30\%\ \text{H}_2\text{O}_2$.
  - Operating bath temperature: $70^\circ\text{C}\text{ to } 75^\circ\text{C}$ in a quartz or PTFE immersion bath.
  - Megasonic frequency: $1\ \text{MHz}$.
  - Immersion duration: $10\text{ minutes}$.
  - Rinse specification: 5 dump cycles with $18.2\ \text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ DIW until resistivity $> 16\ \text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Maintaining steady-state 75°C bath temperature during 5:1:1 DIW/NH4OH/H2O2 bath life requires inline closed-loop quartz heating elements with PID feedback (< ±1.0°C overshoot). Rapid catalytic degradation of H2O2 into H2O and O2 gas shifts bath stoichiometry and creates microbubbles that attenuate 1 MHz megasonic acoustic coupling, requiring active spiking or bath-life cutoffs under 45 minutes.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 75°C with a 5:1:1 mixing ratio, NH3 volatilization occurs rapidly alongside H2O2 decomposition. The concurrent silicon base-etch rate (~0.5 nm/10 min) must be balanced against chemical re-oxidation to prevent sub-nanometer surface roughening (RMS > 0.15 nm), which directly degrades the breakdown field (Ebd) and interface state density (Dit) of the subsequent 3.5 nm dry gate oxide.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Electronic Grade / SEMI C79 Grade 5 (ppb-level trace metals) ammonium hydroxide and hydrogen peroxide are prone to localized supply bottlenecks in Vietnam. Sourcing 29% NH4OH and 30% stabilized H2O2 in fluoropolymer-lined drums with certified low Fe/Cu (< 0.1 ppb) is mandatory to prevent catalytic bath decomposition and metallic gate contamination.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The manual batch mixing and 75°C thermal profiling step presents an operational safety gate and high bath-turnover cost. The qualification protocol must validate thermal ramp stability and bath composition lifetime in a single 4-hour qualification block to avoid holding up the gate oxide dry furnace run schedule.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal runaway or severe stoichiometric depletion due to accelerated exothermic decomposition of H2O2 in the presence of transition metal contaminants (Fe/Cu > 1 ppb), causing rapid NH3 outgassing and silicon surface pitting.
1. Megasonic acoustic decoupling caused by outgassing oxygen micro-bubble nucleation on transducer surfaces, dropping particle removal efficiency (PRE) below 95% at the 0.18 µm particle threshold.
1. Excessive queue time post-SC-1 without controlled cascade rinse, resulting in dried chemical residue, salt formation (ammonium salts), and native oxide microroughening exceeding gate dielectric breakdown limits.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-1-2-2-01` | **SC-1 Bath 75°C Thermal Stability and H2O2 Stoichiometric Decay Profiling** | PTFE-sheathed 4-wire RTD temperature sensor connected to calibrated datalogger, inline optical UV-Vis absorption spectrometer for H2O2/NH4OH concentration tracking, and calibrated digital flow-bench timer. | 1. Charge bath with 5 parts UPW, heat to 65°C using PID immersion heater. 2. Add 1 part 29% NH4OH followed by 1 part 30% H2O2. 3. Engage closed-loop heater set to 75°C and start continuous RTD datalogging at 1 Hz. 4. Record bath temperature profile during heat-up to 75°C and maintain for 60 minutes. 5. Extract 10 mL bath aliquots at t = 0, 15, 30, 45, and 60 minutes for UV-Vis absorption analysis of active H2O2 and NH4OH molarity. | `Bath temperature stabilizes at 75.0°C ± 1.5°C within 8 minutes of chemical introduction and exhibits no overshoot > 77.5°C. H2O2 concentration remains >= 70% of initial mixing concentration at t = 45 minutes.` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-1-2-2-02` | **Post-SC-1 Silicon Etch Rate and Surface Roughness Benchmark on 180nm Bare Si** | Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (J.A. Woollam or equivalent) and Atomic Force Microscope (AFM in tapping mode, 1 µm x 1 µm scan area). | 1. Immerse test wafer in freshly prepared 75°C 5:1:1 SC-1 bath for exactly 10 minutes with megasonic agitation. 2. Transfer immediately to quick-dump rinse (QDR) for 5 cycles with 18.2 MOhm-cm UPW until effluent resistivity > 16.5 MOhm-cm. 3. Spin-rinse-dry with heated N2 (80°C). 4. Measure chemical oxide thickness via spectroscopic ellipsometry at 9 points. 5. Perform AFM surface scans at center, middle, and edge sites to measure root-mean-square roughness (Rq). | `Chemical oxide thickness must measure 0.8 nm to 1.2 nm across 9 points with uniformity < 5% 1-sigma. Post-clean AFM surface roughness Rq must remain <= 0.15 nm (delta Rq <= 0.03 nm relative to baseline).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Chemical-resistant butyl or heavy neoprene gloves over inner nitrile gloves, Full-face polycarbonate splash shield conforming to ANSI Z87.1, Acid/alkali-resistant chemical apron (polyvinyl chloride or heavy neoprene), Safety goggles with indirect side vents, Steel-toe chemical-resistant neoprene work boots
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye Contact: Immediately flush with copious isotonic eyewash or UPW for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek emergency medical attention. Skin Contact: Immediately remove contaminated clothing under safety shower; flush affected area with copious water for >= 15 minutes. Inhalation: Relocate victim immediately to fresh air; administer supplemental oxygen if breathing is labored; seek pulmonary evaluation for acute ammonia/steam vapor exposure.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated corrosive/alkaline exhaust hood operating with face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) ± 10%, connected directly to wet bench scrubbers with continuous differential pressure monitoring and auto-interlock.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent SC-1 solution must be cooled to < 40°C in dedicated quench tank to prevent thermal decomposition hazards, routed to base-corrosive drain, and neutralized in automated wastewater treatment facility using dilute sulfuric acid (H2SO4) to pH 6.5-8.5 prior to discharge.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Ammonium Hydroxide** | `1336-21-6` | SEMI C79 Grade 5 | `29.0% w/w` |
| **Hydrogen Peroxide** | `7722-84-1` | SEMI C79 Grade 5 | `30.0% w/w` |
| **Deionized Water (Ultra-Pure)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM D5127 Type E-1 (18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100.0% w/w` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Degreased silicon substrate with native oxide and organic/particulate surface contamination from preceding handling.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Particle-free, hydrophilic chemical oxide passivated surface (thickness ~1.0 nm, water contact angle < 10°).
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding Q-time induces airborne trace organic adsorption and airborne airborne molecular contamination (boron/phosphorus/hydrocarbons) on the active chemical oxide, generating interface trap states (Dit) and pinholes in the 3.5 nm dry gate oxide.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full recipe qualification and validation of the 5:1:1 UPW/NH4OH/H2O2 SC-1 formulation at 75°C, establishing thermal bath stability within ±1.5°C over 45 minutes, confirming stoichiometric decay limits, and verifying minimal surface roughening (Rq <= 0.15 nm) for 180nm dry gate oxidation pre-clean.

- [ ] `SC1_Formulation_Stoichiometry_Decay_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `Post_SC1_Surface_Roughness_AFM_Map.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

The concurrent silicon base-etch rate (~0.5 nm/10 min) must be balanced against chemical re-oxidation to prevent sub-nanometer surface roughening (RMS > 0.15 nm), which directly degrades the breakdown field (Ebd) and interface state density (Dit) of the subsequent 3.5 nm dry gate oxide.

Excessive queue time post-SC-1 without controlled cascade rinse, resulting in dried chemical residue, salt formation (ammonium salts), and native oxide microroughening exceeding gate dielectric breakdown limits.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-WET-RCA1-CAL-002`
**Title:** Megasonic Quartz Bath Reagent Staging and Automated 5:1:1 $\text{DIW}/\text{NH}_4\text{OH}/\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ Dispense Calibration  
**Hierarchy Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > 180nm Dry Gate Oxide Growth (3.5 nm) > Pre-Oxidation RCA Clean and In-Situ HF Dip Surface Preparation > RCA-1 (SC-1) Organic & Particle Removal Bath Formulation and Bench Qualification > Megasonic Quartz Bath Reagent Staging and Automated 5:1:1 $\text{DIW}/\text{NH}_4\text{OH}/\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ Dispense Calibration  
**Process Generation:** Gen 2 (µm) | **Action Type:** Make

---

### 1. Purpose & Scope
This procedure specifies the mechanical staging, line priming, and volumetric pump calibration for automated chemical dispensing of standard RCA-1 (SC-1) solution into a quartz wet bench bath. The target mixture ratio is strictly 5:1:1 ($\text{DIW} : 29\%\ \text{NH}_4\text{OH} : 30\%\ \text{H}_2\text{O}_2$) maintained prior to bath temperature ramp-up.

---

### 2. Required Chemical Reagents & Equipment
- **Ultra-Pure Deionized Water (DIW):** Continuous facility loop, resistivity specification $\ge 18.2\ \text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$.
- **Ammonium Hydroxide ($\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$):** Semiconductor Grade / Electronic grade $29\%\ \text{NH}_4\text{OH}_{(\text{aq})}$.
- **Hydrogen Peroxide ($\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$):** Semiconductor Grade / Electronic grade $30\%\ \text{H}_2\text{O}_2_{(\text{aq})}$.
- **Bath & Metering Hardware:** High-purity megasonic quartz tank, automated PTFE positive displacement pumps / mass flow meters, class A PFA volumetric calibration cylinder, calibrated thermocouple well.

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

```
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| Step 1: Quartz Bath Inspection & DIW Prime                  |
| - Verify tank cleanliness and purge lines                   |
| - Prime DIW loop (18.2 MOhm-cm)                             |
+------------------------------+------------------------------+
                               |
                               v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| Step 2: Automated Volumetric Calibration                    |
| - Calibrate 5 parts DIW dispense delivery                   |
| - Calibrate 1 part 29% NH4OH dispense delivery              |
| - Calibrate 1 part 30% H2O2 dispense delivery               |
+------------------------------+------------------------------+
                               |
                               v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| Step 3: Bath Staging & Sequence Dispense                    |
| - Dispense DIW base charge -> Add NH4OH -> Add H2O2         |
| - Verify 5:1:1 volumetric ratio balance                     |
+------------------------------+------------------------------+
                               |
                               v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| Step 4: Thermal Ramp Initiation                             |
| - Engage inline heating to target operating band 70°C - 80°C|
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
```

#### Step 1: Pre-Operation Inspection & DIW Loop Verification
1. Inspect the quartz tank inner walls and megasonic transducer array for chemical crystallization or surface fouling.
2. Verify that DIW line resistivity reads strictly $\ge 18.2\ \text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ at the delivery manifold.
3. Open the automated DIW bleed valve for $60\ \text{s}$ to flush dead-leg plumbing.

#### Step 2: Automated Chemical Dispense Calibration
1. Route the automated chemical delivery lines to the bypass PFA graduated calibration chamber.
2. **DIW Calibration:** Trigger a 5-unit pulse delivery command. Verify dispensed volume against target within volumetric tolerance.
3. **$\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$ (29%) Calibration:** Trigger a 1-unit pulse of $29\%\ \text{NH}_4\text{OH}$. Confirm pump stroke displacement / mass meter balance.
4. **$\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ (30%) Calibration:** Trigger a 1-unit pulse of $30\%\ \text{H}_2\text{O}_2$. Confirm volumetric consistency.
5. Check calibration run consistency across 3 consecutive cycles.

#### Step 3: Sequential Chemical Staging & Bath Filling
1. Lock the bath drain valve in the automated wet bench controller.
2. Dispense **5 parts DIW** directly into the quartz tank to establish the liquid heat transfer buffer and prevent concentrated exothermic runaway.
3. Dispense **1 part 29% $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$** through the submerged bottom manifold.
4. Dispense **1 part 30% $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$** slowly to complete the 5:1:1 ratio.

#### Step 4: Thermal Profiling Readiness
1. Enable the quartz bath immersion heaters.
2. Set target thermal loop setpoint to maintain the bath between $70^\circ\text{C}$ and $80^\circ\text{C}$ for the upcoming organic and particle strip cycle ($10\text{--}15\ \text{minutes}$).

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Physical Units | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **DIW Loop Resistivity** | $\ge 18.2$ | $\text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ | In-situ inline resistivity sensor |
| **Volumetric Dispense Ratio** | $5 : 1 : 1$ ($\text{DIW} : \text{NH}_4\text{OH} : \text{H}_2\text{O}_2$) | Relative volumetric ratio | PFA bypass volumetric measurement cylinder |
| **Reagent Concentration Staging** | $29\%$ ($\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$) / $30\%$ ($\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$) | $\%$ (wt concentration) | In-line chemical assay / CoA verification |
| **Bath Thermal Operating Range** | $70 \text{ to } 80$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ | Immersion thermocouple in quartz thermowell |

---

### 5. Literature Citations & Traceability
- **[Standard RCA-1 and RCA-2 Silicon Wafer Cleaning Procedure]:**
  - Chemical formulation: *5 parts Deionized $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, 1 part Ammonium Hydroxide ($29\%\ \text{NH}_4\text{OH}$), 1 part Hydrogen Peroxide ($30\%\ \text{H}_2\text{O}_2$)*.
  - Temperature window: *Heated to $70^\circ\text{C}\text{--}80^\circ\text{C}$ for $10\text{--}15\ \text{minutes}$*.
  - Water quality standard: *Dump rinse with $18.2\ \text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ deionized water*.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Automated chemical dispense via closed-loop metering pumps (PTFE/PFA diaphragm type) must strictly decouple the static quartz immersion tank from line pressure pulsations. Coriolis mass flow meters must provide live density and mass feedback rather than relying on open-loop stroke counting, preventing stoichiometric skew during automated 5:1:1 DIW/NH4OH/H2O2 staging. Furthermore, the 1 MHz megasonic piezoelectric transducer bonded to the quartz vessel bottom must have interlocked liquid-level optical sensors to prevent transducer delamination or dry cavitation burnout.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: In SC-1 cleaning, NH4OH simultaneously etches silicon while H2O2 passivates it; shifting away from the precise 5:1:1 volumetric ratio alters both the chemical redox potential and the solution pH (~10.5 at 25°C, shifting lower at 75°C). Excess NH4OH causes surface micro-roughening (increasing gate oxide interface trap density Dit), while depleted H2O2 leads to unpassivated anisotropic pitting. Automated replenishment and staging must strictly maintain chemical stoichiometry prior to thermal ramp to avoid non-uniform native oxide growth prior to the 3.5 nm dry gate oxidation.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Electronic-grade SEMI-C8/C12 standard NH4OH (29%) and unstabilized semiconductor-grade H2O2 (30%) have aggressive outgassing and limited shelf life. Sourcing UPW-grade fluoropolymer tubing (PFA 451HP) and quartz tank assemblies with high-frequency transducer bonding from certified domestic and regional distributors in Vietnam/ASEAN is critical, as lead times for custom acoustic quartz vessels frequently exceed 16 to 20 weeks.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Procuring pre-integrated wet bench sub-assemblies (Action Type: Buy) accelerates delivery against the 180nm DRAM gate oxidation milestones. However, acceptance testing must require factory acceptance testing (FAT) data proving automated dispense volume accuracy of ±1.5% across 50 consecutive dispense cycles prior to shipping, ensuring bench commissioning does not stall the downstream 75°C thermal stability profiling schedule.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Transducer thermal shock or dry firing: Activation of megasonic power prior to reaching minimum DIW bath fill height causes localized quartz fracture or acoustic bond failure.
1. Stoichiometric ratio drift from vapor-lock: Bubble accumulation in NH4OH metering lines leads to under-dispensing, resulting in accelerated surface silicon etching and gate dielectric breakdown voltage (Vbd) degradation.
1. Exothermic thermal runaway during staging: Adding concentrated H2O2 into hot NH4OH without initial DIW thermal buffering induces rapid, violent peroxide self-decomposition.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-1-2-2-1-01` | **Automated 5:1:1 Reagent Dispense Volume and Stoichiometric Mass Calibration** | Mettler Toledo Precision Analytical Balance (0.01 g resolution), inline Bronkhorst micro-Coriolis mass flow meter, Anton Paar DMA 4500M density meter, calibrated Class-A PFA graduated receiver. | 1. Program automated dispense cycle for a 10.5 L target batch (7.5 L UPW, 1.5 L NH4OH 29%, 1.5 L H2O2 30%). 2. Sequence chemical injection: first dispense UPW buffer, followed by NH4OH, then H2O2 into isolated calibration vessels. 3. Record individual reagent masses on calibrated analytical balance. 4. Extract 50 mL aliquot and measure mixture density at 25°C. 5. Repeat for N=10 consecutive automated staging cycles. | `Dispense volume for each component must be within ±1.5% of target (UPW: 7500 ± 112.5 mL; NH4OH: 1500 ± 22.5 mL; H2O2: 1500 ± 22.5 mL). Resulting 25°C mixture density must measure between 1.010 g/cm³ and 1.025 g/cm³ across all 10 runs.` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-1-2-2-1-02` | **Megasonic Quartz Bath Acoustic Power Density and Fluid Level Interlock Verification** | Ono Sokki acoustic cavitation hydrophone meter, calibrated Pt100 RTD multi-point immersion probe array, Banner Engineering optical liquid level sensor. | 1. Verify low-level interlock trip by lowering fluid level below transducer plane; confirm generator inhibit. 2. Refill to nominal line (10.5 L). 3. Energize megasonic generator at 100 W, 250 W, and 500 W forward power settings. 4. Map spatial cavitation acoustic pressure using hydrophone across 9 grid points in the wafer immersion zone at 20 mm above bath bottom. 5. Monitor bath fluid temperature rise over 15 minutes of continuous agitation. | `Megasonic interlock must inhibit RF output at bath level < 85% full height. Spatial acoustic power uniformity across 9 grid points must be > 90% (standard deviation / mean < 0.10). Fluid temperature ramp due to acoustic dissipation must not exceed 0.8°C/min without external bath heating active.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Chemical splash face shield over ANSI Z87.1 safety goggles, Heavy-duty chemical-resistant butyl/neoprene outer gloves over nitrile inner gloves, PFA/Vinyl acid-base protective apron, Steel-toe chemically resistant boot covers
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact: Immediately flush eyes with laminar isotonic saline or clean water for a minimum of 20 minutes while holding eyelids open; seek emergency medical attention. Skin contact: Remove contaminated clothing immediately under safety deluge shower; flush area with copious water for at least 15 minutes. Inhalation: Evacuate worker to fresh air immediately; provide 100% humidified oxygen if breathing is labored. Do not induce vomiting if swallowed.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Wet bench wet-scrubber exhaust with minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) across the quartz bath sash opening. Ambient NH3 electrochemical monitor interlocked to alarm at 15 ppm (warning) and 25 ppm (evacuation).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Segregated automated wet bench drainage to alkaline/peroxide waste collection sump. Quench residual peroxide with dilute sodium bisulfite (NaHSO3) or catalytic carbon bed decomposition prior to adjusting effluent pH to 6.5-8.5 using 10% H2SO4 before discharge to industrial wastewater treatment.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Ammonium Hydroxide** | `1336-21-6` | SEMI Tier-3 / C8 High-Purity Electronic Grade | `28.0% - 30.0% w/w` |
| **Hydrogen Peroxide** | `7722-84-1` | SEMI Tier-3 Electronic Grade (Unstabilized) | `30.0% - 32.0% w/w` |
| **Deionized Ultra-Pure Water (UPW)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM D5127 Type E-1.2 Semiconductor Grade | `100% (Resistivity > 18.2 MOhm-cm at 25°C)` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pre-cleaned bare silicon wafer with native oxide (thickness ~0.8-1.2 nm) exhibiting contact angle < 10° (hydrophilic) following initial degrease/rinse.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Particle-free, chemically oxidized passivated SiO2 layer (~0.5-0.7 nm) free of trace organics, transitioning immediately to cascade dump rinse and native oxide HF dip.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding Q-time induces ambient airborne organic vapor (volatile organic compounds/siloxanes) chemisorption, leading to high-temperature gate oxide breakdown voltage dispersion and non-uniform native oxide growth during furnace staging.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full qualification and acceptance signoff of the automated 5:1:1 DIW/NH4OH/H2O2 reagent dispensing system, liquid level interlocks, and megasonic quartz bath assembly under Gen 1 (mm) baseline parameters.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `automated_dispense_stoichiometry_calibration_report.csv`
- [ ] `megasonic_quartz_bath_acoustic_mapping_and_interlock_qualification.pdf`
- [ ] `chemical_ratio_density_titration_verification.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Volumetric dispense repeatability of DIW, NH4OH, and H2O2 into the quartz immersion vessel** | `5.00 : 1.00 : 1.00 ratio` | ±1.5% volumetric deviation per component across 10 sequential cycles | Inline Coriolis mass flow logging cross-checked via calibrated gravimetric balance tare weighing. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Acoustic field uniformity across the 180nm active wafer boat immersion field at 1.0 MHz** | `92.0%` | ≥ 90.0% acoustic power density uniformity (CV ≤ 10%) | 9-point immersed hydrophone acoustic pressure scan at 100% nominal RF output. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Successful execution of 10 consecutive automated dispense cycles meeting ±1.5% volumetric tolerance without level-sensor fault, zero vapor locks in reagent manifolds, and formal signoff on EHS scrubber interlock verification.

Energize megasonic generator at 100 W, 250 W, and 500 W forward power settings. 4. Map spatial cavitation acoustic pressure using hydrophone across 9 grid points in the wafer immersion zone at 20 mm above bath bottom. 5. Monitor bath fluid temperature rise over 15 minutes of continuous agitation.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Megasonic interlock must inhibit RF output at bath level < 85% full height. Spatial acoustic power uniformity across 9 grid points must be > 90% (standard deviation / mean < 0.10). Fluid temperature ramp due to acoustic dissipation must not exceed 0.8°C/min without external bath heating active.

ppe_required: Chemical splash face shield over ANSI Z87.1 safety goggles
Heavy-duty chemical-resistant butyl/neoprene outer gloves over nitrile inner gloves
PFA/Vinyl acid-base protective apron
Steel-toe chemically resistant boot covers

cas_chemicals.name: Deionized Ultra-Pure Water (UPW)

ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: Eye contact: Immediately flush eyes with laminar isotonic saline or clean water for a minimum of 20 minutes while holding eyelids open; seek emergency medical attention. Skin contact: Remove contaminated clothing immediately under safety deluge shower; flush area with copious water for at least 15 minutes. Inhalation: Evacuate worker to fresh air immediately; provide 100% humidified oxygen if breathing is labored. Do not induce vomiting if swallowed.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Wet bench wet-scrubber exhaust with minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) across the quartz bath sash opening. Ambient NH3 electrochemical monitor interlocked to alarm at 15 ppm (warning) and 25 ppm (evacuation).
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Segregated automated wet bench drainage to alkaline/peroxide waste collection sump. Quench residual peroxide with dilute sodium bisulfite (NaHSO3) or catalytic carbon bed decomposition prior to adjusting effluent pH to 6.5-8.5 using 10% H2SO4 before discharge to industrial wastewater treatment.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Pre-cleaned bare silicon wafer with native oxide (thickness ~0.8-1.2 nm) exhibiting contact angle < 10° (hydrophilic) following initial degrease/rinse.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Acoustic field uniformity across the 180nm active wafer boat immersion field at 1.0 MHz
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: 9-point immersed hydrophone acoustic pressure scan at 100% nominal RF output.

expected_result.signoff_criteria: Successful execution of 10 consecutive automated dispense cycles meeting ±1.5% volumetric tolerance without level-sensor fault, zero vapor locks in reagent manifolds, and formal signoff on EHS scrubber interlock verification.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-WET-RCA1-75C-THRM`
**Title:** RCA-1 Solution 75°C Closed-Loop Thermal Ramp and In-Situ H₂O₂ Decomposition Exotherm Profiling  
**Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > 180nm Dry Gate Oxide Growth (3.5 nm) > Pre-Oxidation RCA Clean and In-Situ HF Dip Surface Preparation > RCA-1 (SC-1) Chemical Mixing Formulation and Thermal Stability Bench Qualification  
**Target Action Type:** Make  
**Technology Generation:** Gen 2 (180 nm / µm)

---

### 1. Equipment & Chemical Reagents
* **Bench:** Automated / semi-automated wet chemical station with PTFE/PVDF chemical bath vessel and closed-loop PID immersion heater (quartz-sheathed or PFA-coated thermocouple).
* **Deionized Water (DIW):** High-purity semiconductor grade, resistivity = $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$.
* **Ammonium Hydroxide ($\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$):** 29 wt% aqueous solution (electronic / semi-grade).
* **Hydrogen Peroxide ($\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$):** 30 wt% aqueous solution (unstabilized / semi-grade).
* **Mixing Volumetric Ratio:** $5 : 1 : 1$ ($\text{DIW} : \text{NH}_4\text{OH} : \text{H}_2\text{O}_2$).

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

```
  [Step 1: Bath Fill]       5 parts DIW (18.2 MOhm-cm) + 1 part NH4OH (29%)
           │
           ▼
  [Step 2: Thermal Ramp]    Initiate PID ramp toward 75°C baseline
           │
           ▼
  [Step 3: H2O2 Dosing]     Add 1 part H2O2 (30%) under closed-loop agitation
           │
           ▼
  [Step 4: Exotherm Profile]Monitor Delta-T and decay rate within 70°C–80°C window
           │
           ▼
  [Step 5: Process Window]  Stabilize 10–15 min cleaning soak
```

1. **Vessel Charge (Pre-Mix):**
   * Dispense 5 volume parts of $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ DI water into the bath tank.
   * Add 1 volume part of $29\%\text{ NH}_4\text{OH}$. Turn on continuous circulation/stirring to prevent concentration stratification.

2. **Base Pre-Heat Ramp:**
   * Engage closed-loop PID immersion heater to ramp the $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}/\text{DIW}$ mixture toward the nominal setpoint ($75^\circ\text{C}$).

3. **Peroxide Dosing & Exotherm Initiation:**
   * Dispense 1 volume part of $30\%\text{ H}_2\text{O}_2$ into the bath.
   * Ensure closed-loop thermocouple logging tracks the transient catalytic decomposition exotherm:
     $$\text{H}_2\text{O}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{OH}^-} \text{H}_2\text{O} + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2 + \Delta H_{\text{reaction}}$$

4. **In-Situ Exotherm Profiling & Closed-Loop Control:**
   * Adjust the PID controller gain/attenuation to absorb self-heating and prevent thermal runaway, clamping bath temperature strictly inside the qualified $70^\circ\text{C}\text{ to }80^\circ\text{C}$ envelope.
   * Maintain the bath at the stabilized $75^\circ\text{C}$ target for the qualified wafer immersion duration of $10\text{ to }15\text{ minutes}$.

5. **Exhaust & Safety Monitoring:**
   * Verify continuous tank lip exhaust to purge liberated gaseous $\text{O}_2$ and volatilized $\text{NH}_3$ vapors.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Specification | Physical Unit | Measurement Tool / Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Steady-State Bath Temperature** | $75.0 \pm 5.0$ (Operating window: $70.0 - 80.0$) | $^\circ\text{C}$ | PFA/Quartz In-Situ Thermocouple |
| **DI Water Feed Resistivity** | $\ge 18.2$ | $\text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ | In-Line Conductance/Resistivity Probe |
| **Nominal Chemical Mixing Ratio** | $5 : 1 : 1$ ($\text{DIW} : \text{NH}_4\text{OH} : \text{H}_2\text{O}_2$) | Volumetric Ratio | Mass Flow Controller (MFC) / Calibrated Dosing Syringe |
| **Qualified Cleaning Hold Duration** | $10\text{ to }15$ | $\text{minutes}$ | Automated Wet Bench Recipe Execution Timer |

---

### 4. Verified Literature References
* **Standard RCA-1 and RCA-2 Silicon Wafer Cleaning Procedure:** Specifies the formulation of RCA-1 (SC-1) as 5 parts $\text{DI H}_2\text{O}$, 1 part Ammonium Hydroxide ($29\%\text{ NH}_4\text{OH}$), and 1 part Hydrogen Peroxide ($30\%\text{ H}_2\text{O}_2$); operating temperature range of $70^\circ\text{C} - 80^\circ\text{C}$ for $10 - 15\text{ minutes}$; and intermediate dump rinse with $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ deionized water.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Closed-loop thermal ramp control of RCA-1 (5:1:1 DIW/NH4OH/H2O2) up to 75°C introduces dynamic non-linearities due to the exothermic decomposition of H2O2 (2 H2O2 -> 2 H2O + O2, delta_H = -98.2 kJ/mol). The PID controller loop must utilize feedforward compensation based on bath volume and continuous rate-of-temperature-rise sensing to prevent runaway thermal overshoot past 78°C, which leads to exponential ammonia degassing and aggressive silicon microroughening.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 75°C, the simultaneous oxidative attack by H2O2 and continuous etching of chemical SiO2 by NH4OH reaches an equilibrium etch/growth rate of ~0.5-1.0 nm/min. If the initial heating ramp causes localized hot spots (>80°C) near quartz immersion heating elements, localized H2O2 depletion occurs, shifting the redox balance toward uninhibited anisotropic etching of crystalline Si(100), destroying sub-nanometer surface roughness required for 3.5 nm dry gate oxide.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Semiconductor-grade 29% NH4OH and 30% H2O2 (SEMI Grade 4/5) must be certified with trace transition metal contaminants (Fe, Cu, Ni) below 0.1 ppb. Trace transition metal impurities act as potent heterogeneous catalytic sites for accelerated H2O2 auto-decomposition, rendering bath exotherm profiles erratic and drastically shortening functional bath chemical lifetime below the target 4-hour window.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Thermal ramp profiling and exotherm characterization are gating milestones before batch wafer immersion qualification for 180nm DRAM gate stack pre-cleans. We must establish an unambiguous, automated recipe that hits 75°C ± 1.0°C within 18 minutes without manual operator intervention or recipe aborts caused by spurious over-temperature interlocks.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal runaway overshoot beyond 80°C driven by catalytic H2O2 decomposition exotherm, precipitating rapid NH3 volatilization and catastrophic bath destabilization.
1. Localized thermal gradients (>2.5°C differential across quartz tank) resulting in non-uniform chemical SiO2 dissolution and wafer-to-wafer gate oxide breakdown voltage (BV_ox) degradation.
1. Premature H2O2 exhaustion (<50% nominal molarity within 45 min) due to uncontrolled heating rates, leading to severe bare silicon micro-pitting and elevated surface haze (HPD > 0.08 ppm).

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-1-2-2-2-01` | **Closed-Loop 75°C Ramp Profile and Steady-State Temperature Uniformity** | Multi-point PTFE-encapsulated Class-A 4-wire Pt100 RTD array (5 submerged sensors: 4 corners, 1 center), Eurotherm 3504 PID controller, PFA-sheathed immersion quartz heater (3.0 kW), and automated agitation recirculation pump (5 L/min). | 1. Initiate closed-loop thermal ramp recipe from 22.0°C to 75.0°C setpoint at a controlled target rate of 3.5°C/min. 2. Log temperature at 1.0-second intervals across all 5 RTD points during ramp. 3. Record maximum transient temperature overshoot upon reaching setpoint. 4. Maintain bath at 75.0°C setpoint for 60 minutes and log steady-state spatial temperature deviation across center and edge sensors. | `Ramp duration from 22.0°C to 75.0°C must be <= 18.0 minutes; peak transient overshoot must not exceed 76.5°C (<= 1.5°C above setpoint); steady-state spatial temperature gradient across all 5 RTD points must be <= 0.8°C throughout the 60-minute dwell.` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-1-2-2-2-02` | **In-Situ H2O2 Decomposition Kinetics and Chemical Concentration Depletion Profiling** | In-line fiber-optic NIR spectroscopic concentration monitor (CI Semi ChemScan or Horiba CS-100 series) calibrated for H2O2 (wt%) and NH3 (wt%), backed by redundant automated potentiometric ceric sulfate [Ce(SO4)2] redox titrations. | 1. Collect continuous NIR absorption spectra every 30 seconds for 120 minutes while maintaining closed-loop bath temperature at 75.0°C. 2. Extract 10 mL bath aliquots at t = 0, 30, 60, 90, and 120 minutes for manual titrimetric verification against 0.1 N Ce(SO4)2 standard. 3. Calculate first-order decomposition rate constant (k_decomp) and cumulative H2O2 concentration decay curve over the 2-hour operational window. | `Active H2O2 concentration must remain >= 2.50 wt% (initial: ~3.85 wt%) after 60 minutes at 75.0°C; maximum first-order decomposition rate constant k_decomp must be <= 6.5 x 10^-3 min^-1; titrimetric validation must match NIR optical telemetry within ± 0.15 wt%.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Chemical-resistant neoprene/Viton dual-matrix gloves with extended gauntlet (EN 374-3 Class JKL), ANSI Z87.1 full-face splash shield combined with high-impact chemical splash goggles, Heavy-duty chemical splash apron (PVDF/PTFE laminated), Safety boots with chemical-resistant neoprene overshoes, Emergency cartridge half-mask respirator approved for ammonia/inorganic vapors (NIOSH AM/OV/P100)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact: Flush with copious volumes of isotonic saline or tempered UPW for at least 20 minutes holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmological trauma evaluation. Skin contact: Drench contaminated area under emergency safety shower for >= 15 minutes, remove contaminated clothing; apply mild soothing lotion if irritation persists. Inhalation: Evacuate immediately to fresh air; if dyspnea develops, administer medical-grade humidified oxygen via trained personnel; monitor for delayed pulmonary edema up to 24 hours.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated chemical wet-bench polypropylene exhaust ducting maintaining continuous face velocity >= 0.50 m/s (100 ft/min) at sash opening (250 mm height); duct negative static pressure maintained at -0.45 to -0.60 in. w.g.; integrated NH3 toxic gas monitoring interlocked to auto-dump bath if ambient NH3 exceeds 15 ppm.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent bath must be cooled below 40°C before pneumatic transfer to dedicated alkaline/oxidizer waste collection sump. Neutralization requires slow dosing of 10% sulfuric acid (H2SO4) or sodium bisulfite (NaHSO3) under agitation to reduce residual peroxide and neutralize NH4OH to ammonium sulfate [(NH4)2SO4] until effluent reaches pH 6.5 - 8.5 with zero active oxidant residual.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Ammonium Hydroxide** | `1336-21-6` | SEMI Tier C / Grade 5 | `28.0 - 30.0 wt% NH3 in H2O` |
| **Hydrogen Peroxide** | `7722-84-1` | SEMI Tier C / Grade 5 (Stabilizer-free) | `30.0 - 32.0 wt%` |
| **Deionized Water (UPW)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM D5127 Type E-1.2 Electronic Grade | `100 wt% (Resistivity 18.2 MOhm-cm at 25°C)` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophobic native/chemical oxide post-degrease or de-ash, contaminated with trace organic residues, particulate matter (LPDs > 0.15 um), and atmospheric hydrocarbon condensates.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Atomically smooth, highly hydrophilic chemical passivation oxide (SiO2 thickness 0.8 - 1.2 nm) with contact angle < 5°, zero organic surface contamination, and particle count delta <= 5 particles at >= 0.18 um.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding cleanroom air Q-time (>30 min) causes airborne volatile organic compound (VOC) condensation and particulate redeposition onto fresh chemical oxide, resulting in localized gate dielectric punch-through, increased interface trap density (D_it > 2.0 x 10^10 cm^-2 eV^-1), and premature 3.5 nm dry gate oxide breakdown (E_bd < 10 MV/cm).

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full engineering validation of the closed-loop 75°C thermal ramp and chemical decomposition stability for the 5:1:1 RCA-1 wet bench recipe. Confirms sub-18 minute ramp time, zero thermal runaway (<=1.5°C peak overshoot), <=0.8°C spatial bath uniformity, and sustained H2O2 concentration >= 2.50 wt% over a 60-minute qualification run, guaranteeing an optimal surface state for subsequent 3.5 nm dry gate oxide growth.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `rca1_thermal_ramp_profile_5pt_rtd.csv`
- [ ] `h2o2_nh4oh_decomposition_kinetics_report.pdf`
- [ ] `bath_uniformity_and_exotherm_contour_map.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Maximum thermal ramp duration from ambient 22.0°C to steady-state 75.0°C setpoint** | `16.5` | ± 1.5 min | Automated time-stamped telemetry logged from 5-point Pt100 RTD array via supervisory wet-bench SCADA |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Peak dynamic temperature overshoot during transition to 75.0°C setpoint dwell** | `75.8` | +0.7 / -0.8 °C | High-frequency (1 Hz) digital RTD acquisition at central immersion sensor |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Residual active H2O2 chemical concentration remaining after 60 minutes dwell at 75.0°C** | `2.85` | ± 0.35 wt% | In-situ NIR transmission spectroscopy cross-validated against potentiometric ceric sulfate titration |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Successful execution of 3 consecutive automated 75°C thermal ramps meeting all ASSERT criteria without heater interlock trips, exhibiting peak bath temperature <= 76.5°C, spatial bath temperature variance <= 0.8°C across 5 points, and residual H2O2 concentration >= 2.50 wt% after 60 minutes dwell, formally qualifying the RCA-1 bench for production 180nm DRAM pre-oxidation lot runs.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

**Document ID:** SOP-WET-180-042  
**Title:** Post-Clean Thermal Stability Verification via Bath Concentration Titration and Particle Adders Metrology  
**Context:** DRAM Foundation VN | 180nm Open-Source DRAM | Pre-Gate Oxidation Wet Bench Qualification  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm / 180nm node) | **Action Type:** Buy (Metrology / Wet Bench Tool Qualification)

---

## 1. Scope & Objective
This procedure defines the protocol to verify the thermal stability, chemical concentration decay kinetics (via acid-base and redox titration), and particle addition performance of the 5:1:1 $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}/\text{H}_2\text{O}_2/\text{DIW}$ (RCA-1 / SC-1) bath during steady-state heating at 75°C prior to 3.5 nm dry gate oxide pre-clean processing.

---

## 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

```
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                  RCA-1 Wet Bench Verification Flow                      |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                    |
                                    v
     [Step 1] Bath Preparation (5:1:1 DIW:NH4OH:H2O2) @ 75°C
                                    |
                                    v
     [Step 2] In-Situ Thermal Profiling (Multi-point RTD / Thermocouple)
                                    |
                                    v
     [Step 3] Chemical Concentration Sampling & Dual Titration
                                    |
                                    v
     [Step 4] Bare Si Monitor Pre-Scan Metrology (DLS / Laser Surface Scanner)
                                    |
                                    v
     [Step 5] Bath Immersion (10-15 min) + 18.2 MOhm-cm Dump Rinse
                                    |
                                    v
     [Step 6] Post-Scan Particle Metrology & Adder Calculation
```

### Step 1: Bath Makeup and Thermal Stabilization
1. Charge the quartz recirculation bath with high-purity chemicals in the exact volumetric ratio of **5 parts Deionized $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ : 1 part 29% $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$ : 1 part 30% $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$**.
2. Engage the inline chemical heater and set the target process temperature setpoint to **75°C** (process window: **70°C–80°C**).
3. Allow the bath to stabilize under continuous chemical recirculation for a minimum of 20 minutes.

### Step 2: In-Situ Thermal Stability Verification
1. Insert calibrated PFA-encapsulated temperature probes across 5 distributed points in the wet bench tank (four corners and bath center).
2. Record steady-state thermal drift over a 30-minute logging window to ensure stability within process limits.

### Step 3: Chemical Bath Titration Sampling
1. Draw a 20 mL aliquot of the mixed bath using a clean PFA syringe at $t = 0\text{ min}$, $t = 30\text{ min}$, and $t = 60\text{ min}$.
2. Perform potentiometric neutralization titration against certified standard hydrochloric acid ($\text{HCl}$) to quantify residual active $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$ concentration.
3. Perform redox titration using standard ceric sulfate or potassium permanganate ($\text{KMnO}_4$) to quantify active $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ concentration decay caused by thermal decomposition at 75°C.

### Step 4: Particle Adders Metrology Pre-Scan
1. Load 200 mm bare test/monitor silicon wafers into a calibrated laser surface inspection tool (dark-field unpatterned surface inspection).
2. Execute a pre-clean inspection pass and map baseline defect counts down to the tool’s critical particle sizing threshold for the 180nm technology node.

### Step 5: Test Wafer Processing & Rinse
1. Transfer the pre-scanned monitor wafers into the qualified 75°C RCA-1 bath.
2. Maintain immersion for **10 to 15 minutes**.
3. Transfer wafers immediately to the quick-dump rinser (QDR) and rinse using **$18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ deionized water** for **3 minutes**.
4. Spin-rinse dry using high-purity filtered $\text{N}_2$.

### Step 6: Post-Clean Metrology and Adder Calculation
1. Re-scan the monitor wafers on the surface inspection system using the identical optical recipe.
2. Run defect-pair analysis to subtract pre-existing defects and determine net particle adders.

---

## 3. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Limits | Units | Status |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Bath Operating Temperature** | `75.0` | `70.0 - 80.0` | `°C` | Mandatory |
| **Intermediate Rinse Water Resistivity** | `18.2` | $\ge 18.2$ | `MΩ·cm` | Mandatory |
| **Immersion Process Duration** | `10.0 - 15.0` | $\pm 0.5$ | `minutes` | Mandatory |
| **Rinse Cycle Duration** | `3.0` | $\pm 0.1$ | `minutes` | Mandatory |

---

## 4. Literature & Context Citations

* **Bath Stoichiometry & Processing Regimes:**
  * *Citation:* `Standard RCA-1 and RCA-2 Silicon Wafer Cleaning Procedure`
  * *Parameters extracted:* RCA-1 (SC-1) composition of **5 parts Deionized $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, 1 part Ammonium Hydroxide (29% $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$), 1 part Hydrogen Peroxide (30% $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$)**; process temperature range of **70°C–80°C**; immersion duration of **10–15 minutes**; intermediate dump rinse with **$18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ deionized water for 3 minutes** followed by high-purity $\text{N}_2$ dry.
* **Device Integration Boundary Conditions:**
  * *Citation:* `180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench`
  * *Parameters extracted:* Target node architecture at gate length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, gate width $W = 220\text{ nm}$, requiring ultra-clean, particle-free silicon surfaces prior to 3.5 nm dry gate dielectric growth to preserve target leakage current ($< 1\text{ fA/cell at 85°C}$).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Maintaining the SC-1 bath at 75°C without automated chemical spike-replenishment causes accelerated loss of NH3 gas and H2O2 catalytic decomposition, altering pH and etch rates over bath lifetime. Offline titration must be tightly synchronized with wafer run frequency to prevent undetected bath depletion, while particle adders metrology must isolate bench fluidic recirculation filtration artifacts from furnace loading transfer contamination.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 75°C in a 5:1:1 NH4OH/H2O2/DIW formulation, the decomposition of H2O2 into H2O and O2 combined with NH3 outgassing shifts the chemical potential. If H2O2 drops below critical oxidation potential while NH4OH remains high, silicon microroughness drastically increases via anisotropic etching. Conversely, excessive NH4OH loss reduces zeta potential, eliminating electrostatic particle repulsion and causing catastrophic particulate redeposition on bare Si.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Electronic-grade UPW, semiconductor-grade NH4OH (29%), and unstabilized high-purity H2O2 (30%) SEMI Grade 5 (ppb metal contamination) are required to avoid introducing trace Fe, Cu, or Al into gate oxide pre-clean. Local availability in Vietnam for high-consumption wet bench replenishment requires strict chemical inventory tracking and dedicated fluoropolymer chemical delivery canisters.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Thermal stability qualification and particle adder metrology represent a strict gating step for the 3.5 nm dry gate oxide pre-clean sequence. Unqualified bath lifetime directly threatens pilot line wafer throughput and furnace scheduling due to unpredictable bath dumps and recalibrations.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal runaway decomposition of H2O2 catalyzed by trace metal impurities causing micro-boiling, violent outgassing, and localized dry spots on wafer surfaces.
1. Zeta potential collapse between SiO2 particles and Si wafer surface due to NH4OH depletion, resulting in post-clean particle adder density exceeding > 0.05 particles/cm2 at >= 0.18 um.
1. Excessive silicon surface microroughness (RMS roughness > 0.25 nm) induced by preferential etching when H2O2 concentration falls below critical passivation threshold.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |

Sample 10 mL of bath chemistry using a clean PTFE pipette at t = 0, 15, 30, 45, 60, and 90 minutes. 2. Cool sample rapidly to 20°C in an ice-water quenched PFA container to halt decomposition. 3. Dispense 5 mL aliquot into titration beaker, dilute with 50 mL UPW, and titrate with 0.1 N HCl to determine remaining NH4OH concentration. 4. Dispense second 5 mL aliquot, acidify with 10 mL 20% H2SO4, and titrate with 0.1 N KMnO4 to potentiometric endpoint to determine H2O2 concentration. 5. Calculate percentage decay rate of both active species per unit time. | `Active NH4OH concentration must remain >= 70% of initial mixing value and H2O2 concentration must remain >= 65% of initial value after 60 minutes continuous hold at 75°C. Total calculated bath lifetime >= 60 minutes before re-spiking or dump.` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-1-2-2-3-02` | **Post-SC-1 Particle Adder and Surface Defectivity Metrology** | Laser Surface Particle Scanner / Defect Inspection System (KLA-Tencor Surfscan SP1 or equivalent unpatterned wafer inspector calibrated to 0.15 um PSL equivalent diameter). | 1. Load pre-inspected monitor wafers into high-purity PFA wafer cassette. 2. Process wafers in SC-1 bath at 75°C for 10 minutes with continuous 0.1 um PTFE recirculating filtration. 3. Transfer immediately to quick-dump rinse (QDR) bath with resistivity > 18.2 MOhm-cm UPW until effluent resistivity reaches 17.5 MOhm-cm. 4. Perform final spin-rinse-dry (SRD) cycle under high-purity N2 purge. 5. Post-scan monitor wafers on surface scanner with edge exclusion of 5 mm. 6. Compute net particle adders: Delta = Post_scan_particles - Pre_scan_particles. | `Net particle adders at >= 0.18 um must be <= 0.05 particles/cm2 (<= 8 net adders across entire 150mm wafer clear aperture area) across all 3 monitor wafers.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Full chemical splash face shield with safety goggles (ANSI Z87.1 approved), Heavy-duty chemical-resistant butyl/neoprene gloves over nitrile exam gloves, PFA/Vinyl acid-base resistant cleanroom chemical apron with full sleeve protectors, Steel-toe chemical boots with cleanroom boot covers
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact: Immediately flush eyes with emergency eyewash for minimum 20 minutes holding eyelids open; seek urgent ophthalmologist evaluation. Skin contact: Drench under safety shower for >= 15 minutes while stripping contaminated clothing; treat alkaline burns with copious water (do not apply neutralizing acids). Inhalation: Move victim to fresh air immediately; provide 100% humidified oxygen if breathing is labored; seek immediate medical assistance for potential pulmonary edema.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Wet bench dedicated wet chemical fume exhaust with face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) across lip exhaust slots. Acid/alkaline vapor scrubber ducting must maintain negative static pressure >= -0.75 in. w.g. continuously monitored with differential pressure interlocks.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Continuous gravity drain to dedicated alkaline chemical waste drain system. Effluent collected in containment sump, automatically neutralized using dilute H2SO4 to pH 6.5 - 8.5 prior to industrial wastewater discharge. Concentrated dumps require peroxide quenching and temperature cooling below 35°C prior to neutralization.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| **Ammonium Hydroxide** | `1336-21-6` | SEMI Grade 5 (Trace metals < 100 ppt) | `28.0% - 30.0% NH3 in H2O` |
| **Hydrogen Peroxide** | `7722-84-1` | SEMI Grade 5 (Unstabilized VLSI grade, trace metals < 100 ppt) | `30.0% - 32.0% in H2O` |
| **Ultra-Pure Water (UPW)** | `7732-18-5` | SEMI Type E-1 (18.2 MOhm-cm at 25°C, TOC < 1 ppb) | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophobic/Partially organic-contaminated bare crystalline silicon with broken native oxide or pre-existing handling residue.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic, particle-free passivated chemical oxide (SiO2 thickness 0.6 - 1.0 nm) with water contact angle < 10 degrees ready for HF dip or direct clean rinse.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Airborne molecular contamination (AMC) adsorption (volatile organic compounds and ambient siloxanes) leading to uncontrolled native oxide growth, degradation of gate oxide breakdown field (E_bd < 10 MV/cm), and interface trap density escalation (D_it > 1E11 eV-1 cm-2).

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Bench-level thermal stability validation of 5:1:1 SC-1 cleaning solution operating at 75°C, confirming chemical concentration decay kinetics over a 60-minute bath lifetime and demonstrating particulate adder suppression below 0.05 adders/cm2 (>= 0.18 um) for 150mm prime wafers prior to 3.5 nm dry gate oxidation.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `SC1_75C_Titration_Concentration_Decay_Profile.csv`
- [ ] `Post_SC1_Surfscan_Particle_Adder_Inspection_Map.tiff`
- [ ] `SC1_Thermal_Stability_Bench_Qualification_Report.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| `ASSERT-01` | **NH4OH and H2O2 concentration retention after 60 min at 75°C** | `>= 70% NH4OH retention, >= 65% H2O2 retention` | ±3.0% | Automated potentiometric acid-base and redox titration log analysis |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Net post-clean surface particle adder density at >= 0.18 um** | `<= 0.05 particles/cm2 (<= 8 adders/wafer on 150mm substrate)` | +0.01 particles/cm2 | Full-wafer laser light scattering defect surface inspection (KLA Surfscan) |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Bath operational temperature stability across continuous process run** | `75.0°C` | ±1.0°C | In-situ quartz-sheathed Pt100 RTD bath probe logging at 1 Hz |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Post-SC-1 Megasonic Bath Particle Removal Efficiency & Surface Roughness Qualification

**Module:** Pre-Oxidation RCA Clean and In-Situ HF Dip Surface Preparation [Wet Chemistry]  
**Sub-Process:** Metrology Qualification  
**Generation:** Gen 1 (mm) / 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip  
**Action Type:** Buy (Metrology Tool Qualification & Verification)

---

### 1. Process Workflow

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│      1. Incoming      │
│  Metrology: Pre-Scan  │
│   Particles and AFM   │
│         Base          │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  2. SC-1 Megasonic:   │
│  5:1:1 at 70C-75C, 1  │
│      MHz, 10 min      │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│    3. Cascade Dump    │
│  Rinse: 5 Cycles UPW  │
│   to gt 16 MOhm-cm    │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   4. Substrate Dry:   │
│      Filtered N2      │
│   Marangoni or IPA    │
│         Vapor         │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│     5. Metrology      │
│  Qualification: PRE   │
│     Calc and AFM      │
│    Roughness Check    │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

#### Step 1: Pre-Clean Metrology Baseline
1. Take incoming silicon test wafers designated for the 180nm dry gate oxide sequence.
2. Load test wafers into an automated darkfield laser surface particle scanner (threshold set to capture particles $\ge 0.18\,\mu\text{m}$). Record baseline surface defect/particle count ($N_{\text{initial}}$).
3. Measure initial surface roughness on 5 designated wafer sites (center, 4 orthogonal points at $R/2$) using Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM, $2\,\mu\text{m} \times 2\,\mu\text{m}$ scan field) to establish baseline root-mean-square roughness ($R_q$ baseline).

#### Step 2: RCA-1 (SC-1) Megasonic Immersion Clean
1. Verify SC-1 chemical bath ratio formulation:
   $$\text{UPW} : \text{NH}_4\text{OH (29\%)} : \text{H}_2\text{O}_2\text{ (30\%)} = 5 : 1 : 1\text{ (by volume)}$$
2. Confirm temperature controller stabilizes bath temperature at **$70^\circ\text{C}$ to $75^\circ\text{C}$** in the quartz/PTFE tank.
3. Power on transducer array and verify megasonic acoustic excitation operates at **$1.0\text{ MHz}$**.
4. Immerse wafers in quartz carrier cassette into the active megasonic SC-1 bath for exactly **$10\text{ minutes}$** to enable organic dissolution, surface micro-etching ($\approx 0.5\text{ nm}$), and particle dislodgement via zeta potential repulsion.

#### Step 3: Cascade Dump Rinse
1. Transfer wafer cassette rapidly from the SC-1 tank to the Cascade Dump Rinse (CDR) tank.
2. Execute **5 complete dump-and-fill cycles** using Ultra-Pure Water (UPW, input resistivity $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$).
3. Monitor final discharge resistivity cell; verify effluent rinse bath resistivity rises to **$> 16\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$** before cassette transfer.

#### Step 4: Substrate Drying
1. Transfer rinsed cassette into the drying chamber.
2. Dry substrate surfaces using filtered $\text{N}_2$ Marangoni drying or isopropyl alcohol (IPA) vapor drying until wafers are completely dry without water-mark staining.

#### Step 5: Post-Clean Metrology & Metric Calculation
1. Reload wafers onto the automated laser particle scanner using the identical recipe/threshold ($\ge 0.18\,\mu\text{m}$) and map post-clean particle count ($N_{\text{post}}$).
2. Calculate Particle Removal Efficiency (PRE):
   $$\text{PRE (\%)} = \left(\frac{N_{\text{initial}} - N_{\text{post}}}{N_{\text{initial}}}\right) \times 100\%$$
3. Re-scan the identical 5 measurement coordinates using AFM ($2\,\mu\text{m} \times 2\,\mu\text{m}$ scan). Extract post-clean $R_q$ surface roughness to ensure the microscopic base etching does not cause surface pitting.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
       PRE (Clean)┤████████████████████████████████████│
                  │████████████████████████████████████│
                  └┬────────┬────────┬───────┬────────┬┘
                  0.0     23.8     47.5    71.2    95.0 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Acceptance Target | Tolerance / Boundary | Measurement Method & Instrument |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Particle Removal Efficiency (PRE)** | $\ge 95.0\%$ | Lower bound: $95.0\%$ for particles $\ge 0.18\,\mu\text{m}$ | Darkfield Laser Surface Particle Scanner |
| **SC-1 Microscopic Etch Thickness** | $\approx 0.5\text{ nm}$ | Range: $0.4\text{ nm} - 0.6\text{ nm}$ | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / AFM Step Profiling |
| **Dump Rinse Effluent Resistivity** | $> 16.0\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ | Feed UPW standard: $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ | In-situ Inline Conductance/Resistivity Probe |
| **SC-1 Bath Operating Temperature** | $70^\circ\text{C} - 75^\circ\text{C}$ | Allowable bath window: $70^\circ\text{C} - 80^\circ\text{C}$ max | In-situ Calibrated Immersion RTD Sensor |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

- **[Source: RCA Standard Clean SC-1, SC-2, and Native Oxide HF Dip Engineering]**:
  - *SC-1 Chemistry & Agitation*: 5 parts UPW : 1 part 29% $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$ : 1 part 30% $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$; heated in quartz or PTFE immersion bath with megasonic agitation at $1\text{ MHz}$; immersion time 10 minutes at $70^\circ\text{C}$ to $75^\circ\text{C}$.
  - *Mechanism*: Microscopic base etching of silicon ($\approx 0.5\text{ nm}$) and zeta potential repulsion for particle lift-off.
  - *Rinse & Endpoint*: Cascade Dump Rinse: 5 cycles with $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ UPW until bath resistivity $> 16\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$.
  - *Drying*: Filtered $\text{N}_2$ Marangoni or IPA vapor drying.
- **[Source: Standard RCA-1 and RCA-2 Silicon Wafer Cleaning Procedure]**:
  - *Verification Range*: $5:1:1$ ratio formulation at $70^\circ\text{C} - 80^\circ\text{C}$ for 10–15 minutes with deionized water intermediate dump rinse ($18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Megasonic acoustic energy dissipation and streaming velocity fields inside the wet bench tank must maintain spatial uniformity within +/- 3% across all 25 wafer slots. Cavitation-induced micro-streaming is required for breaking sub-0.18 um boundary layers, but uncontrolled acoustic power hotspots (> 1.2 W/cm^2 localized) induce crystal pitting and localized surface roughening directly beneath transducer seams.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: In an alkaline SC-1 solution (pH ~10-10.5 at 70°C), particle removal operates through simultaneous chemical oxidation/etching (~0.5 nm Si etch) and negative zeta potential electrostatic repulsion between silicon substrate and SiOx/organic particulates. If H2O2 is depleted prematurely relative to NH4OH, the etch rate increases drastically, transitioning the surface into anisotropic micro-roughness (pyramid facet formation), degrading subsequent 3.5 nm gate oxide breakdown electric field (Ebd).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Megasonic transducer arrays (1.0 MHz PZT piezoelectric plates bonded to quartz baths) have limited domestic availability in Southeast Asia and require specialized impedance matching generators. Piezoelectric delamination and quartz faceplate erosion require dual-sourcing of transducer assemblies and strict bath power telemetry to prevent unplanned bench downtime.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Qualification of particle removal efficiency (PRE) must be coupled with Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) root-mean-square roughness (Rq) measurements in a single shift. Any qualification protocol requiring extended off-line metrology queue times beyond 45 minutes will bottleneck dry oxidation furnace lot releases.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Acoustic cavitation pitting: excessive localized megasonic power density (> 1.5 W/cm^2) causing physical pit defects and gate oxide pinhole shorting.
1. Silicon surface micro-roughening: NH4OH:H2O2 ratio imbalance (> 1:1) leading to uncontrolled hydroxide etching, increasing surface Rq > 0.2 nm and lowering gate oxide dielectric breakdown voltage (Vbd < 11 MV/cm).
1. Particle re-deposition during QDR/transfer: inadequate chemical overflow velocity and cascade dump rinse resistivity decay (< 16 MOhm-cm) causing electrostatic re-attachment of suspended sub-micron particulates.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-1-2-3-01` | **Sub-Micron Particle Removal Efficiency (PRE) Bench Qualification via Laser Surface Scanning** | KLA-Tencor Surfscan SP1 or equivalent Darkfield Laser Surface Particle Scanner calibrated with 80 nm and 120 nm Polystyrene Latex (PSL) spheres. | 1. Measure and map initial defect density and coordinates across wafer active area with 3 mm edge exclusion. 2. Immerse wafer carrier in megasonic SC-1 bath for 10 minutes with continuous megasonic agitation. 3. Quick Dump Rinse (QDR) for 5 cycles using 18.2 MOhm-cm UPW until effluent resistivity > 16.5 MOhm-cm. 4. Spin-rinse dry under heated filtered N2 (> 99.9999% purity). 5. Re-measure wafer on laser surface scanner for particle counts >= 0.12 um (N_final). 6. Calculate PRE = ((N_initial - N_final) / N_initial) * 100%. | `Particle Removal Efficiency (PRE) >= 95.0% for particles >= 0.12 um; total post-clean adder particle count <= 15 particles per 150 mm wafer (edge exclusion 3 mm).` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-1-2-3-02` | **Post-Megasonic SC-1 Silicon Surface Micro-Roughness Qualification via Tapping-Mode AFM** | Bruker Dimension Icon Atomic Force Microscope (AFM) with silicon cantilever tips (nominal tip radius < 10 nm) in Tapping Mode. | 1. Load dried post-SC-1 wafer into AFM vibration-isolated chamber under laminar flow hood. 2. Engage tapping mode on 5 designated site coordinates (center, top, bottom, left, right at r = 50 mm). 3. Perform 2.0 um x 2.0 um scan per site at 512 x 512 pixels resolution at a scan rate of 0.8 Hz. 4. Execute 1st order flattening filter to correct sample tilt and bow without altering high-frequency roughness data. 5. Extract average root-mean-square surface roughness (Rq) and maximum peak-to-valley height (Rmax). | `Surface roughness Rq <= 0.15 nm across all 5 test sites; Rmax <= 1.50 nm; zero evidence of localized acoustic cavitation pitting defects on any 2.0 um x 2.0 um image field.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Chemical-resistant neoprene/nitrile apron, Full-face polycarbonate splash shield (ANSI Z87.1), Heavy-duty butyl or silver-shield chemical gloves over nitrile inner gloves, Acid/base chemical vapor cartridge respirator (NIOSH-approved for ammonia and oxidizers), Safety steel-toe chemical-resistant boots
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact: Immediately flush eyes at dedicated safety eyewash station with tempered water for a minimum of 15 minutes, holding eyelids wide open; seek urgent ophthalmologist evaluation. Skin contact: Flush skin under deluge emergency safety shower for 15 minutes while stripping off contaminated clothing; apply soothing wet compress and monitor for chemical alkaline burns. Inhalation: Relocate victim to fresh outdoor air immediately; administer humidified medical oxygen if breathing is labored; seek immediate emergency medical services.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated wet bench polypropylene plenum exhaust with continuous negative pressure; minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) across bath opening. Wet ammonia scrubber tied to dedicated base/alkaline exhaust ductwork with low-flow interlocks connected to heater and megasonic power shutoff.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Aqueous spent SC-1 effluent must be drained to segregated alkaline/peroxide waste plumbing. Solution is routed to automated neutralization sump equipped with dual pH probes, cooled to < 40°C, quenched with sodium metabisulfite or catalytic carbon bed to decompose residual H2O2, and neutralized with dilute sulfuric acid (H2SO4) to pH 6.5 - 8.5 prior to industrial wastewater discharge.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Ammonium Hydroxide** | `1336-21-6` | SEMI Grade 4 / VLSI Grade | `29 wt% NH3 in H2O` |
| **Hydrogen Peroxide** | `7722-84-1` | SEMI Grade 4 / VLSI Grade (unstabilized electronics grade) | `30 wt% in H2O` |
| **Ultra-Pure Water (UPW)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM D5127 Type E-1 / SEMI C79 Standard | `100 vol% (18.2 MOhm-cm at 25°C)` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic silicon surface with thin chemically grown chemical oxide (~0.8 - 1.0 nm) and residual PSL or particulate load from preceding operations.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Ultra-clean hydrophilic chemical oxide passivated with silanol (Si-OH) terminal groups, free of organic contamination and particles >= 0.12 um, ready for dilute HF native oxide strip.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Extended air exposure causes ambient airborne volatile organic compound (VOC) condensation, airborne boron/phosphorus dopant contamination, and capillary adsorption of cleanroom particulate matter, which voids particle-free gating and degrades 3.5 nm dry gate oxide dielectric breakdown integrity.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full physical and metrological qualification of the post-SC-1 megasonic bath confirms particle removal efficiency exceeds 95% at 0.12 um without inducing surface micro-roughening or cavitation pitting, establishing a robust sub-surface baseline prior to dilute HF native oxide strip and 3.5 nm dry gate oxide growth.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `SC1_MEGASONIC_PRE_QUALIFICATION_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `POST_SC1_AFM_ROUGHNESS_TOPOGRAPHY_MAPS.tiff`
- [ ] `SURFSCAN_DEFECT_COORDINATES_AND_SIZE_HISTOGRAM.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Particle Removal Efficiency (PRE) for particles >= 0.12 um** | `>= 95.0%` | +/- 1.5% | Laser surface darkfield scanning (Surfscan SP1) pre- and post-cleaning defect differential analysis |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Post-cleaning Silicon (100) Surface Roughness (Rq)** | `<= 0.15 nm` | +0.02 nm max | Atomic Force Microscopy (Bruker Dimension Icon, 2.0 um x 2.0 um tapping mode, 5-point wafer map) |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Post-Megasonic Acoustic Cavitation Pit Density** | `0 pits/wafer` | +0 pits | Automated defect classification (ADC) via darkfield optical laser scanning with AFM review validation |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Successful execution of 3 consecutive qualification lots meeting PRE >= 95.0%, AFM Rq <= 0.15 nm across all 5 test sites, zero cavitation pits detected, and signoff endorsement by Metrology Lead, Wet Bench Process Engineer, and DRAM Integration Lead.
