# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

**Title:** Procurement and Sizing Verification of Certified $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ and $\text{SiO}_2$ Calibration PSL/Nanoparticle Standards  
**Node & Action:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (Gen 2 µm) | Action Type: Make / Metrology Baseline  
**Context:** Metrology qualification for Post-RCA-1 Particle Removal Efficiency (PRE), gate oxidation surface preparation, and surface roughness verification.

---

### Process Workflow Diagram

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Procurement and CoA  │
│     Verification      │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│    NIST Traceable     │
│  Sizing Verification  │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Refractive Index    │
│    Metrology Match    │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│    Particle Stock     │
│      Dispersion       │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Procurement & Certificate of Analysis (CoA) Ingestion**:
   - Order NIST-traceable certified monodisperse Polystyrene Latex (PSL) spheres, amorphous silicon dioxide ($\text{SiO}_2$), and silicon nitride ($\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$) nanoparticle calibration standards targeting critical feature sizing for the 180nm DRAM node (nominal critical dimensions matching bitline/wordline pitch limits: $360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$, and sub-node gate oxide sensitivity thresholds).
   - Log manufacturer lot numbers, mean hydrodynamic diameter, standard deviation, and certification expiry dates into the cleanroom MES.

2. **Optical & Material Constant Qualification**:
   - Verify that the refractive index specifications of the purchased $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ standards precisely match the LPCVD process standard: $n = 2.00 \pm 0.02$ at $\lambda = 632.8\text{ nm}$.
   - Ensure the $\text{SiO}_2$ standards reflect thermal gate oxide optical baselines ($n \approx 1.46$).

3. **Size Distribution Verification (DLS / TEM Metrology)**:
   - Perform Dynamic Light Scattering (DLS) or calibrated Scanning/Transmission Electron Microscopy (SEM/TEM) size validation on diluted aliquots.
   - Confirm monodispersity with a coefficient of variation ($CV$) $< 3\%$ across the target sizing channel.

4. **Stock Dispersion & Cleanroom Preparation**:
   - Suspend certified spheres in ultra-pure deionized water ($\text{UPW}$) with trace non-ionic surfactant.
   - Degas and ultrasonic-agitate for 5 minutes to eliminate agglomeration prior to controlled surface deposition onto bare silicon test wafers for post-RCA-1 cleaning efficiency (PRE) benchmarking.

---

### Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

```text
Metrology Target Standards (180nm Node)
                       ┌───────────────────────────────┐
                       │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
       Cap Max EOT (nm)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
                       │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒       │
       Cap Min EOT (nm)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒       │
    Gate Ox Target (nm)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓    │
                       │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓    │
Si3N4 RI (n at 632.8nm)┤████████████████               │
                       │████████████████               │
                       └┬───────┬──────┬───────┬──────┬┘
                        0       1      2       3      4 
```

| Metric / Parameter | Target Value | Tolerance / Range | Physical Units |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **$\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ Calibration Refractive Index** | $2.00$ | $\pm 0.02$ (at $\lambda = 632.8\text{ nm}$) | Dimensionless ($n$) |
| **Calibration Particle Size Range (Pitch Baseline)** | $360\text{ to }400$ | $\pm 5\%$ | $\text{nm}$ |
| **Gate Oxide Reference Layer Sensitivity Range** | $3.5\text{ to }4.0$ | $\pm 0.2$ | $\text{nm}$ (EOT) |
| **Particle Size Distribution Monodispersity ($CV$)** | $< 3.0$ | Max $\le 3.0$ | $\%$ |

---

### Literature Context & Citations

- **Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD) of Silicon Nitride Hard Masks**:  
  Used to establish the optical refractive index benchmark ($n = 2.00 \pm 0.02$ at $632.8\text{ nm}$) and material density expectations for calibration nitride particles.
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**:  
  Defines bitline and wordline pitch specifications ($360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$) and physical equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) requirements ($3\text{ to }4\text{ nm}$, with gate dielectric dry oxidation thickness of $3.5\text{ to }4.0\text{ nm}$) driving metrology calibration limits.
- **Deal-Grove Silicon Thermal Oxidation Kinetics in Quartz Tube Furnace**:  
  Sets physical gate oxide thickness baseline targets ($3.5\text{ to }4.0\text{ nm}$) grown at $900^\circ\text{C}-1000^\circ\text{C}$ to evaluate surface roughness and particle contamination thresholds.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Procuring polystyrene latex (PSL) along with inorganic SiO2 and Si3N4 standard nanoparticles creates an optical scattering discrepancy on bare Si wafers that must be reconciled. While PSL spheres have a refractive index of n=1.59 (with k=0 at 488/633 nm), silicon nitride exhibits n~2.05 and silicon dioxide exhibits n~1.46. Dark-field surface inspection systems (laser particle counters) calibrated strictly via PSL will assign an erroneous Light Scattering Equivalent (LSE) optical diameter to nitride and oxide particles due to differences in polarizability and Mie scattering cross-sections. Verification sizing must integrate orthogonal metrology (DLS/AFM/SEM) rather than trusting uncorrected laser scanner binning.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Nanoparticle standards in colloidal suspension are prone to agglomeration, sedimentation, and surfactant/stabilizer residue contamination during wafer deposition (e.g., via aerosol nebulization). For RCA-1 Particle Removal Efficiency (PRE) baseline qualification on 180nm gate dielectric surfaces, doublets and triplets skew the baseline defect counts and mimic post-clean residue failures. The procurement specification must mandate NIST-traceable narrow size distributions (CV < 3%), monodisperse suspensions in trace-metal-free ultra-pure water (<1 ppb ionic background), and verification protocols using Dynamic Light Scattering (DLS) or Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) before aerosolization.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Certified NIST-traceable Si3N4 and SiO2 nanoparticles with narrow geometric standard deviations (nominal diameters 100 nm and 180 nm) have long lead times (6 to 10 weeks) and cold-chain shipping requirements (stored at 2°C to 8°C, strictly preventing freezing which induces irreversible flocculation). Dual-sourcing between specialized metrology suppliers (such as Applied Physics/Thermo Fisher/Duke Standards) and establishing immediate receiving inspection protocols are mandatory to avoid holding up the RCA-1 clean bench qualification timeline.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Procurement cost for NIST-certified polydisperse/monodisperse dielectric standards is substantial and recurring due to limited colloidal shelf life (typically 12 months unopened, 3 months opened). Unopened containers must be registered in the Fab inventory database with clear barcode tracking, expiration monitors, and quarantine protocols upon cold-chain breach, preventing downstream contamination of the pre-oxidation wet bench.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Irreversible colloidal agglomeration due to shipping/storage temperature excursion below 0°C or beyond expiry, resulting in multi-micron cluster deposition instead of nominal 180 nm single-particle challenge.
1. Surfactant and ionic contamination (e.g., sodium, sulfates) in standard stabilizer solution cross-contaminating the pre-oxidation RCA bench, causing mobile ionic charge degradation in the 3.5 nm dry gate oxide.
1. Mie scattering calibration skew: Misinterpreting Si3N4 180 nm particles as >250 nm LSE on dark-field wafer inspection due to optical index mismatch, corrupting post-RCA-1 PRE percentage calculations.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-1-3-1-1-01` | **Colloidal Hydrodynamic Diameter and Polydispersity Verification via DLS** | Malvern Zetasizer Nano ZS / Dynamic Light Scattering (DLS) Spectrometer with 633 nm He-Ne Laser | 1. Pipette 1.0 mL of as-received certified SiO2 or Si3N4 nanoparticle standard into clean cuvette under ISO Class 5 laminar flow. 2. Sonicate in ultrasonic bath at 40 kHz for 60 seconds to eliminate loose agglomerates. 3. Insert cuvette into DLS sample chamber thermostatted at 25.0°C ± 0.1°C. 4. Acquire 3 consecutive runs of 15 sub-runs each, measuring intensity-weighted hydrodynamic diameter (Z-average) and Polydispersity Index (PDI). 5. Compute mean Z-average diameter and check distribution monodispersity. | `Z-average hydrodynamic diameter must match nominal certified diameter within ±5.0% (e.g., 180.0 nm ± 9.0 nm for nominal 180 nm standard); Polydispersity Index (PDI) must be <= 0.050; secondary agglomeration peak intensity (>500 nm) must be 0.0%.` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-1-3-1-1-02` | **Physical Geometric Sizing and Monodispersity Verification via AFM/SEM** | Atomic Force Microscope (AFM in Tapping Mode) with calibrated silicon tip (tip radius < 10 nm) or CD-SEM (Cold Field Emission at 1.0 kV) | 1. Load coupon with deposited nanoparticle standards onto AFM vacuum chuck. 2. Acquire 5 um x 5 um tapping mode topographic scans across 5 designated dies/regions. 3. Perform particle height analysis on minimum 100 individual discrete particles using SPM image processing software. 4. Generate histogram of physical spherical heights (Z-axis height measurement, avoiding tip-convolution lateral broadening). 5. Calculate mean geometric diameter, standard deviation, and doublet-to-singlet ratio. | `Mean physical particle height must measure within ±3.0% of NIST certificate value; standard deviation (sigma) must be <= 5.0 nm; aggregated/doublet fraction must be < 2.0% of total identified particles.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (double gloving required), ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical safety goggles, ISO Class 5 compatible cleanroom bunny suit with integrated hood, N95 or P100 particulate respirator during aerosolization system setup
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Inhalation: Move exposed researcher to fresh air immediately; seek medical attention if cough or dyspnea develops due to aerosolized nanoparticle inhalation. Skin contact: Flush affected skin with abundant UPW for 15 minutes and wash with non-abrasive soap. Eye contact: Irrigate eyes at eyewash station for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open. Ingestion: Rinse mouth thoroughly with water; do not induce vomiting.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Nanoparticle preparation and aerosolization deposition chamber must operate strictly inside an ISO Class 5 laminar flow hood equipped with dedicated HEPA/ULPA filtration and certified local exhaust ventilation (minimum face velocity 100 FPM / 0.51 m/s) to prevent inhalation of airborne nanoparticles.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Aqueous nanoparticle suspensions must be collected into designated heavy metal/inorganic chemical waste carboys. Nanoparticles must not be poured into domestic or general cleanroom drains. Waste must undergo flocculation filtration with polyacrylamide or be disposed of via certified hazardous waste management.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Silicon Dioxide (Amorphous / Colloidal Silica)** | `7631-86-9` | NIST Traceable Analytical Standard | `1.0 wt% in aqueous suspension` |
| **Silicon Nitride Nanoparticles** | `12033-89-5` | Certified Nanoparticle Metrology Standard (>99.9% metal basis) | `0.1 wt% in aqueous suspension` |
| **Polystyrene Latex (PSL) Spheres** | `9003-53-6` | NIST Traceable Size Standard | `1.0 wt% in aqueous suspension with trace surfactant` |
| **Deionized Ultra-Pure Water (UPW)** | `7732-18-5` | Semiconductor Grade Type E-1 (18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100 wt%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `15 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `2 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly opened, cold-chain-verified sealed amber glass or fluoropolymer bottles of certified standards at 20°C-25°C.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Sized, verified, and sonicated monodisperse stock suspensions loaded into sealed aerosolization delivery canisters under dry N2 head-space.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding ambient queue time leads to evaporation, increased local ionic strength, irreversible colloidal aggregation into micron-scale clumps, and microbial/airborne contamination compromising baseline PRE wafer deposition.

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Procurement receipt, cold-chain compliance verification, and multi-technique hydrodynamic and physical sizing validation for certified 100 nm and 180 nm Si3N4, SiO2, and PSL nanoparticle calibration standards, confirming NIST-traceable monodispersity and absence of aggregates prior to baseline wafer seeding.

| `ASSERT-02` | **Polydispersity Index (PDI) of certified aqueous standard** | `0.030` | <= 0.050 maximum | ISO 22412 DLS autocorrelation curve slope fitting |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Singlet discrete particle population fraction verified by AFM topographic height** | `99.0%` | >= 98.0% (agglomerate/doublet rate < 2.0%) | AFM tapping-mode 5x5 um topographic profiling counting minimum 100 isolated particles |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal signoff requires 100% cold-chain documentation compliance from dispatch to receipt, successful DLS Z-average and PDI criteria fulfillment on all procured lots, and AFM verification proving <2.0% doublet fraction, with signed approval from Domain Metrology Expert and Lead Cleanroom Systems Engineer.

critics.systems_engineer: Procuring polystyrene latex (PSL) along with inorganic SiO2 and Si3N4 standard nanoparticles creates an optical scattering discrepancy on bare Si wafers that must be reconciled. While PSL spheres have a refractive index of n=1.59 (with k=0 at 488/633 nm), silicon nitride exhibits n~2.05 and silicon dioxide exhibits n~1.46. Dark-field surface inspection systems (laser particle counters) calibrated strictly via PSL will assign an erroneous Light Scattering Equivalent (LSE) optical diameter to nitride and oxide particles due to differences in polarizability and Mie scattering cross-sections. Verification sizing must integrate orthogonal metrology (DLS/AFM/SEM) rather than trusting uncorrected laser scanner binning.
critics.domain_expert: Nanoparticle standards in colloidal suspension are prone to agglomeration, sedimentation, and surfactant/stabilizer residue contamination during wafer deposition (e.g., via aerosol nebulization). For RCA-1 Particle Removal Efficiency (PRE) baseline qualification on 180nm gate dielectric surfaces, doublets and triplets skew the baseline defect counts and mimic post-clean residue failures. The procurement specification must mandate NIST-traceable narrow size distributions (CV < 3%), monodisperse suspensions in trace-metal-free ultra-pure water (<1 ppb ionic background), and verification protocols using Dynamic Light Scattering (DLS) or Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) before aerosolization.
critics.supply_chain: Certified NIST-traceable Si3N4 and SiO2 nanoparticles with narrow geometric standard deviations (nominal diameters 100 nm and 180 nm) have long lead times (6 to 10 weeks) and cold-chain shipping requirements (stored at 2°C to 8°C, strictly preventing freezing which induces irreversible flocculation). Dual-sourcing between specialized metrology suppliers (such as Applied Physics/Thermo Fisher/Duke Standards) and establishing immediate receiving inspection protocols are mandatory to avoid holding up the RCA-1 clean bench qualification timeline.
critics.laya_pm: Procurement cost for NIST-certified polydisperse/monodisperse dielectric standards is substantial and recurring due to limited colloidal shelf life (typically 12 months unopened, 3 months opened). Unopened containers must be registered in the Fab inventory database with clear barcode tracking, expiration monitors, and quarantine protocols upon cold-chain breach, preventing downstream contamination of the pre-oxidation wet bench.

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document Details
- **Title:** Aerosol Deposition and Surface Seeding of Controlled Test Particles on Monitor Wafers
- **Target Node:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (Gen 2 / µm)
- **Module:** Wet Chemistry / Metrology Surface Qualification
- **Action Type:** Make

---

### 1. Process Overview & Objective
Establish a reproducible, cleanroom-compliant procedure for seeding controlled inorganic test particles ($\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ / $\text{SiO}_2$) onto monitor silicon wafers. This baseline preparation is required to calibrate metrology systems and qualify the Particle Removal Efficiency (PRE) of downstream clean processes (such as RCA-1 / SC-1) prior to critical 180nm gate oxidation.

```text
+-----------------------+     +-------------------------+     +-----------------------+
|  Bare / Monitor Si    | --> | Pre-Deposition Surface  | --> | Controlled Aerosol    |
|  Wafer Inspection     |     | Prep (Dehydration/Clean)|     | Particle Seeding      |
+-----------------------+     +-------------------------+     +-----------------------+
                                                                          |
                                                                          v
+-----------------------+     +-------------------------+     +-----------------------+
| PRE / Clean Benchmark | <-- | Metrology Baseline      | <-- | N2 Purge & Soft Bake  |
| Ready                 |     | Surface Defect Mapping  |     | Fixation              |
+-----------------------+     +-------------------------+     +-----------------------+
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Substrate Pre-Cleaning & Dehydration:**
   - Prepare bare monitor wafers by executing an intermediate dump rinse using $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ deionized water for 3 minutes.
   - Strip any non-uniform native oxide layers using a $1:50\text{ HF}:\text{H}_2\text{O}$ dip for 15–30 seconds until the surface transitions to hydrophobic.
   - Perform wafer dehydration in a clean convection oven or hotplate at $150^\circ\text{C}\text{ to }200^\circ\text{C}$ for 30 minutes to desorb physisorbed water molecules prior to particle loading.

2. **Aerosol Particle Suspension & Generation:**
   - Prepare a certified liquid suspension of uniform test particles ($\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ / $\text{SiO}_2$ spheres calibrated for Gen 2 sub-micron qualification) diluted in ultra-pure deionized water ($18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$).
   - Load the colloidal suspension into a calibrated aerosol atomizer connected to high-purity carrier gas ($\text{N}_2$).

3. **Chamber Seeding & Deposition Cycle:**
   - Load the prepared monitor wafer onto the deposition chuck inside the sealed aerosol deposition chamber.
   - Introduce the atomized aerosol stream at a regulated gas flow rate, ensuring a uniform laminar flow showerhead distribution across the wafer surface.
   - Maintain the deposition cycle to target controlled particle count distribution across the wafer area.

4. **Drying and Particle Fixation:**
   - Purge the deposition chamber using high-purity $\text{N}_2$ to clear residual aerosol mist and prevent uncontrolled agglomeration.
   - Perform a low-temperature fixation bake at $150^\circ\text{C}$ to evaporate any residual moisture droplets, leaving dry, seeded surface particles adhered via van der Waals forces.

5. **Post-Seeding Metrology Handoff:**
   - Transfer the seeded wafer to an automated optical surface defect mapper (particle counter) to establish the pre-clean baseline count and coordinate map.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric | Tolerance / Limit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Rinse Water Resistivity** | $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ | Minimum threshold | In-line resistivity sensor |
| **Native Oxide Strip Time** | $15\text{ to }30\text{ s}$ | In $1:50\text{ HF}:\text{H}_2\text{O}$ solution | Immersion timer / Contact angle inspection |
| **Wafer Dehydration Bake Temperature** | $150^\circ\text{C}\text{ to }200^\circ\text{C}$ | Maintained for 30 minutes | Calibrated thermal thermocouple |
| **Test Particle Film Refractive Index ($\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$)** | $n = 2.00$ | $\pm 0.02$ at $632.8\text{ nm}$ | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry |

---

### 4. Verified Source Citations

- **Source: Standard RCA-1 and RCA-2 Silicon Wafer Cleaning Procedure**
  - Rinse specification: Dump rinse with $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ deionized water for 3 minutes.
  - HF strip parameters: $1:50\text{ HF}:\text{H}_2\text{O}$ dip for 15–30 seconds for surface oxide removal and transition from hydrophilic to hydrophobic.
  - Final dry specification: High-purity $\text{N}_2$ blow-dry.

- **Source: Photoresist Spin Coating Dynamics and HMDS Vapor Priming**
  - Substrate dehydration parameters: Bake at $150^\circ\text{C}\text{ to }200^\circ\text{C}$ for 30 minutes to desorb physisorbed water molecules.

- **Source: Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD) of Silicon Nitride Hard Masks**
  - $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ physical metrics: Refractive index $n = 2.00 \pm 0.02$ at $632.8\text{ nm}$, high etch resistance against HF/BOE ($< 0.5\text{ nm/min}$).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Seeding PSL (polystyrene latex) or Si3N4/SiO2 test particles via aerosol generation directly challenges cross-contamination boundaries in cleanroom wet benches. The aerosol chamber, pneumatic transport tubing, and electrostatic neutralizer must be strictly physically isolated from the primary pre-diffusion RCA wet bench line. In addition, using liquid atomization introduces droplet residue artifacts (solvent rings, surfactant dry-out) which mimic real defect counts on laser scattering defect inspection tools unless drying gas velocity and sheath flow are tightly regulated.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Particle size standards for 180nm node pre-clean PRE (Particle Removal Efficiency) qualification require a strict monodisperse distribution centered at 150-200 nm for standard qualification and down to 80-100 nm for baseline sensitivity mapping. Atomization of colloidal Si3N4 or silica spheres requires active differential mobility analysis (DMA) or electrostatic classification to prevent particle doublet/triplet agglomerates from depositing onto the wafer, which would distort PRE calculations by artificially shifting the optical scattering cross-section.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Certified monodisperse colloidal silica (SiO2) and silicon nitride (Si3N4) calibration suspensions with NIST-traceable particle size certificates have extended procurement lead times (>8-12 weeks in Vietnam). Secondary sources and domestic chemical distribution networks must be audited for surfactant types present in the colloidal matrix, as non-ionic surfactants can foul wet bench quartz tanks and alter surface zeta potential during SC-1 immersion.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Aerosol deposition must yield a uniform wafer defect density between 3,000 and 6,000 defects/wafer (100mm/150mm monitor) within a deposition run of under 5 minutes per wafer to support iterative RCA-1 cleaning trials without creating a metrology queue bottleneck before thermal gate oxidation.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Particle agglomeration during aerosol desolvation leading to multi-particle cluster deposition and inaccurate optical defect classification on wafer inspection tools.
1. Surfactant and ionic residue drying onto the monitor surface from the carrier suspension, inducing localized chemical masking and blocking standard SC-1 chemical etching/undercut mechanisms.
1. Uncontrolled electrostatic charging of the monitor wafer surface causing radial non-uniformity and edge-exclusion particle clustering due to field-enhanced deposition.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-1-3-1-2-01` | **Aerosol Deposition Density and Monodispersity Qualification** | Scanning Surface Inspection System (Laser Scattering Defect Tool, e.g., KLA Tencor Surfscan / particle counter) and Differential Mobility Analyzer (DMA) Aerosol Generator | 1. Load clean monitor wafer into aerosol deposition chamber under laminar N2 sheath flow. 2. Atomize colloidal silica standard (nominal 150 nm NIST-traceable) at 35 psi N2 carrier pressure. 3. Pass aerosol through diffusion dryer (RH < 5%) and DMA configured for 150 nm monodisperse selection. 4. Expose monitor wafer to electrostatic-assisted deposition for 180 seconds. 5. Unload wafer into clean FOUP and transfer to laser surface defect inspection tool to map defect count, size binning, and spatial uniformity. | `Total added defect count must be between 3,500 and 5,500 particles per 150mm wafer; >= 85% of detected particles must fall within the 140-160 nm size bin; radial variation (center-to-edge defect density ratio) must be <= 1.25.` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-1-3-1-2-02` | **Surface Zeta Potential and Non-Volatile Residue Verification** | SurPASS Electrokinetic Surface Analyzer / Streaming Potential Metrology and Total Reflection X-Ray Fluorescence (TXRF) | 1. Measure streaming potential of virgin vs seeded wafer coupon across pH 3 to pH 10 electrolyte solution (1 mM KCl) to calculate surface isoelectric point (IEP). 2. Run TXRF across 5 wafer points to quantify non-volatile ionic residues (Na, K, Ca, Fe) introduced from colloidal suspension stabilizers. 3. Inspect high-density seeding zones under High-Resolution SEM (50kX) to detect presence of dry halos or chemical ring stains. | `Isoelectric point (IEP) shift between virgin and seeded surface must be <= 0.3 pH units; metallic contamination (Na, Ca, Fe) by TXRF must be <= 5.0E10 atoms/cm^2; zero visible chemical residue halos detected via SEM across 20 inspection sites.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (double gloved, 12-inch cuff), Chemical splash goggles with ANSI Z87.1 rating, HEPA-rated particle respirator (N95 or P100) during powder/concentrated suspension handling, Class 100 cleanroom antistatic ESD smock and head covering
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Inhalation: Remove victim to fresh air immediately; seek medical attention if cough or dyspnea develops. Skin Contact: Wash thoroughly with mild soap and deionized water for at least 15 minutes; remove contaminated cleanroom garments. Eye Contact: Flush eyes with sterile eye-wash solution for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open. Ingestion: Rinse mouth with water; do not induce vomiting; contact cleanroom emergency response coordinator immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Aerosol deposition chamber must be exhausted to dedicated industrial scrubbed cleanroom exhaust at negative static pressure (-0.5 to -1.0 in. w.g.) with an in-line ULPA/HEPA filtration trap (99.999% efficiency at 0.1 um) before building effluent release.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent colloidal suspensions and rinse effluents must be collected in closed polyethylene hazardous waste containers; do not discharge concentrated nanomaterials into the general acid waste (AWW) drain; package with absorbed pads and manifest for certified micro-particle hazardous disposal.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Colloidal Silicon Dioxide (SiO2)** | `7631-86-9` | NIST-Traceable Calibration Grade / Nanoparticle Standard | `0.1% w/v aqueous suspension` |
| **Silicon Nitride (Si3N4)** | `12033-89-5` | High Purity Sub-Micron Grade (>99.9%) | `0.05% w/v dispersed in UPW` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade (VLSI/SEMI-1) | `99.9%` |
| **Ultra-Pure Deionized Water (UPW)** | `7732-18-5` | SEMI C35 Grade (18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `6 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Chemical Oxide Passivated Hydrophilic Surface (post-clean native/chemical oxide ~0.8-1.2 nm, contact angle < 10 degrees, particle count < 20 at >= 0.12 um).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Particle-Seeded Controlled Monitor Surface (3,500-5,500 monodisperse particles/wafer, dry N2-purged, zero liquid droplet staining).
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive queue time causes irreversible chemisorption of airborne molecular contaminants (siloxanes, phthalates, amine organics) and capillary-induced particle adhesion bridging (van der Waals to covalent siloxane bond transition), artificially suppressing measured SC-1 particle removal efficiency (PRE).

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful aerosol deposition and surface seeding of monodisperse SiO2/Si3N4 calibration test particles onto monitor wafers to establish a reproducible, known defect baseline for qualifying RCA-1 particle removal efficiency prior to 180nm gate oxidation.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `Aerosol_Deposition_Defect_Map_TC_1_1_3_1_2.csv`
- [ ] `Particle_Size_Distribution_Histogram_150nm.pdf`
- [ ] `Monitor_Wafer_Seeding_SEM_Confirmation.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Total controlled test particle seeding count on 150mm monitor wafer** | `4500` | ±1000 particles | Automated Laser Surface Particle Inspection (Surfscan) full-wafer scan (>= 0.12 um threshold) |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Seeded particle monodispersity ratio within target sizing bin (140 nm - 160 nm)** | `90.0` | >= 85.0% | Optical defect size binning from calibrated laser scattering histogram |

critics.systems_engineer: Seeding PSL (polystyrene latex) or Si3N4/SiO2 test particles via aerosol generation directly challenges cross-contamination boundaries in cleanroom wet benches. The aerosol chamber, pneumatic transport tubing, and electrostatic neutralizer must be strictly physically isolated from the primary pre-diffusion RCA wet bench line. In addition, using liquid atomization introduces droplet residue artifacts (solvent rings, surfactant dry-out) which mimic real defect counts on laser scattering defect inspection tools unless drying gas velocity and sheath flow are tightly regulated.
critics.domain_expert: Particle size standards for 180nm node pre-clean PRE (Particle Removal Efficiency) qualification require a strict monodisperse distribution centered at 150-200 nm for standard qualification and down to 80-100 nm for baseline sensitivity mapping. Atomization of colloidal Si3N4 or silica spheres requires active differential mobility analysis (DMA) or electrostatic classification to prevent particle doublet/triplet agglomerates from depositing onto the wafer, which would distort PRE calculations by artificially shifting the optical scattering cross-section.
critics.supply_chain: Certified monodisperse colloidal silica (SiO2) and silicon nitride (Si3N4) calibration suspensions with NIST-traceable particle size certificates have extended procurement lead times (>8-12 weeks in Vietnam). Secondary sources and domestic chemical distribution networks must be audited for surfactant types present in the colloidal matrix, as non-ionic surfactants can foul wet bench quartz tanks and alter surface zeta potential during SC-1 immersion.
critics.laya_pm: Aerosol deposition must yield a uniform wafer defect density between 3,000 and 6,000 defects/wafer (100mm/150mm monitor) within a deposition run of under 5 minutes per wafer to support iterative RCA-1 cleaning trials without creating a metrology queue bottleneck before thermal gate oxidation.
critical_failure_modes: Particle agglomeration during aerosol desolvation leading to multi-particle cluster deposition and inaccurate optical defect classification on wafer inspection tools.
Surfactant and ionic residue drying onto the monitor surface from the carrier suspension, inducing localized chemical masking and blocking standard SC-1 chemical etching/undercut mechanisms.
Uncontrolled electrostatic charging of the monitor wafer surface causing radial non-uniformity and edge-exclusion particle clustering due to field-enhanced deposition.

testcases.pre_conditions: 150mm P-type <100> monitor wafer with pre-deposition baseline particle count < 20 defects at >= 0.12 um; atomization suspension diluted with 18.2 MOhm-cm UPW to target concentration; aerosol neutralizer (Kr-85 or soft X-ray) active.

testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Total added defect count must be between 3,500 and 5,500 particles per 150mm wafer; >= 85% of detected particles must fall within the 140-160 nm size bin; radial variation (center-to-edge defect density ratio) must be <= 1.25.

testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Isoelectric point (IEP) shift between virgin and seeded surface must be <= 0.3 pH units; metallic contamination (Na, Ca, Fe) by TXRF must be <= 5.0E10 atoms/cm^2; zero visible chemical residue halos detected via SEM across 20 inspection sites.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-MET-180-LSS-001`
**Title:** Pre-Clean Baseline Laser Surface Scanning and Defect Coordinate Metrology Mapping  
**Node Generation:** Gen 2 (180 nm DRAM Integration)  
**Process Step Classification:** Metrology / Make  
**Parent Hierarchy:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > 180nm Dry Gate Oxide Growth (3.5 nm) > Pre-Oxidation RCA Clean and In-Situ HF Dip Surface Preparation > RCA-1 (SC-1) Organic & Particle Removal Bath Formulation and Bench Qualification > Post-RCA-1 Particle Removal Efficiency (PRE) and Surface Roughness Metrology Qualification > Si3N4/SiO2 Test Particle Deposition and Pre-Clean Baseline Defect Mapping > Pre-Clean Baseline Laser Surface Scanning and Defect Coordinate Metrology Mapping

---

### 1. Workflow Architecture

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Wafer Load & Chuck   │
│  Vacuum Verification  │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│   Notch Alignment &   │
│   Coordinate Origin   │
│         Setup         │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│   Full-Wafer Laser    │
│  Surface Dark-Field   │
│       Scanning        │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│   Defect Coordinate   │
│  Binning & KLARF Map  │
│        Export         │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Concise Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Substrate Handling & Chuck Loading:**
   - Transfer the post-deposition test wafer (deposited with $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4/\text{SiO}_2$ calibration/challenge particles) onto the automated laser surface scanner end-effector.
   - Load wafer face-up onto the vacuum chuck. Engage vacuum retention ($\ge 80\text{ kPa}$) to eliminate wafer slip or vibration during high-speed rotation/translation.
2. **Pre-Alignment & Coordinate Origin Indexing:**
   - Optical pre-aligner detects the wafer notch/flat and center coordinates.
   - Establish the polar-to-Cartesian global reference coordinate system $(X=0.000\text{ mm}, Y=0.000\text{ mm})$ referenced directly to the wafer center with notch orientation defined at $0^\circ / 180^\circ$.
3. **Laser Optics & Dark-Field Scanning Setup:**
   - Select dark-field oblique/normal incidence solid-state laser channel calibrated for unpatterned bare silicon and ultra-thin dielectric surfaces.
   - Set scan recipe with a 3 mm edge exclusion zone across the wafer surface.
4. **Helical / Raster Surface Scan Execution:**
   - Initiate laser surface inspection via coordinated chuck rotation (r-$\theta$) or high-speed X-Y stage translation.
   - Collect scattered light signal through low-angle and high-angle PMT/photodiode collectors to capture Rayleigh-scattered signatures from particulate matter down to sub-micron baseline thresholds.
5. **Coordinate Extraction, Binning & Map Generation:**
   - Extract raw defect scatter events: compile physical coordinate pairs $(X_i, Y_i)$, scattering cross-section, and equivalent polystyrene latex (PSL) sphere diameter bin.
   - Export standard baseline defect coordinate map (`.klarf` / Klarf file format) into the metrology server for subsequent Post-RCA-1 Particle Removal Efficiency (PRE) coordinate-by-coordinate matching.

---

### 3. Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Physical Unit | Measurement Method / Tool |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Edge Exclusion Zone** | $3.0 \pm 0.5$ | $\text{mm}$ | Automated recipe perimeter mask |
| **Coordinate Location Repeatability ($3\sigma$)** | $\le 10$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Repeat-pass defect re-detection registration |
| **Scan Surface Vacuum Chuck Pressure** | $\ge 80$ | $\text{kPa}$ | In-situ vacuum transducer interlock |
| **Substrate Center Offset ($\Delta X, \Delta Y$)** | $\le 15$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Optical notch/center pre-aligner sensor |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Context & Citations

1. **[180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench](docs/context.yaml)**:
   - Identifies the critical active area and feature dimensions for the 180nm DRAM node (access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$). Baseline particle coordinate fidelity prior to wet cleaning is critical to prevent bridging across cell contact geometries and stacked capacitor structures.
2. **[Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology](docs/context.yaml)**:
   - Establishes the non-destructive optical characterization framework and tight process limits required for thin dielectrics (e.g. 3.5 nm dry gate oxide with sub-Ångström precision $\pm 0.05\text{ nm}$ and multi-point automated mapping). Ensures zero chemical or optical contamination from prior metrology passes before thermal oxidation.
3. **[Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering](docs/context.yaml)**:
   - Details critical dimensions including the 360 nm to 400 nm bitline/wordline pitches and the $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ physical gate oxide thickness grown at 850°C–900°C dry oxidation. Undetected pre-clean particulate defects propagate directly into fatal dielectric gate punch-through and retention degradation ($< 64\text{ ms}$ at 85°C).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: In Gen 1 macro-scale implementation, optical laser surface scanning (unpatterned wafer inspection via dark-field scattering) must align coordinate reference frames directly with notch/flat orientation fiducials to enable 1-to-1 defect tracking post-RCA-1. Without a rigid kinematically repeatable stage and automated coordinate transform matrix, spatial defect correlation errors will exceed the millimeter-level baseline grid tolerance (±100 µm stage jitter), invalidating Particle Removal Efficiency (PRE) calculations across sequential process steps.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Baseline laser scattering metrology for pre-clean inspection relies on Mie scattering physics for Si3N4 and SiO2 challenge particles. At Gen 1 macroscopic limits, distinguishing haze (micro-roughness background scattering, Ra > 0.2 nm) from localized point defect light scattering (LSE - Latex Sphere Equivalent diameter down to 100-200 nm) requires calibrated polarization ratioing (P-pol vs S-pol illumination) and clear photomultiplier tube (PMT) gain thresholds to prevent false positive saturation from ambient cleanroom dust fall.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Commercial automated wafer surface defect inspection tools (e.g., KLA-Tencor Surfscan) are cost-prohibitive and export-restricted for open-source garage-scale fabs. Sourcing or retrofitting second-hand laser particle counters or constructing an open-source 405nm diode laser scanning gantry with calibrated NIST-traceable polystyrene latex (PSL) sphere wafers is mandatory to sustain repeatable calibration standards within local budget constraints.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Defect scanning sits directly on the critical path prior to RCA-1 bench immersion. Any bottleneck or delay during baseline map acquisition risks breaching the atmospheric Q-time envelope, leading to unmonitored organic aerosol adsorption and native oxide regrowth prior to clean bath dipping. Map generation and file export must take under 15 minutes per wafer run.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Coordinate system drift (>200 µm mismatch between pre-clean and post-clean scans), rendering automated subtraction algorithms unable to pair individual deposited test particles and causing false PRE reporting.
1. Laser flare and specular reflection leakage into the dark-field PMT collector due to wafer edge bevel scattering, obscuring peripheral defect detection across the outer 5 mm exclusion zone.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-1-3-1-3-01` | **NIST-Traceable PSL Sphere Size and Coordinate Calibration Scan** | Dark-Field Laser Surface Defect Scanner (405nm diode laser, NA 0.40 collection optics, dual PMT detectors, motorized XY stage with 1 µm optical rotary encoders) | 1. Load calibration wafer onto kinematic 3-pin chuck with wafer notch aligned to optical home sensor. 2. Execute spiral or raster laser scanning across the 100mm wafer area with 3 mm edge exclusion at 10 mm/s scan speed. 3. Acquire analog scatter pulses, digitize via high-speed ADC, and bin scattered pulse height intensities. 4. Map detected centroid coordinates (X, Y) relative to notch origin (0, 0). 5. Compute capture rate against certified challenge particle count and evaluate spatial coordinate repeatability over 3 successive scans. | `Particle sizing accuracy within ±10% of nominal (180 nm - 220 nm bin for 200 nm spheres); positional repeatability standard deviation sigma_(X,Y) <= 15 µm; false count rate on background blank region < 5 counts/wafer.` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-1-3-1-3-02` | **Pre-Clean Baseline Defect Coordinate Mapping for Si3N4/SiO2 Deposited Wafers** | Calibrated Laser Surface Scanner, Optical Review Microscope (100x Darkfield/Brightfield DIC with digital CMOS camera), Wafer Inspection Coordinate Analysis Software | 1. Transfer test wafer from N2 carrier to inspection stage within 5 minutes of carrier opening. 2. Initiate full-wafer automated surface defect scan across active area (5 mm edge exclusion). 3. Record all localized scattering events exceeding 150 nm LSE threshold into a coordinate point-cloud array (Defect ID, X, Y, Scatter Magnitude, Estimated Bin Size). 4. Drive stage to 10 randomly sampled defect coordinates under optical review microscope to cross-verify physical particle presence vs optical noise artifact. 5. Export coordinate KLARF/CSV map file and lock file checksum. | `Total baseline defect count recorded between 1,000 and 5,000 discrete points; optical review confirmation rate >= 90% (>= 9 of 10 sampled coordinates physically verified as real particles); scan cycle time <= 12 minutes.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 3B/4 certified laser safety goggles rated for 405nm (Optical Density OD 6+), Non-shedding nitrile cleanroom gloves (Class 100 compatible), Anti-static ESD cleanroom lab coat, Polypropylene safety face shield during wafer handling, Particulate-filtering face mask (N95 or cleanroom-rated surgical mask)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Laser exposure: Immediate medical attention for retinal or dermal beam strike; do not rub eyes. IPA contact: Flush skin or eyes with emergency eye-wash/shower station for 15 minutes; remove contaminated cleanroom garments. Inhalation of solvent fumes: Move victim to fresh air immediately; provide artificial respiration if not breathing.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated mini-environment Class 100 laminar flow hood with HEPA filtration (0.3 µm at 99.97% capture); local exhaust ventilation (LEV) on optics enclosure with static pressure maintained at -0.05 in. w.g. to evacuate solvent vapours and ozone from laser head.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA wipes sealed in airtight hazardous solvent waste bins and disposed of according to flammable waste regulatory streams; empty solvent containers triple-rinsed and aerated before hazardous disposal.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) for stage/optics wipe** | `67-63-0` | Electronic / MOS Grade (VLSI) | `99.9%` |
| **Nitrogen Gas (Purge and Air Curtain)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity (UHP Grade 5.0) | `99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Dry silicon wafer bearing dispersed Si3N4/SiO2 test particles, hydrophobic/semi-hydrophilic native oxide state, free of gross liquid droplet stains.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Scanned baseline wafer with verified coordinate map, stored in sealed purged fluoropolymer (PFA/PTFE) wafer carrier ready for RCA-1 bath loading.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excess air exposure (>30 min) causes uncontrolled airborne organic hydrocarbon adsorption and airborne molecular contamination (AMC), altering particle adhesion force via capillary condensation and skewing subsequent RCA-1 Particle Removal Efficiency measurements.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Complete non-destructive baseline surface defect inspection and coordinate mapping of the 100mm silicon test wafer prior to RCA-1 cleaning. A high-resolution spatial coordinate map (KLARF/CSV) is generated, quantifying pre-clean particle counts, size distributions, and physical stage coordinates with micro-positioning accuracy.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `PRE_CLEAN_BASELINE_DEFECT_MAP_W01.csv`
- [ ] `SURFACE_SCAN_INTENSITY_HISTOGRAM_W01.pdf`
- [ ] `DEFECT_COORDINATE_OVERLAY_REPORT_W01.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-1-3-1-3-01` | **Stage coordinate positioning repeatability standard deviation across 3 reference scans** | `10.0` | +5.0 µm | Laser scanning encoder feedback and optical fiducial cross-correlation |
| `ASSERT-TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-1-3-1-3-02` | **Optical microscope cross-verification capture rate of sampled scattering coordinates** | `95.0` | -5.0 % | Automated dark-field review optical imaging at 100x magnification |
| `ASSERT-TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-1-3-1-3-03` | **Total unpatterned wafer scan and map generation duration per 100mm substrate** | `10.0` | +2.0 minutes | Integrated software scan timestamp log |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Researcher signs off only when baseline coordinate CSV contains >= 1,000 distinct particle entries, optical confirmation rate exceeds 90%, background noise floor remains < 5 counts/wafer, and the wafer is transferred to N2 storage within 30 minutes of initial room air exposure.

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Laser Surface Particle Scanning and PRE Quantification Across Particle Size Bins

**Branch Path:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > 180nm Dry Gate Oxide Growth (3.5 nm) > Pre-Oxidation RCA Clean and In-Situ HF Dip Surface Preparation > RCA-1 (SC-1) Organic & Particle Removal Bath Formulation and Bench Qualification > Post-RCA-1 Particle Removal Efficiency (PRE) and Surface Roughness Metrology Qualification > **Laser Surface Particle Scanning and PRE Quantification Across Particle Size Bins**  
**Technology Node:** 180nm CMOS DRAM | **Generation:** Gen 2 (µm) | **Action Type:** Buy (Commercial Laser Surface Scanner / Wafer Defect Inspection System)

---

### Metrology Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│      Wafer Load &      │
│  Pre-Scan Calibration  │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Pre-Clean Baseline   │
│  Laser Darkfield Scan  │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Post-RCA-1 Scan &    │
│     Defect Mapping     │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Differential PRE    │
│  Calculation by Size   │
│          Bin           │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Acceptance Gate &    │
│    Tool Disposition    │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Substrate Handling & Stage Positioning**:
   - Transfer bare or post-process 180nm test wafers to the commercial laser surface particle scanner chuck using an automated end-effector or vacuum wand.
   - Align wafer notch/flat and verify stage motion repeatability and alignment tolerance within **±5 µm** (Gen 2 standard alignment constraint).

2. **Optical System Setup & Surface Calibration**:
   - Set laser source to darkfield scattering detection mode to detect particulate light scattering across the substrate plane.
   - For dielectric verification monitoring (underlying oxide/photoresist thickness), configure 9-point or 49-point automated wafer mapping tracking radial film non-uniformity across the substrate.

3. **Pre-Clean Baseline Inspection (Pre-Scan)**:
   - Perform full-surface laser scan on the wafer prior to RCA-1 immersion.
   - Classify scattered defect counts into standard particle diameter bins:
     - Sub-micron fine particles: $\le 0.5\ \mu\text{m}$
     - Standard defect particles: $0.5\ \mu\text{m} - 1.3\ \mu\text{m}$
     - Gross particulate contaminants: $> 1.3\ \mu\text{m}$
   - Store baseline spatial coordinates $(X_i, Y_i)$ and count $N_{\text{pre}, \text{bin}}$.

4. **Post-RCA-1 Wet Clean Inspection (Post-Scan)**:
   - Following SC-1 bath processing and DI water spin-drying, reload the wafer into the laser scanner under identical coordinate alignment (within **±5 µm**).
   - Execute darkfield laser raster scan and log post-clean defect count $N_{\text{post}, \text{bin}}$ and newly added particles ($N_{\text{added}}$).

5. **Particle Removal Efficiency (PRE) Quantification**:
   - Compute PRE across each discrete particle size bin using:
     $$\text{PRE}_{\text{bin}} (\%) = \frac{N_{\text{pre}, \text{bin}} - N_{\text{post}, \text{bin}}}{N_{\text{pre}, \text{bin}}} \times 100\%$$
   - Verify that residual particle density does not violate the active area budget for 180nm access transistor layouts ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$).

6. **Defect Map Disposition & Archival**:
   - Export 49-point spatial particle density heatmaps to the fab manufacturing execution database.
   - Flag wafers exceeding critical defect thresholds for wet-bench reclean or bath reclamation.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Metric / Target | Exact Physical Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Stage Alignment Tolerance (Gen 2)** | $\le \pm 5$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Laser interferometer & optical edge sensor |
| **Film Thickness Measurement Precision** | $\pm 0.05$ | $\text{nm}$ | Spectroscopic ellipsometry validation |
| **Wafer Mapping Grid Density** | $9\text{ or }49$ | $\text{points / wafer}$ | Automated radial raster mapping |
| **Critical Defect Size Inspection Floor** | $180$ | $\text{nm}$ | Darkfield Rayleigh scatter threshold |

---

### 3. Context Citations

- **[Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology]**:
  - Validates automated 9-point or 49-point wafer mapping for tracking radial non-uniformity across runs.
  - Specifies gate dielectric measurement precision benchmark at $\pm 0.05\text{ nm}$ ($\pm 0.5\text{ \AA}$) and photoresist metrology ($1.3\ \mu\text{m}$ measured within $\pm 2\text{ nm}$).
- **[Sam Zeloof Z1 Garage Semiconductor Journal (2018)]**:
  - Establishes the Gen 2 macroscopic mechanical stage alignment tolerance specification of $\pm 5\ \mu\text{m}$ (improved from Gen 1 $\pm 100\ \mu\text{m}$).
  - Defines particulate and layer scaling baseline referenced against $1.3\ \mu\text{m}$ thin films.
- **[180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench]**:
  - Establishes critical defect sensitivity constraints based on the unit cell layout geometry: access transistor gate channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$ and width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-RCA-1 particle scanning serves as a gating check before high-temperature dry gate oxide growth (3.5 nm target). While Gen 1 operates on millimeter/macroscopic sizing principles, micro-particulate contamination (>0.2 µm and >0.5 µm) acts as localized thermal and diffusion barriers, causing catastrophic gate oxide thinning, pinhole shorts, and early time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB). The dark-field laser scattering metrology recipe must accurately register coordinate-level defect maps across 100mm/150mm wafers without particle re-deposition during stage acceleration.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Particle Removal Efficiency (PRE) quantification across discrete size bins (e.g., 0.18–0.3 µm, 0.3–0.5 µm, and >0.5 µm) requires rigorous calibration against NIST-traceable polystyrene latex (PSL) sphere standards. Laser surface particle scanners (such as KLA Tencor Surfscan or equivalent dark-field optical scatterometers) must decouple localized surface haze from discrete particulate scattering; excessive surface roughness from SC-1 etching (NH4OH:H2O2:H2O) can artificially elevate background Rayleigh scatter and cause false particle counts.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procuring a production-grade automated laser surface particle counter (e.g., Surfscan series) in Gen 1 entails high capital expenditure and extended refurbishment lead times (16–24 weeks). As an Action Type 'Buy', sourcing an entry-level refurbished unpatterned wafer particle counter or contract metrology service requires strict verification of laser diode longevity (488nm Ar-ion or 405nm solid-state laser source), optical sensor calibration, and certified cleanroom compatibility (ISO Class 4/5).
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Metrology throughput must not bottleneck the RCA clean to gate oxidation critical path. The entire scan sequence, multi-bin PRE computation, and wafer map generation must execute within 12 minutes per cassette batch to ensure the wafer queue time to thermal oxidation (max 30 minutes in cleanroom ambient) is strictly maintained without inducing native oxide growth or atmospheric airborne molecular contamination (AMC).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. High background surface haze (>0.8 ppm) induced by silicon micro-roughening in aggressive SC-1 solutions, desensitizing the photomultiplier tube (PMT) detectors and blinding detection of sub-0.3 µm defect bins.
1. Electrostatic particle re-attachment during wafer transit and spin-dry chuck unloading, causing negative calculated PRE values and catastrophic gate dielectric pinholes.
1. Laser diode power degradation or detector drift resulting in systematic particle sizing underestimation and false-positive qualification of contaminated wafers.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-1-3-2-01` | **Full-Wafer Laser Dark-Field Surface Particle Binning and Count Verification** | Laser Surface Particle Scanner / Unpatterned Wafer Defect Inspection System (e.g., KLA-Tencor Surfscan 6200/SP1 or equivalent 405nm/488nm dark-field scatterometer with calibrated PMT detectors) | 1. Load the pre-cleaned wafer onto the vibration-isolated vacuum chuck using clean automated or manual PTFE vacuum wand handling edge-grip. 2. Initiate auto-focus and laser surface scan with a 3mm edge exclusion zone. 3. Collect total dark-field scatter signals and categorize defects into discrete bins: Bin A (0.18 µm to 0.3 µm), Bin B (0.3 µm to 0.5 µm), and Bin C (>0.5 µm). 4. Record total count, spatial defect coordinates (r, theta), and average surface haze across 100% of the active scanning area. 5. Unload wafer to clean antistatic fluoropolymer cassette. | `Total particles >0.2 µm must be <= 15 defects per 100mm wafer (<0.2 defects/cm2); zero killer defects (>1.0 µm); average background surface haze <= 0.35 ppm across the scanned area.` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-1-3-2-02` | **Post-RCA-1 Particle Removal Efficiency (PRE) Quantification via Controlled Challenge Wafers** | Automated Laser Surface Particle Inspection System, ultrasonic/megasonic SC-1 clean bath bench, silicon challenge wafer pre-dosed with calibrated Si3N4/SiO2 slurry particulates. | 1. Scan pre-dosed challenge wafer on laser surface inspection system and export coordinate map and count N_pre. 2. Process the challenge wafer through standard RCA-1 bath (NH4OH:H2O2:H2O = 1:1:5 at 70°C for 10 minutes with megasonic agitation at 1.0 MHz), followed by DI water cascade rinse (resistivity > 18.0 MOhm*cm) and spin-rinse-dry. 3. Transfer wafer immediately to laser inspection station within 5 minutes. 4. Perform post-clean scan using identical recipe, PMT gain, and threshold parameters; export post-clean count N_post. 5. Compute PRE across each bin using PRE (%) = ((N_pre - N_post) / N_pre) * 100. | `PRE for particles >= 0.3 µm must be >= 98.0%; PRE for particles in the 0.18 µm to 0.3 µm range must be >= 95.0%; no post-clean localized cluster defects (>5 particles within a 1mm radius).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (double gloving), ANSI Z87.1 certified laser safety glasses matched to inspection laser wavelength (OD 5+ at 405nm / 488nm), Class 100 cleanroom bunny suit with integrated hood, conductive ESD booties, and particulate face mask
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Laser exposure: Immediately turn off laser power supply; for accidental beam strike to the eye, cover eye with sterile dressing and seek immediate ophthalmological trauma evaluation. IPA exposure: Rinse eyes or skin with flowing DI water for 15 minutes; move victim to fresh air if vapors cause dizziness.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Tool enclosure maintained under positive-pressure HEPA laminar airflow (ISO Class 4 mini-environment); internal mechanical vacuum pump exhaust ducted to external fab solvent/general exhaust header at minimum 50 CFM.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used optical cleaning swabs and IPA wipes double-bagged in hazardous solvent waste receptacles; PSL calibration rinse effluents collected in designated carboys for hazardous chemical waste disposal.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Polystyrene Latex (PSL) Calibration Suspensions** | `9003-53-6` | NIST-Traceable Calibration Standard | `0.1% w/v aqueous suspension` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) Optics Clean** | `67-63-0` | VLSI / Electronic Grade | `>= 99.9%` |
| **Deionized Water** | `7732-18-5` | Semiconductor Grade (Type E-1) | `100% (Resistivity >= 18.2 MOhm-cm)` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic chemically oxidized silicon termination post-RCA-1 clean (thin chemical oxide ~0.8-1.2 nm with high surface energy and contact angle < 10 degrees).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Metrology-qualified clean hydrophilic silicon surface, verified free of discrete particulate contamination (>0.2 µm) and ready for in-situ HF oxide strip / gate oxidation pre-clean.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding queue time causes airborne organic/siloxane molecular contamination adsorption and particulate deposition from ambient air, degrading PRE benefits and nucleating gate oxide pinholes during subsequent 3.5 nm dry gate oxidation.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Quantitative laser surface defect inspection and PRE validation report confirming post-RCA-1 particulate density and multi-bin removal efficiency conform to 180nm dry gate dielectric substrate specifications.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `PRE_Bin_Quantification_Report.csv`
- [ ] `Wafer_Defect_Scatter_Map_PostRCA1.pdf`
- [ ] `Surface_Haze_Spatial_Distribution.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Total post-RCA-1 particle count density for particles >= 0.2 µm across 100mm substrate active area** | `0.15 defects/cm2` | <= 0.20 defects/cm2 | Automated dark-field laser surface defect scanner full-wafer integration (excluding 3mm edge) |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Particle Removal Efficiency (PRE) for challenge wafers in the 0.3 µm to 1.0 µm particle size bin** | `98.5%` | >= 98.0% | Pre- and post-clean challenge wafer particle bin differential computation: PRE = ((N_pre - N_post) / N_pre) * 100 |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Average post-clean surface optical haze across the entire substrate wafer** | `0.25 ppm` | <= 0.35 ppm | Low-angle integrated dark-field Rayleigh scatter measurement calibrated against baseline prime virgin Si |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Laser particle inspection completed on 100% of qualification cassette wafers with PRE >= 98.0% for >= 0.3 µm particles, defect density <= 0.20 defects/cm2, zero killer clusters (>1.0 µm), and signed sign-off certificate archived in fab database within the 30-minute queue time limit.
