nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-MET-AFM-001`
**Title:** AFM Post-SC-1 Surface Microroughness ($R_q$/$R_a$) and Etch Pitting Topography Qualification  
**Process Step Hierarchy:**  
`180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip` $\rightarrow$ `180nm Dry Gate Oxide Growth (3.5 nm)` $\rightarrow$ `Pre-Oxidation RCA Clean & In-Situ HF Dip` $\rightarrow$ `RCA-1 (SC-1) Organic & Particle Removal Bath` $\rightarrow$ `Post-RCA-1 PRE & Surface Roughness Metrology` $\rightarrow$ `AFM Post-SC-1 Surface Microroughness Qualification`  
**Classification:** Gen 1 (mm) Baseline / Metrology Qualification  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Purpose & Scope
This SOP defines the Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) inspection protocol used to verify silicon surface topography, root-mean-square microroughness ($R_q$), arithmetic average roughness ($R_a$), and etch pit formation following the RCA-1 (SC-1) alkaline clean. 

Prior to thermal dry oxidation of a ultra-thin 3.5 nm gate oxide (for 180nm / Gen 1 DRAM pass gates), excessive microroughness or local crystal-originated pit (COP) etching induced by SC-1 ($5:1:1\ \text{H}_2\text{O}:\text{NH}_4\text{OH}:\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ base etching) can cause gate oxide dielectric breakdown, degraded electron channel mobility, and premature breakdown voltage ($V_{BD}$) failure.

```
       +-------------------------------------------------------+
       |   Post-SC-1 Cleaned & Dump-Rinsed Wafer (18.2 MOhm-cm)|
       +---------------------------+---------------------------+
                                   |
                                   v
       +-------------------------------------------------------+
       |  Tapping-Mode AFM Stage Load & Laser Alignment        |
       |  (Drive Freq ~300 kHz, Scan Area: 1 um x 1 um / 5 um)  |
       +---------------------------+---------------------------+
                                   |
                                   v
       +-------------------------------------------------------+
       |  Topography Mapping & 2nd-Order Flattening            |
       |  Extraction of Rq (RMS), Ra, and Peak-to-Valley (Z)   |
       +---------------------------+---------------------------+
                                   |
                                   v
       +-------------------------------------------------------+
       |  Acceptance Criteria Check:                           |
       |  - Rq <= 0.15 nm                                      |
       |  - Max Etch Pit Depth <= 0.50 nm                      |
       |  - Surface Roughness Ra <= 0.12 nm                    |
       +-------------------------------------------------------+
```

---

### 2. Equipment & Tooling Setup
- **Metrology System:** Atomic Force Microscope (AFM) equipped with acoustic isolation hood and active vibration isolation table.
- **Probe Tip:** High-resolution non-contact / tapping-mode silicon cantilever probe (nominal tip radius $\le 10\text{ nm}$, force constant $k \approx 40\text{ N/m}$, resonant frequency $f_0 \approx 300\text{ kHz}$).
- **Environment:** Class 100 / ISO 5 cleanroom airflow bay; temperature: $22.0^\circ\text{C} \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$; relative humidity: $45\% \pm 5\%$.
- **Sample:** Prime p-type Si (100) test coupon/wafer, sampled immediately following the 10-minute SC-1 clean ($70^\circ\text{C}\text{ to }75^\circ\text{C}$, 5-cycle cascade dump rinse to $>16\text{ M}\Omega\text{-cm}$) and $\text{N}_2$ dry.

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

#### Step 1: Pre-Inspection Tool Verification & Tip Integrity
1. Verify AFM vibration isolation stage pressure and acoustic hood lock.
2. Load a fresh silicon tapping-mode probe into the cantilever holder.
3. Align the four-quadrant photodiode detector laser until sum signal is maximized ($> 6.0\text{ V}$) and vertical/horizontal deflection voltages are balanced to $0.00\text{ V} \pm 0.05\text{ V}$.
4. Run tune sweep to locate probe resonance; lock the operating drive frequency at $-5\%$ below peak resonance ($\sim 290\text{--}300\text{ kHz}$) with a free-air oscillation amplitude setpoint of $2.0\text{ V}$.

#### Step 2: Sample Loading & Coordinate Alignment
1. Transfer post-SC-1 dried Si coupon to the AFM sample vacuum chuck.
2. Engage vacuum hold-down ($> 70\text{ kPa}$).
3. Position the optical objective over the wafer active device region:
   - Sample at least 5 standard site locations (Center, North, South, East, West with edge exclusion $\ge 5\text{ mm}$).
   - Set scan window resolution grid:
     - **Survey Scan:** $5.0\ \mu\text{m} \times 5.0\ \mu\text{m}$ (512 lines $\times$ 512 samples) to inspect for localized etch pits and pinholes.
     - **Fine Roughness Scan:** $1.0\ \mu\text{m} \times 1.0\ \mu\text{m}$ (512 lines $\times$ 512 samples) for precise $R_q$ and $R_a$ calculation.

#### Step 3: Topographic Scanning Protocol
1. Initiate automated approach until amplitude setpoint damping reaches $75\%\text{--}80\%$ of free air amplitude.
2. Configure scan parameters:
   - **Scan Rate:** $0.50\text{ Hz}$ to $0.75\text{ Hz}$ (trace/retrace).
   - **Integral Gain:** Optimized until trace and retrace profile curves overlay without ringing.
   - **Proportional Gain:** Set to $1.5\times$ Integral Gain.
3. Acquire raw height retrace channels for both the $5.0\ \mu\text{m}$ survey and $1.0\ \mu\text{m}$ fine scans at each location.

#### Step 4: Flattening & Metrology Extraction
1. Apply a standard 2nd-order polynomial plane fit (`Flattening - Order 2`) across the raw height image to eliminate thermal drift and sample tilt artifacts.
2. Extract the surface microroughness statistics across the $1.0\ \mu\text{m} \times 1.0\ \mu\text{m}$ field:
   $$R_q = \sqrt{\frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N (Z_i - \bar{Z})^2}, \quad R_a = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N |Z_i - \bar{Z}|$$
3. Perform a depth threshold analysis on the $5.0\ \mu\text{m} \times 5.0\ \mu\text{m}$ survey image to calculate:
   - Maximum Peak-to-Valley height ($Z_{max} - Z_{min}$).
   - Pit depth count for depressions exceeding baseline roughness.

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter ID | Parameter Name | Metric Specification | Unit | Verification Tool |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **AC-AFM-01** | Post-SC-1 RMS Microroughness ($R_q$) | **$\le 0.15$** ($1.0\ \mu\text{m} \times 1.0\ \mu\text{m}$ scan) | $\text{nm}$ | Automated AFM Software Metric |
| **AC-AFM-02** | Arithmetic Average Roughness ($R_a$) | **$\le 0.12$** ($1.0\ \mu\text{m} \times 1.0\ \mu\text{m}$ scan) | $\text{nm}$ | Automated AFM Software Metric |
| **AC-AFM-03** | Max Etch Pit Depth / Peak-to-Valley Delta | **$\le 0.50$** (relative to nominal background Si etch) | $\text{nm}$ | AFM Section Profile Analysis |
| **AC-AFM-04** | Cascade Rinse Deionized Water Resistivity | **$> 16.0$** (prior to wafer unload) | $\text{M}\Omega\text{-cm}$ | In-line Resistivity Sensor |

*Disposition Rule:* If $R_q > 0.15\text{ nm}$ or etch pit depth $> 0.50\text{ nm}$, the SC-1 bath ammonium hydroxide ($\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$) ratio or bath temperature ($70^\circ\text{C}\text{--}75^\circ\text{C}$) exceeds acceptable micro-etch limits; quarantine the lot, dump SC-1 chemistry, and reformulate.

---

### 5. Context Citations
1. **RCA Standard Clean SC-1, SC-2, and Native Oxide HF Dip Engineering:**
   - Chemistry formulation ($5\ \text{UPW} : 1\ \text{NH}_4\text{OH} : 1\ \text{H}_2\text{O}_2$), bath temperature ($70^\circ\text{C}\text{ to }75^\circ\text{C}$, 10 min immersion), micro-etching baseline ($\sim 0.5\text{ nm}$ silicon base etch), and cascade dump rinse resistivity target ($18.2\text{ M}\Omega\text{-cm}$ DI water, rinse endpoint $> 16\text{ M}\Omega\text{-cm}$).
2. **Architecture & Integration Context (180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip):**
   - 3.5 nm dry gate oxide thickness constraints dictating sub-angstrom/angstrom-level surface roughness thresholds ($R_q \le 0.15\text{ nm}$).
3. **SkyWater SKY130 Open PDK Design Rules & Lithography Grid:**
   - 180nm critical dimension and baseline physical grid resolution ($5\text{ nm}$) constraints.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) inspection operates as an off-line, high-resolution metrological gate prior to dry gate oxidation. Integrating tapping-mode AFM into the 180nm process flow requires stringent tracking of queue times between SC-1 wet cleaning, AFM scanning, and final pre-gate oxide HF dip. Because AFM exposes wafers to ambient cleanroom air during tip approach and rastering, native oxide regrows and airborne molecular contamination (AMC) accumulates, which can skew subsequent Deal-Grove oxidation kinetics if Q-time to furnace insertion is violated.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Standard SC-1 (NH4OH:H2O2:H2O at 1:1:5 or modified dilute 1:1:10 at 70°C) simultaneously strips particles via zeta potential repulsion while oxidizing and mildly etching silicon. If the ammonium hydroxide concentration is too high or bath temperature exceeds 75°C with depleted H2O2, anisotropic micro-etching along Si(100) and Si(111) planes initiates, forming pyramidal etch pits. AFM topographical qualification must verify that root-mean-square roughness (Rq) remains below 0.20 nm (2.0 Å) over a 2 µm x 2 µm scan area to prevent premature dielectric breakdown (TDDB) and channel mobility degradation in 3.5 nm gate oxides.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: AFM silicon cantilever tips with tip radius <10 nm and high resonance frequency (~300 kHz) are consumable bottlenecks in Vietnam. AFM tip wear or apex chipping induces scan convolution artifacts, artificially suppressing or broadening measured pit depths. Silicon calibration grating standards (e.g., 100 nm pitch, 20 nm depth) and cantilever inventory must be qualified with certified vendors to prevent metrology stalls during baseline ramp.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: AFM is inherently throughput-limited, taking 15 to 30 minutes per wafer site. Running 9-point or 49-point wafer mapping on every production lot will cause severe wet bench and furnace queue backups, leading to Q-time expiration. Layer PM requires AFM qualification to execute as a statistical process control (SPC) 5-point monitor coupon routine (center, top, bottom, left, right) per wet bath turnover rather than 100% in-line production screening.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. NH4OH/H2O2 stoichiometric ratio collapse in the SC-1 bath causing aggressive anisotropic Si etching and surface pit formation deeper than 1.0 nm.
1. AFM tip apex blunting or contamination leading to tip convolution artifacts, under-reporting Rq/Ra and masking critical gate-channel micro-roughness.
1. Cleanroom ambient AMC adsorption during AFM scanning, causing organic hydrocarbon redeposition that degrades 3.5 nm gate oxide breakdown voltage.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-1-3-3-01` | **Post-SC-1 Surface Microroughness (Rq and Ra) Tapping-Mode AFM Scan** | Atomic Force Microscope (Tapping/Non-Contact Mode, resonance frequency ~300 kHz, tip radius < 10 nm, acoustic enclosure and vibration isolation table) | 1. Align laser beam onto AFM cantilever back and tune resonance frequency to identify primary peak (~300 kHz) with free vibration amplitude set to 2.0 V. 2. Approach tip to substrate surface in tapping mode with 80% amplitude setpoint. 3. Perform 512 x 512 pixel raster scan over a 2.0 um x 2.0 um area at a scan rate of 0.8 Hz at wafer center. 4. Repeat scan at 4 peripheral points (10 mm from wafer edge: 12, 3, 6, 9 o'clock). 5. Apply 1st-order plane fit and 2nd-order flattening algorithm to eliminate tilt and sample bow. 6. Compute arithmetic average roughness (Ra) and root-mean-square roughness (Rq). | `Rq must be <= 0.20 nm (2.0 A) and Ra must be <= 0.15 nm (1.5 A) across all 5 measured points. No single scan site shall exceed Rq = 0.25 nm.` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-1-3-3-02` | **Post-SC-1 Anisotropic Etch Pit Density and Peak-to-Valley (Rmax) Depth Analysis** | Atomic Force Microscope with offline PSD (Power Spectral Density) and bearing/pit analysis topographical software | 1. Open 2.0 um x 2.0 um height sensor channel AFM files from 5 sample locations. 2. Set depth threshold marker at -0.5 nm below the mean plane. 3. Count etch pits deeper than 0.5 nm and calculate pit areal density per um^2. 4. Measure maximum peak-to-valley height (Rmax / Rz) within each 2.0 um x 2.0 um field. 5. Perform cross-sectional line profile across the largest detected pit to confirm sidewall slope and geometry. | `Zero etch pits with depth >= 1.0 nm allowed across all scanned fields. Pit density with depth between 0.5 nm and 1.0 nm must be <= 2 pits/um^2. Peak-to-valley roughness Rmax must be <= 1.80 nm.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom-compatible nitrile gloves (double gloving), ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical/splash safety glasses, Cleanroom lint-free antistatic bunny suit and hood, Static-dissipative ESD cleanroom footwear
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: AFM metrology itself involves dried wafers, but if chemical trace contact occurs: Skin: Flush immediately with copious deionized water for at least 15 minutes. Eyes: Irrigate eye wash station for 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmological attention. Inhalation: Move to fresh air; administer oxygen if breathing is labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: AFM instrument must be located in an ISO 5 (Class 100) cleanroom environment with laminar downflow HEPA/ULPA filtration (velocity 0.45 m/s +/- 20%) and dedicated acoustic chamber; local chemical wet bench handling utilizes dedicated exhaust duct velocity >= 100 FPM.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent AFM tips and lint-free wipes contaminated with trace solvents disposed of in labeled solid hazardous waste bins. Chemical bath rinsates from pre-AFM prep routed to industrial acid-base neutralization system (titrated to pH 6.5-8.5 before POTW discharge).

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Ammonium Hydroxide (SC-1 bath residue trace)** | `1336-21-6` | SEMI Tier 3 / Electronic Grade | `28-30% in stock solution; diluted to ~1-4% in bath` |
| **Hydrogen Peroxide (SC-1 bath residue trace)** | `7722-84-1` | SEMI Tier 3 / Electronic Grade | `30% in stock solution; diluted to ~1-4% in bath` |
| **Isopropanol (AFM stage and tip holder maintenance)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI Grade | `> 99.8%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `6 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic chemical oxide (~0.8 to 1.2 nm thick) formed in SC-1 bath, terminated with Si-OH hydroxyl groups, thoroughly DI rinsed to 18.2 MOhm-cm and spin-dried.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Qualified low-roughness hydrophilic chemical oxide surface ready for pre-gate HF dip or immediate transfer to dry oxidation pre-clean queue.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air Q-time causes uncontrolled organic airborne molecular contamination (AMC) adsorption and humidity-driven surface restructuring, invalidating AFM roughness baseline and leading to severe interface trap density (Dit) and early dielectric breakdown in 3.5 nm dry gate oxide.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Verifiable surface topography and micro-roughness qualification of post-SC-1 silicon surfaces, ensuring Rq <= 0.20 nm and absence of micro-etch pits prior to gate dielectric thermal oxidation.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `AFM_SC1_Topography_5pt_Map.tiff`
- [ ] `Roughness_Rq_Ra_Pits_Distribution.csv`
- [ ] `AFM_Surface_Qualification_Report.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Root-Mean-Square Surface Roughness (Rq) within 2.0 um x 2.0 um scan window** | `0.16 nm` | <= 0.20 nm max | Tapping-mode AFM 512x512 topography scan flattened with 2nd-order polynomial subtraction across 5 sample sites. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Maximum Etch Pit Depth across active silicon scan field** | `0.00 nm` | < 1.00 nm max | Bearing depth analysis and sectional line profiling on AFM height sensor channel data. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Peak-to-Valley Roughness (Rmax / Rz)** | `1.20 nm` | <= 1.80 nm max | Automated statistical surface calculation on 5-point AFM 2.0 um x 2.0 um scan areas. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 5 AFM wafer points demonstrate Rq <= 0.20 nm, zero pits deeper than 1.0 nm, Rmax <= 1.80 nm, verified tip apex resolution < 10 nm via pre/post reference grating check, and final signed qualification report archived.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-MET-AFM-021`
**Title:** AFM Instrument Cantilever Calibration and Reference Substrate Baseline Setup  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm)  
**Process Step:** Context: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > 180nm Dry Gate Oxide Growth (3.5 nm) > Pre-Oxidation RCA Clean and In-Situ HF Dip Surface Preparation > RCA-1 (SC-1) Organic & Particle Removal Bath Formulation and Bench Qualification > Post-RCA-1 Particle Removal Efficiency (PRE) and Surface Roughness Metrology Qualification > AFM Post-SC-1 Surface Microroughness ($R_q/R_a$) and Etch Pitting Topography Qualification > **AFM Instrument Cantilever Calibration and Reference Substrate Baseline Setup**  
**Action Type:** Make

---

### 1. Calibration Workflow

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│    Mount Reference    │
│     Sample & Tip      │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Laser Alignment &   │
│  Photodiode Zeroing   │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Cantilever Thermal   │
│   Tune & Deflection   │
│      Sensitivity      │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Reference Standard   │
│    Scan & Baseline    │
│        Zeroing        │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Acceptance Criteria  │
│     Verification      │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Vibration Isolation & Environment Setup**:
   - Verify acoustic enclosure seal and active pneumatic isolation table pressure. Ensure the acoustic and mechanical vibration damping is stabilized.
2. **Cantilever Loading & Laser Alignment**:
   - Securely load an AFM cantilever probe (tapping/non-contact mode silicon tip) into the cantilever holder assembly.
   - Adjust the optical tracking laser optics to center the beam spot onto the reflective backside of the cantilever apex.
   - Center the reflected beam onto the 4-quadrant position-sensitive photodetector (PSPD) to zero the vertical ($A-B$) and horizontal ($C-D$) differential photodiode signals ($\text{Differential Voltage} \approx 0.00\text{ V}$).
3. **Thermal Tune & Optical Deflection Sensitivity ($InvOLS$)**:
   - Disengage probe $> 1\text{ mm}$ above the substrate; execute a cantilever thermal power spectrum capture in ambient air to determine fundamental resonance frequency ($f_0$) and quality factor ($Q$).
   - Perform a ramp cycle on a rigid sapphire/silicon calibration reference substrate to establish optical deflection sensitivity ($\text{nm/V}$).
4. **Spring Constant ($k$) Calibration & Baseline Noise Floor Verification**:
   - Calculate effective spring constant via thermal noise power integration (Sader/Equipartition method).
   - Park tip at scanning setpoint height above a reference standard; capture a zero-scan amplitude profile for 60 seconds to quantify baseline $Z$-sensor RMS noise floor.
5. **Reference Baseline Lateral & Vertical Calibration**:
   - Engage on the Gen 2 reference standard step grid. Calibrate lateral scanner piezo non-linearity and verify stage positioning accuracy across orthogonal axes within the Gen 2 calibration envelope.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
       AFM Baseline Metrology Acceptance Thresholds
 ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■ 5.0        │ Stage Alignment Tolerance (± µm)
 │░░░ 0.35                                                │ Optical Z-Noise Floor / Gate Oxide Budget (nm)
 │▒ 0.05                                                  │ Metrology Precision Resolution (± nm)
 └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  0                       2                      4        
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value & Tolerance | Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Gen 2 Stage Positioning / Alignment Tolerance** | $\le \pm 5.0$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Lateral reference grid step-pitch displacement measurement (per Gen 2 mechanical alignment limits) |
| **Optical Metrology Precision Resolution** | $\le \pm 0.05$ | $\text{nm}$ | Sub-Angstrom calibrated $Z$-sensor height repeatability on step standard |
| **Z-Sensor Background Noise Floor (RMS)** | $\le 0.35$ (within $10\%$ budget of $3.5\text{ nm}$ oxide) | $\text{nm}$ | Static zero-scan baseline RMS displacement ($R_q$) measurement |
| **Dry Gate Oxide Target Layer Reference Baseline** | $3.5$ | $\text{nm}$ | Vertical step standard baseline offset corresponding to the gate oxide target thickness |

---

### 4. Verified Context Citations

- **Source: Sam Zeloof Z1 Garage Semiconductor Journal (2018)**:
  - *Context Rule / Metric*: Macroscopic stage alignment tolerance requirements evolve from Gen 1 ($\pm 100\ \mu\text{m}$) down to **$\pm 5\ \mu\text{m}$ in Gen 2**, defining the calibration boundaries for stage travel and alignment.
- **Source: Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology**:
  - *Context Rule / Metric*: Metrology resolution baseline requirements establish sub-Angstrom precision (**$\pm 0.05\text{ nm}$**) when monitoring the **$3.5\text{ nm}$ dry gate oxide** target layer.
- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - *Context Rule / Metric*: Access transistor channel length ($L = 180\text{ nm}$) and unit cell layout constraints set the nanoscale planar sensitivity criteria for critical dielectric interface preparation and gate oxide growth.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: AFM cantilever calibration must rigorously separate intrinsic probe mechanical compliance from acoustic/floor mechanical vibration and thermal drift. Calibrating optical lever sensitivity (Deflection Sensitivity / InvOLS in nm/V) on an uncharacterized, compliant, or contaminated substrate will skew spring constant calculations via Sader or thermal noise methods, yielding invalid force curves and artificial topographical artifacts during subsequent post-SC-1 roughness metrology. Structural isolation using Sorbothane and floating optical breadboards is essential to suppress floor resonances below 30 Hz.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For sub-0.2 nm roughness metrology of post-SC-1 Si(100) surfaces, precise spring constant (k ~ 20-40 N/m for tapping/non-contact mode) and tip apex radius (< 10 nm) baseline qualification are non-negotiable. Using contact mode with high normal force risks scratching bare silicon or inducing tip blunting, which artificially suppresses high-spatial-frequency Rq microroughness data. InvOLS calibration must be performed on an atomically flat sapphire or pristine thermally grown SiO2 calibration standard rather than bare silicon to avoid native oxide indentations.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procurement must secure certified AFM calibration standards (e.g., 100 nm step-height pitch gratings and atomically flat cleaved HOPG or c-axis sapphire) alongside monolithic silicon tapping probes (e.g., BudgetSensors Tap300Al-G or Bruker RTESP-300) with traceable batch inspection sheets. Lead times for NIST-traceable calibration gratings can extend to 6-8 weeks; secondary supplier cross-qualification for equivalent cantilever models is required to prevent fab stoppage.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: AFM baseline qualification is the critical gating milestone prior to clearing the RCA-1 clean station for gate oxide pilot wafer runs. Any delay in verifying instrument noise floor (< 0.05 nm RMS) directly blocks Deal-Grove dry gate oxidation qualification (3.5 nm EOT). The calibration SOP must be standardized to permit rapid cantilever exchange and thermal equilibration within a 45-minute setup envelope.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Tip apex contamination or fracture during hard landing on calibration substrate, resulting in tip-convolution artifacts and false double-tip step height measurements.
1. Inaccurate InvOLS calculation due to thermal drift or uncalibrated photodiode alignment, causing systematic error in cantilever spring constant determination and non-reproducible Rq microroughness extraction.
1. Acoustic and vibrational coupling exceeding the 0.05 nm Z-sensor noise floor, masking genuine etch pitting and sub-angstrom surface roughness post-SC-1.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100/ISO 5 compatible nitrile gloves (powder-free, dual-layer), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/laser safety goggles compatible with AFM laser diode wavelength (650-670 nm, OD >= 3), Lint-free antistatic cleanroom coat and ESD wrist strap
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye exposure to IPA: Flush immediately with emergency cleanroom eye wash station for at least 15 minutes while holding eyelids open. Skin contact: Wash affected area with DI water and mild detergent. Accidental direct beam laser exposure to eye: Immediately report to cleanroom medical officer for ophthalmologic evaluation. Inhalation of solvent vapors: Move personnel to fresh air.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: AFM acoustic enclosure must operate with low-flow passive purge or HEPA downflow exhaust with airflow velocity < 0.15 m/s to prevent micro-vibrations. Substrate solvent degreasing and probe cleaning must take place under a certified chemical bench with laminar exhaust face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA solvent wipes and rinse vials must be collected in dedicated grounded hazardous solvent waste containers for off-site thermal oxidation; no organic solvent disposal down municipal or acid drain lines.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade (VLSI / MOS) | `>= 99.9%` |
| **Deionized Water (DIW)** | `7732-18-5` | Ultra-Pure Water (ASTM Type 1, 18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100%` |

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly cleaved or solvent-degreased (IPA/DIW ultrasonic clean, N2 blown dry) reference substrates, sealed in hermetic antistatic fluoropolymer wafer shippers.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Fully qualified AFM tool baseline with verified InvOLS, k calibration record, < 0.05 nm RMS instrument noise floor, and pristine calibrated probe tip mounted in dry N2 purged enclosure.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Airborne hydrocarbon condensation and organic airborne molecular contamination (AMC) deposition on reference substrates and probe tip, causing tip adhesion hysteresis, erroneous damping phase shifts, and invalid baseline Rq elevation > 0.1 nm.

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful baseline qualification and calibration of the AFM cantilever and instrument noise floor, establishing traceable deflection sensitivity, thermal spring constant, and Z-height measurement accuracy required for sub-0.2 nm post-SC-1 silicon gate area microroughness metrology.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `AFM_Cantilever_Calibration_Report_Tap300_SOP.pdf`
- [ ] `NIST_100nm_StepHeight_Baseline_Verification_Scan.tiff`
- [ ] `Instrument_NoiseFloor_and_InvOLS_Data_Log.csv`

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |

| `ASSERT-01` | **Calibrated AFM system engaged Z-sensor background noise floor on flat reference** | `0.04 nm RMS` | <= 0.05 nm RMS | 1.0 um x 1.0 um tapping mode scan on atomically flat sapphire reference with 512x512 resolution at 1 Hz |
| `ASSERT-02` | **NIST-traceable 100 nm step-height standard mean height measurement** | `100.0 nm` | ± 1.0 nm | Averaged cross-sectional step analysis across 10 pitch periods on flattened AFM topography scan |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Optical lever deflection sensitivity (InvOLS) measurement repeatability** | `55.0 nm/V` | Standard deviation <= 1.5% across 5 ramps | Force-distance curve ramp slope calculation on rigid sapphire substrate |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> The AFM instrument achieves an active noise floor of Rq <= 0.05 nm, NIST step-height error <= 1.0%, cantilever calibration repeatability within 1.5%, and formal generation of all signed calibration logs enabling downstream post-SC-1 microroughness metrology.

critics.systems_engineer: AFM cantilever calibration must rigorously separate intrinsic probe mechanical compliance from acoustic/floor mechanical vibration and thermal drift. Calibrating optical lever sensitivity (Deflection Sensitivity / InvOLS in nm/V) on an uncharacterized, compliant, or contaminated substrate will skew spring constant calculations via Sader or thermal noise methods, yielding invalid force curves and artificial topographical artifacts during subsequent post-SC-1 roughness metrology. Structural isolation using Sorbothane and floating optical breadboards is essential to suppress floor resonances below 30 Hz.
critics.domain_expert: For sub-0.2 nm roughness metrology of post-SC-1 Si(100) surfaces, precise spring constant (k ~ 20-40 N/m for tapping/non-contact mode) and tip apex radius (< 10 nm) baseline qualification are non-negotiable. Using contact mode with high normal force risks scratching bare silicon or inducing tip blunting, which artificially suppresses high-spatial-frequency Rq microroughness data. InvOLS calibration must be performed on an atomically flat sapphire or pristine thermally grown SiO2 calibration standard rather than bare silicon to avoid native oxide indentations.
critics.supply_chain: Procurement must secure certified AFM calibration standards (e.g., 100 nm step-height pitch gratings and atomically flat cleaved HOPG or c-axis sapphire) alongside monolithic silicon tapping probes (e.g., BudgetSensors Tap300Al-G or Bruker RTESP-300) with traceable batch inspection sheets. Lead times for NIST-traceable calibration gratings can extend to 6-8 weeks; secondary supplier cross-qualification for equivalent cantilever models is required to prevent fab stoppage.
critics.laya_pm: AFM baseline qualification is the critical gating milestone prior to clearing the RCA-1 clean station for gate oxide pilot wafer runs. Any delay in verifying instrument noise floor (< 0.05 nm RMS) directly blocks Deal-Grove dry gate oxidation qualification (3.5 nm EOT). The calibration SOP must be standardized to permit rapid cantilever exchange and thermal equilibration within a 45-minute setup envelope.
critical_failure_modes: Tip apex contamination or fracture during hard landing on calibration substrate, resulting in tip-convolution artifacts and false double-tip step height measurements.

Inaccurate InvOLS calculation due to thermal drift or uncalibrated photodiode alignment, causing systematic error in cantilever spring constant determination and non-reproducible Rq microroughness extraction.
Acoustic and vibrational coupling exceeding the 0.05 nm Z-sensor noise floor, masking genuine etch pitting and sub-angstrom surface roughness post-SC-1.

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document Title: Post-SC-1 Silicon Wafer AFM Topographical Scanning and Microroughness ($R_q$/$R_a$) Mapping

- **Module**: Metrology / Pre-Oxidation Surface Qualification
- **Process Step Node**: 180nm Dry Gate Oxide Growth (~3.5 nm physical target)
- **Action Type**: Buy (Automated AFM Metrology Tool Benchmarking & Wafer Acceptance)
- **Target Cell Architecture**: 180nm 1T1C DRAM Cell ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$, $8F^2 / 6F^2$ Folded Bitline Topology)

---

### Process Flow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Wafer Load & Chuck   │
│         Vacuum         │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│     Tip Approach &     │
│    Resonance Tuning    │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Multi-Point AFM     │
│        Scanning        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│      Topography &      │
│  Roughness Extraction  │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Acceptance Decision:  │
│       Ra/Rq Spec       │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Substrate Handling & Vacuum Chucking**:
   - Transfer the post-SC-1 (RCA-1) and post-rinse/dry silicon wafer via automated cleanroom end-effector into the Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) enclosure (Class 1 / ISO Class 3 environment).
   - Seat the wafer onto the vacuum chuck and verify vacuum seal ($\ge 80\text{ kPa}$ differential pressure). Ensure environmental isolation active (anti-vibration table floated, acoustic enclosure sealed).

2. **Probe Inspection & Resonance Tuning (Tapping / Non-Contact Mode)**:
   - Mount a high-aspect-ratio, ultra-sharp single-crystal silicon cantilever (tip nominal radius $\le 7\text{ nm}$, resonant frequency $f_0 \approx 300\text{ kHz}$).
   - Perform automated laser alignment to quadrant photodiode to maximize sum signal.
   - Sweep acoustic excitation frequency around $f_0$ to tune drive amplitude and lock operating tapping amplitude at 80% free amplitude ($A/A_0 = 0.80$).

3. **Coordinate Navigation & Recipe Execution**:
   - Align wafer notch/flat and register coordinate system.
   - Program automated multi-site scanning across the standard wafer layout matching dielectric thickness validation sites (e.g., 9-point or 49-point grid layout spanning center, mid-radius, and edge exclusion zone).
   - Set scan dimensions to $1.0\ \mu\text{m} \times 1.0\ \mu\text{m}$ (with optional $5.0\ \mu\text{m} \times 5.0\ \mu\text{m}$ wide-field scans to detect microroughness and etch pitting clusters) at a scan rate of $0.5\text{ Hz}$ to $1.0\text{ Hz}$ with $512 \times 512$ pixel resolution.

4. **Surface Topography Acquisition & Profile Flattening**:
   - Engage tip with soft-landing algorithm; verify stable phase contrast and feedback lock (integral and proportional gains optimized).
   - Capture height trace/retrace, amplitude, and phase channels.
   - Apply real-time 1st-order/2nd-order plane fit and line-by-line flattening to remove tilt, bowing, and scanner bow artifacts without clipping nanoscale features.

5. **Microroughness Extraction & Defect/Pit Tagging**:
   - Extract arithmetic average roughness ($R_a$), root-mean-square roughness ($R_q$), and maximum peak-to-valley height ($R_{\max}$).
   - Evaluate height distribution histograms for asymmetric negative tailing indicating post-SC-1 chemical etch pits or alkaline-induced micro-voiding.
   - Export 9-point/49-point wafer topographical map to the fab yield and SPC system.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Physical Unit | Measurement Method / Verification Tool |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Silicon Microroughness ($R_q$ / RMS)** | $\le 0.15$ | $\text{nm}$ (RMS) | AFM scan ($1\ \mu\text{m} \times 1\ \mu\text{m}$, 9-point / 49-point wafer map) |
| **Arithmetic Mean Roughness ($R_a$)** | $\le 0.12$ | $\text{nm}$ | AFM trace ($512 \times 512$ points, post-flattening) |
| **Max Peak-to-Valley Height ($R_{\max}$ / Etch Pit Depth)** | $< 1.0$ | $\text{nm}$ | AFM bearing analysis & height histogram thresholding |
| **Surface Scanned Gate Area Feature Scale** | Matches $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$ | $\text{nm}$ | Metrology scan window resolution ($512 \times 512$ grid) |
| **Oxide Pre-Clean Uniformity Baseline** | Surface compatible with $3.5\text{ nm}$ ($\pm 0.05\text{ nm}$) dry gate oxide | $\text{nm}$ | Correlated via downstream Spectroscopic Ellipsometry |

---

### 3. Literature Citations & Context References

- **Gate Dielectric Physical Thickness**: Target gate dielectric is thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ at $850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$ dry oxidation with $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ physical thickness, requiring sub-Angstrom precision surface smoothness before furnace insertion (*Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering*).
- **Sub-Angstrom Metrology Precision Reference**: Dry gate oxide ($3.5\text{ nm}$) requires ellipsometric monitoring with sub-Angstrom precision ($\pm 0.05\text{ nm}$), dictating that pre-oxidation SC-1 cleaning does not roughen the silicon substrate or create atomic steps that induce localized oxide thinning (*Source: Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology*).
- **Wafer Mapping Grid Standard**: Automated 9-point or 49-point wafer mapping tracks radial non-uniformity across process benches and furnaces (*Source: Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology*).
- **Access Transistor Channel Geometry**: Access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$ and width $W = 220\text{ nm}$ with bitline and wordline pitch of approximately $360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$, requiring AFM scan fields ($1\ \mu\text{m} \times 1\ \mu\text{m}$) capable of resolving sub-channel pitch surface morphology (*Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench; Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering*).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: SC-1 chemistry (NH4OH:H2O2:H2O) inherently oxidizes and etches silicon simultaneously. In high pH baths or when the NH4OH:H2O2 ratio exceeds 1:1:5, preferential anisotropic etching along crystal defect planes causes micro-roughening and pitting. If post-SC-1 root-mean-square roughness (Rq) exceeds 0.20 nm before gate oxidation, the 3.5 nm dry thermal gate oxide will experience severe localized electric field crowding, channel carrier mobility degradation, and premature time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB) in DRAM access transistors. AFM mapping must tightly feed back to the wet bench dosing loop before wafers proceed to SC-2 and thermal oxidation.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Tapping mode (amplitude modulation AFM) using ultra-sharp silicon tips (tip radius nominal < 7 nm, resonant frequency ~300 kHz, force constant ~40 N/m) is mandatory to prevent plastic deformation or scraping of the fresh ~0.8-1.2 nm chemical oxide. High-aspect ratio scanning over 1 um x 1 um and 5 um x 5 um windows must decouple high-frequency microroughness (Rq/Ra) from low-frequency waviness. The critical parameter to monitor is etch pit density and peak-to-valley roughness (Rmax/Rz); deep pits (>1.5 nm) on a 3.5 nm oxide target directly erode 40% of the dielectric physical thickness.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: AFM cantilever tips wear rapidly when imaging silicon in ambient conditions due to tip bluntness from capillary forces and tip-sample adhesion. For open-source 180nm pilot line operations, cantilever tip consumption must be budgeted (typically 1 tip per 3-5 full wafer maps). Sourcing semiconductor-grade n-doped silicon probes (e.g., NCHV-A or equivalent with tip radius <= 8 nm) must have secondary qualified vendors to prevent metrology stoppage, and standard roughness calibration gratings (SiO2 steps on Si, 100 nm pitch / 20 nm step) must be recertified quarterly.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: AFM is fundamentally a low-throughput metrology technique (each 512x512 line map takes 8-15 minutes per site). A full 9-point or 49-point wafer map risks violating the critical cleanroom Q-time prior to the gate oxidation furnace load. To maintain throughput while safeguarding yield, implement a 5-point sampling scheme (Center, Top, Bottom, Left, Right at 10 mm edge exclusion) on 1 pilot wafer per lot, gating the wet clean run within a 45-minute Q-time window before final SC-2/HF clean.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Tip convolution and bluntness artifact: Worn or chipped AFM tips (radius > 15 nm) artificially smooth measured surface profiles, under-reporting Rq by up to 60% and concealing micro-pits.
1. Capillary condensation and ambient moisture artifact: Humidity > 45% RH creates a water meniscus between tip and chemical oxide, inducing phase shift anomalies, force snap-in instability, and false topographical spikes.
1. SC-1 bath ratio drift inducing silicon pitting: Depletion of H2O2 in the SC-1 bath causing NH4OH-dominated alkaline anisotropic etching, generating high-density square pyramidal etch pits > 2 nm deep.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-1-3-3-2-01` | **Post-SC-1 Surface Microroughness (Rq and Ra) 5-Point Wafer Topography Mapping** | Atomic Force Microscope (AFM) in Tapping/Non-Contact Mode, calibrated with certified silicon grating; High-resolution n-type Si probe (tip radius <= 8 nm, spring constant 40 N/m, resonant frequency 300-330 kHz); Class 100 cleanroom acoustic and vibration isolation enclosure. | 1. Load wafer onto electrostatic/vacuum chuck and align wafer notch to 6 o'clock. 2. Establish tip resonance curve; select drive frequency 5% below resonant peak with free vibration amplitude A0 = 1.5 V and setpoint ratio Asp/A0 = 0.80. 3. Engage tip at Center (Site 1: 0,0) and acquire 1.0 um x 1.0 um scan at 512 x 512 pixels, scan rate 0.8 Hz. 4. Apply 1st-order polynomial line flatten and 2nd-order plane fit to remove wafer tilt. 5. Calculate Ra and Rq. 6. Repeat steps 3-5 at 4 perimeter sites (Top: 0,+40mm; Bottom: 0,-40mm; Left: -40mm,0; Right: +40mm,0). 7. Verify tip integrity against reference grating post-scan. | `Pass if 5-point mean Rq <= 0.18 nm (1.8 Angstroms), maximum single-site Rq <= 0.22 nm, and no spatial gradient (edge-to-center delta <= 0.05 nm). Fail if any single-site Rq > 0.22 nm or Ra > 0.18 nm.` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-1-3-3-2-02` | **SC-1 Etch Pitting and Peak-to-Valley (Rmax) Defect Topography Scan** | AFM tapping mode with tip check software (blind tip reconstruction algorithm); Acoustic isolation hood with active piezo vibration damping table. | 1. Move stage to Wafer Center (Site 1) and expand scan area to 5.0 um x 5.0 um at 1024 x 1024 pixels, scan rate 0.5 Hz. 2. Acquire height, amplitude, and phase channels simultaneously. 3. Execute 2nd-order polynomial background flattening. 4. Run depth histogram analysis and bearing area curve to identify negative excursions (pits). 5. Measure maximum peak-to-valley height (Rmax) and quantify pit count with depth > 1.0 nm. 6. Repeat scan at worst-case edge site identified in TC-01. | `Pass if peak-to-valley Rmax <= 1.20 nm across 5 um x 5 um area, zero etch pits observed with depth >= 1.0 nm below mean surface plane, and pit density < 1 pit / 25 um^2. Fail if any pit depth >= 1.0 nm or Rmax > 1.20 nm.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (double gloving), Anti-static ESD cleanroom lab coat and hood, ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, ESD wrist strap or grounding footwear connected to grounded AFM chassis
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Inhalation of N2 purge gas in confined enclosure: Remove victim to fresh air immediately; administer artificial respiration or oxygen if breathing is labored. Skin/eye contact with IPA chuck cleaner: Flush affected eyes or skin with running DI water for at least 15 minutes. In case of mechanical pinch or electrical shock from AFM piezoelectric actuator stages: Disconnect main power breaker and seek qualified medical attention.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: AFM acoustic enclosure vented to cleanroom general recirculating exhaust at 50 SCFM to prevent local nitrogen gas accumulation; Local oxygen monitoring sensor with audible alarm (<19.5% O2) in metrology bay.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent AFM tips and calibration gratings disposed of as non-hazardous electronic/solid waste in dedicated sharp containers; IPA-saturated cleanroom polyester wipes sealed in fire-rated volatile organic solvent waste bin for hazardous incineration.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (N2 Gas purge for AFM acoustic chamber)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity (Grade 5.0, 99.999%) | `100%` |
| **Isopropanol (IPA - for AFM stage and chuck wipe down only)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor / VLSI Grade | `99.9%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic silicon surface terminated with 0.8-1.2 nm chemical oxide (Si-OH / Si-O-Si bonds) from SC-1 Megasonic clean and spin-rinse dry, particle count < 15 adders at >= 0.2 um.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Intact hydrophilic chemical oxide, verified micro-smooth (Rq < 0.20 nm), free of organic adsorption, ready for immediate SC-2 metallic decontamination or in-situ dilute HF oxide stripping.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exposure to ambient air beyond 30 minutes causes volatile airborne molecular contamination (AMC - organic siloxanes and hydrocarbons) condensation and uncontrolled native oxide growth non-uniformity, causing AFM phase imaging noise, inaccurate roughness baseline, and non-uniform gate oxide nucleation kinetics.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full 5-point topographical AFM characterization of post-SC-1 180nm DRAM test wafer, confirming low surface microroughness (Rq <= 0.18 nm, Ra <= 0.14 nm), absence of alkaline anisotropic etch pits (>1.0 nm depth), and intact chemical oxide morphology qualifying the SC-1 bath for gate dielectric thermal processing.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `AFM_POST_SC1_TOPOGRAPHY_5PT_MAP.csv`
- [ ] `AFM_MICROROUGHNESS_METROLOGY_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `AFM_SURFACE_MORPHOLOGY_3D_RENDER.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-AFM-01` | **Root-mean-square roughness (Rq) over 1.0 um x 1.0 um area across 5 wafer sites** | `0.15 nm` | ±0.03 nm (upper control limit 0.18 nm) | 512x512 tapping-mode AFM height trace calculation after 1st-order line flattening and 2nd-order plane tilt correction |
| `ASSERT-AFM-02` | **Maximum peak-to-valley height (Rmax) across 5.0 um x 5.0 um area** | `0.90 nm` | +0.30 nm (hard limit <= 1.20 nm) | 1024x1024 high-density AFM surface scanning and depth histogram threshold extraction |
| `ASSERT-AFM-03` | **Density of etch pits with depth greater than or equal to 1.0 nm** | `0 pits/25 um^2` | 0 (zero defect tolerance for pits >= 1.0 nm) | Automated bearing area defect detection analysis across center and perimeter 5 um x 5 um scans |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 5 wafer map points exhibit Rq <= 0.18 nm, zero etch pits >= 1.0 nm detected in 25 um^2 areas, AFM calibration reference step validated within ±2% prior to and post run, and total wafer queue time from SC-1 spin-dry to metrology completion recorded <= 25 minutes.

critics.systems_engineer: SC-1 chemistry (NH4OH:H2O2:H2O) inherently oxidizes and etches silicon simultaneously. In high pH baths or when the NH4OH:H2O2 ratio exceeds 1:1:5, preferential anisotropic etching along crystal defect planes causes micro-roughening and pitting. If post-SC-1 root-mean-square roughness (Rq) exceeds 0.20 nm before gate oxidation, the 3.5 nm dry thermal gate oxide will experience severe localized electric field crowding, channel carrier mobility degradation, and premature time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB) in DRAM access transistors. AFM mapping must tightly feed back to the wet bench dosing loop before wafers proceed to SC-2 and thermal oxidation.
critics.domain_expert: Tapping mode (amplitude modulation AFM) using ultra-sharp silicon tips (tip radius nominal < 7 nm, resonant frequency ~300 kHz, force constant ~40 N/m) is mandatory to prevent plastic deformation or scraping of the fresh ~0.8-1.2 nm chemical oxide. High-aspect ratio scanning over 1 um x 1 um and 5 um x 5 um windows must decouple high-frequency microroughness (Rq/Ra) from low-frequency waviness. The critical parameter to monitor is etch pit density and peak-to-valley roughness (Rmax/Rz); deep pits (>1.5 nm) on a 3.5 nm oxide target directly erode 40% of the dielectric physical thickness.
critics.supply_chain: AFM cantilever tips wear rapidly when imaging silicon in ambient conditions due to tip bluntness from capillary forces and tip-sample adhesion. For open-source 180nm pilot line operations, cantilever tip consumption must be budgeted (typically 1 tip per 3-5 full wafer maps). Sourcing semiconductor-grade n-doped silicon probes (e.g., NCHV-A or equivalent with tip radius <= 8 nm) must have secondary qualified vendors to prevent metrology stoppage, and standard roughness calibration gratings (SiO2 steps on Si, 100 nm pitch / 20 nm step) must be recertified quarterly.
critics.laya_pm: AFM is fundamentally a low-throughput metrology technique (each 512x512 line map takes 8-15 minutes per site). A full 9-point or 49-point wafer map risks violating the critical cleanroom Q-time prior to the gate oxidation furnace load. To maintain throughput while safeguarding yield, implement a 5-point sampling scheme (Center, Top, Bottom, Left, Right at 10 mm edge exclusion) on 1 pilot wafer per lot, gating the wet clean run within a 45-minute Q-time window before final SC-2/HF clean.
critical_failure_modes: Tip convolution and bluntness artifact: Worn or chipped AFM tips (radius > 15 nm) artificially smooth measured surface profiles, under-reporting Rq by up to 60% and concealing micro-pits.

Capillary condensation and ambient moisture artifact: Humidity > 45% RH creates a water meniscus between tip and chemical oxide, inducing phase shift anomalies, force snap-in instability, and false topographical spikes.

SC-1 bath ratio drift inducing silicon pitting: Depletion of H2O2 in the SC-1 bath causing NH4OH-dominated alkaline anisotropic etching, generating high-density square pyramidal etch pits > 2 nm deep.

testcases.title: Post-SC-1 Surface Microroughness (Rq and Ra) 5-Point Wafer Topography Mapping
testcases.instrumentation: Atomic Force Microscope (AFM) in Tapping/Non-Contact Mode, calibrated with certified silicon grating; High-resolution n-type Si probe (tip radius <= 8 nm, spring constant 40 N/m, resonant frequency 300-330 kHz); Class 100 cleanroom acoustic and vibration isolation enclosure.
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafer has undergone standard SC-1 clean, megasonic DI water rinse (resistivity >= 18.2 MOhm*cm), and spin-rinse dry; Wafer loaded in AFM cleanroom acoustic box under dry N2 purge (<30% RH) within 20 minutes of spin-dry.
testcases.procedure: 1. Load wafer onto electrostatic/vacuum chuck and align wafer notch to 6 o'clock. 2. Establish tip resonance curve; select drive frequency 5% below resonant peak with free vibration amplitude A0 = 1.5 V and setpoint ratio Asp/A0 = 0.80. 3. Engage tip at Center (Site 1: 0,0) and acquire 1.0 um x 1.0 um scan at 512 x 512 pixels, scan rate 0.8 Hz. 4. Apply 1st-order polynomial line flatten and 2nd-order plane fit to remove wafer tilt. 5. Calculate Ra and Rq. 6. Repeat steps 3-5 at 4 perimeter sites (Top: 0,+40mm; Bottom: 0,-40mm; Left: -40mm,0; Right: +40mm,0). 7. Verify tip integrity against reference grating post-scan.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Pass if 5-point mean Rq <= 0.18 nm (1.8 Angstroms), maximum single-site Rq <= 0.22 nm, and no spatial gradient (edge-to-center delta <= 0.05 nm). Fail if any single-site Rq > 0.22 nm or Ra > 0.18 nm.

testcases.title: SC-1 Etch Pitting and Peak-to-Valley (Rmax) Defect Topography Scan
testcases.instrumentation: AFM tapping mode with tip check software (blind tip reconstruction algorithm); Acoustic isolation hood with active piezo vibration damping table.
testcases.pre_conditions: Same wafer immediately following TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-1-3-3-2-01; AFM tip condition validated (effective tip radius confirmed <= 10 nm via blind reconstruction).
testcases.procedure: 1. Move stage to Wafer Center (Site 1) and expand scan area to 5.0 um x 5.0 um at 1024 x 1024 pixels, scan rate 0.5 Hz. 2. Acquire height, amplitude, and phase channels simultaneously. 3. Execute 2nd-order polynomial background flattening. 4. Run depth histogram analysis and bearing area curve to identify negative excursions (pits). 5. Measure maximum peak-to-valley height (Rmax) and quantify pit count with depth > 1.0 nm. 6. Repeat scan at worst-case edge site identified in TC-01.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Pass if peak-to-valley Rmax <= 1.20 nm across 5 um x 5 um area, zero etch pits observed with depth >= 1.0 nm below mean surface plane, and pit density < 1 pit / 25 um^2. Fail if any pit depth >= 1.0 nm or Rmax > 1.20 nm.

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

**Document ID:** `SOP-MET-180NM-GTOX-007`  
**Title:** Etch Pitting Statistical Analysis and Surface Quality Qualification for Gate Oxidation  
**Process Step Hierarchy:** Context: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) [Architecture & Integration] > 180nm Dry Gate Oxide Growth (3.5 nm) [Thermal Processing] > Pre-Oxidation RCA Clean and In-Situ HF Dip Surface Preparation [Wet Chemistry] > RCA-1 (SC-1) Organic & Particle Removal Bath Formulation and Bench Qualification [Wet Chemistry] > Post-RCA-1 Particle Removal Efficiency (PRE) and Surface Roughness Metrology Qualification [Metrology] > AFM Post-SC-1 Surface Microroughness (Rq/Ra) and Etch Pitting Topography Qualification [Metrology] > Etch Pitting Statistical Analysis and Surface Quality Qualification for Gate Oxidation [Metrology]  
**Technology Generation:** Gen 2 (180 nm / µm class)  
**Action Type:** Make / Metrology Execution & Disposition  

---

### 1. Scope & Objective
This SOP defines the statistical sampling, AFM etch pit density quantification, surface microroughness extraction, and final wafer surface quality qualification protocol prior to loading bare silicon wafers into the dry thermal oxidation quartz tube furnace for 3.5 nm gate dielectric growth ($E_{bd} > 10\text{ MV/cm}$, $D_{it} < 10^{10}\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ eV}^{-1}$).

---

### 2. Concise Step-by-Step Procedure

```text
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                       AFM & Surface Metrology Flow                       |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  [Step 1] 9-Point Radial Wafer Sampling (Center, Mid-radius, Edge)       |
|                                    |                                     |
|                                    v                                     |
|  [Step 2] AFM Scan Acquisition (1 um x 1 um & 5 um x 5 um Tapping Mode)  |
|                                    |                                     |
|                                    v                                     |
|  [Step 3] Flattening & Statistical Extraction (Rq, Ra, Pit Count/Depth)  |
|                                    |                                     |
|                                    v                                     |
|  [Step 4] Lot Disposition & Transfer to 850°C-900°C Quartz Tube Furnace  |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

1. **Wafer Inspection & Automated Sampling Setup**:
   - Transfer post-SC-1/pre-gate oxidation monitor wafers to the automated Atomic Force Microscope (AFM) cassette station under Class 1 laminar flow hood.
   - Program a standard 9-point radial sampling map across the 200 mm wafer (Center, 4 points at mid-radius $r = R/2$, and 4 points at edge exclusion boundary $5\text{ mm}$ from bevel).

2. **High-Resolution Topography & Etch Pit Scanning**:
   - Engage non-contact / tapping mode AFM probe (tip radius $< 5\text{ nm}$).
   - Perform dual-field scanning at each site:
     - Area A: $1\ \mu\text{m} \times 1\ \mu\text{m}$ scan ($512 \times 512$ pixels, scan rate $0.5\text{ Hz}$) for high-frequency microroughness ($R_a$, $R_q$).
     - Area B: $5\ \mu\text{m} \times 5\ \mu\text{m}$ scan ($512 \times 512$ pixels, scan rate $0.5\text{ Hz}$) for crystallographic SC-1 induced etch pit / micro-void detection.

3. **Statistical Topography Flattening & Defect Extraction**:
   - Apply 2nd-order polynomial plane flattening to remove macro-bowing/tilt.
   - Identify etch pits using depth-threshold segmentation: flag any depressions with depth $> 0.5\text{ nm}$ and aspect ratio indicative of SC-1 chemical etching along (111) planes.
   - Calculate total pit count per scan area, compute Etch Pit Density (EPD in $\text{pits/cm}^2$), and extract root-mean-square roughness ($R_q$).

4. **Statistical Lot Disposition & Furnace Release**:
   - Perform ANOVA and $3\sigma$ control limit analysis across the 9 sampling sites.
   - Verify all sites meet roughness and pit density criteria to prevent local oxide thinning and premature breakdown of the 3.5 nm physical gate oxide.
   - If qualified, generate electronic run-card sign-off and immediately dispatch the lot to the quartz oxidation tube furnace (within $< 2\text{ hours}$ Q-time to prevent native oxide regrowth).

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Targets

| Metric | Target / Specification | Tool / Metrology Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Surface Microroughness ($R_q$ / RMS)** | $\le 0.15\text{ nm}$ across all 9 scan points ($1\ \mu\text{m} \times 1\ \mu\text{m}$ scan) | High-Resolution Tapping-Mode AFM |
| **Etch Pit Density (EPD)** | $\le 5 \times 10^3\text{ pits/cm}^2$ (Zero pits detected in $5\ \mu\text{m} \times 5\ \mu\text{m}$ area) | Automated AFM Topographical Particle/Void Filter |
| **Etch Pit Maximum Depth ($d_{max}$)** | $< 0.5\text{ nm}$ (to prevent local electric-field distortion under 3.5 nm gate oxide) | AFM Cross-Sectional Profilometry |
| **Pre-Oxidation Clean-to-Furnace Q-Time** | $\le 120\text{ minutes}$ ($< 2.0\text{ hours}$) | Cleanroom MES Automated Lot Tracker |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

- **Deal-Grove Silicon Thermal Oxidation Kinetics in Quartz Tube Furnace**:
  - *Context applied*: Thermal oxidation kinetics governing the thin gate oxide regime; specifies dry oxidation at 900°C–1000°C in pure dry $\text{O}_2$ producing high-dielectric breakdown gate oxide ($E_{bd} > 10\text{ MV/cm}$) with minimal interface trap density ($D_{it} < 10^{10}\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ eV}^{-1}$) at a target thickness of 3.5 nm to 4.0 nm. Surface pitting and roughness must be strictly controlled at this stage because any step or pit approaching ~0.5 nm introduces critical localized thinning in a 3.5 nm film.
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**:
  - *Context applied*: 180nm DRAM 1T1C transistor integration baseline with thermally grown gate dielectric ($\text{SiO}_2$) at 850°C–900°C dry oxidation with $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ physical thickness and bitline/wordline pitch of 360 nm to 400 nm.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Downstream 3.5 nm dry gate oxidation reliability hinges on limiting high-frequency interface roughness and atomic-step pit clustering. With an E_bd requirement exceeding 10 MV/cm, any etch pit depth greater than 0.5 nm introduces localized electrostatic field intensification (E = V_gate / t_ox_eff), which drastically degrades Time-Dependent Dielectric Breakdown (TDDB) and increases 1/f flicker noise in the DRAM peripheral access transistors.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Standard SC-1 chemistry (NH4OH:H2O2:H2O) dissolves silicon via concurrent oxidation by H2O2 and nucleophilic dissolution of hydrous silica by OH-. If the peroxide/hydroxide ratio drops locally or if bath temperatures exceed 75°C, micro-anisotropic etching along Si(111) planes causes pyramidal etch pits (haze defectivity). Statistical qualification must decouple stochastic intrinsic surface microroughness (Rq < 0.15 nm) from deterministic etch-pitting clusters via multi-site high-aspect-ratio AFM metrology.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Ultra-sharp AFM probe cantilevers (tip radius < 2 nm, high-resonance tapping mode tips such as Si3N4/diamond-coated ultra-sharp silicon probes) suffer rapid apex bluntness during automated wafer-scale rastering. Metrology tip consumption per 25-wafer lot represents an operational bottleneck and cost spike; tip qualification and tip-radius deconvolution algorithms must be standardized across scan iterations.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: AFM metrology throughput is inherently low (5 to 10 minutes per 2x2 µm site, 9-point wafer mapping requires ~60-90 minutes per wafer). To maintain the line cadence and prevent queue-time violations prior to furnace loading, the statistical sampling plan must establish a verified correlation between fast laser-scattering darkfield haze metrology and AFM etch-pit count.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Gate Dielectric Premature Breakdown: Etch pits > 0.6 nm depth cause localized oxide thinning to < 2.9 nm, triggering Fowler-Nordheim leakage and early B-mode TDDB failures across active transfer gates.
1. Threshold Voltage (Vth) Mismatch and Subthreshold Hump: Localized atomic terrace facet pits cause non-uniform fixed interface charge (Q_it) and interface trap density (D_it > 10^10 cm^-2 eV^-1), inducing severe subthreshold slope degradation and retention leakage in DRAM cell transistors.
1. Tip Convolution Artefact False Pass: Degradation of AFM probe tip radius (R_tip > 10 nm) geometrically obscures narrow etch pits (< 15 nm width), leading to false-negative surface qualification and subsequent furnace contamination.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-1-3-3-3-01` | **Automated Multi-Site AFM Microroughness and Etch Pit Depth Metrology** | Atomic Force Microscope (Bruker Dimension Icon or equivalent) equipped with ultra-sharp Si tips (nominal tip radius <= 2 nm, cantilever resonance ~300 kHz, spring constant ~40 N/m) in PeakForce Tapping / Tapping Mode. | 1. Load wafer into cleanroom automated AFM chuck under laminar flow. 2. Perform 9-point radial map (Center, 4 mid-radius at 0.5R, 4 edge exclusion at 3mm edge). 3. Acquire high-resolution 2.0 µm x 2.0 µm topographical scans at 512 x 512 pixels (scan rate 0.5 Hz). 4. Apply 1st-order flattening and 2nd-order plane fit algorithms to eliminate sample tilt. 5. Extract root-mean-square roughness (Rq) and arithmetic roughness (Ra). 6. Apply automated grain/pit analysis using thresholding at 0.35 nm below baseline to extract pit density (pits/µm^2), max pit depth, and lateral diameter. | `Surface roughness Rq <= 0.15 nm (1.50 Å) across all 9 sites; Ra <= 0.12 nm (1.20 Å); Maximum etch pit depth < 0.40 nm; Etch pit spatial density <= 0.05 pits/µm^2. Zero pit clusters with depth >= 0.50 nm.` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-1-3-3-3-02` | **Whole-Wafer Laser Scattering Haze-to-Pit Correlation and Statistical Distribution Analysis** | Laser Surface Particle and Haze Scanner (KLA-Tencor Surfscan SP2 or equivalent, 405 nm laser, narrow/wide darkfield channels) coupled with statistical R/Python analysis engine. | 1. Load wafer into unpatterned surface defect inspection system. 2. Execute high-sensitivity haze mapping across entire 150mm/200mm wafer surface (edge exclusion 3 mm). 3. Record average low-frequency and high-frequency haze levels in parts per million (ppm). 4. Overlay AFM coordinates from TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-1-3-3-3-01 and compute Pearson correlation coefficient between high-frequency haze and AFM Rq/pit count. 5. Perform Weibull and normal distribution goodness-of-fit analysis on pit depths across wafer lots to verify process capability index (Cpk). | `Mean whole-wafer optical haze <= 0.12 ppm; high-frequency haze standard deviation <= 0.015 ppm; Statistical process capability index Cpk >= 1.67 for Rq distribution; Correlation coefficient r >= 0.85 between laser haze and AFM Rq.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom clean vinyl or nitrile gloves (double-gloved), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Full cleanroom ESD-safe bunny suit with hood and boot covers, ESD wrist strap connected to grounding point during sample handling
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For IPA skin contact: Remove contaminated clothing and rinse skin thoroughly with deionized water for 15 minutes. For eye contact: Flush eyes with sterile eyewash for 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek medical attention if irritation persists. For inhalation: Move personnel to fresh air. In case of cleanroom nitrogen displacement alarm: Evacuate area immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: AFM metrology tool enclosure maintained under clean dry air (CDA) or Class 1 laminar downward airflow (0.45 m/s +/- 20%). IPA maintenance squeeze bottles must be stored in vented flammable solvent cabinet when not in use.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA lint-free wipes and contaminated AFM tips must be disposed of in dedicated, grounded, flame-retardant solvent solid waste bins. No liquid effluent discharged.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) for AFM tip/stage cleaning** | `67-63-0` | Electronic grade / Semi Grade 5 | `>= 99.8%` |
| **Ultra-High Purity Compressed Nitrogen (N2) for blow-off** | `7727-37-9` | UHP Grade 6.0 (99.9999% purity, < 10 ppb H2O/O2) | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic chemical oxide passivated surface post-SC-1 (SiO2 thickness ~0.6-0.8 nm, contact angle < 10°), free of particulate debris.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Qualified microroughness and low-pitting passivated wafer, pre-conditioned for dilute HF dip (HF-last) and immediate 3.5 nm dry gate oxidation.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air queue time causes airborne molecular contamination (AMC) adsorption (volatile organic compounds and sulfur-bearing hydrocarbons), moisture-induced native oxide thickening, and unquantifiable haze shifts which skew AFM Rq readings and compromise gate dielectric breakdown.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Complete metrological and statistical qualification confirming that the pre-oxidation SC-1 clean maintains sub-angstrom microroughness without inducing anisotropic etch pitting, fulfilling gate dielectric requirements for 180nm open-source DRAM 3.5 nm dry oxide.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `AFM_SC1_Surface_Roughness_9Point_Map_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `Etch_Pit_Statistical_Distribution_and_Cpk_Analysis.csv`
- [ ] `High_Res_AFM_Surface_Topography_Raw_Scans.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Mean surface microroughness (Rq) across all 9 inspection sites on the wafer must not exceed the maximum allowable threshold.** | `0.14 nm` | +/- 0.01 nm (upper limit 0.15 nm) | AFM 2x2 µm PeakForce tapping mode scan with 512x512 resolution after 2nd-order plane subtraction |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Maximum individual etch pit depth measured anywhere on active area test sites must remain strictly below the oxide thinning risk limit.** | `0.30 nm` | < 0.40 nm absolute maximum | Automated depth histogram and bearing curve analysis on flattened AFM topography images |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Statistical process capability index (Cpk) for Rq microroughness across qualified wafer lots must meet Six Sigma standards.** | `1.67` | >= 1.67 | Statistical process evaluation against upper specification limit (USL = 0.15 nm) over 3 consecutive qualification lots |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 9 AFM inspection locations demonstrate Rq <= 0.15 nm and Ra <= 0.12 nm with zero etch pits exceeding 0.40 nm depth, Cpk >= 1.67 achieved across 3 qualification runs, and formal approval by Metrology Council and Thermal Oxidation Process Owner prior to gate furnace loading.

testcases.title: Automated Multi-Site AFM Microroughness and Etch Pit Depth Metrology
testcases.instrumentation: Atomic Force Microscope (Bruker Dimension Icon or equivalent) equipped with ultra-sharp Si tips (nominal tip radius <= 2 nm, cantilever resonance ~300 kHz, spring constant ~40 N/m) in PeakForce Tapping / Tapping Mode.
testcases.pre_conditions: Prime-grade 150mm/200mm p-type Si (100) test wafers post-SC-1 Megasonic clean and Marangoni dry; cleanroom class 1 (ISO 3); anti-vibration table active; AFM tip calibration verified against standard 100nm pitch / 0.5nm step height calibration artifact.
testcases.procedure:
1. Load wafer into cleanroom automated AFM chuck under laminar flow.
2. Perform 9-point radial map (Center, 4 mid-radius at 0.5R, 4 edge exclusion at 3mm edge).
3. Acquire high-resolution 2.0 µm x 2.0 µm topographical scans at 512 x 512 pixels (scan rate 0.5 Hz).
4. Apply 1st-order flattening and 2nd-order plane fit algorithms to eliminate sample tilt.
5. Extract root-mean-square roughness (Rq) and arithmetic roughness (Ra).
6. Apply automated grain/pit analysis using thresholding at 0.35 nm below baseline to extract pit density (pits/µm^2), max pit depth, and lateral diameter.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Surface roughness Rq <= 0.15 nm (1.50 Å) across all 9 sites; Ra <= 0.12 nm (1.20 Å); Maximum etch pit depth < 0.40 nm; Etch pit spatial density <= 0.05 pits/µm^2. Zero pit clusters with depth >= 0.50 nm.

testcases.title: Whole-Wafer Laser Scattering Haze-to-Pit Correlation and Statistical Distribution Analysis
testcases.instrumentation: Laser Surface Particle and Haze Scanner (KLA-Tencor Surfscan SP2 or equivalent, 405 nm laser, narrow/wide darkfield channels) coupled with statistical R/Python analysis engine.
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafers inspected within 15 minutes of SC-1 processing; optical haze baseline calibrated on virgin reference prime monitor wafer (< 0.08 ppm).
testcases.procedure:
1. Load wafer into unpatterned surface defect inspection system.
2. Execute high-sensitivity haze mapping across entire 150mm/200mm wafer surface (edge exclusion 3 mm).
3. Record average low-frequency and high-frequency haze levels in parts per million (ppm).
4. Overlay AFM coordinates from TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-1-3-3-3-01 and compute Pearson correlation coefficient between high-frequency haze and AFM Rq/pit count.
5. Perform Weibull and normal distribution goodness-of-fit analysis on pit depths across wafer lots to verify process capability index (Cpk).
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Mean whole-wafer optical haze <= 0.12 ppm; high-frequency haze standard deviation <= 0.015 ppm; Statistical process capability index Cpk >= 1.67 for Rq distribution; Correlation coefficient r >= 0.85 between laser haze and AFM Rq.

ppe_required: Class 100 cleanroom clean vinyl or nitrile gloves (double-gloved)
ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields
Full cleanroom ESD-safe bunny suit with hood and boot covers
ESD wrist strap connected to grounding point during sample handling

cas_chemicals.name: Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) for AFM tip/stage cleaning
Ultra-High Purity Compressed Nitrogen (N2) for blow-off

ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: For IPA skin contact: Remove contaminated clothing and rinse skin thoroughly with deionized water for 15 minutes. For eye contact: Flush eyes with sterile eyewash for 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek medical attention if irritation persists. For inhalation: Move personnel to fresh air. In case of cleanroom nitrogen displacement alarm: Evacuate area immediately.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: AFM metrology tool enclosure maintained under clean dry air (CDA) or Class 1 laminar downward airflow (0.45 m/s +/- 20%). IPA maintenance squeeze bottles must be stored in vented flammable solvent cabinet when not in use.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Spent IPA lint-free wipes and contaminated AFM tips must be disposed of in dedicated, grounded, flame-retardant solvent solid waste bins. No liquid effluent discharged.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Hydrophilic chemical oxide passivated surface post-SC-1 (SiO2 thickness ~0.6-0.8 nm, contact angle < 10°), free of particulate debris.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Qualified microroughness and low-pitting passivated wafer, pre-conditioned for dilute HF dip (HF-last) and immediate 3.5 nm dry gate oxidation.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Exceeding air queue time causes airborne molecular contamination (AMC) adsorption (volatile organic compounds and sulfur-bearing hydrocarbons), moisture-induced native oxide thickening, and unquantifiable haze shifts which skew AFM Rq readings and compromise gate dielectric breakdown.

expected_result.summary: Complete metrological and statistical qualification confirming that the pre-oxidation SC-1 clean maintains sub-angstrom microroughness without inducing anisotropic etch pitting, fulfilling gate dielectric requirements for 180nm open-source DRAM 3.5 nm dry oxide.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Mean surface microroughness (Rq) across all 9 inspection sites on the wafer must not exceed the maximum allowable threshold.
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: AFM 2x2 µm PeakForce tapping mode scan with 512x512 resolution after 2nd-order plane subtraction

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Maximum individual etch pit depth measured anywhere on active area test sites must remain strictly below the oxide thinning risk limit.
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Automated depth histogram and bearing curve analysis on flattened AFM topography images

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Statistical process capability index (Cpk) for Rq microroughness across qualified wafer lots must meet Six Sigma standards.
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Statistical process evaluation against upper specification limit (USL = 0.15 nm) over 3 consecutive qualification lots

expected_result.signoff_criteria: All 9 AFM inspection locations demonstrate Rq <= 0.15 nm and Ra <= 0.12 nm with zero etch pits exceeding 0.40 nm depth, Cpk >= 1.67 achieved across 3 qualification runs, and formal approval by Metrology Council and Thermal Oxidation Process Owner prior to gate furnace loading.
