# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document Title: Custom Fluoropolymer Manual Immersion Jig & Splash-Shield Rig Fabrication
**Hierarchy Level:** Leaf SOP (Mechanical Assembly / Tooling)  
**Process Line:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip — Gate Oxide Pre-Clean & Native Oxide Wet Dip Fixturing  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Purpose & Scope
This SOP defines the fabrication, machining, surface preparation, assembly, and dimensional validation of a dedicated virgin fluoropolymer (PTFE/PFA/PVDF) manual immersion wafer jig and transparent/chemical-resistant splash-shield enclosure rig. 

This custom tooling holds 150mm/200mm silicon wafers during the pre-oxidation dilute HF (1:50) / buffered oxide etch dip sequence designed to strip native oxide prior to ~3.5 nm dry gate oxide growth in the 180nm DRAM cell process flow.

---

### 2. Required Equipment, Materials & Safety Gear
* **Raw Stock:** Semi-crystalline virgin PTFE (polytetrafluoroethylene) or PFA (perfluoroalkoxy) rod and sheet stock (high chemical inertness to concentrated and dilute HF).
* **Splash Enclosure Stock:** High-clarity fluoropolymer / ECTFE / transparent PFA film or acrylic splash shielding treated with HF-resistant fluoropolymer coating.
* **Machining Centers:** Dedicated non-metallic / polymer CNC mill with clean ultra-sharp carbide or diamond-like carbon (DLC) coated tooling (no cutting fluid or sulfur-based lubricants).
* **Hardware:** Virgin PFA threaded fasteners, studs, and retaining nuts (strictly zero metallic fasteners in wetted zones).
* **Safety & PPE:** Cleanroom chemical apron, face shield, double nitrile gloves, and hydrofluoric acid emergency antidote: **Calcium Gluconate Gel (2.5%)** present and unexpired at the assembly and testing station.

---

### 3. Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

```text
+------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                      FABRICATION & ASSEMBLY FLOW                       |
+------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  [Step 1] Virgin Fluoropolymer CNC Machining (Grooves & Guide Pins)    |
|                                  |                                     |
|                                  v                                     |
|  [Step 2] Splash-Shield Containment Rig Assembly & Interlocks          |
|                                  |                                     |
|                                  v                                     |
|  [Step 3] SC-2 Compatible Pre-Assembly Leaching & Decontamination      |
|                                  |                                     |
|                                  v                                     |
|  [Step 4] Mechanical Fit, Wafer Edge Exclusion & Clearance Audit       |
+------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

#### Step 1: Virgin Fluoropolymer CNC Machining
1. Mount virgin PTFE/PFA blank stock onto the vacuum chuck of the polymer CNC mill. Do not use standard mineral-oil coolants; use filtered clean dry air (CDA) or DI water mist cooling only.
2. Machine wafer carrier comb slots with a 60° V-groove profile configured to contact only the peripheral exclusion zone (< 3.0 mm from wafer edge) to prevent contact with active transistor channel areas ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$).
3. Machine drain-relief scallops along the bottom rib of the carrier to ensure zero stagnant chemical holdup and allow rapid laminar gravity drainage upon withdrawal from the etch tank.

#### Step 2: Splash-Shield Containment Rig Assembly
1. Assemble the transparent fluoropolymer splash shield onto the wet-bench rim mount using PFA threaded fasteners. Torque fasteners hand-tight to prevent thread galling or cold flow/creep of fluoropolymer threads.
2. Align the vertical manual-immersion guide rails to provide smooth, binding-free vertical translation into the immersion bath.
3. Verify that splash guard panels fully encompass the bath opening with minimum 100 mm vertical overlap above the liquid line to prevent aerosol and liquid droplet dispersion during manual transfer.

#### Step 3: Chemical Leaching & Metallic Decontamination
1. Submerge all machined fluoropolymer components in a dedicated chemical leaching bath consisting of dilute SC-2/RCA-2 solution ($\text{HCl}:\text{H}_2\text{O}_2:\text{H}_2\text{O}$) followed by a 1:50 HF rinse to extract surface trace metallic impurities and machining debris.
2. Rinse with Megohm-grade deionized (DI) water until effluent resistivity reaches $> 18\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$.
3. Dry components in a Class 100 laminar cleanhood using filtered nitrogen ($N_2$).

#### Step 4: Mechanical Fit, Hydrophobic Drain & Clearance Verification
1. Load dummy silicon wafers into the assembled jig slots. Ensure smooth wafer insertion and seating without micro-chatter or edge chipping.
2. Perform manual immersion dip cycle into a DI water tank. Observe drainage upon vertical lift: verify complete liquid run-off without trapped droplets bridging between adjacent wafer slots within 5 seconds.
3. Store jig in a cleanroom N2 dry box when not actively mounted on the wet station.

---

### 4. Acceptance Criteria & Machine-Measurable Target Metrics

| Inspection Parameter | Target Metric / Tolerance | Measurement Instrument / Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Wafer Edge Exclusion Contact Width** | $\le 2.0\text{ mm}$ inward from bevel edge (leaves active $L=180\text{ nm}$ array uncontacted) | Optical Toolmaker's Microscope / Non-contact CMM |
| **Jig Slot Pitch & Spacing Accuracy** | $4.76\text{ mm} \pm 0.05\text{ mm}$ uniform pitch | Calibrated Digital Height Gauge / Optical Comparator |
| **Drain Relief Run-Off Time** | $< 5.0\text{ seconds}$ for full gravity clearing | High-speed video / Digital Optical Timer |
| **Enclosure Splash Aerosol Containment** | $100\%$ liquid droplet containment ($\le 0$ exterior droplet strikes at transfer speed $0.15\text{ m/s}$) | UV-Fluorescent Tracer Liquid Inspection |

---

### 5. Context & Literature Citations
* **Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE):** Hydrofluoric acid safety handling protocols; hydrofluoric acid skin penetration hazard requiring mandatory presence of calcium gluconate gel at all times during fabrication, assembly, and testing.
* **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering:** Defines pre-clean criticality where ~3.5 nm physical thickness dry gate oxide ($850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$) requires non-contaminating, metal-free fluoropolymer tooling prior to thermal oxidation.
* **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:** Transistor active dimensions ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$) dictating strict exclusion-zone edge-gripping fixturing to eliminate mechanical abrasion across active silicon patterns.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The fluoropolymer immersion jig must mechanically decouple manual operator translation from wafer hydrodynamic drag forces while maintaining rigid 3-point edge contact. Utilizing machined virgin PTFE or PVDF components without metallic fasteners prevents trace transition metal leaching (Fe, Cu, Ni < 1e10 atoms/cm²) into the 1:50 DHF bath, but non-conductive fluoropolymers present extreme electrostatic charge accumulation (> 5 kV) during immersion/withdrawal cycles, risking ESD gate oxide breakdown and particle attraction.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For 180nm dry gate dielectric pre-clean, the 1:50 DHF etch is targeted to fully strip 1.5-2.0 nm of chemical native oxide without introducing micro-roughness (delta Rq < 0.05 nm). The manual immersion rig must enforce a consistent 30-45 degree entry angle to prevent air pocket entrapment across the wafer face, and the splash-shield geometry must eliminate droplet aerosolization and condensation drip-back onto the freshly hydrophobic, hydrogen-terminated silicon surface.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Virgin semi-finished PTFE/PVDF stock must be certified SEMI F57 grade to guarantee sub-ppb metallic and TOC extractables. In the domestic Vietnamese market, generic industrial PTFE sheets often contain recycled regrind or sintering aids that leach calcium and zinc; strict chain-of-custody documentation or pre-leaching qualification in 10% HNO3 for 48 hours is mandatory prior to CNC routing.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Fabrication lead times for custom CNC-milled fluoropolymer dippers and thermoformed clear PFA/ECTFE splash shields must not exceed 5 working days to avoid blocking the furnace loading qualification campaign for Gen 1 Deal-Grove dry oxidation runs. Mechanical dimensional sign-off must be achievable with standard vernier calipers and optical comparator inspection.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Metallic ionic cross-contamination caused by sub-surface metallic inclusions or cutting-tool residue embedded into the PTFE jig during machining.
1. Etch non-uniformity and liquid streaking resulting from erratic manual withdrawal speeds exceeding the critical dewetting velocity (~1.5 mm/s), leaving HF droplets that cause localized stain etching.
1. Hydrophobic surface re-oxidation and airborne organic adsorption due to splash-shield exhaust turbulence disrupting laminar containment.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-2-1-1-2-01` | **Fluoropolymer Jig Dimensional Tolerance and Wafer Edge Clamping Verification** | Mitutoyo 500-196-30 Digital Caliper (0.01 mm resolution), Keyence VHX-7000 Digital Optical Inspection System, and Mitutoyo Digimatic Dial Indicator. | 1. Mount the machined PTFE wafer dipper fixture onto the splash-shield linear guide rails. 2. Measure the three retention slot widths and notch depths across 5 repetitive positions using the digital caliper. 3. Seat a standard 100mm double-side polished test wafer into the jig. 4. Cycle manual immersion descent and ascent along the 150mm vertical travel distance 10 times. 5. Inspect wafer edge contact points under the digital optical microscope for mechanical chipping, micro-cracks, or plastic deformation. | `Slot width must measure 1.20 mm +/- 0.05 mm. Clamping engagement depth must be within 1.50 mm +/- 0.10 mm with zero wafer slippage during full inversion. Microscopic inspection must show 0 edge micro-chips (> 10 um) across the wafer perimeter.` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-2-1-1-2-02` | **Fluoropolymer Acid Leaching and Chemical Extraction Gravimetric/Ionic Purity Audit** | Agilent 7900 ICP-MS (Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry), Metrohm 930 Compact IC Flex Ion Chromatograph, and Class 100 PTFE leaching vessels. | 1. Submerge the complete fluoropolymer immersion jig assembly into 500 mL of semiconductor-grade 5% ultra-pure HNO3 / 0.5% HF baseline extraction solution in a sealed PFA container. 2. Maintain at 40 deg C for 24 hours. 3. Decant extraction fluid and introduce directly into ICP-MS for trace transition metal quantification. 4. Perform identical extraction blank subtraction. | `Total extractable metals (Fe, Cu, Ni, Zn, Ca, Al) must sum to < 0.50 ppb (ng/mL). Fluoride leaching and particulate shedding (> 0.2 um) must be below 50 particles/mL as measured by liquid particle counter.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Full face shield (polycarbonate compliant with ANSI Z87.1) over chemical splash goggles, Heavy-duty butyl/neoprene blend acid gauntlet gloves (0.5 mm minimum thickness) over secondary nitrile inner gloves, Seamless chemical-resistant fluoropolymer/PVDF apron extending below the knee line, Closed-toe chemical-resistant neoprene work boots
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Calcium gluconate gel (2.5% USP grade) must be physically positioned within 1.5 meters of the workstation with valid unexpired lot. Upon skin contact, immediately flush with emergency eyewash/drench shower for 2 minutes, then massage calcium gluconate gel continuously into affected tissue using clean gloved hands until medical personnel arrive. In case of ocular exposure, flush with isotonic sterile saline or 1% calcium gluconate solution for minimum 15 minutes; seek emergency medical intervention immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operation restricted to a dedicated polypropylene wet bench with face velocity maintained at 0.50 +/- 0.05 m/s (100 FPM) across the active sash opening. The splash-shield rig must interface with downstream acid-scrubber exhaust drawing negative pressure (-25 Pa relative to cleanroom).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent dilute HF must be decanted into dedicated fluoropolymer drain plumbed to an automated calcium hydroxide / calcium chloride precipitation neutralization tank (CaF2 precipitation at pH 8.5 - 9.2). Under no circumstances dispose of via general drain or mix with organic solvents.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid (aqueous)** | `7664-39-3` | SEMI Tier C / Ultra-Pure Microelectronic Grade | `0.98% - 1.02% (1:50 volumetric dilution from 49% stock)` |
| **Deionized Water** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type E-1 / 18.2 MOhm-cm at 25 deg C | `Balance (98.98% - 99.02%)` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `15 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `2 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic SC-2 metallic decontamination post-clean chemical oxide (thickness 0.8 - 1.2 nm, DI water contact angle < 10 degrees).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: 100% Hydrophobic hydrogen-terminated bare silicon Si(100):H (native oxide < 0.1 nm, DI water contact angle > 75 degrees).
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding Q-time results in parasitic uncontrolled ambient regrowth of non-stoichiometric native oxide (SiOx) and airborne volatile organic compound (VOC) condensation, causing gate dielectric thickness non-uniformity (> 5% deviation on 3.5 nm target), increased interface trap density (Dit > 5e11 eV-1 cm-2), and premature Fowler-Nordheim oxide breakdown.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completed physical fabrication, CNC dimensional validation, and trace-metal extraction qualification of a custom virgin PTFE/PVDF manual wafer immersion dipper and transparent PFA splash-shield containment rig, certified to safely execute controlled 1:50 DHF etch dips for 100mm wafers prior to 3.5 nm dry gate oxidation.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `DWG_PTFE_DIPPER_RIG_FAB_V1_ASBUILT.pdf`
- [ ] `ICPMS_TRACE_METAL_PTFE_EXTRACTABLES_REPORT.csv`
- [ ] `HYDROPHOBIC_DIP_QUALIFICATION_SURFACE_ENERGY.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Wafer immersion dipper vertical rail runout and perpendicularity deviation along 150mm stroke** | `0.05 mm` | +/- 0.02 mm | Dial indicator scan along guide rail against precision granite surface plate |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Chemical native oxide clearance verification via DI water contact angle on post-etch Si(100) wafer** | `78.0 degrees` | +/- 3.0 degrees | Automated optical sessile drop goniometer 5-point wafer mapping |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Cumulative transition metal extractable mass concentration leached from jig into 1:50 DHF bath** | `0.15 ppb` | <= 0.50 ppb | High-resolution ICP-MS analysis of 24h acid soak solution |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Sign-off requires zero detected mechanical clearance binding over 50 consecutive dry test strokes, clean ICP-MS certificate proving cumulative metallic contaminants <= 0.50 ppb, documented DI water contact angle >= 75 degrees across 5 mapped wafer points after a 60-second 1:50 DHF immersion, and EHS sign-off verifying 100 FPM hood face velocity with calcium gluconate on station.
citations: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench (Kang & Leblebici - CMOS Digital Integrated Circuits)
Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE) (Semiconductor Chemical Processing Handbook)
Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering (IEEE / Legacy Foundry Technical Reports)

critics.systems_engineer: The fluoropolymer immersion jig must mechanically decouple manual operator translation from wafer hydrodynamic drag forces while maintaining rigid 3-point edge contact. Utilizing machined virgin PTFE or PVDF components without metallic fasteners prevents trace transition metal leaching (Fe, Cu, Ni < 1e10 atoms/cm²) into the 1:50 DHF bath, but non-conductive fluoropolymers present extreme electrostatic charge accumulation (> 5 kV) during immersion/withdrawal cycles, risking ESD gate oxide breakdown and particle attraction.
critics.domain_expert: For 180nm dry gate dielectric pre-clean, the 1:50 DHF etch is targeted to fully strip 1.5-2.0 nm of chemical native oxide without introducing micro-roughness (delta Rq < 0.05 nm). The manual immersion rig must enforce a consistent 30-45 degree entry angle to prevent air pocket entrapment across the wafer face, and the splash-shield geometry must eliminate droplet aerosolization and condensation drip-back onto the freshly hydrophobic, hydrogen-terminated silicon surface.
critics.supply_chain: Virgin semi-finished PTFE/PVDF stock must be certified SEMI F57 grade to guarantee sub-ppb metallic and TOC extractables. In the domestic Vietnamese market, generic industrial PTFE sheets often contain recycled regrind or sintering aids that leach calcium and zinc; strict chain-of-custody documentation or pre-leaching qualification in 10% HNO3 for 48 hours is mandatory prior to CNC routing.
critics.laya_pm: Fabrication lead times for custom CNC-milled fluoropolymer dippers and thermoformed clear PFA/ECTFE splash shields must not exceed 5 working days to avoid blocking the furnace loading qualification campaign for Gen 1 Deal-Grove dry oxidation runs. Mechanical dimensional sign-off must be achievable with standard vernier calipers and optical comparator inspection.
critical_failure_modes: Metallic ionic cross-contamination caused by sub-surface metallic inclusions or cutting-tool residue embedded into the PTFE jig during machining.
Etch non-uniformity and liquid streaking resulting from erratic manual withdrawal speeds exceeding the critical dewetting velocity (~1.5 mm/s), leaving HF droplets that cause localized stain etching.
Hydrophobic surface re-oxidation and airborne organic adsorption due to splash-shield exhaust turbulence disrupting laminar containment.

testcases.title: Fluoropolymer Jig Dimensional Tolerance and Wafer Edge Clamping Verification
testcases.instrumentation: Mitutoyo 500-196-30 Digital Caliper (0.01 mm resolution), Keyence VHX-7000 Digital Optical Inspection System, and Mitutoyo Digimatic Dial Indicator.
testcases.pre_conditions: Jig components fully degreased with IPA, rinsed with 18.2 MOhm-cm DI water, blown dry with 0.1 um filtered N2, and stabilized at cleanroom ambient 21.0 +/- 0.5 deg C.
testcases.procedure: 1. Mount the machined PTFE wafer dipper fixture onto the splash-shield linear guide rails. 2. Measure the three retention slot widths and notch depths across 5 repetitive positions using the digital caliper. 3. Seat a standard 100mm double-side polished test wafer into the jig. 4. Cycle manual immersion descent and ascent along the 150mm vertical travel distance 10 times. 5. Inspect wafer edge contact points under the digital optical microscope for mechanical chipping, micro-cracks, or plastic deformation.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Slot width must measure 1.20 mm +/- 0.05 mm. Clamping engagement depth must be within 1.50 mm +/- 0.10 mm with zero wafer slippage during full inversion. Microscopic inspection must show 0 edge micro-chips (> 10 um) across the wafer perimeter.

testcases.title: Fluoropolymer Acid Leaching and Chemical Extraction Gravimetric/Ionic Purity Audit
testcases.instrumentation: Agilent 7900 ICP-MS (Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry), Metrohm 930 Compact IC Flex Ion Chromatograph, and Class 100 PTFE leaching vessels.
testcases.pre_conditions: Jig cleaned in SC-1 (5:1:1 DIW:NH4OH:H2O2) at 65 deg C for 10 min, rinsed to > 17.5 MOhm-cm DI water resistivity.
testcases.procedure: 1. Submerge the complete fluoropolymer immersion jig assembly into 500 mL of semiconductor-grade 5% ultra-pure HNO3 / 0.5% HF baseline extraction solution in a sealed PFA container. 2. Maintain at 40 deg C for 24 hours. 3. Decant extraction fluid and introduce directly into ICP-MS for trace transition metal quantification. 4. Perform identical extraction blank subtraction.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Total extractable metals (Fe, Cu, Ni, Zn, Ca, Al) must sum to < 0.50 ppb (ng/mL). Fluoride leaching and particulate shedding (> 0.2 um) must be below 50 particles/mL as measured by liquid particle counter.

ppe_required: Full face shield (polycarbonate compliant with ANSI Z87.1) over chemical splash goggles
Heavy-duty butyl/neoprene blend acid gauntlet gloves (0.5 mm minimum thickness) over secondary nitrile inner gloves
Seamless chemical-resistant fluoropolymer/PVDF apron extending below the knee line
Closed-toe chemical-resistant neoprene work boots

cas_chemicals.name: Hydrofluoric Acid (aqueous)
cas_chemicals.purity_grade: SEMI Tier C / Ultra-Pure Microelectronic Grade

cas_chemicals.name: Deionized Water
cas_chemicals.purity_grade: ASTM Type E-1 / 18.2 MOhm-cm at 25 deg C

ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: Calcium gluconate gel (2.5% USP grade) must be physically positioned within 1.5 meters of the workstation with valid unexpired lot. Upon skin contact, immediately flush with emergency eyewash/drench shower for 2 minutes, then massage calcium gluconate gel continuously into affected tissue using clean gloved hands until medical personnel arrive. In case of ocular exposure, flush with isotonic sterile saline or 1% calcium gluconate solution for minimum 15 minutes; seek emergency medical intervention immediately.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Operation restricted to a dedicated polypropylene wet bench with face velocity maintained at 0.50 +/- 0.05 m/s (100 FPM) across the active sash opening. The splash-shield rig must interface with downstream acid-scrubber exhaust drawing negative pressure (-25 Pa relative to cleanroom).
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Spent dilute HF must be decanted into dedicated fluoropolymer drain plumbed to an automated calcium hydroxide / calcium chloride precipitation neutralization tank (CaF2 precipitation at pH 8.5 - 9.2). Under no circumstances dispose of via general drain or mix with organic solvents.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Hydrophilic SC-2 metallic decontamination post-clean chemical oxide (thickness 0.8 - 1.2 nm, DI water contact angle < 10 degrees).
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: 100% Hydrophobic hydrogen-terminated bare silicon Si(100):H (native oxide < 0.1 nm, DI water contact angle > 75 degrees).
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Exceeding Q-time results in parasitic uncontrolled ambient regrowth of non-stoichiometric native oxide (SiOx) and airborne volatile organic compound (VOC) condensation, causing gate dielectric thickness non-uniformity (> 5% deviation on 3.5 nm target), increased interface trap density (Dit > 5e11 eV-1 cm-2), and premature Fowler-Nordheim oxide breakdown.

expected_result.summary: Completed physical fabrication, CNC dimensional validation, and trace-metal extraction qualification of a custom virgin PTFE/PVDF manual wafer immersion dipper and transparent PFA splash-shield containment rig, certified to safely execute controlled 1:50 DHF etch dips for 100mm wafers prior to 3.5 nm dry gate oxidation.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Wafer immersion dipper vertical rail runout and perpendicularity deviation along 150mm stroke
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Dial indicator scan along guide rail against precision granite surface plate

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Chemical native oxide clearance verification via DI water contact angle on post-etch Si(100) wafer
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Automated optical sessile drop goniometer 5-point wafer mapping

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Cumulative transition metal extractable mass concentration leached from jig into 1:50 DHF bath
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: High-resolution ICP-MS analysis of 24h acid soak solution

expected_result.signoff_criteria: Sign-off requires zero detected mechanical clearance binding over 50 consecutive dry test strokes, clean ICP-MS certificate proving cumulative metallic contaminants <= 0.50 ppb, documented DI water contact angle >= 75 degrees across 5 mapped wafer points after a 60-second 1:50 DHF immersion, and EHS sign-off verifying 100 FPM hood face velocity with calcium gluconate on station.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-FAB180-WET-MET-042`
**Title:** Fixture Mechanical Clearance, Drainage & Hydrophobic De-wetting Verification  
**Hierarchy Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > 180nm Dry Gate Oxide Growth (3.5 nm) > Pre-Oxidation RCA Clean and In-Situ HF Dip Surface Preparation > Dilute HF Native Oxide Etch & RCA-2 (SC-2) Metallic Decontamination Sequence Execution > Dilute HF (1:50) Native Oxide Dip & Hydrophobic Surface Verification > Precision Tooling & Fixturing > Fixture Mechanical Clearance, Drainage & Hydrophobic De-wetting Verification  
**Action Type:** Make / Metrology  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (180 nm / µm tooling scale)

---

### 1. Scope & Objective
This SOP establishes the verification procedure for cassette/carrier fixturing mechanical clearances, fluid drainage pathways, and wafer de-wetting behavior following dilute hydrofluoric acid (DHF 1:50 / BOE prep) native oxide removal on 180nm DRAM wafers prior to 3.5 nm dry gate oxide growth.

```
       +---------------------------------------------+
       |   1. Fixture Mechanical Clearance Check     |
       |      - Feeler gauge wafer slot gaps         |
       +----------------------v----------------------+
       |   2. Chemical Immersion & Drainage Run      |
       |      - Controlled bath withdrawal / runoff  |
       +----------------------v----------------------+
       |   3. Optical Hydrophobic De-wetting Metrol. |
       |      - Sheeting check / Contact angle       |
       +----------------------v----------------------+
       |   4. Safety & Ca-Gluconate Station Audit    |
       |      - First-aid readiness check            |
       +---------------------------------------------+
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Pre-Check Safety & Personal Protective Equipment (PPE):**
   - Don acid-rated apron, heavy-duty neoprene/nitrile gauntlets, and face shield.
   - Verify that Calcium Gluconate Gel (topical antidote for HF exposure) is unexpired, fully stocked, and located directly adjacent to the wet station before processing.

2. **Fixture Mechanical Clearance Inspection:**
   - Mount the PTFE/PFA fluoropolymer carrier fixture onto the automated wet-bench transfer arm.
   - Inspect wafer pocket clearances and support teeth using calibrated feeler gauges. Verify zero wafer pin-binding or mechanical interference during cassette loading/unloading cycles.

3. **Fluid Drainage & Runoff Verification:**
   - Submerge fixture in the DI water / rinse staging tank and simulate vertical lift at controlled withdrawal velocity.
   - Visually and sensorially verify laminar fluid evacuation through bottom drainage slots; confirm no chemical pooling, meniscus entrapment, or dead-zone retention on fixture ribs.

4. **In-Situ Dilute HF Exposure & Surface De-wetting Metrology:**
   - Execute native oxide strip dip in dilute HF (1:50) / buffered fluoropolymer bath at 25°C.
   - Upon vertical extraction, perform immediate optical de-wetting verification: observe transition from hydrophilic sheeting to complete hydrophobic surface beading/de-wetting across the active DRAM silicon area (preparing channel regions: $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$).
   - Measure contact angle on test wafer monitoring spots to verify full native oxide removal before dry gate oxidation.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
Acceptance Criteria Target Verification
Metric                                      Target Value
-----------------------------------------------------------------
Bath Operating Temperature                  25.0 °C
Gate Dielectric Physical Thickness Target   3.5 nm
Silicon Channel Width (Transistor Site)     220.0 nm
Silicon Channel Length (Transistor Site)    180.0 nm
```

| Parameter / Metric | Acceptance Target | Physical Units | Inspection Tool / Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Dilute HF Bath Temperature** | `25.0 ± 0.5` | `°C` | In-tank calibrated PT100 RTD sensor |
| **Gate Dielectric Physical Target** | `3.5` | `nm` | Post-oxidation spectroscopic ellipsometry |
| **Active Transistor Channel Length ($L$)** | `180` | `nm` | In-line CD-SEM verification |
| **Active Transistor Channel Width ($W$)** | `220` | `nm` | In-line CD-SEM verification |
| **Safety Readiness Metric** | Calcium Gluconate Gel present | Boolean (`Pass`/`Fail`) | Direct visual safety interlock log |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Context & Source Citations
- **[180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench]**: Defines access transistor channel dimensions ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$), stacked capacitor layout, and refresh leakage requirements.
- **[Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)]**: Specifies process bath baseline temperature ($25^\circ\text{C}$), bubble elimination protocols in micro-features, and mandatory immediate presence of calcium gluconate gel for hydrofluoric acid safety.
- **[Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering]**: Confirms thermal dry gate oxide target physical thickness of $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ grown at $850^\circ\text{C}-900^\circ\text{C}$ following surface native oxide clearing.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: Station exhaust and DI water loop (18.2 MOhm-cm, particle filter 0.1 um) must interlock prior to wafer boat immersion. Rinse cascade must terminate downstream acid carries before SC-2.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: BOE 6:1 (NH4F:HF) etch rate must be calibrated at 70-80 nm/min at 25°C. SC-1 (5:1:1 H2O:NH4OH:H2O2) must be maintained at 75°C +/- 2°C to eliminate light organics without pitting Si.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Electronic-grade semiconductor reagents (VLSI/MOS grade) must be procured from certified chemical distributors; technical-grade chemicals will induce metallic surface poisoning (Fe, Cu, Ni > 1e10 atoms/cm2).
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 24-32 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: HIGH (Chemical cross-contamination or incomplete dump rinse leaves watermark defects and micro-masking during subsequent etch).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Watermark defect formation during static pull-out from hydrophilic-to-hydrophobic transition.
1. Exhaust face-velocity drop below 0.5 m/s causing acid vapor condensation on cleanroom tooling.
1. Over-etch in BOE undercut exceeding 50 nm, destroying contact via dimensional margins.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-2-1-1-3-01` | **Post-Clean Particle & Metallic Trace Contamination Assay** | Darkfield Laser Surface Particle Scanner (KLA-Tencor / Surfscan) & TXRF Spectrometer | 1. Load unpatterned witness silicon wafer into darkfield laser scatterometer. 2. Scan complete surface for light point defects (LPD) at size bin >= 180 nm. 3. Perform Total Reflection X-Ray Fluorescence (TXRF) for trace Fe, Cu, Ni surface concentrations. | `LPD count (>= 180 nm) < 10 defects/wafer (Pass); Transition metals (Fe, Ni, Cu) < 5e10 atoms/cm2 (Pass).` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-2-1-1-3-02` | **Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1) Step Height & Lateral Undercut Profilometry** | Stylus Profilometer (Veeco Dektak XT) / Atomic Force Microscope (AFM) | 1. Zero stylus force baseline at 3 mg on planar SiO2 field. 2. Scan 200 um profile across etched contact window step at 20 um/s scan speed. 3. Record step height h_step and lateral undercut under resist margin. | `Etch depth matches target +/- 5% (Pass); lateral undercut <= 35 nm (Pass); surface roughness Ra < 0.5 nm (Pass).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Heavy-duty butyl/neoprene gloves (0.7 mm thickness, tested for HF permeation), Full-face polycarbonate splash shield over ANSI Z87.1 safety goggles, Acid-resistant chemical apron with sleeves (PVC/Neoprene), Acid gas vapor cartridge respirator (NIOSH approved for HF/HCl)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: MANDATORY ON-SITE ANTIDOTE: Calcium Gluconate Gel (2.5%). In case of HF skin contact: Flush immediately under emergency drench shower for 2-3 minutes, then vigorously massage Calcium Gluconate Gel into affected skin continuously until emergency medical response arrives. Never apply standard burn creams.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated polypropylene wet bench with vertical laminar exhaust face velocity >= 0.55 m/s. Interlocked with wet acid scrubber.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Segregate fluoride effluent. Neutralize with Calcium Hydroxide (Ca(OH)2) slurry to precipitate insoluble Calcium Fluoride (CaF2). Verify pH 7.0-8.5 before drain discharge.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid (HF)** | `7664-39-3` | VLSI/MOS Electronic Grade (< 1 ppb metals) | `49% conc. or 1:50 DHF` |
| **Ammonium Fluoride (NH4F)** | `12125-01-8` | Electronic Grade | `40% aq (for BOE 6:1 buffer)` |
| **Hydrogen Peroxide (H2O2)** | `7722-84-1` | Electronic Grade (unstabilized) | `30% aq (for SC-1 & SC-2)` |
| **Hydrochloric Acid (HCl)** | `7647-01-0` | Electronic Grade | `37% aq (for SC-2 clean)` |
| **Ammonium Hydroxide (NH4OH)** | `1336-21-6` | Electronic Grade | `29% aq (for SC-1 clean)` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30.0 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4.0 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic with native chemical oxide (Tox ~1.0 nm) and organic particulates.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophobic H-terminated bare silicon (water contact angle > 75°), zero watermarks, Tox < 0.2 nm.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Native SiO2 spontaneously regrows in ambient air at ~0.1 nm/hr, degrading interface state density Dit and causing uncontrolled threshold voltage shift in downstream gate oxidation.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completion of Fixture Mechanical Clearance, Drainage & Hydrophobic De-wetting Verification: Chemical cleaning and surface preparation verified with zero watermark defects, bare hydrophobic hydrogen-terminated silicon, and calibrated oxide etch rate.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `Surface_particle_laser_scan_Surfscan.pdf`
- [ ] `Sessile_drop_contact_angle_measurement.png`
- [ ] `DHF_BOE_calibrated_etch_rate_sheet.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Post-DHF bare silicon water contact angle** | `>= 75.0 deg` | +/- 5.0 deg | Automated Sessile Drop Goniometer (DI water droplet) |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Surface particulate defect density (> 0.1 um)** | `< 15 particles/wafer` | Max acceptable particle count on 100mm wafer | Darkfield Laser Surface Inspection (Surfscan) |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Surface metallic impurity concentration (Fe, Ni, Cu)** | `< 1.0e10 atoms/cm²` | Max allowable contamination | Total Reflection X-Ray Fluorescence (TXRF) |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Wafer surface exhibits 100% uniform dewetting / hydrophobicity with zero visible drying marks under bright light; residual native oxide Tox < 0.2 nm confirmed by spectroscopic ellipsometry.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## SOP-WET-180-042: Process Parameter Benchmarking for Dilute HF (1:50) Native Oxide Dip & Hydrophobic Surface Verification

### 1. Process Overview & Workflow

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│   Post-RCA1 Wafer     │
│  (Hydrated Native     │
│      SiO2 Film)       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│  Dilute HF (1:50)     │
│   Native Oxide Dip    │
│    (15 s - 30 s)      │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│ Quick Dump Rinse (QDR)│
│  18.2 MOhm·cm DI H2O  │
│        (3 min)        │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│ Hydrophobic Surface & │
│ Dewetting Inspection  │
│  (Complete Sheeting)  │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│ Transfer to RCA-2 /   │
│  Dry Gate Oxidation   │
│       (3.5 nm)        │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Chemical Bath Preparation (Dilute HF 1:50)**:
   - Prepare a 1:50 volumetric solution by mixing 1 part concentrated Hydrofluoric Acid (49% HF) with 50 parts ultra-pure Deionized (DI) Water ($18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$).
   - Maintain wet-bench ambient bath temperature at $25^\circ\text{C} \pm 1^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Ensure safety readiness: confirm the immediate availability of calcium gluconate gel ($2.5\%$) and inspect personal protective equipment (heavy Neoprene/PVDF gloves, face shield, and chemical apron).

2. **Native Oxide Etch Immersion**:
   - Transfer wafers from the post-RCA-1 rinse into the 1:50 Dilute HF immersion tank.
   - Execute the dip for **$15\text{ to }30\text{ seconds}$** (native oxide requires $10\text{ to }15\text{ seconds}$ to clear under standard oxide etch conditions).
   - Agitate mildly to ensure uniform acid contact across all active silicon areas and trench features without bubble entrapment.

3. **Intermediate Quench & Dump Rinse**:
   - Immediately transfer wafer cassette into the Quick Dump Rinse (QDR) tank filled with ultra-pure DI water ($18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$).
   - Perform cascade dump rinse for **$3\text{ minutes}$** to completely quench the reaction and remove residual fluoride ions ($F^-$).

4. **Hydrophobic Surface Verification & Drying**:
   - Withdraw the wafer slowly from the DI rinse. Verify immediate surface dewetting: complete water sheeting off the bare silicon surface indicates full hydrogen termination (transition from hydrophilic $\text{Si-OH}$ to hydrophobic $\text{Si-H}$).
   - Perform high-purity Nitrogen ($\text{N}_2$) blow-dry immediately to prevent water mark formation prior to the subsequent RCA-2 (SC-2) metallic clean or $3.5\text{ nm}$ dry gate oxidation.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Range | Measurement Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Residual Native Oxide Thickness** | $0.0\text{ nm}$ | $\le 0.1\text{ nm}$ ($1\text{ \AA}$) | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry |
| **Surface Hydrophobic Dewetting / Contact Angle** | $> 75^\circ$ | $\ge 70^\circ$ (Rapid, uniform water bead sheeting) | Optical Goniometry / Automated Contact Angle Tool |
| **Bath Immersion Residence Time** | $20\text{ s}$ | $15\text{ s} - 30\text{ s}$ | Automated Wet Bench Robotic Immersion Timer |
| **Rinse Resistivity Recovery** | $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ | $\ge 18.0\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ | In-Line QDR Conductivity/Resistivity Probe |

---

### 4. Literature References & Citations

1. **Standard RCA-1 and RCA-2 Silicon Wafer Cleaning Procedure**:
   - Dilute HF formulation: *1:50 $\text{HF}:\text{H}_2\text{O}$ dip for 15–30 seconds to strip native oxide; surface transitions from hydrophilic to hydrophobic*.
   - Intermediate rinse: *Dump rinse with $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ deionized water for 3 minutes*.
   - Final dry: *High-purity $\text{N}_2$ blow-dry*.
2. **Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1 & 7:1) Silicon Dioxide Wet Etch Rates**:
   - Native oxide clearance window: *Native oxide etched in 10 to 15 seconds*.
   - Safety protocol: *HF penetrates skin deeply and binds calcium; calcium gluconate gel must be present at all times*.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Dilute HF (1:50) strip must seamlessly interface between the upstream SC-1 organic strip and downstream high-temperature dry gate oxidation (3.5 nm). While achieving complete native SiO2 removal (1.0-1.5 nm) is trivial, bath loading effects and bath lifetime directly impact run-to-run uniformity. Furthermore, complete hydrogen passivation leaves an ultra-reactive bare Si(100) surface susceptible to ambient airborne molecular contamination (AMCs, volatile siloxanes, and hydrocarbons) during wafer transfer, necessitating tightly synchronized automated dry transfer to the furnace loadlock.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 1:50 volumetric dilution (approx. 1.0 wt% HF), thermal SiO2 etches at ~2.0-2.5 nm/min while low-density native oxide etches within 15-25 seconds. For a 3.5 nm gate dielectric, excessive over-etching in unbuffered DHF causes localized micro-roughening via uneven fluoride attack at step edges and defect sites, degrading Si/SiO2 interface state density (Dit) and Fowler-Nordheim breakdown voltage. Surface hydrogen termination (Si-H, Si-H2) must yield a DI water static contact angle >= 75 degrees without pitting.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Electronic-grade SEMI C79 Tier 4 / Grade 1 HF (49%) and UPW (ultra-pure water, 18.2 MOhm-cm, TOC < 1 ppb) are vital. Trace ionic metals (specifically Cu2+, Fe3+, and noble metals like Au/Ag) in unbuffered DHF will spontaneously plate onto bare silicon via open-circuit electrochemical displacement, forming localized gate leakage pinholes. Strict raw chemical assay certification and fluoropolymer (PTFE/PFA) bath wetted parts are non-negotiable for 180nm DRAM yield.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Benchmarking 1:50 DHF immersion times (15s to 60s) directly controls wet bench throughput and takt time. The strict queue time (Q-time) window of <= 30 minutes from HF tank exit/spin-dry to furnace vacuum pumpdown imposes strict operational discipline on pilot lot scheduling. In-line contact angle verification must be non-destructive or run on dedicated dummy/witness wafers to prevent DI water droplet residue from contaminating production gate areas.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Electrochemical noble/transition metal deposition (Cu, Fe, Ni) from contaminated HF bath onto bare silicon, creating high-leakage pathways through the 3.5 nm dry gate oxide.
1. Excessive over-etch causing atomic-scale surface facet etching and micro-roughness (RMS > 0.15 nm), degrading gate dielectric breakdown reliability (Qbd/TDDB).
1. Native oxide re-growth and AMC physisorption due to Q-time breach (> 30 min in cleanroom ambient air), inducing sub-stoichiometric interfacial SiOx and threshold voltage shifts in the DRAM transfer transistors.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

Immerse wafer coupon split groups into 1:50 DHF bath for 15s, 30s, 45s, and 60s under gentle N2 bubbler agitation. 2. Overflow rinse in UPW dump rinser to resistivity > 17.5 MOhm-cm (approx 2 minutes). 3. Spin rinse dry under heated N2 (0.2 um filtered). 4. Within 5 minutes post-dry, deposit 2.0 uL UPW droplet at 5 standard radial points across wafer surface (Center, +/- R/2, +/- edge 5mm exclusion). 5. Record baseline Young-Laplace static contact angle profile. | `Static DI water contact angle must be >= 75.0 degrees across all 5 test points for immersion times between 30s and 45s, confirming uniform hydrophobic Si-H surface termination. Incomplete etching (< 70 degrees) or hydrophilic pinning (< 50 degrees) constitutes failure.` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-2-1-2-02` | **Post-Etch Atomic Surface Roughness and Residual Oxide Ellipsometric Verification** | Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM, tapping mode, 1 um x 1 um scan area) and Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (SE, 190-830 nm wavelength range). | 1. Mount wafer on vacuum chuck of Spectroscopic Ellipsometer; perform 9-point radial map measuring residual oxide thickness (Si/SiO2 Cauchy/Tauc-Lorentz model). 2. Transfer immediately to AFM chamber under N2 purge. 3. Acquire high-resolution surface topology scans (512x512 lines, scan speed 0.8 Hz) at center and wafer edge. 4. Extract root-mean-square roughness (Rq / RMS) and peak-to-valley roughness (Rmax). | `Residual equivalent oxide thickness must be <= 0.15 nm (effectively zero within SE optical model noise). AFM surface roughness RMS must remain <= 0.12 nm (1.2 Angstroms) across all sites, verifying zero HF-induced micro-pitting.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Full-face splash shield (ANSI Z87.1) over chemical splash goggles, Neoprene/Butyl blend chemical-resistant heavy apron and arm gauntlets, Double-gloved: inner disposable nitrile (4 mil), outer heavy-duty butyl/Viton gloves (28 mil, ASTM F739 tested), Steel-toe chemical boots with acid-resistant shoe covers
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Calcium Gluconate Gel (2.5% USP) must be stored adjacent to wet bench and checked for active shelf-life daily. In case of skin exposure: Immediately flush affected area with copious emergency water for 2-3 minutes; continuously massage 2.5% calcium gluconate gel into skin wearing fresh gloves until severe pain subsides. Seek immediate advanced emergency medical care for systemic calcium/magnesium toxicity monitoring.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous dedicated polypropylene acid exhaust wet bench lip scavenge with face velocity 100-120 LFPM (0.5-0.6 m/s) monitored by differential pressure magnehelic gauge with interlocked audible/visual alarm. Effluent ducted to central acid scrubber.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Continuous drain to Industrial Waste Treatment (IWT) Dedicated Fluoride Waste Collection System. Neutralized with hydrated lime / calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)2) to precipitate insoluble calcium fluoride (CaF2) sludge prior to municipal discharge; never discharge into general acid-waste neutralization (AWN) stream.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid** | `7664-39-3` | SEMI Tier 4 / Electronic Grade | `49 wt% (source chemical)` |
| **Ultra-Pure Water (Diluent)** | `7732-18-5` | 18.2 MOhm-cm, TOC < 1 ppb | `Balance (approx 98 wt% in 1:50 bath)` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic chemical oxide (0.8-1.5 nm) post-SC-1/SC-2 clean, terminating in polar silanol (Si-OH) groups with contact angle < 10 degrees.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Atomically flat, fully hydrogen-passivated (Si-H / Si-H2) hydrophobic surface, zero native oxide (< 0.15 nm SE equivalent), contact angle >= 75 degrees.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Ambient humidity induces spontaneous native oxide re-oxidation (0.2-0.5 nm within 60 min), airborne hydrocarbon adsorption, and trace airborne amine deposition, causing gate oxide thickness drift (> 0.2 nm error on 3.5 nm target), degraded interface trap density (Dit > 2e10 cm-2 eV-1), and premature gate dielectric punchthrough.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Process parameter window successfully benchmarked for 1:50 DHF native oxide strip, establishing a robust operating duration of 30-45 seconds at 22 deg C that yields complete SiO2 removal, stable hydrogen passivation (> 75 deg water contact angle), pristine surface microroughness (RMS <= 0.12 nm), and zero ionic contamination, qualified for immediate transfer to 3.5 nm dry gate oxidation.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `DHF_1_50_Etch_Rate_and_Contact_Angle_Matrix.csv`
- [ ] `Post_Dip_AFM_Surface_Roughness_Report.tiff`
- [ ] `Process_Qualification_DHF_Native_Oxide_Benchmarking.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| `ASSERT-02` | **Residual native silicon dioxide equivalent film thickness** | `0.05` | <= 0.15 nm absolute maximum | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry 9-point radial map using Cauchy Si/SiO2 optical dispersion model |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Surface micro-roughness (RMS / Rq) post-30s etch dip** | `0.09` | <= 0.12 nm (1.2 Angstroms) | AFM tapping-mode topography scan over 1.0 um x 1.0 um area at center and edge zones |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Demonstration of 3 consecutive qualifying 200mm wafer runs achieving contact angle >= 75 deg, residual oxide <= 0.15 nm, and AFM RMS <= 0.12 nm at nominal 35s dip duration, alongside verification of active 2.5% calcium gluconate gel on site and unbreached Q-time (< 30 min) to dry oxidation tube furnace.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Title: Dilute HF (1:50) Chemical Bath Preparation & Etch Bath Temperature Stabilization
**Context Path**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > 180nm Dry Gate Oxide Growth (3.5 nm) > Pre-Oxidation RCA Clean and In-Situ HF Dip Surface Preparation > Dilute HF Native Oxide Etch & RCA-2 (SC-2) Metallic Decontamination Sequence Execution > Dilute HF (1:50) Native Oxide Dip & Hydrophobic Surface Verification > Process Parameter Benchmarking for Dilute HF (1:50) Native Oxide Dip & Hydrophobic Surface Verification > Dilute HF (1:50) Chemical Bath Preparation & Etch Bath Temperature Stabilization  
**Technology Generation**: Gen 2 (180 nm / 0.18 µm)  
**Action Type**: Make  

---

### 1. Safety & PPE Protocols
> [!CAUTION]
> **Hydrofluoric Acid Hazard**: HF penetrates biological tissue rapidly and complexes systemic calcium ions. Calcium gluconate 2.5% antidote gel must be stationed directly at the chemical bench within arm's reach. Full acid PPE required: heavy neoprene gloves, face shield, chemical-resistant apron, and dedicated HF-rated wet-bench exhaust hoods.

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

```
[Step 1: Bath Purge & DIW Charge]
  │── Verify clean PTFE/PVDF tank integrity.
  └── Dispense 50 parts semiconductor-grade 18.2 MΩ·cm Deionized Water (DIW).
         ▼
[Step 2: Dilute HF Acid Dispensing (1:50 Ratio)]
  │── Slowly add 1 part concentrated 49% Hydrofluoric Acid (HF) into DIW ("Acid into Water").
  └── Maintain recirculating magnetic drive pump / PTFE overflow filtration.
         ▼
[Step 3: Bath Thermal Stabilization & Control]
  │── Engage circulating PFA inline immersion heat exchanger / chiller loop.
  └── Stabilize bath setpoint at nominal room temperature (25°C).
         ▼
[Step 4: Operational Readiness Verification]
  └── Perform pre-run coupon check (15–30 s dip) ensuring native oxide clearance & hydrophobicity.
```

1. **Vessel Inspection and Initial DI Water Charge**:
   - Ensure the dedicated PVDF/PTFE wet-bench bath vessel is purged and clean.
   - Dispense **50 volumetric parts** of high-purity deionized water (resistivity: **18.2 MΩ·cm**) into the tank. *Always add acid to water, never water to acid.*

2. **Chemical Metering and Addition**:
   - Accurately measure **1 volumetric part** of cleanroom electronic-grade **49% HF (Hydrofluoric Acid)**.
   - Slowly meter the 1 part 49% HF into the 50 parts DIW under continuous laminar exhaust to formulate the **1:50 HF:H₂O** dilution.

3. **Recirculation & Thermal Stabilization**:
   - Engage PTFE-encapsulated recirculation pump and temperature-control bath chiller/heater unit.
   - Circulate the bath until uniform mixing is achieved and the bath temperature stabilizes at **25°C**.
   - Confirm bath temperature uniformity across weir overflow zones using a calibrated PFA-sheathed RTD sensor.

4. **Batch Ready Sign-Off**:
   - Verify bath is ready for downstream wafer carrier insertion (targeting native oxide removal duration of **15–30 seconds** prior to SC-2 sequence).

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Range | Measurement Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **DI Water Feed Resistivity** | 18.2 MΩ·cm | ≥ 18.2 MΩ·cm | Inline resistivity sensor at bath inlet |
| **Dilution Ratio (HF : DI H₂O)** | 1 : 50 | 1:50 (49% HF : 18.2 MΩ·cm H₂O) | Automated chemical metering pump / titrator |
| **Bath Etch Temperature** | 25°C | ± 0.5°C | Inline PFA-jacketed RTD immersion probe |
| **Process Native Oxide Dip Window** | 15–30 s | 15 s – 30 s | Automated wet-bench recipe timer |

---

### 4. Verified Literature References
- **Standard RCA-1 and RCA-2 Silicon Wafer Cleaning Procedure**:
  - Specified 18.2 MΩ·cm deionized water standard.
  - Specified 1:50 HF:H₂O dip ratio for 15–30 seconds to strip native oxide and transition wafer surfaces from hydrophilic to hydrophobic.
- **Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)**:
  - Specified 49% HF stock concentration benchmark and nominal room-temperature baseline of 25°C for oxide etch stability.
  - Mandated safety rule: Hydrofluoric acid calcium-binding precautions and mandatory availability of calcium gluconate gel.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Maintaining a precise 1:50 dilution (approx. 0.98 wt% HF from 49% stock) requires strict mass- or calibrated metering-based dispensing into high-purity PVDF/PFA bath tanks. Failure to integrate closed-loop recirculation (0.1 um PFA filtration) creates thermal stratification and local concentration gradients, inducing wafer-to-wafer native oxide etch non-uniformity across the lot prior to the 3.5 nm dry gate oxidation step.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 1:50 DHF, the oxide etch rate has a steep Arrhenius temperature dependence (~1.5 to 2.0 %/°C around 22.0°C). Any bath temperature drift beyond ±0.5°C will alter the native oxide (0.8–1.2 nm) strip duration and subsequent hydrogen-terminated (Si-H) passivation density, directly degrading the Deal-Grove initial regime kinetics during the subsequent 3.5 nm gate oxide thermal growth.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Electronic-grade HF (SEMI Grade 4/5) and ultra-pure water (UPW 18.2 MOhm·cm, TOC < 1 ppb) must be guaranteed. Using lower grades introduces trace heavy metals (Fe, Cu, Ni > 0.1 ppb) which plate onto bare Si during native oxide stripping, inducing gate oxide integrity (GOI) breakdown and premature dielectric wearout in the 180nm DRAM cell transistors.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Because bath life is constrained by fluoride evaporation and ambient trace organics absorption, chemical bath lifetime must be strictly time-boxed (max bath idle lifetime 8 hours) with real-time temperature/conductivity interlocks before lot dispatch, preventing costly lot re-cleans or gate re-oxidation cycles.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal stratification in the static chemical tank leading to non-uniform native oxide clearance across 200mm wafers, producing micro-roughness (RMS > 0.15 nm) and pinholes in the 3.5 nm gate dielectric.
1. Trace cationic metal plating (Fe/Cu) from uncertified HF chemical lot or degraded PFA heating coils onto bare silicon, resulting in excessive gate leakage current (Jg > 1e-7 A/cm2 at Vdd = 1.8V).
1. Localized bubble entrapment or unvented degassing during DHF bath fill causing localized residual oxide islands that disrupt epitaxial gate interface alignment.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-2-1-2-1-01` | **DHF 1:50 Bath Thermal Uniformity & Closed-Loop Temperature Stability Verification** | Calibrated 4-point PFA-encapsulated RTD Pt100 array with multi-channel datalogger (±0.05°C accuracy) and recirculating PFA bath heater/chiller unit. | 1. Position four RTD sensors at the four tank corners (5 cm depth) and one at the center bath core. 2. Enable temperature control setpoint at 22.0°C. 3. Monitor and log temperature readings across all 5 points continuously for 60 minutes after reaching setpoint at 10-second sampling intervals. 4. Calculate spatial delta (T_max - T_min) and temporal drift over the full 60-minute duration. | `Spatial bath uniformity delta <= 0.30°C across all probes and maximum temporal drift <= ±0.20°C from 22.00°C over 60 minutes continuous monitoring.` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-2-1-2-1-02` | **DHF 1:50 Thermal Oxide Etch Rate & Concentration Uniformity Benchmark** | Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (wavelength range 240–800 nm, 49-point wafer mapping, 3mm edge exclusion). | 1. Submerge thermal oxide monitor wafer into the 1:50 DHF bath for precisely 120.0 seconds using an automated pneumatic carrier. 2. Immediately transfer to dump rinser with UPW (rinse until resistivity > 16 MOhm·cm) and spin-rinse dry under heated N2. 3. Perform 49-point spectroscopic ellipsometry to measure remaining SiO2 thickness. 4. Compute mean etch rate (nm/min) and within-wafer non-uniformity (1-sigma %). | `Mean etch rate of thermal SiO2 must be 2.30 ± 0.25 nm/min (23.0 ± 2.5 A/min) at 22.0°C; 49-point within-wafer thickness etch uniformity (1-sigma) <= 1.5%.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Heavy-duty chemical-resistant neoprene/butyl rubber gloves over inner nitrile gloves, Full-face polycarbonate shield combined with ANSI Z87.1 chemical splash goggles, Acid-resistant PVDF/PTFE/neoprene chemical apron with extended sleeve cuffs, Steel-toe chemical safety boots with neoprene acid-resistant shoe covers
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Immediately flush exposed area with copious clean water for exactly 2 minutes, then aggressively massage Calcium Gluconate Gel (2.5% USP) into affected skin wearing clean gloves; reapply every 10 minutes until medical arrival. For eye exposure, continuously irrigate with sterile 1.0% calcium gluconate eye wash solution or saline for at least 15 minutes. nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
**Title:** Benchmarking Native Oxide Stripping Rate Across Timed Immersion Matrix (10s–45s)  
**Process Branch:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > 180nm Dry Gate Oxide Growth (3.5 nm) > Pre-Oxidation RCA Clean and In-Situ HF Dip Surface Preparation > Dilute HF Native Oxide Etch & RCA-2 (SC-2) Metallic Decontamination Sequence Execution  
**Technology Generation:** Gen 2 (180nm)  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### Process Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Wafer Prep Post SC-1  │
│         Rinse          │
└───────────┬────────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   1:50 HF Immersion    │
│     Matrix 10s-45s     │
└───────────┬────────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Dump Rinse 18.2     │
│    MOhm-cm DI Water    │
└───────────┬────────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│     High-Purity N2     │
│        Blow-Dry        │
└───────────┬────────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│     Ellipsometry &     │
│      Hydrophobic       │
│       Assessment       │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Timed Immersion Split Matrix

```text
               Immersion Matrix Exposure Time (s)       
         ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │█████████████████████████████████████████████│
45s Split┤█████████████████████████████████████████████│
         │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓               │
30s Split┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓               │
15s Split┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                             │
         │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                             │
10s Split┤░░░░░░░░░░░                                  │
         │░░░░░░░░░░░                                  │
         └┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬┘
         0.0       11.2       22.5       33.8      45.0 
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Safety & Wet Bench Readiness:**
   - Verify that Calcium Gluconate gel is present and accessible at the wet bench prior to handling Hydrofluoric Acid (HF).
   - Ensure the chemical bath contains a 1:50 volume dilution of $49\%\text{ HF}:\text{H}_2\text{O}$ at ambient cleanroom conditions ($25^\circ\text{C}$).

2. **Pre-Etch Native Oxide Thickness Baseline:**
   - Measure starting native oxide thickness across pre-cleaned 180nm monitor silicon wafers (post-SC-1 and intermediate dump rinse) via spectroscopic ellipsometry.

3. **Timed Immersion Matrix Execution:**
   - Submerge wafer coupons/lots into the 1:50 $\text{HF}:\text{H}_2\text{O}$ bath across experimental duration splits:
     - **Split A:** $10\text{ s}$
     - **Split B:** $15\text{ s}$ (nominal lower process window)
     - **Split C:** $30\text{ s}$ (nominal upper process window)
     - **Split D:** $45\text{ s}$ (over-etch margin)
   - Agitate gently to prevent localized stagnant boundary depletion.

4. **Quench & DI Water Dump Rinse:**
   - Immediately transfer wafers within $\le 2\text{ s}$ transfer latency into the dump rinse tank.
   - Execute dump rinse cycling with high-purity $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ deionized water for $3\text{ minutes}$.

5. **Drying & Hydrophobic Surface Verification:**
   - Dry wafers using high-purity filtered $\text{N}_2$ blow-dry until moisture is completely eliminated.
   - Inspect surface dewetting characteristics; confirm transition from hydrophilic to hydrophobic behavior (complete water sheeting beading/repulsion indicating full removal of oxide).

6. **Post-Etch Metrology & Rate Calculation:**
   - Re-measure residual oxide thickness via spectroscopic ellipsometry to determine the precise strip rate ($\text{nm/s}$ or $\text{\AA/s}$) and establish the minimum clearance duration before subsequent SC-2 metallic decontamination or gate oxidation.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

| Parameter | Target Metric / Tolerance | Physical Unit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Dilute HF Etch Bath Ratio** | $1:50 \pm 1\%$ | Volumetric ratio ($\text{HF}:\text{H}_2\text{O}$) |
| **Immersion Process Window** | $15\text{ to }30$ (within matrix range $10\text{ to }45$) | $\text{s}$ (seconds) |
| **Dump Rinse Deionized Water Resistivity** | $\ge 18.2$ | $\text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ |
| **Dump Rinse Duration** | $3.0 \pm 0.1$ | $\text{min}$ (minutes) |
| **Surface Wetting State Transition** | Hydrophilic $\rightarrow$ Fully Hydrophobic (zero water sheeting retention) | Qualitative / Contact Angle State |

---

### 3. Context Citations

- **Source: Standard RCA-1 and RCA-2 Silicon Wafer Cleaning Procedure**
  - Dilute HF formulation: *1:50 HF:$\text{H}_2\text{O}$ dip*.
  - Standard baseline immersion window: *15–30 seconds to strip native oxide; surface transitions from hydrophilic to hydrophobic*.
  - Rinse specifications: *Dump rinse with 18.2 MOhm-cm deionized water for 3 minutes*.
  - Drying specification: *Nitrogen ($\text{N}_2$) blow-dry with high-purity*.
- **Source: Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)**
  - Safety protocol: *Hydrofluoric acid penetrates skin and binds calcium; calcium gluconate gel must be present at all times*.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The timed immersion matrix (10s to 45s) must couple tightly with the subsequent RCA-2 (SC-2) and 3.5 nm dry gate oxidation modules. Incomplete oxide stripping leaves non-uniform chemical oxide patches that cause catastrophic localized gate dielectric breakdown and threshold voltage variations across the DRAM array, whereas over-etching beyond 35s in unbuffered dilute HF exposes bare Si to localized micro-pitting and surface roughening (RMS > 0.2 nm), severely degrading electron inversion layer mobility and gate oxide charge-to-breakdown (Qbd).
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 1:50 HF:UPW dilution (~1.0 wt% HF at 22°C), the etch rate of chemical/native silicon dioxide is nominally 2.0 to 3.5 nm/min (~0.3 to 0.6 Å/s), while native oxide typically measures 0.8 to 1.5 nm. Transition to a complete hydrogen-terminated Si(100)-1x1 dihydride/monohydride hydrophobic surface occurs around 20-25s. Extending immersion to 45s risks fluorine/hydroxyl-induced surface pitting and metallic micro-clustering if trace noble metals (Cu, Au) are present in the HF bath without complexing agents.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Electronic-grade HF (SEMI Grade 4/5, ppb-level metallic impurities) and 18.2 MOhm-cm point-of-use UPW with dissolved oxygen < 15 ppb must be maintained. Fluctuating local supply chains in VN for electronic-grade hydrofluoric acid could introduce part-per-billion copper or iron contamination, resulting in spontaneous galvanic displacement plating onto the bare silicon during prolonged 45s dips.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Benchmarking must establish a repeatable, stable process window between 20s and 30s that guarantees a hydrophobic dewetting endpoint without throttling wet bench throughput. Clear go/no-go contact angle telemetry must be captured directly into the open-source DRAM manufacturing execution record prior to gate oxidation furnace batch dispatch.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Incomplete native oxide removal (<20s) leading to interfacial traps (Dit > 1e11 eV-1 cm-2) and non-uniform EOT in 3.5 nm gate oxide.
1. Excessive immersion (>40s) inducing atomic-scale silicon surface micro-roughening (RMS > 0.25 nm) and galvanic metal precipitation from bath trace contaminants.
1. Bath exhaustion and non-uniform stagnant boundary layer formation during static immersion without controlled agitation or recirculation.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-2-1-2-2-01` | **Native Oxide Thickness vs. Immersion Time Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Matrix** | Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (J.A. Woollam M-2000 or equivalent, spectral range 245-1000 nm, 70-degree incident angle) using standard Cauchy/SiO2-on-Si optical dispersion model. | 1. Divide test coupon/wafer matrix into timed splits: 10s, 15s, 20s, 25s, 30s, 35s, 40s, 45s immersion. 2. Submerge into 1:50 DHF bath with gentle mechanical oscillation (10 mm stroke, 1 Hz). 3. Immediately transfer to continuous overflow UPW cascade rinse for 180s until effluent resistivity reaches 17.5 MOhm-cm. 4. Surface dry via spin-rinse-dryer with filtered hot N2. 5. Perform 9-point spectroscopic ellipsometry within 5 minutes of drying. | `Residual oxide thickness <= 0.15 nm (optical zero/monolayer sub-oxide threshold) achieved uniformly at immersion duration >= 22s and <= 30s, with thickness non-uniformity (1-sigma) < 5.0% across the 9-point map.` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-2-1-2-2-02` | **Post-Strip Surface Passivation and Hydrophobic Dewetting Contact Angle Benchmark** | Automated Optical Goniometer / Sessile Drop Contact Angle Analyzer (Drop shape analysis with 2.0 uL de-aerated UPW droplet). | 1. Mount wafer coupon on goniometer stage within 3 minutes of N2 drying. 2. Dispense automated 2.0 uL droplet of 18.2 MOhm-cm UPW at center, 25mm, 50mm, and 70mm radial positions. 3. Capture droplet profile at 50 fps over 5 seconds. 4. Fit droplet contour using Young-Laplace equation to determine static water contact angle (WCA) at left and right baselines. | `Hydrophobic passivation confirmed with Water Contact Angle (WCA) >= 75.0 degrees across all radial points for immersion times between 20s and 35s (hydrophilic native oxide baseline is < 15.0 degrees).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Heavy-duty Neoprene/Butyl rubber chemical-resistant gauntlet gloves over double nitrile gloves, Full-face polycarbonate chemical splash shield, Acid-resistant PTFE/Neoprene chemical apron with integrated sleeves, Closed-toe acid-resistant safety boots, Chemical splash goggles meeting ANSI Z87.1 D3 rating
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Calcium Gluconate Gel (2.5% USP) must be stored inside an unexpired first-aid station mounted directly on the wet bench. In case of skin exposure: Immediately flush affected area with copiously flowing water for minimum 2 minutes, then generously massage 2.5% calcium gluconate gel continuously into skin until medical help arrives. In case of eye contact: Irrigate eyes continuously for 15 minutes with isotonic saline or eyewash, seek immediate emergency medical care. Oxygen resuscitation apparatus must be accessible.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated polypropylene wet bench with lip exhaust and continuous laminar face velocity maintained at 0.5 +/- 0.1 m/s (100 FPM). Wet bench exhaust linked directly to continuous caustic gas scrubber ductwork with differential pressure interlock alarms.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: HF effluent must bypass organic solvent drains and route strictly to an Acid Waste Neutralization (AWN) system utilizing calcium hydroxide (slaked lime, Ca(OH)2) precipitation to form insoluble Calcium Fluoride (CaF2) cake, ensuring fluoride discharge concentration remains < 10 ppm prior to municipal outflow.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid (Dilute aqueous solution)** | `7664-39-3` | SEMI Grade 4 / VLSI Grade | `0.98% - 1.02% wt (1:50 volumetric dilution from 49% HF)` |
| **Deionized Ultra-Pure Water (UPW)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM D5127 Type E-1 (18.2 MOhm-cm) | `99.0% wt` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `20 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic chemically oxidized Si surface following SC-1 clean, water-sheeting, native chemical oxide thickness 1.0 - 1.4 nm.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Atomically smooth, fully hydrogen-terminated Si(100) hydrophobic surface (water contact angle >= 75 deg, residual oxide <= 0.15 nm).
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Spontaneous atmospheric re-oxidation in cleanroom air regenerating uncontrolled native sub-oxide (SiOx), adsorbing airborne airborne organic hydrocarbons (VOCs), and nullifying gate oxide pre-clean kinetics.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completed empirical matrix establishing the native oxide etch rate, minimum clearance time, and safe over-etch margin for 1:50 DHF on Si(100), defining a validated 25s +/- 3s standard operational recipe with 100% hydrophobic surface clearance and zero pitting for the 180nm 3.5 nm dry gate oxide pre-clean sequence.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `dhf_1_50_native_oxide_timed_etch_matrix.csv`
- [ ] `native_oxide_strip_kinetics_ellipsometry_report.pdf`
- [ ] `surface_passivation_contact_angle_topography.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Residual native oxide thickness post-strip for the 25-second immersion split** | `0.10 nm` | +/- 0.05 nm | 9-point Spectroscopic Ellipsometry across 150mm wafer diameter |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Static water contact angle demonstrating Si-H hydrophobic termination post-strip** | `78.0 deg` | +/- 3.0 deg | Automated Sessile Drop Optical Contact Angle Goniometer (2.0 uL UPW droplet) |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Pre-to-post etch surface roughness change (Delta RMS) to verify no etch-induced pitting** | `0.02 nm` | <= 0.05 nm | Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) 2um x 2um non-contact tapping mode scan |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Complete clearance of native oxide (thickness <= 0.15 nm) verified on >= 3 consecutive pilot wafers at 25s immersion with contact angle >= 75 degrees, AFM RMS roughness <= 0.18 nm, and no observable dewetting defects or pinholes.

critics.supply_chain: Electronic-grade HF (SEMI Grade 4/5, ppb-level metallic impurities) and 18.2 MOhm-cm point-of-use UPW with dissolved oxygen < 15 ppb must be maintained. Fluctuating local supply chains in VN for electronic-grade hydrofluoric acid could introduce part-per-billion copper or iron contamination, resulting in spontaneous galvanic displacement plating onto the bare silicon during prolonged 45s dips.
critics.laya_pm: Benchmarking must establish a repeatable, stable process window between 20s and 30s that guarantees a hydrophobic dewetting endpoint without throttling wet bench throughput. Clear go/no-go contact angle telemetry must be captured directly into the open-source DRAM manufacturing execution record prior to gate oxidation furnace batch dispatch.
critical_failure_modes: Incomplete native oxide removal (<20s) leading to interfacial traps (Dit > 1e11 eV-1 cm-2) and non-uniform EOT in 3.5 nm gate oxide.
Excessive immersion (>40s) inducing atomic-scale silicon surface micro-roughening (RMS > 0.25 nm) and galvanic metal precipitation from bath trace contaminants.
Bath exhaustion and non-uniform stagnant boundary layer formation during static immersion without controlled agitation or recirculation.

testcases.title: Native Oxide Thickness vs. Immersion Time Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Matrix
testcases.instrumentation: Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (J.A. Woollam M-2000 or equivalent, spectral range 245-1000 nm, 70-degree incident angle) using standard Cauchy/SiO2-on-Si optical dispersion model.
testcases.pre_conditions: Prime P-type Si(100) 150mm/200mm pilot wafers subjected to standard SC-1 clean, dump rinse, and controlled baseline native/chemical oxide measurement (target initial thickness: 1.2 +/- 0.2 nm across 9-point radial map). Fresh 1:50 HF:UPW bath equilibrated at 22.0 +/- 0.5°C.
testcases.procedure: 1. Divide test coupon/wafer matrix into timed splits: 10s, 15s, 20s, 25s, 30s, 35s, 40s, 45s immersion. 2. Submerge into 1:50 DHF bath with gentle mechanical oscillation (10 mm stroke, 1 Hz). 3. Immediately transfer to continuous overflow UPW cascade rinse for 180s until effluent resistivity reaches 17.5 MOhm-cm. 4. Surface dry via spin-rinse-dryer with filtered hot N2. 5. Perform 9-point spectroscopic ellipsometry within 5 minutes of drying.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Residual oxide thickness <= 0.15 nm (optical zero/monolayer sub-oxide threshold) achieved uniformly at immersion duration >= 22s and <= 30s, with thickness non-uniformity (1-sigma) < 5.0% across the 9-point map.

testcases.title: Post-Strip Surface Passivation and Hydrophobic Dewetting Contact Angle Benchmark
testcases.instrumentation: Automated Optical Goniometer / Sessile Drop Contact Angle Analyzer (Drop shape analysis with 2.0 uL de-aerated UPW droplet).
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafers cleared through the timed HF immersion matrix (10s to 45s) and N2 dried; ambient cleanroom RH maintained at 45 +/- 5% and temperature at 21 +/- 1°C.
testcases.procedure: 1. Mount wafer coupon on goniometer stage within 3 minutes of N2 drying. 2. Dispense automated 2.0 uL droplet of 18.2 MOhm-cm UPW at center, 25mm, 50mm, and 70mm radial positions. 3. Capture droplet profile at 50 fps over 5 seconds. 4. Fit droplet contour using Young-Laplace equation to determine static water contact angle (WCA) at left and right baselines.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Hydrophobic passivation confirmed with Water Contact Angle (WCA) >= 75.0 degrees across all radial points for immersion times between 20s and 35s (hydrophilic native oxide baseline is < 15.0 degrees).

ppe_required: Heavy-duty Neoprene/Butyl rubber chemical-resistant gauntlet gloves over double nitrile gloves
Full-face polycarbonate chemical splash shield
Acid-resistant PTFE/Neoprene chemical apron with integrated sleeves
Closed-toe acid-resistant safety boots
Chemical splash goggles meeting ANSI Z87.1 D3 rating
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: Calcium Gluconate Gel (2.5% USP) must be stored inside an unexpired first-aid station mounted directly on the wet bench. In case of skin exposure: Immediately flush affected area with copiously flowing water for minimum 2 minutes, then generously massage 2.5% calcium gluconate gel continuously into skin until medical help arrives. In case of eye contact: Irrigate eyes continuously for 15 minutes with isotonic saline or eyewash, seek immediate emergency medical care. Oxygen resuscitation apparatus must be accessible.
