critics.systems_engineer: Automating multi-point sessile droplet dispense on Gen 1 mm-scale hardware introduces mechanical vibration coupling from motorized syringe pumps and XY translation stages directly into the high-speed optical capture axis. The optical goniometer must isolate mechanical resonances to prevent meniscus oscillation during high-speed image acquisition. Furthermore, droplet volume repeatability at the sub-microliter level (1.0 to 2.0 uL) is critically sensitive to syringe needle gauge, hydrophobic PTFE needle coating wear, and air entrapment in the dispense manifold, directly biasing the measured contact angle baseline.
critics.domain_expert: Following an HF-last clean, the silicon surface is H-terminated (Si-H, Si-H2, Si-H3) and highly hydrophobic with a nominal contact angle between 75° and 86°. Any delay during multi-point spatial mapping risks airborne trace organic contamination (volatile organic compounds) and native oxide regowth, which rapidly lowers the contact angle toward hydrophilicity (<30°). The dispense-to-acquisition cycle time per point must not exceed 10 seconds, and the droplet dispense volume must remain below 2.0 uL to avoid gravitational flattening violating the Young-Laplace spherical cap assumption.
critics.supply_chain: Specifying a commercial automated goniometer (e.g., Krüss DSA or ramé-hart) under 'Buy' constraints for Gen 1 requires tracking lead times on calibrated micro-syringe assemblies (Hamilton gastight syringes), optical calibration reticles (certified circle/angle targets), and optical-grade anti-reflection coated telecentric lenses. Dual-sourcing standard PTFE-coated stainless steel dispense needles (gauge 30-32) is critical to prevent supply bottlenecks from single-vendor proprietary consumables.
critics.laya_pm: Budget and schedule must account for certified optical magnification calibration grid standards and recurring needle replacement logs. Multi-point mapping protocols must complete 9-point or 49-point wafer mapping within the strict pre-oxidation queue-time window without starving downstream dry thermal oxidation furnace loads, preventing wafer batch scrap due to clean-to-furnace hold violations.
critical_failure_modes: Micro-vibration induced capillary wave distortion during high-speed optical edge detection resulting in >3° Young-Laplace baseline fitting error.
Droplet evaporation and organic adsorption during sequential multi-point mapping causing artificial drift in contact angle measurements from point 1 to point 9.
Dispense needle clogging or PTFE tip delamination causing droplet pinning, asymmetrical droplet volume ejection, and optical distortion.

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-MET-YLC-180NM`
**Title:** Young-Laplace Baseline Contour Extraction & Contact Angle Fitting Calibration  
**Hierarchy Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > 180nm Dry Gate Oxide Growth (3.5 nm physical thickness) > Pre-Oxidation RCA Clean & In-Situ HF Dip Surface Preparation > Post-Clean Contact Angle & Surface Defect Metrology > Goniometer Water Contact Angle Metrology > Young-Laplace Fitting & Surface H-Passivation Uniformity Screening > Young-Laplace Baseline Contour Extraction & Contact Angle Fitting Calibration  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm)  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Process Overview & Objective
Establish a high-precision, automated optical baseline contour extraction and Young-Laplace profile-fitting calibration routine for sessile deionized (DI) water droplets. This calibration ensures quantitative verification of hydrogen termination ($Si\text{--}H$ passivation) and removal of native/chemical oxide across the silicon substrate prior to 850°C–900°C furnace loading for 3.5 nm dry gate oxide growth ($E_{bd} > 10\text{ MV/cm}$, $D_{it} < 10^{10}\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ eV}^{-1}$).

---

### 2. Equipment, Materials & Environmental Controls
- **Tooling:** Automated optical contact angle goniometer equipped with telecentric lens, sub-pixel edge detection CCD/CMOS camera, and automated micro-syringe dispenser (accuracy $\pm 0.05\ \mu\text{L}$).
- **Calibration Standard:** Certified optical contact angle calibration grid/target with precision glass-etched sessile drop profiles ($60.00^\circ$, $90.00^\circ$, $110.00^\circ$ standard drop baselines, traceable certified tolerance $\pm 0.1^\circ$).
- **Fluid & Dispenser:** Ultra-pure Deionized Water (resistivity $\ge 18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ at 25°C, dispense droplet volume $2.0\ \mu\text{L} \pm 0.1\ \mu\text{L}$).
- **Environment:** Cleanroom class 10/100, ambient temperature $22.0^\circ\text{C} \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$, relative humidity $45\% \pm 3\%$.

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Procedure

```text
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|           Young-Laplace Contour Calibration & Metrology Flow                     |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  [ Step 1: Optical Alignment ]
        |  --> Level stage (pitch/roll < 0.05°), focus telecentric optics
        v
  [ Step 2: Pixel-to-Micron Calibration ]
        |  --> Measure certified calibration ball/grid (scaling in µm/pixel)
        v
  [ Step 3: Baseline Detection & Tilt Calibration ]
        |  --> Sub-pixel edge detection (Canny/Sobel) & reflection mirror baseline
        v
  [ Step 4: Young-Laplace Fitting Execution ]
        |  --> Integrate axisymmetric Young-Laplace equation across contour
        v
  [ Step 5: Residual Error & Drift Verification ]
        |  --> Verify RMSE < 0.05 px; confirm automated pass/fail gate
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

1. **Optical System Alignment & Leveling:**
   - Mount the optical calibration reticle on the motorized sample stage.
   - Adjust stage tilt and goniometer roll/pitch until stage horizon tilt angle is $\le 0.05^\circ$ from true horizontal.
   - Calibrate the telecentric illumination back-light to prevent optical blooming or diffraction artifacts along droplet edges.

2. **Pixel-to-Micrometer Magnification Calibration:**
   - Image a certified calibration sphere/target of known physical diameter ($D = 4.000\text{ mm} \pm 0.001\text{ mm}$).
   - Set software optical scaling factor ($\mu\text{m}/\text{pixel}$) across orthogonal axes ($X$ and $Y$ aspect ratio distortion $< 0.1\%$).

3. **Sub-Pixel Edge & Solid-Liquid Baseline Extraction:**
   - Position the calibration drop target. Execute derivative sub-pixel edge detection (Sobel/Canny filter combined with polynomial interpolation).
   - Detect the solid-liquid interface baseline utilizing the drop profile and its mirror reflection on the reflective silicon substrate. Enforce baseline position repeatability within $\pm 0.5\ \mu\text{m}$.

4. **Axisymmetric Young-Laplace Differential Curve Fitting:**
   - Fit the extracted boundary coordinates to the theoretical Young-Laplace equation balancing capillary and hydrostatic pressure:
     $$\Delta P = \gamma \left( \frac{1}{R_1} + \frac{1}{R_2} \right) = \Delta P_0 + \Delta \rho g z$$
   - Numerically integrate the profile shape from the apex radius of curvature ($R_0$) down to the detected triple-phase contact line to extract left/right contact angles ($\theta_L$, $\theta_R$).

5. **Repeatability Verification & Reference Run:**
   - Execute five consecutive automated droplet captures and fittings on the certified $90.00^\circ$ calibration target.
   - Confirm residual fit errors and drift meet acceptance thresholds before unlocking the tool for post-HF dip silicon wafer screening.

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Range | Measurement Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Goniometer Baseline Tilt** | $0.00^\circ$ | $\le \pm 0.05^\circ$ | Software optical horizon calculation |
| **Calibration Target Fit Accuracy** | Certified standard angle ($90.00^\circ$) | $\le \pm 0.20^\circ$ | Young-Laplace contour fit vs. standard target |
| **Contour Edge Extraction Residual (RMSE)** | $0.00\text{ pixels}$ | $\le 0.05\text{ pixels}$ | Least-squares residual of optical edge coordinates |
| **Dispense Volume Precision** | $2.00\ \mu\text{L}$ | $\pm 0.10\ \mu\text{L}$ | Micro-syringe optical droplet volume metrology |

---

### 5. Context Citations
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:** Transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$; unit cell area $8F^2$ or $6F^2$; dielectric layers require ultra-clean interfaces to maintain leakage targets $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at 85°C.
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering:** 1T1C architecture; dry gate oxidation targeting physical thickness of $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ grown at 850°C–900°C.
- **Deal-Grove Silicon Thermal Oxidation Kinetics in Quartz Tube Furnace:** Interface reaction-rate limited regime ($x_0 \ll A/2$) for ultra-thin 3.5 nm to 4.0 nm dry gate oxides; dictates minimal interface trap density ($D_{it} < 10^{10}\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ eV}^{-1}$) and breakdown field $E_{bd} > 10\text{ MV/cm}$, strictly dependent on uniform pre-oxidation HF-dip surface preparation and accurate hydrophobicity verification.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Automated baseline tilt detection must be decoupled from droplet reflection artifacts. On mirror-finish Si(100) wafers, the optical specular reflection of the sessile drop creates an apparent virtual drop beneath the substrate baseline. If the Canny or Sobel edge detection threshold is not strictly locked to the sub-pixel inflection point between the real meniscus contact line and the mirror image, the fitted baseline will drift vertically by 2-5 pixels, inducing an artificial contact angle error exceeding 4.5 degrees.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For 3.5 nm dry gate oxide pre-cleans, water contact angle on HF-last silicon quantifies Si-H versus Si-F / Si-OH termination. A truly hydrophobic H-passivated Si(100) surface must exhibit an advancing contact angle of 75° to 86° with deionized water. Applying a spherical approximation instead of numerical integration of the Young-Laplace equation (Bashforth-Adams method) for droplet volumes between 2 µL and 5 µL introduces hydrostatic gravity distortion errors up to 3.2°, falsely failing passivated clean batches.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Custom goniometer setups often fail due to optical objective distortion and non-telecentric lens aberration. Sourcing a calibrated optical calibration reticle (e.g., Thorlabs or Edmund Optics distortion target with 10 µm dot grid) and a high-purity glass sessile-drop calibration standard (certified 60.0° and 90.0° contact angle phantom) is critical. In Vietnamese supply chain environments, automated micro-dispenser syringes must use fluoropolymer-free blunt needles (30-gauge passivated 316 stainless steel) to avoid fluorocarbon leaching into ultra-pure DI water.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Calibration of the Young-Laplace contour baseline extraction must not become a bottleneck that breaches the strict 30-minute pre-oxidation Q-time. The image acquisition, automated contour extraction, and Bashforth-Adams fitting routine must execute within 45 seconds per measurement site (5-point wafer map) with zero manual user intervention on the baseline coordinates.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Specular mirror reflection pseudo-contact: Edge detection algorithm mistakes droplet reflection on polished silicon for the liquid-solid interface, shifting baseline upward and underestimating contact angle by 6° to 12°.
1. Capillary syringe needle retraction perturbation: Droplet volume pinning during needle withdrawal distorts drop axisymmetry, violating the axisymmetric requirement of the Young-Laplace differential equation.
1. Vibrational contour blurring: Lack of pneumatic optical vibration isolation blurs the meniscus edge during high-speed CMOS shutter acquisition, causing numerical divergence in the Bashforth-Adams non-linear least squares fit.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-3-1-3-2-01` | **Baseline Extraction Orthogonality and Calibration Phantom Verification** | Optical contact angle goniometer equipped with 1/1.8-inch monochrome CMOS sensor, telecentric imaging lens (distortion < 0.05%), monochromatic 530nm LED collimated backlighting, and certified quartz contact angle calibration standard (NIST-traceable 60.00° ± 0.20° and 90.00° ± 0.20°). | 1. Position certified 60.00° and 90.00° quartz contact angle calibration standards on sample stage. 2. Capture 10 static frames at 30 fps. 3. Execute automated edge detection with sub-pixel Sobel filtering. 4. Run automated baseline contour algorithm to detect contact line without manual pinning. 5. Perform numerical non-linear regression using the Young-Laplace equation. 6. Record mean contact angle, baseline tilt angle, and root-mean-square residual error. | `Measured contact angle on 60.00° standard must read 60.00° ± 0.30°; on 90.00° standard must read 90.00° ± 0.30°. Baseline tilt must be <= 0.15° relative to horizontal sensor plane. Fit residual RMS error must be < 0.015 mm.` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-3-1-3-2-02` | **Sessile Drop Young-Laplace Axisymmetry and Reflection-Rejection on HF-Last Silicon** | Automated micro-dispenser with 30-gauge electropolished 316 stainless steel blunt needle, ASTM Type I Ultra-Pure Deionized Water (resistivity 18.2 MOhm-cm, TOC < 5 ppb), telecentric goniometer, class 100 cleanroom laminar flow bench. | 1. Dispense a 2.0 µL ± 0.1 µL droplet of 18.2 MOhm-cm DI water at 0.5 µL/s. 2. Lower droplet onto wafer surface and retract needle at 2.0 mm/s. 3. Trigger image capture exactly 3.0 seconds post-deposition. 4. Execute automated mirror-image reflection discriminator to segment physical droplet from optical reflection. 5. Extract contour and fit left and right contact angles using the Bashforth-Adams Young-Laplace model. 6. Repeat across 5 standard die locations (Center, Top, Bottom, Left, Right). | `Contact angle asymmetry |theta_left - theta_right| must be <= 0.8°. Contact angle across all 5 sites on freshly passivated Si-H surface must fall strictly between 78.0° and 85.0°. Standard deviation across 5 sites must be <= 1.2°.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: 100% nitrile chemical gloves (minimum 6 mil thickness, double gloving), ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical splash goggles, Cleanroom-grade antistatic ESD-safe polyester coat, Class 100 lint-free shoe covers and hair bonnet
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye exposure to IPA: Flush eyes immediately with copious amounts of tempered water for at least 15 minutes at eyewash station. Skin exposure to IPA: Wash affected area with soap and water; remove contaminated clothing. Inhalation: Move personnel to fresh air. Note: While test liquid is DI water, wafers originate from HF wet bench; in case of suspected trace HF contact, immediately massage 2.5% calcium gluconate gel onto exposed skin and seek emergency medical evaluation.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operation conducted within laminar flow hood providing ISO Class 5 air velocity of 0.45 m/s ± 0.05 m/s; stage solvent cleaning vented via dedicated local exhaust slot pulling >= 50 CFM.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent DI water droplets collected on cleanroom absorbent pads and disposed of in standard solid waste. IPA wipe solvent waste segregated in FM-approved self-closing hazardous solvent waste cans for organic waste reclamation.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Deionized Ultra-Pure Water** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type I / SEMI C35 Tier 1 | `100%` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (Stage/Needle Decontamination)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (SEMI C1) | `>= 99.8%` |
| **Nitrogen Gas (Purge and Drying)** | `7727-37-9` | High Purity Grade 5.0 (99.999%) | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophobic H-terminated silicon Si(100):Si-H mono- and di-hydride passivated surface, native oxide stripped (< 0.1 nm equivalent oxide thickness), particle count < 10 particles at >= 0.2 µm.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Screened hydrophobic Si(100):Si-H surface, contact angle validated between 78.0° and 85.0°, verified unoxidized and ready for immediate loading into thermal gate oxidation furnace boat.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding 30 minutes in cleanroom ambient leads to native oxide regrowth (Si-O-Si / Si-OH formation via atmospheric oxygen and moisture adsorption), shifting contact angle below 70°, increasing interface trap density (Dit > 5e11 eV^-1 cm^-2), and compromising 3.5 nm dry gate oxide breakdown voltage.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full calibration and algorithmic validation of the automated Young-Laplace baseline contour extraction and contact angle fitting routine, ensuring accurate, operator-independent hydrophobicity quantification of post-RCA/HF-dip Si(100) wafers prior to 3.5 nm dry thermal gate oxidation.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `CAL-GONIOMETER-YOUNG-LAPLACE-CALIBRATION-REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `METROLOGY-RAW-CONTOUR-COORDINATES-DATASET.csv`
- [ ] `SURFACE-PASSIVATION-5POINT-FIT-CONTOUR.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Optical calibration accuracy against certified 90.00° contact angle standard phantom** | `90.00°` | ±0.30° | Automated Young-Laplace fitting over 10 consecutive frames on NIST-traceable quartz standard |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Baseline contact line localization tilt deviation across wafer chuck plane** | `0.00°` | ±0.15° | Sub-pixel inflection line regression algorithm compared to stage mechanical optical datum |
| `ASSERT-03` | **H-passivated Si(100) DI water contact angle verification across 5 wafer test points** | `81.50°` | +3.50° / -3.50° (range 78.0° to 85.0°) | Sessile drop 2.0 µL Young-Laplace Bashforth-Adams fitting executed within 5 minutes of HF-last drying |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Researcher exit signoff requires 100% pass on phantom calibration ASSERT-01 and ASSERT-02, automated baseline extraction with zero algorithm crashes or reflection misidentifications across 25 consecutive droplet dispenses, and successful verification of 5-point wafer uniformity yielding DI contact angles between 78.0° and 85.0° within the 30-minute air Q-time window.

Execute automated edge detection with sub-pixel Sobel filtering. 4. Run automated baseline contour algorithm to detect contact line without manual pinning. 5. Perform numerical non-linear regression using the Young-Laplace equation. 6. Record mean contact angle, baseline tilt angle, and root-mean-square residual error.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Measured contact angle on 60.00° standard must read 60.00° ± 0.30°; on 90.00° standard must read 90.00° ± 0.30°. Baseline tilt must be <= 0.15° relative to horizontal sensor plane. Fit residual RMS error must be < 0.015 mm.

testcases.title: Sessile Drop Young-Laplace Axisymmetry and Reflection-Rejection on HF-Last Silicon
testcases.instrumentation: Automated micro-dispenser with 30-gauge electropolished 316 stainless steel blunt needle, ASTM Type I Ultra-Pure Deionized Water (resistivity 18.2 MOhm-cm, TOC < 5 ppb), telecentric goniometer, class 100 cleanroom laminar flow bench.
testcases.pre_conditions: Prime-grade 100mm p-type Si(100) wafer subjected to RCA-1, RCA-2, and 0.5% in-situ HF dip (60 s), DI rinse (60 s), spin-dried under N2; wafer placed on goniometer vacuum chuck within 5 minutes of drying; environmental chamber maintained at 22.0°C ± 0.5°C and 45% ± 3% RH.
testcases.procedure: 1. Dispense a 2.0 µL ± 0.1 µL droplet of 18.2 MOhm-cm DI water at 0.5 µL/s. 2. Lower droplet onto wafer surface and retract needle at 2.0 mm/s. 3. Trigger image capture exactly 3.0 seconds post-deposition. 4. Execute automated mirror-image reflection discriminator to segment physical droplet from optical reflection. 5. Extract contour and fit left and right contact angles using the Bashforth-Adams Young-Laplace model. 6. Repeat across 5 standard die locations (Center, Top, Bottom, Left, Right).
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Contact angle asymmetry |theta_left - theta_right| must be <= 0.8°. Contact angle across all 5 sites on freshly passivated Si-H surface must fall strictly between 78.0° and 85.0°. Standard deviation across 5 sites must be <= 1.2°.

ppe_required: 100% nitrile chemical gloves (minimum 6 mil thickness, double gloving)
ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical splash goggles
Cleanroom-grade antistatic ESD-safe polyester coat
Class 100 lint-free shoe covers and hair bonnet

cas_chemicals.name: Deionized Ultra-Pure Water
cas_chemicals.purity_grade: ASTM Type I / SEMI C35 Tier 1

ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: Eye exposure to IPA: Flush eyes immediately with copious amounts of tempered water for at least 15 minutes at eyewash station. Skin exposure to IPA: Wash affected area with soap and water; remove contaminated clothing. Inhalation: Move personnel to fresh air. Note: While test liquid is DI water, wafers originate from HF wet bench; in case of suspected trace HF contact, immediately massage 2.5% calcium gluconate gel onto exposed skin and seek emergency medical evaluation.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Operation conducted within laminar flow hood providing ISO Class 5 air velocity of 0.45 m/s ± 0.05 m/s; stage solvent cleaning vented via dedicated local exhaust slot pulling >= 50 CFM.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Spent DI water droplets collected on cleanroom absorbent pads and disposed of in standard solid waste. IPA wipe solvent waste segregated in FM-approved self-closing hazardous solvent waste cans for organic waste reclamation.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Hydrophobic H-terminated silicon Si(100):Si-H mono- and di-hydride passivated surface, native oxide stripped (< 0.1 nm equivalent oxide thickness), particle count < 10 particles at >= 0.2 µm.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Screened hydrophobic Si(100):Si-H surface, contact angle validated between 78.0° and 85.0°, verified unoxidized and ready for immediate loading into thermal gate oxidation furnace boat.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Exceeding 30 minutes in cleanroom ambient leads to native oxide regrowth (Si-O-Si / Si-OH formation via atmospheric oxygen and moisture adsorption), shifting contact angle below 70°, increasing interface trap density (Dit > 5e11 eV^-1 cm^-2), and compromising 3.5 nm dry gate oxide breakdown voltage.

expected_result.summary: Full calibration and algorithmic validation of the automated Young-Laplace baseline contour extraction and contact angle fitting routine, ensuring accurate, operator-independent hydrophobicity quantification of post-RCA/HF-dip Si(100) wafers prior to 3.5 nm dry thermal gate oxidation.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Optical calibration accuracy against certified 90.00° contact angle standard phantom
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Automated Young-Laplace fitting over 10 consecutive frames on NIST-traceable quartz standard

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Baseline contact line localization tilt deviation across wafer chuck plane
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Sub-pixel inflection line regression algorithm compared to stage mechanical optical datum

quantitative_assertions.assertion: H-passivated Si(100) DI water contact angle verification across 5 wafer test points
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Sessile drop 2.0 µL Young-Laplace Bashforth-Adams fitting executed within 5 minutes of HF-last drying

expected_result.signoff_criteria: Researcher exit signoff requires 100% pass on phantom calibration ASSERT-01 and ASSERT-02, automated baseline extraction with zero algorithm crashes or reflection misidentifications across 25 consecutive droplet dispenses, and successful verification of 5-point wafer uniformity yielding DI contact angles between 78.0° and 85.0° within the 30-minute air Q-time window.

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Full-Wafer Hydrophobicity Uniformity Mapping & H-Passivation Defect Screening

**Process Level:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > 180nm Dry Gate Oxide Growth (3.5 nm) > Pre-Oxidation RCA Clean and In-Situ HF Dip > Post-Clean Metrology  
**Node:** Gen 2 (180 nm / 0.18 µm) | **Action Type:** Buy (Automated Goniometer Metrology Tool)

---

### Process Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Load Wafer into     │
│  Automated Goniometer  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  49-Point Polar Grid   │
│   Dispense 1 uL DIW    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Young-Laplace      │
│   Contour & Baseline   │
│        Fitting         │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      Uniformity &      │
│  H-Passivation Defect  │
│       Screening        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────◇───────────┐
│                        │
│  Criteria Check: Mean  │
│     WCA >= 75 deg,     │
│    Non-Unif <= 2.5%    │
│                        │
└────────────◇───────────┘
             │
             ├──────────────────────────────╮Fail
         Pass│                              │
             ▼                              ▼
┌────────────────────────┐     ┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │     │                        │
│  Transfer to Dry Gate  │     │  Quarantine & Rework:  │
│   Oxidation Furnace    │     │     Re-Dip / Strip     │
│                        │     │                        │
└────────────────────────┘     └────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Tool Initialization & Cleanroom Ambient Control**:
   - Ensure the automated contact angle goniometer enclosure is purged with filtered $N_2$ (or Class 1 mini-environment airflow) at $21.0 \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ and relative humidity $40 \pm 2\%$.
   - Verify calibrated automated micropipette/syringe dosing module loaded with ultra-pure degassed deionized water (DIW, resistivity $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$).
2. **Wafer Loading & Alignment**:
   - Transfer the post-HF dip wafer directly via robotic end-effector onto the motorized $R$-$\theta$ vacuum chuck within a queue time limit $\le 15\text{ min}$ to prevent native oxide regrowth.
   - Perform automated optical notch/flat pre-alignment.
3. **Automated Multi-Point Droplet Dispensing**:
   - Execute an automated 49-point full-wafer polar inspection map (center, mid-radius concentric rings, and edge exclusion zone $\ge 3\text{ mm}$).
   - Dispense a sessile drop of $1.0 \pm 0.1\ \mu\text{L}$ DIW at each inspection site using automated needle lift-off to eliminate kinetic impact distortion.
4. **Image Acquisition & Young-Laplace Contour Fitting**:
   - Capture high-resolution telecentric side-profile optical images within $1.5\text{ s}$ of droplet deposition to avoid evaporation artifacts.
   - Execute automated baseline edge detection and apply the Young-Laplace axisymmetric droplet shape fitting algorithm to determine left/right contact angles ($\theta_L$, $\theta_R$) and compute mean site Water Contact Angle (WCA).
5. **Uniformity Calculation & Defect Screening**:
   - Calculate full-wafer mean WCA, standard deviation ($\sigma$), and percent non-uniformity:
     $$\text{Non-Uniformity (\%)} = \frac{\theta_{\max} - \theta_{\min}}{2 \times \theta_{\text{mean}}} \times 100\%$$
   - Flag any local drop anomaly where $\theta < 70^\circ$ as an unpassivated native oxide patch / rinsing chemical residue defect.
6. **Pass/Fail Disposition**:
   - If within criteria, clear the wafer lot for immediate entry into the quartz tube furnace for dry gate oxidation (target: $3.5\text{ nm}$ $\text{SiO}_2$ at $850^\circ\text{C}$–$900^\circ\text{C}$).
   - If non-conforming, quarantine the lot for re-clean/re-dip investigation.

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Physical Units | Sampling / Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Mean H-Passivated Surface WCA** | $\ge 75.0^\circ$ (Nominal $78^\circ \text{--} 84^\circ$) | Degrees ($^\circ$) | 49-point full-wafer polar map |
| **Full-Wafer Contact Angle Non-Uniformity** | $\le 2.5\%$ ($1\sigma \le 1.2^\circ$) | Percent ($\%$) | Across all 49 measured sites |
| **Dispense Droplet Volume Precision** | $1.00 \pm 0.05$ | Microliters ($\mu\text{L}$) | Micro-solenoid / syringe doser |
| **Post-Clean Queue Time to Furnace Loading** | $\le 45$ | Minutes ($\text{min}$) | MES lot tracker timestamp |

---

### Literature & Context Citations

- **Source:** *Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering*  
  - Baseline gate dielectric target requires thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ at $850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$ dry oxidation with $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ physical thickness; complete elimination of native oxide and uniform H-passivation via HF-last clean is critical to gate oxide integrity.
- **Source:** *Deal-Grove Silicon Thermal Oxidation Kinetics in Quartz Tube Furnace*  
  - In the thin oxidation regime ($x_0 \ll A/2$), oxidation kinetics are strictly interface reaction-rate limited ($k_l = B/A$). Unpassivated patches or uneven H-termination cause initial oxide thickness disparities, degraded breakdown field ($E_{bd} < 10\text{ MV/cm}$), and elevated interface trap density ($D_{it} > 10^{10}\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{eV}^{-1}$).
- **Source:** *180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench*  
  - Access transistor channel length ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$) requires sub-threshold and junction leakage $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$; uniform pre-gate surface termination guarantees threshold voltage ($V_{th}$) uniformity across the memory array.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Automating full-wafer hydrophobicity mapping via water droplet dispensing poses significant integration trade-offs: while optical contact angle measurement provides direct proxy data for Si-H bond density prior to thermal oxidation, water droplet deposition itself introduces localized oxygen and organic contamination if droplet volumes exceed 2 uL or if nitrogen dry-purge is non-uniform. Furthermore, droplet-based goniometry is an inherently contact/destructive test on the mapped sites unless sacrificial exclusion zones (wafer edge/scribe lines) or ultra-fast non-contact reflectometric/ellipsometric screening are utilized as the primary baseline.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: A perfectly hydrogen-terminated silicon (100) surface post-HF-last clean exhibits a pristine hydrophobic contact angle of 78° to 86° depending on mono-, di-, and tri-hydride distribution and ambient hydrocarbon adsorption. Surface oxidation or sub-monolayer native oxide pinholes immediately cause localized hydrophilic pinning, dropping contact angles below 60° within minutes in atmospheric air. Young-Laplace contour fitting across a 49-point wafer grid must account for droplet evaporation kinetics and surface roughness effects (Wenzel vs. Cassie-Baxter states) to prevent false-positive defect reporting.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Specialized automated goniometers (e.g., Ramé-Hart or DataPhysics) are cost-prohibitive for open-source low-budget runs. For Gen 1 garage/pilot line implementation in Vietnam, the optical goniometry subsystem must rely on a standard 3-axis motorized CNC stage, an industrial USB3 telecentric camera/10x macro optics, calibrated microliter PTFE needle dispensers, and open-source OpenCV Young-Laplace contour solvers, avoiding single-vendor lock-in while maintaining sub-degree contact angle repeatability.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Every additional minute spent on full-wafer goniometer mapping burns the critical pre-oxidation Q-time envelope. If goniometer metrology consumes more than 10 minutes per wafer in ambient cleanroom air, the process itself induces the exact catastrophic defect—native oxide regrowth (>0.3 nm) and interface trap density degradation (Dit > 5e11 eV^-1 cm^-2)—that it is intended to screen. Metrology protocol must be lean, automated, and tightly coupled with a sealed N2 transfer box.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Micro-droplet residual moisture marks triggering localized thermal oxidation non-uniformities and dielectric breakdown (pinholes in 3.5 nm dry gate oxide).
1. Ambient oxygen and airborne molecular contamination (AMC) causing Si-H depassivation during measurement delays exceeding the allowable air queue time.
1. Dispensing needle organic contamination or droplet vibration causing droplet asymmetry and non-convergence in Young-Laplace contour fitting.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-3-1-3-3-01` | **49-Point Full-Wafer Hydrophobicity Uniformity and Young-Laplace Contact Angle Mapping** | Automated Optical Goniometer with Telecentric Macro Lens, 1.0 uL Calibrated PTFE Needle Dispenser, 3-Axis Motorized Stage, Pure N2 Environmental Enclosure, Image Processing Young-Laplace Fitting Software | 1. Load wafer onto goniometer vacuum chuck inside N2-purged glovebox. 2. Initialize automated 49-point radial and polar mapping pattern (concentric rings at r = 0, 15, 30, 42 mm). 3. At each coordinate, dispense a 1.0 +/- 0.1 uL droplet of 18.2 MOhm-cm deionized water. 4. Capture baseline droplet profile within 1.5 seconds of touchdown using high-resolution telecentric camera. 5. Execute Young-Laplace profile extraction to compute left and right contact angles. 6. Automatically aspirate/N2-dry droplet prior to index stepping to the next coordinate. | `Wafer-mean contact angle theta >= 78.0 deg; 49-point standard deviation sigma <= 2.5 deg (uniformity >= 95%); zero points with theta < 70.0 deg across all mapped sites.` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-3-1-3-3-02` | **Post-Metrology Surface Moisture and Particle Residue Screening via Darkfield Optical Inspection** | Automated Darkfield Surface Particle Scanner / Optical Microscope with 10x Plan Achromat NA 0.25 and 455nm Blue Laser Grazing Incident Light Source | 1. Transfer wafer to darkfield inspection stage. 2. Perform full-surface raster scan across 100mm wafer area excluding 3mm edge ring. 3. Detect scattering centers corresponding to residual water drying rings (coffee-ring stains), watermark silica deposits, or particulate contamination. 4. Correlate coordinate map of detected scattering defects with the 49 goniometer droplet dispense coordinates. | `Zero watermark residue rings detected at any of the 49 droplet contact coordinates; added defect count > 0.5 um diameter <= 5 defects/wafer.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (double-gloved, powder-free), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Cleanroom ESD-safe anti-static coat and hood, Acid-resistant apron and face shield (during HF/wet-clean handling upstream)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Water contact angle metrology uses non-toxic UPW and N2. However, for preceding surface clean hazards (HF residuals): If skin contact occurs with lingering acid from wet-bench transfers, immediately flush with copious cold water for 5 minutes and massage 2.5% calcium gluconate gel continuously into affected area until medical arrival. For nitrogen enclosure oxygen displacement: immediately evacuate unconscious victim to fresh air, administer artificial respiration or oxygen if qualified.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Goniometer metrology must be enclosed in a certified laminar flow hood with HEPA filtration (Class 100 / ISO 5) equipped with low-velocity local exhaust (0.5 m/s capture velocity) and an oxygen-deficiency monitor (alarm set at < 19.5% O2) to protect against inert N2 gas accumulation.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent droplet DI water and rinse effluent are drained directly into the cleanroom neutralized acid-waste drainage system. No organic solvents or hazardous heavy metals permitted in the goniometer fluid path.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Deionized Water (Ultrapure 18.2 MOhm-cm)** | `7732-18-5` | Semiconductor Grade (UPW / ASTM D5127 Type E-1) | `100%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (Ultra-High Purity N2)** | `7727-37-9` | Grade 5.0 (99.999% purity) | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `20 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `3 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly etched, pristine H-terminated silicon Si(100):2x1 surface post-1% DHF dip and marangoni/SRD dry, free of native oxide (SiO2 thickness < 0.1 nm).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Screened H-passivated wafer surface with validated hydrophobic angle (>= 78 deg), zero watermark drying residues, ready for immediate loadlock pumpdown and dry oxidation furnace push.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Native oxide (SiOx) regrowth and airborne organic siloxane/hydrocarbon adsorption (> 0.4 nm), leading to uncontrolled interfacial trap density (Dit > 1e11 cm^-2 eV^-1), non-uniform Deal-Grove linear growth rate, and gate oxide premature dielectric breakdown (TDDB < 10^3 s at 5 MV/cm).

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full-wafer 49-point contact angle hydrophobicity map successfully generated within 8 minutes of HF-last clean. Demonstrates uniform H-passivation (mean theta >= 78.0 deg, 1-sigma <= 2.5 deg) with zero detected watermarks, validating the wafer lot for immediate 3.5 nm dry gate oxide furnace insertion.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `WAF_HYDROPHOB_MAP_49PT_DATA.csv`
- [ ] `YOUNG_LAPLACE_CONTOUR_FIT_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `POST_METROLOGY_DARKFIELD_DEFECT_MAP.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Wafer-level mean water contact angle indicates complete hydrogen surface termination post-HF-last** | `81.5 deg` | +/- 3.5 deg (minimum >= 78.0 deg) | Automated Young-Laplace contour fitting on 49-point full-wafer goniometer grid |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Full-wafer hydrophobicity uniformity standard deviation across 49 test coordinates** | `1.8 deg` | <= 2.5 deg (1-sigma) | Statistical spatial distribution analysis across center, middle, and edge radial zones in WAF_HYDROPHOB_MAP_49PT_DATA.csv |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Metrology run execution time within cleanroom air envelope to avoid native oxide regrowth** | `420 seconds` | <= 480 seconds (8.0 minutes) | Automated system timestamp log comparison between wafer cassette unload and dry N2 box re-seal |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Researcher signoff requires WAF_HYDROPHOB_MAP_49PT_DATA.csv confirming mean contact angle >= 78.0 deg with no single point < 70.0 deg, darkfield optical inspection confirming zero added watermark defects, and total elapsed air Q-time <= 15 minutes before furnace tube loading.

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Laser Light Scattering Particle Scanning & Defect Density Mapping (<180nm Threshold)

**Module:** Pre-Gate Oxidation Metrology / Defect Inspection  
**Node:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Target Critical Dimension (CD):** Access Transistor Channel Length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, Channel Width $W = 220\text{ nm}$  
**Substrate State:** Post-RCA Clean & In-Situ HF Dip prior to Dry Gate Oxide Growth ($3.5\text{ nm}$)

---

### 1. Process Workflow

```text
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│   Load Wafer & Vacuum Chuck Clamping (FOUP)  │
└──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                       │
                       ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Dark-Field Laser Optics Auto-Calibration    │
└──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                       │
                       ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Full-Wafer Polar/Spiral Surface Scan        │
└──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                       │
                       ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Coordinate Registration & PSL Sphere Binning │
└──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                       │
                       ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Pass/Fail Verification vs Gate Oxide Spec    │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Substrate Handling & Chamber Loading:**
   - Transfer wafer from the wet bench FOUP into the Laser Surface Scanning Inspection chamber using an edge-grip robotic end-effector (exclusion edge zone: $3\text{ mm}$).
   - Engage backside vacuum chucking to hold flatness within $\le 0.5\text{ }\mu\text{m}$.

2. **Optical Calibration & Gain Normalization:**
   - Initialize solid-state/argon-ion dark-field laser source ($488\text{ nm}$ or UV laser beam).
   - Perform auto-calibration against an in-situ Polystyrene Latex (PSL) standard wafer with sensitivity calibrated to resolve light point defects (LPD) at the critical threshold $d_{\text{particle}} < 180\text{ nm}$.
   - Balance narrow and wide collection photomultiplier tube (PMT) gains for Rayleigh scattering signal discrimination against bare silicon background haze.

3. **Full-Wafer Polar/Spiral Surface Scan:**
   - Execute continuous rotation and radial translation stage scan across the 200mm wafer surface.
   - Scan velocity synchronized to maintain 100% surface inspection coverage without dead bands.
   - Capture scattered intensity profiles and detect light scattering anomalies across both center and edge dies.

4. **Defect Coordinate Mapping & Size Binning:**
   - Translate scattering cross-sections into equivalent optical diameters using Mie scattering calibration curves.
   - Bin detected particles into standard categories:
     - **Critical Gate Defect Bin:** $d_{\text{particle}} \le 180\text{ nm}$ (risk to $L=180\text{ nm}$ access transistor channel and $3.5\text{ nm}$ dry oxide breakdown).
     - **Sub-Micron Channel Bin:** $180\text{ nm} < d_{\text{particle}} \le 220\text{ nm}$ (bridging risk for channel width $W=220\text{ nm}$).
     - **Macro Killer Defect Bin:** $d_{\text{particle}} > 220\text{ nm}$.
   - Generate $(X, Y)$ coordinate defect map and compute localized Defect Density ($D_0$).

5. **Acceptance Evaluation & Lot Disposition:**
   - Compare total defect count and localized cluster density against gate-dielectric pre-clean thresholds.
   - If acceptance criteria pass, transfer wafer lot immediately to the dry oxidation furnace tube ($850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$). If failed, route wafer for re-cleaning.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Measurement Target / Limit | Engineering Rationale & Node Context |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Minimum Detectable Defect Threshold** | $\le 180\text{ nm}$ equivalent PSL sphere diameter | Resolves killer particles matching the access transistor channel length ($L = 180\text{ nm}$) |
| **Critical Defect Density ($d \le 180\text{ nm}$)** | $\le 0.05\text{ defects/cm}^2$ ($\le 15\text{ counts/200mm wafer}$) | Prevents pinholes and early dielectric breakdown in the $3.5\text{ nm}$ dry gate oxide |
| **Killer Macro Particle Count ($d > 220\text{ nm}$)** | $\le 2\text{ particles/wafer}$ | Protects against shorting across active channel width ($W = 220\text{ nm}$) |
| **Optical Haze (Surface Micro-Roughness)** | $\le 0.12\text{ ppm}$ normalized haze signal | Confirms clean hydrogen-passivated silicon surface post-HF dip prior to oxidation |

---

### 4. Typical Defect Distribution Benchmark

```text
Defect Density Distribution (counts/wafer)
                   ┌───────────────────────────────────┐
                   │███████████████████████████████████│
     Crit (<0.18um)┤███████████████████████████████████│
                   │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓              │
Bin 3 (0.18-0.22um)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓              │
Bin 2 (0.22-0.50um)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                         │
                   │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                         │
    Bin 1 (>0.50um)┤░░░░                               │
                   │░░░░                               │
                   └┬────────┬───────┬────────┬───────┬┘
                    0        3       6        9      12 
```

---

### 5. Literature Citations & Context Grounding

- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:**
  - Access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$ establishes the primary threshold for laser light scattering sensitivity.
  - Access transistor channel width $W = 220\text{ nm}$ establishes the upper critical defect boundary where particles cause terminal bridging or source/drain leakage.
- **Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering:**
  - Dry gate dielectric thickness is thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ at $850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$ to a physical thickness of $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$, mandating ultra-low particulate contamination to prevent gate oxide integrity (GOI) breakdown.
- **Source: Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology:**
  - Establishes the downstream non-destructive optical monitoring framework and sub-Angstrom precision requirements ($\pm 0.05\text{ nm}$) for the $3.5\text{ nm}$ dry gate oxide film.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Laser light scattering (LLS / Surfscan principle) at <180 nm threshold operates in the Rayleigh scattering regime where scattering cross-section scales inversely with wavelength to the 4th power (sigma ~ d^6 / lambda^4). Using a standard 405 nm or 488 nm solid-state laser requires extremely low optical noise floor and confocal dark-field spatial filtering to prevent silicon substrate micro-roughness (haze) from overwhelming true point-defect scattering signals. Furthermore, handling and stage motion inside a Class 100/ISO 5 clean mini-environment must not contribute secondary particulate contamination during the inspection raster scan.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Post-RCA and HF-last surfaces are hydrogen-terminated and highly hydrophobic, with contact angles >70 degrees. This non-polar surface attracts airborne molecular organic contaminants and particulate settling via electrostatic charges. To reliably resolve <180 nm Latex Sphere Equivalents (LSE) without false positives, the dark-field optics must decouple localized surface scattering from diffuse background haze (which correlates with chemical surface roughness and oxide regrowth). Calibration wafers with 150 nm polystyrene latex (PSL) standard spheres must validate sizing bins prior to running bare Si production lots.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Commercial automated wafer surface particle counters (e.g., KLA-Tencor Surfscan SP1/SP2) are capital-prohibitive for Gen 1 open-source fabs. The decentralized alternative utilizes an open-architecture CNC motorized R-theta or XY stage coupled to a 405 nm CW diode laser (50-100 mW), elliptic collection mirrors, and high-sensitivity photomultiplier tubes (PMT) or avalanche photodiodes (APD). Sourcing certified 150 nm and 200 nm NIST-traceable PSL calibration suspensions and PMT preamplifiers requires domestic Vietnamese optical and laboratory distributors with 4-6 week lead times.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Metrology must avoid becoming the critical bottleneck between wet bench pre-clean and oxidation furnace insertion. Wafer inspection must execute in under 3 minutes per 100mm wafer. Total cumulative queue time between HF-last etch and oxidation furnace load is strictly budgeted at 45 minutes; particle inspection cannot consume more than 8 minutes total (including loading, alignment, rastering, and coordinate defect file generation).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Substrate Haze Saturation: High baseline surface roughness (>0.3 nm RMS) or native oxide island formation saturates PMT background channels, masking individual <180 nm particle scattering pulses.
1. Electrostatic Particulate Scavenging: Wafer charging during dry nitrogen blow-off or automated vacuum chucking attracts ambient aerosols, creating false catastrophic particle-adder counts post-clean.
1. Defect Coordinate Drift: Mechanical backlash or thermal drift in open-source stage encoder causes misregistration of particle defect coordinates relative to subsequent gate oxide dielectric breakdown locations.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-3-2-01` | **NIST PSL Sphere Size-Binning and Detection Sensitivity Calibration (<180nm)** | Dark-field laser surface scanner (405nm diode, 60mW CW, PMT detector), NIST-traceable 152nm PSL sphere standard wafer, oscilloscope/digitizer (100 MS/s). | 1. Load calibration wafer onto vacuum chuck inside Class 100 laminar enclosure. 2. Align wafer notch/flat and establish optical focus at center coordinate (0,0). 3. Perform spiral/raster scan across wafer surface with 5um spot diameter at 100 mm/s scan speed. 4. Record pulse height histogram and background baseline voltage. 5. Calculate SNR of 152nm scattering peaks over background substrate haze. | `Peak pulse height for 152nm PSL standards must achieve SNR >= 5:1 relative to baseline RMS haze noise. Particle capture efficiency for 152nm spheres must be >= 95% across 3 consecutive scans.` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-3-2-02` | **Post-RCA HF-Last Clean Wafer Defect Density and Particle Adder Mapping** | Automated laser scattering particle scanner, Class 100 HEPA hood, non-contact optical thickness/reflectometer. | 1. Transfer wafer from wet station carrier into laser scanner using antistatic carbon-tipped tweezers. 2. Initiate 3mm edge-exclusion full-wafer scan with detection threshold set to 150nm LSE. 3. Generate radial defect density map (rings: 0-25mm, 25-45mm, 47mm edge zone). 4. Export Kla-Tencor compatible KLARF or CSV defect coordinate file detailing X, Y, and scattering intensity. | `Total particle count >= 150nm LSE must be <= 15 particles per 100mm wafer (defect density <= 0.20 particles/cm^2 across active zone with 3mm edge exclusion). Zero killer clusters (>= 3 contiguous defects within 500um radius).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 3B/Class 4 laser safety goggles certified for 405nm (OD 6+), Nitrile cleanroom gloves (powder-free, static dissipative), Full cleanroom bunny suit with ESD grounding wrist strap, Laser protective interlock shrouds on metrology enclosure
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For direct laser beam eye exposure, seek immediate emergency ophthalmological evaluation; do not rub eyes. For IPA skin or eye contact, flush with emergency eyewash/drench shower for 15 minutes. In case of inhalation of aerosolized PSL or IPA vapors, move victim to fresh clean air and monitor respiration.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operation conducted under dedicated Class 100 (ISO 5) laminar flow clean hood with HEPA filtration (0.12um at 99.999% efficiency) and horizontal positive air pressure. Solvent wipe areas vented to local exhaust ventilation (LEV) operating at minimum 100 FPM face velocity.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA lint-free wipes collected in sealed flammable waste bins. Waste liquid PSL suspension diluted 10:1 with water and disposed of via hazardous non-chlorinated solvent/aqueous waste stream. Empty chemical containers triple-rinsed and segregated.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Polystyrene Latex (PSL) Nanosphere Suspension** | `9003-53-6` | NIST-Traceable Calibration Standard (in DI water/surfactant) | `0.1% w/w solids` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) (Stage Cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI/Electronic Grade | `99.9%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `20 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `2 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophobic hydrogen-terminated Si(100) (water contact angle >= 72 degrees) with native chemical oxide fully stripped (<0.2 nm SiO2).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Particle-mapped, unoxidized pristine hydrophobic silicon surface with zero optical laser-induced damage and no organic condensation.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding queue time in ambient air causes uncontrolled, non-stoichiometric native oxide regrowth (SiOx, x < 2) up to 0.6-0.8 nm and airborne organic hydrocarbon adsorption, inducing severe gate oxide thinning non-uniformity, high interface trap density (Dit > 5e11 eV^-1 cm^-2), and premature time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB).

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Non-destructive full-wafer dark-field laser scattering scan quantifying surface defect density and absolute particle distribution (<180nm LSE) on post-clean 100mm silicon wafers, generating defect coordinate maps and verifying cleanroom cleanliness prior to 3.5 nm dry gate oxidation.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `SURF_DEFECT_MAP_LOT01_W03.csv`
- [ ] `HAZE_AND_PARTICLE_HISTOGRAM_LOT01_W03.pdf`
- [ ] `SCATTER_DARKFIELD_IMAGE_RAW_W03.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Maximum particle count for size bin >= 150nm LSE within 3mm edge exclusion** | `10` | +5 particles / 100mm wafer | Calibrated PMT dark-field scattering pulse integration and coordinate mapping |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Average wafer background optical haze (substrate micro-roughness proxy)** | `0.12` | ±0.04 ppm relative to incident beam | Diffuse DC collection channel voltage compared to specular beam calibration standard |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Inspection cycle time per 100mm wafer (load to file write)** | `150` | +30 seconds | Automated system scan timestamp log comparison |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Wafer lot exhibits <= 0.20 particles/cm^2 (>150nm LSE), zero macro clusters (>5 particles within 1 mm^2), average substrate haze < 0.18 ppm, and completes inspection within 15 minutes of HF-last rinse-dry, enabling immediate dry-nitrogen purged transfer to the Deal-Grove dry gate oxidation furnace.

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document Details
- **Title:** Calibration Standard Wafer Setup & Laser Scatter Recipe Tuning (<180nm PSL Threshold)
- **Hierarchy:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > 180nm Dry Gate Oxide Growth (3.5 nm) > Pre-Oxidation RCA Clean and In-Situ HF Dip Surface Preparation > Post-Clean Contact Angle & Surface Particle/Metallic Defect Metrology > Laser Light Scattering Particle Scanning & Defect Density Mapping (<180nm Threshold) > Calibration Standard Wafer Setup & Laser Scatter Recipe Tuning (<180nm PSL Threshold)
- **Generation:** Gen 2 (µm)
- **Action Type:** Make

---

## 1. Objective & Scope
Establish, calibrate, and tune the laser light scattering surface inspection recipe using certified Polystyrene Latex (PSL) sphere calibration wafers to reliably detect particle defects down to the sub-180 nm threshold on bare and cleaned silicon substrates prior to 3.5 nm dry gate oxide growth.

---

## 2. Process Flow & Step-by-Step Procedure

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  1. Inspection & Stage Verification                                   |
|     Inspect PSL calibration standard wafer; verify stage alignment.   |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                  |
                                  v
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  2. Optical Recipe Setup & Gain Calibration                           |
|     Configure laser incident beam and tune PMT detector sensitivity.  |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                  |
                                  v
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  3. Multi-Point Mapping & Size Calibration                            |
|     Execute automated wafer scan across mapping points.               |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                  |
                                  v
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  4. Recipe Locking & Handoff                                          |
|     Confirm sizing bin peak and lock recipe for production.           |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

### Step 1: Inspection & Stage Alignment Setup
1. Transfer the certified PSL sphere reference wafer (deposition standard for <180 nm equivalent diameter) from its sealed pod to the automated inspection stage under ISO Class 1 mini-environment / laminar hood.
2. Verify stage translation alignment and zero reference position to ensure mechanical travel is within the Gen 2 alignment specification of $\pm 5\ \mu\text{m}$.

### Step 2: Optical Calibration & Detector Gain Tuning
1. Initialize the solid-state laser light source and verify beam intensity and polarization alignment across the incident optics.
2. Align dark-field collection optics (ellipsoidal mirror / photomultiplier tube (PMT) collector) to capture Rayleigh/Mie scattered light from the substrate surface.
3. Tune detector pre-amplifier gain and threshold voltage curves using the known scattering cross-section of the sub-180 nm PSL reference peaks.

### Step 3: Automated Wafer Mapping & Signal Response Verification
1. Program the recipe coordinate system to perform a high-density automated surface scan using standard 9-point or 49-point wafer mapping protocols to verify radial defect detection uniformity across the substrate.
2. Execute the scan on the standard wafer; collect raw scatter counts and map pulse-height distributions against coordinate locations.
3. Verify that the scattering intensity histogram resolves the primary PSL sphere calibration peak distinctly above the substrate background optical haze/noise floor.

### Step 4: Recipe Validation & Basemapping
1. Repeat 3 consecutive scans on the calibration standard to determine repeatability and sizing resolution.
2. Lock the laser inspection recipe threshold and export baseline particle coordinates for production in-line screening before gate oxidation.

---

## 3. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Physical Units | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Stage Alignment Tolerance (Gen 2)** | $\pm 5$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Optical stage encoder / fiducial alignment |
| **Particle Detection Threshold Sizing** | $< 180$ | $\text{nm}$ | Laser scatter pulse-height histogram vs. PSL standard |
| **Wafer Mapping Grid Resolution** | $9 \text{ to } 49$ | points / sectors | Automated wafer map recipe inspection log |
| **Pre-Oxide Gate Film Thickness Control** | $3.5$ (tolerance $\pm 0.05$) | $\text{nm}$ | Spectroscopic ellipsometry validation |

---

## 4. Context References & Citations
- **Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology**: Prescribes automated 9-point or 49-point wafer mapping for radial non-uniformity tracking and defines dry gate oxide measurement precision at 3.5 nm with sub-Angstrom precision ($\pm 0.05\ \text{nm}$).
- **Sam Zeloof Z1 Garage Semiconductor Journal (2018)**: Sets Gen 2 mechanical alignment tolerance bounds at $\pm 5\ \mu\text{m}$.
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**: Defines access transistor channel scaling constraints ($L = 180\ \text{nm}$, $W = 220\ \text{nm}$) establishing the requirement for sub-180 nm defect threshold mapping.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: Station exhaust and DI water loop (18.2 MOhm-cm, particle filter 0.1 um) must interlock prior to wafer boat immersion. Rinse cascade must terminate downstream acid carries before SC-2.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: BOE 6:1 (NH4F:HF) etch rate must be calibrated at 70-80 nm/min at 25°C. SC-1 (5:1:1 H2O:NH4OH:H2O2) must be maintained at 75°C +/- 2°C to eliminate light organics without pitting Si.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Electronic-grade semiconductor reagents (VLSI/MOS grade) must be procured from certified chemical distributors; technical-grade chemicals will induce metallic surface poisoning (Fe, Cu, Ni > 1e10 atoms/cm2).
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 24-32 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: HIGH (Chemical cross-contamination or incomplete dump rinse leaves watermark defects and micro-masking during subsequent etch).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Watermark defect formation during static pull-out from hydrophilic-to-hydrophobic transition.
1. Exhaust face-velocity drop below 0.5 m/s causing acid vapor condensation on cleanroom tooling.
1. Over-etch in BOE undercut exceeding 50 nm, destroying contact via dimensional margins.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

Load unpatterned witness silicon wafer into darkfield laser scatterometer. 2. Scan complete surface for light point defects (LPD) at size bin >= 180 nm. 3. Perform Total Reflection X-Ray Fluorescence (TXRF) for trace Fe, Cu, Ni surface concentrations. | `LPD count (>= 180 nm) < 10 defects/wafer (Pass); Transition metals (Fe, Ni, Cu) < 5e10 atoms/cm2 (Pass).` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-1-3-2-1-02` | **Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1) Step Height & Lateral Undercut Profilometry** | Stylus Profilometer (Veeco Dektak XT) / Atomic Force Microscope (AFM) | 1. Zero stylus force baseline at 3 mg on planar SiO2 field. 2. Scan 200 um profile across etched contact window step at 20 um/s scan speed. 3. Record step height h_step and lateral undercut under resist margin. | `Etch depth matches target +/- 5% (Pass); lateral undercut <= 35 nm (Pass); surface roughness Ra < 0.5 nm (Pass).` |

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Heavy-duty butyl/neoprene gloves (0.7 mm thickness, tested for HF permeation), Full-face polycarbonate splash shield over ANSI Z87.1 safety goggles, Acid-resistant chemical apron with sleeves (PVC/Neoprene), Acid gas vapor cartridge respirator (NIOSH approved for HF/HCl)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: MANDATORY ON-SITE ANTIDOTE: Calcium Gluconate Gel (2.5%). In case of HF skin contact: Flush immediately under emergency drench shower for 2-3 minutes, then vigorously massage Calcium Gluconate Gel into affected skin continuously until emergency medical response arrives. Never apply standard burn creams.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated polypropylene wet bench with vertical laminar exhaust face velocity >= 0.55 m/s. Interlocked with wet acid scrubber.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Segregate fluoride effluent. Neutralize with Calcium Hydroxide (Ca(OH)2) slurry to precipitate insoluble Calcium Fluoride (CaF2). Verify pH 7.0-8.5 before drain discharge.

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

| **Ammonium Fluoride (NH4F)** | `12125-01-8` | Electronic Grade | `40% aq (for BOE 6:1 buffer)` |
| **Hydrogen Peroxide (H2O2)** | `7722-84-1` | Electronic Grade (unstabilized) | `30% aq (for SC-1 & SC-2)` |

| **Ammonium Hydroxide (NH4OH)** | `1336-21-6` | Electronic Grade | `29% aq (for SC-1 clean)` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30.0 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4.0 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic with native chemical oxide (Tox ~1.0 nm) and organic particulates.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophobic H-terminated bare silicon (water contact angle > 75°), zero watermarks, Tox < 0.2 nm.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Native SiO2 spontaneously regrows in ambient air at ~0.1 nm/hr, degrading interface state density Dit and causing uncontrolled threshold voltage shift in downstream gate oxidation.

**Exit Objective Summary**:

- [ ] `DHF_BOE_calibrated_etch_rate_sheet.csv`

> Wafer surface exhibits 100% uniform dewetting / hydrophobicity with zero visible drying marks under bright light; residual native oxide Tox < 0.2 nm confirmed by spectroscopic ellipsometry.
