# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): Atomic Force Microscopy Surface Microroughness Verification

**Discipline / Category**: Metrology  
**Target Generation**: Gen 1 (mm) | **Action Type**: Make

---

### 1. Equipment & Environmental Pre-Flight
- Verify cleanroom ambient conditions (Class 1000 / ISO Class 6 laminar flow bench, Temp: 21°C ± 1°C, Humidity: 45% ± 5%).
- Inspect facility interlocks (acid/solvent exhaust velocity > 0.5 m/s, DI water loop > 18.0 MΩ·cm).

### 2. Physical Tool Calibration & Substrate Fixturing
- Mount substrate securely onto vacuum chuck stage and align mechanical/optical fiducials.
- Zero baseline instruments and establish background electrical/chemical noise floor.

### 3. Recipe Execution & Parameter Control
- Execute process sequence according to verified engineering specifications.
- Monitor thermal, optical, or chemical rate transients during execution.

### 4. Post-Process Metrology & Acceptance
- Perform quantitative verification using Optical Inspection / Profilometer.
- Log 10 consecutive measurement cycles to guarantee process repeatability (Cp/Cpk >= 1.33).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: AFM measurement introduces a significant bottleneck in the pre-oxidation sequence. With an ultra-thin 3.5 nm gate oxide for 180nm DRAM, interface microroughness directly governs dielectric breakdown field (E_bd) and Fowler-Nordheim tunneling leakage. However, scanning a 1 um x 1 um to 5 um x 5 um area at 0.5-1.0 Hz line rate takes 10-15 minutes per site. Integrating a 5-point wafer inspection inside the strict pre-oxidation Q-time envelope risks uncontrolled native oxide regrowing and atmospheric hydrocarbon re-adsorption. AFM must be performed in non-contact/tapping mode under an inert mini-environment or high-throughput sampling regime.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: SC-1 alkaline cleaning (NH4OH:H2O2:DIW) etches silicon via competing oxidation and dissolution mechanisms. An excessively high NH4OH ratio or temperature (>75°C) produces atomic-scale surface roughening via anisotropic micro-etching along Si(100) crystallographic terraces. For a 3.5 nm dry gate oxide, RMS roughness (Rq) must remain below 0.15 nm (1.5 Å); any Rq > 0.20 nm increases local electric field concentration, degrading time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB) and lowering low-field electron mobility in the inversion channel. Tip convolution artifacts must be mitigated by using sharpened silicon probes with tip radius < 7 nm.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Standard monolithic silicon AFM cantilevers (e.g., tap300Al-G) have high attrition rates due to tip dulling and crash events during manual or semi-automated loading. In open-source and low-tier foundry setups, sourcing high-resonance (300 kHz), ultra-sharp (<7 nm tip radius) probes with gold or aluminum reflex coating is prone to import lead times and cost escalations. A secondary qualification of batch-fabricated piezoresistive or standard silicon cantilevers with a strict tip qualification coupon protocol must be established.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: AFM is inherently a local physical metrology tool, not a full-wafer imaging scanner. Over-allocating inspection spots across production wafers will breach the 30-minute clean-to-furnace queue time window, stalling the DRAM gate oxide pipeline. Metrology protocol must define a 5-point representative die sampling map (Center, North, South, East, West at 3mm edge exclusion) and utilize dedicated dummy monitor wafers for destructive or lengthy AFM scans, clearing the prime wafer lot directly into the oxidation tube.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Tip crash or rapid tip blunting leading to artificial surface smoothing and false-negative roughness readings (reported Rq artificially low despite pitted Si substrate).
1. Q-time expiration during extended multi-site AFM scanning, leading to native oxide growth (>0.4 nm) and airborne molecular contamination (AMC) adsorption prior to dry thermal oxidation.
1. Mechanical and acoustic vibration coupling into the AFM stage inducing artificial high-frequency periodic ripples in the topograph, distorting spatial frequency PSD (Power Spectral Density) calculations.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-2-1-1-3-3-01` | **5-Point Wafer Surface RMS Microroughness Verification (1 um x 1 um)** | Atomic Force Microscope (Tapping/Non-Contact Mode, Sharpened Silicon Tip Radius < 7 nm, Resonance Frequency ~300 kHz, Acoustic Isolation Hood, Active Vibration Isolation Table) | 1. Load monitor wafer onto AFM vacuum chuck under localized ISO Class 1 laminar flow hood. 2. Align laser beam onto cantilever tip apex and center photodiode differential signal (A-B = 0.0 V, C-D = 0.0 V, Sum > 2.0 V). 3. Program automated 5-point recipe (Center, Top, Bottom, Left, Right at 10mm edge exclusion). 4. Perform auto-approach at Site 1 (Center). 5. Scan 1.0 um x 1.0 um area at 512 x 512 pixel resolution with a scan rate of 0.8 Hz. 6. Repeat scan for remaining 4 sites. 7. Apply 1st order line-fit flattening to raw height images and calculate Root Mean Square roughness (Rq) and average roughness (Ra). | `RMS surface microroughness (Rq) <= 0.15 nm (1.5 Å) across all 5 measured points. Peak-to-Valley height (Z-range) <= 1.2 nm. No localized etch pit defects with depth > 0.5 nm.` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-2-1-1-3-3-02` | **Tip Apex Quality and Power Spectral Density (PSD) Artifact Verification** | Atomic Force Microscope with Silicon Cantilever (Tip radius <= 7 nm), Standard Titanium Roughness Calibration Standard (RS-15M) or Polystyrene Spheres Standard | 1. Approach calibration reference grating and acquire 2.0 um x 2.0 um scan at 512 lines. 2. Calculate 1D/2D Power Spectral Density (PSD) spectrum from flattened topographic scan. 3. Check for tip-geometry dilation signatures or multi-tip artifacts (shadowed double-features). 4. Extract effective tip radius using blind tip reconstruction algorithm. 5. Move tip to test wafer and verify no feedback ringing or trace/retrace hysteresis divergence (>3%). | `Reconstructed tip radius <= 7.0 nm. Trace and retrace profile correlation >= 98.0%. PSD spectrum shows white noise floor at frequencies > 100 um^-1 with no discrete harmonic spikes from acoustic/electrical interference.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom bunny suit (low-linting polyester), Cleanroom nitrile gloves (double-gloved, powder-free, ESD-safe), Safety glasses with side shields (ANSI Z87.1 certified), ESD wrist strap or conductive ESD heel grounders
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of IPA eye contact: Flush eyes immediately with copious amounts of clean DI water or eyewash station for at least 15 minutes while holding eyelids open; seek medical evaluation. In case of skin exposure: Wash with cleanroom DI water and mild soap. In case of inhalation of solvent vapors: Move individual to fresh air.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: AFM operates in an enclosed acoustic isolation cabinet situated within an ISO Class 5 (Class 100) cleanroom laminar flow bay. Local solvent wipe stations utilize point exhaust hoods with face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) to vent volatile organic vapors.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: IPA-wetted cleanroom wipes are collected in a dedicated, sealed, flame-resistant flammable solid waste bin and disposed of via certified hazardous chemical waste handlers according to EPA/OSHA standards. No liquid chemical effluent discharged.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA, for tip/stage cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade / Semiconductor VLSI Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (N2, for blow-off)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra High Purity (UHP) Grade 6.0 | `99.9999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic, chemical-oxide terminated Si(100) surface post-SC-1 clean (native chemical oxide thickness ~0.6-0.8 nm, zero organic residues, surface free of loose particulate contamination).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Verified pristine flat Si(100) substrate with Rq <= 0.15 nm, free of tip contamination or organic drag tracks, cleared for immediate furnace boat loading.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding 30 minutes in cleanroom air results in airborne molecular contamination (volatile organic compounds/siloxanes) and unconstrained native oxide growth (>1.0 nm total thickness with irregular stoichiometry), which severely degrades 3.5 nm dry gate oxide thickness uniformity, increases D_it (interface trap density), and induces premature gate dielectric breakdown.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful non-destructive acquisition, processing, and metrological signoff of the post-SC-1 Si(100) surface microroughness across a 5-point wafer inspection map. The wafer meets sub-0.15 nm RMS roughness criteria, confirming absence of caustic chemical micro-roughening and ensuring ideal substrate planarity for 3.5 nm dry gate dielectric growth.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `AFM_SC1_Microroughness_5Point_Topography_Map.tiff`
- [ ] `AFM_PreOx_Roughness_Statistical_Metrics.csv`
- [ ] `Metrology_Signoff_GateOx_Substrate_PassReport.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Root Mean Square microroughness (Rq) of Si(100) over 1 um x 1 um scan area** | `0.12 nm` | <= 0.15 nm | AFM Tapping Mode, 512x512 pixels, 1st order flattening, 5-point wafer average |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Maximum Peak-to-Valley topographic height variation (Rmax / Z-range)** | `0.80 nm` | <= 1.20 nm | AFM Topography Height Channel Histogram Analysis |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Total metrology cycle time per monitor wafer to protect Q-time envelope** | `18.0 min` | <= 25.0 min | Automated AFM recipe run-timer log |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 5 inspection sites exhibit Rq <= 0.15 nm and Z-range <= 1.2 nm with no evidence of tip blunting or cantilever drag artifacts. The CSV metrics report is electronically signed and linked into the MES furnace track, releasing prime lot wafers to pre-diffusion loading within the remaining <= 10 minute air Q-time budget.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Dilute HF Oxide Strip and SC-2 Heavy Metal Decontamination Sequence

**Process Domain**: Wet Chemistry & Surface Preparation  
**Parent Integration**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip — 180nm Dry Gate Oxide Growth (3.5 nm)  
**Generation**: Gen 2 (µm) / 180nm Node  
**Action Type**: Make  

---

### Process Workflow Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Pre-Oxidation Wet    │
│      Bench Ready       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Step 1: Dilute HF    │
│    Dip 50:1 / 100:1    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Step 2: Quick Dump   │
│   Rinse QDR DI Water   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Step 3: SC-2 Bath    │
│    HCl:H2O2:H2O at     │
│         75-80C         │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Step 4: Final      │
│   Overflow Rinse DI    │
│         Water          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Step 5: Surface     │
│  Surface Conditioning  │
│         Check          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      Dry Thermal       │
│  Oxidation: 850C-900C  │
│     for 3.5nm SiO2     │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Substrate Pre-Inspection & Chemical Tank Setup**:
   - Verify wet bench tank temperatures and circulation flow rates.
   - Prepare DHF tank with ultra-pure dilute hydrofluoric acid ($50:1$ to $100:1$ $\text{DI H}_2\text{O}:\text{HF}$, $0.5\%-1.0\%\text{ HF}$ by volume) at ambient temperature ($21^\circ\text{C} \pm 1^\circ\text{C}$).
   - Prepare Standard Clean 2 (SC-2 / RCA Clean Part 2) tank with $\text{HCl}:\text{H}_2\text{O}_2:\text{DI H}_2\text{O}$ mixture heated to $75^\circ\text{C}-80^\circ\text{C}$.

2. **Native Oxide Strip (Dilute HF Dip)**:
   - Submerge the wafer cassette into the DHF bath for $60\text{ s}$ to $90\text{ s}$ to completely strip native and chemical surface oxide layers.
   - Etch reaction strips the chemical oxide down to bare single-crystal silicon substrate, forming a hydrogen-terminated, hydrophobic silicon surface.

3. **Intermediate Quick Dump Rinse (QDR)**:
   - Transfer cassette immediately (< 5 seconds transit) to the QDR tank.
   - Execute 4 dump-and-fill cycles using high-purity deionized water ($\text{resistivity} \ge 18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$) to stop acid carryover.

4. **Heavy Metal Decontamination (SC-2 Bath)**:
   - Immersion in the SC-2 tank ($\text{HCl}:\text{H}_2\text{O}_2:\text{DI H}_2\text{O}$ at $75^\circ\text{C}-80^\circ\text{C}$) for $10\text{ minutes}$.
   - Solubilize and complex metallic contaminants (alkali, iron, copper, and heavy metals) into soluble metal chlorides, simultaneously passivating the silicon with a controlled, pristine chemical oxide protective layer.

5. **Final Overflow Rinse & Surface Dry**:
   - Transfer to cascade overflow DI rinse tank; rinse until tank discharge effluent achieves resistivity $> 18.0\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$.
   - Dry wafers using Surface Tension gradient / Marangoni or Isopropanol (IPA) vapor dry to prevent watermarks and particle redeposition.
   - Stage directly into clean dry $\text{N}_2$ pod for transfer to the quartz tube furnace within a maximum queue time ($Q\text{-time} < 2\text{ hours}$).

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                 Acceptance & Thermal Process Criteria  
              ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
              │░                                       │
D_it Threshold┤░                                       │
              │▓                                       │
  Physical Tox┤▓                                       │
Oxidation Temp┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
              │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
   E_bd Target┤█                                       │
              │█                                       │
              └┬─────────┬─────────┬────────┬─────────┬┘
               0        225       450      675      900 
```

1. **Downstream Gate Dielectric Breakdown Field ($E_{bd}$)**:
   - **Target**: $E_{bd} > 10\text{ MV/cm}$
   - **Unit**: $\text{MV/cm}$
   - *Source Verification*: Verified literature context (*Deal-Grove Silicon Thermal Oxidation Kinetics in Quartz Tube Furnace*).

2. **Downstream Interface Trap Density ($D_{it}$)**:
   - **Target**: $D_{it} < 10^{10}\text{ cm}^{-2}\cdot\text{eV}^{-1}$
   - **Unit**: $\text{cm}^{-2}\cdot\text{eV}^{-1}$
   - *Source Verification*: Verified literature context (*Deal-Grove Silicon Thermal Oxidation Kinetics in Quartz Tube Furnace*).

3. **Subsequent Dry Thermal Oxidation Process Temperature**:
   - **Target**: $850^\circ\text{C}\text{ to }900^\circ\text{C}$ (dry oxidation regime in pure dry $\text{O}_2$)
   - **Unit**: $^\circ\text{C}$
   - *Source Verification*: Verified literature context (*Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering* and *Deal-Grove Silicon Thermal Oxidation Kinetics in Quartz Tube Furnace*).

4. **Target Grown Physical Gate Oxide Thickness ($T_{ox}$)**:
   - **Target**: $3.5\text{ nm}$ (acceptable range $3.5\text{ nm to }4.0\text{ nm}$)
   - **Unit**: $\text{nm}$
   - *Source Verification*: Verified literature context (*Deal-Grove Silicon Thermal Oxidation Kinetics in Quartz Tube Furnace* and *Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering*).

---

### Verified Context Citations
- **Deal-Grove Silicon Thermal Oxidation Kinetics in Quartz Tube Furnace**: Citations for dry oxidation temperature ($900^\circ\text{C}-1000^\circ\text{C}$ / dry $\text{O}_2$), high-dielectric breakdown target ($E_{bd} > 10\text{ MV/cm}$), minimal interface trap density ($D_{it} < 10^{10}\text{ cm}^{-2}\cdot\text{eV}^{-1}$), and physical thickness target ($3.5\text{ to }4.0\text{ nm}$).
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**: Citations for gate dielectric thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ at $850^\circ\text{C}-900^\circ\text{C}$ dry oxidation with $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ physical thickness.
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**: Integration context for 180nm access transistor ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The integration sequence between DHF oxide stripping and SC-2 must enforce tight process automation. While DHF terminates the silicon surface with hydrogen (producing a hydrophobic Si-H bond network), introducing hydrophobic wafers directly into an oxidizing acidic SC-2 bath (HCl:H2O2:UPW at 75°C) can cause non-uniform chemical re-oxidation, micro-bubble pinning, and localized pit etching if surfactant-free rinse or immersion dynamics are suboptimal. The dump rinse transfer speed and immersion profile must be tightly coupled to eliminate transit drying artifacts.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For 3.5 nm dry gate oxide reliability, metallic contamination (specifically Fe, Cu, Ni) must be suppressed below 1E10 atoms/cm² to prevent premature time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB) and gate leakage in the DRAM access transistor. SC-2 effectively desorbs metals via soluble chlorocomplex formation ([FeCl6]3-, [CuCl4]2-), while simultaneously growing a clean, passivating, chemical oxide layer of ~0.6-0.8 nm. The chemical oxide quality sets the initial interfacial roughness and seed layer for dry thermal oxidation at 850°C-900°C.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Hydrofluoric acid (HF 49%) and Hydrochloric acid (HCl 37%) must strictly meet SEMI Grade 5 (parts-per-trillion ionic purity) to avoid cross-contaminating pristine silicon baths with trace transition metals. In-country supply chains in Vietnam must ensure fluoropolymer-lined drums (PFA/PVDF) with intact lot-level ICP-MS certificates of analysis (CoA), avoiding prolonged storage that induces container leaching or peroxide decomposition in stabilized 30% H2O2.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The sequence is the gatekeeper step for gate dielectric thermal budget execution. Wet bench MTBF and bath life (maximum 4 hours for SC-2 due to H2O2 thermal dismutation at 75°C) must be scheduled concurrently with vertical oxidation furnace idle windows to satisfy the stringent pre-oxidation Q-time constraint without wafer scrapping or re-cleaning cycles.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Micro-roughening and pitting of bare silicon surface during transition from DHF to hot acidic SC-2 if dissolved oxygen and redox potential are unmonitored.
1. Incomplete oxide strip during DHF dip resulting in islands of native oxide with trapped interface states (Dit > 5E11 eV⁻¹cm⁻²) beneath the 3.5 nm gate oxide.
1. Peroxide depletion in heated SC-2 (75°C) leading to bath reduction potential drop, causing noble metal (e.g., Cu) redeposition onto bare/chemically oxidized silicon.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-2-1-2-01` | **DHF Hydrophobic Stripping Efficiency and Native Oxide Removal Verification** | Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (J.A. Woollam M-2000 or equivalent) and Automated Optical Contact Angle Goniometer (Krüss DSA100) | 1. Immerse wafer in 1:50 DHF (dilute HF:UPW) bath at 21.0°C +/- 0.5°C for 30 seconds. 2. Cascade dump rinse with 18.2 MOhm-cm UPW for 180 seconds until bath resistivity exceeds 18.0 MOhm-cm. 3. Spin dry under filtered N2 (0.02 um filter). 4. Perform 49-point spectroscopic ellipsometry mapping across wafer diameter. 5. critics.systems_engineer: The integration sequence between DHF oxide stripping and SC-2 must enforce tight process automation. While DHF terminates the silicon surface with hydrogen (producing a hydrophobic Si-H bond network), introducing hydrophobic wafers directly into an oxidizing acidic SC-2 bath (HCl:H2O2:UPW at 75°C) can cause non-uniform chemical re-oxidation, micro-bubble pinning, and localized pit etching if surfactant-free rinse or immersion dynamics are suboptimal. The dump rinse transfer speed and immersion profile must be tightly coupled to eliminate transit drying artifacts.
critics.domain_expert: For 3.5 nm dry gate oxide reliability, metallic contamination (specifically Fe, Cu, Ni) must be suppressed below 1E10 atoms/cm² to prevent premature time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB) and gate leakage in the DRAM access transistor. SC-2 effectively desorbs metals via soluble chlorocomplex formation ([FeCl6]3-, [CuCl4]2-), while simultaneously growing a clean, passivating, chemical oxide layer of ~0.6-0.8 nm. The chemical oxide quality sets the initial interfacial roughness and seed layer for dry thermal oxidation at 850°C-900°C.
critics.supply_chain: Hydrofluoric acid (HF 49%) and Hydrochloric acid (HCl 37%) must strictly meet SEMI Grade 5 (parts-per-trillion ionic purity) to avoid cross-contaminating pristine silicon baths with trace transition metals. In-country supply chains in Vietnam must ensure fluoropolymer-lined drums (PFA/PVDF) with intact lot-level ICP-MS certificates of analysis (CoA), avoiding prolonged storage that induces container leaching or peroxide decomposition in stabilized 30% H2O2.
critics.laya_pm: The sequence is the gatekeeper step for gate dielectric thermal budget execution. Wet bench MTBF and bath life (maximum 4 hours for SC-2 due to H2O2 thermal dismutation at 75°C) must be scheduled concurrently with vertical oxidation furnace idle windows to satisfy the stringent pre-oxidation Q-time constraint without wafer scrapping or re-cleaning cycles.
critical_failure_modes: Micro-roughening and pitting of bare silicon surface during transition from DHF to hot acidic SC-2 if dissolved oxygen and redox potential are unmonitored.
Incomplete oxide strip during DHF dip resulting in islands of native oxide with trapped interface states (Dit > 5E11 eV⁻¹cm⁻²) beneath the 3.5 nm gate oxide.
Peroxide depletion in heated SC-2 (75°C) leading to bath reduction potential drop, causing noble metal (e.g., Cu) redeposition onto bare/chemically oxidized silicon.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): Dilute HF Native Oxide Strip and Hydrophobic Surface Transition Verification

**Discipline / Context**: Context: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) [Architecture & Integration] > 180nm Dry Gate Oxide Growth (3.5 nm) [Thermal Processing] > Dry Thermal Oxidation Recipe Execution (850°C-900°C, 3.5 nm SiO2) [Thermal Oxidation] > RCA Clean and Pre-Oxidation Surface Conditioning (SC-1/SC-2/DHF Dip) [Wet Chemistry] > Dilute HF Oxide Strip and SC-2 Heavy Metal Decontamination Sequence [Wet Chemistry] > Dilute HF Native Oxide Strip and Hydrophobic Surface Transition Verification [Wet Chemistry]
**Target Generation**: Gen 1 (mm) | **Action Type**: Make

### 1. Equipment & Environmental Pre-Flight
- Verify cleanroom ambient conditions (Class 1000 / Class 100 laminar flow hood, Temp: 21°C ± 1°C, Humidity: 45% ± 5%).
- Inspect facility interlocks (exhaust velocity > 0.5 m/s, DI water loop > 18.0 MΩ·cm).

### 2. Physical Tool Calibration & Fixturing
- Mount substrate onto vacuum chuck stage and align optical/mechanical fiducials.
- Zero calibration instruments and establish baseline noise floor.

### 3. Process Execution & Parameter Validation
- Execute process sequence according to verified recipe parameters: Oxide Thickness Tox: 3.5 nm (Gate) / 350 nm (Field).
- Monitor thermal/chemical/optical transients during execution.

### 4. Post-Process Metrology & Quality Acceptance
- Perform physical verification using Spectroscopic Ellipsometer / C-V Profiler.
- Log 10 consecutive measurement cycles to guarantee process repeatability (Cp/Cpk >= 1.33).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The transition from hydrophilic chemical oxide (post-SC-1) to hydrogen-terminated hydrophobic silicon upon dilute HF (DHF 50:1 or 100:1) etch creates a severe particle re-deposition vulnerability. Once the surface becomes hydrophobic, non-polar organics and particulate contaminants in the liquid-air interface adhere strongly via capillary forces during wafer pull-out. The wet bench must utilize Marangoni drying or isopropyl alcohol (IPA) vapor drying rather than standard spin-rinse drying to avoid catastrophic defect clusters prior to gate oxidation.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Etching native/chemical oxide (~1.0-1.5 nm) in DHF (0.5-1.0 wt% HF) requires strict immersion time tuning (30-60 s) to achieve complete silicon-hydrogen (Si-H) monohydride/dihydride passivation without micro-roughening the underlying Si(100) surface. Over-etching induces pit formation via OH- ion attack, which degrades gate oxide breakdown field (Ebd) and increases interface trap density (Dit) beyond the 1e10 cm^-2 eV^-1 threshold required for 3.5 nm DRAM gate dielectric integrity.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Aqueous hydrofluoric acid must be sourced strictly at SEMI Grade 5 (UP-S / PPT grade) with trace metallic impurities (Fe, Cu, Ni, Ca) guaranteed below 10 ppt. Local sourcing in Vietnam must account for specialized fluoropolymer (PVDF/PFA) containment logistics; standard electronic grade (ppb level) chemicals will cause metallic contamination plating onto the electronegative bare silicon during the strip.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Strict automation and interlock tracking are required for the chemical bath lifetime. DHF baths exhibit fluoride evaporation and ambient silica loading; bath life must be capped at 8 operating hours or 50 wafer runs. Transitioning to the subsequent SC-2 clean and thermal oxidation furnace must enforce strict automated Q-time gate enforcement in the MES to prevent unmonitored atmospheric re-oxidation.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Incomplete oxide strip leaving patchy sub-oxide (SiOx, x < 2), yielding non-uniform incubation time and gate oxide thickness variations exceeding +/- 0.5 nm.
1. Immersion time over-run or bath contamination causing micro-pitting and surface copper/noble-metal galvanic plating, resulting in catastrophic gate dielectric breakdown leakage.
1. Particle pickup at the liquid-gas interface during bath pull-out due to inadequate Marangoni surface tension gradient, generating localized pinholes in the 3.5 nm thermal gate oxide.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-2-1-2-1-01` | **Goniometric Deionized Water Contact Angle Hydrophobic Verification** | Automated Sessile Drop Contact Angle Goniometer with micro-syringe dispenser (accuracy +/- 0.5 deg) | 1. Transfer wafer directly from dryer to goniometer chamber under filtered N2 purge. 2. Dispense a 2.0 uL droplet of ultra-pure deionized water (resistivity 18.2 MOhm-cm at 25 deg C) onto five standard monitoring sites (Center, North, South, East, West at 10 mm edge exclusion). 3. Capture droplet profile image at 100 ms after stabilization. 4. Calculate static contact angle using Young-Laplace fitting algorithm across all 5 points. | `Static DI water contact angle must be >= 75.0 degrees across all 5 test points (confirming uniform H-termination), with within-wafer variation standard deviation sigma <= 2.5 degrees. Contact angle < 70 degrees constitutes failure (residual hydrophilic oxide).` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-2-1-2-1-02` | **Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Residual Oxide Thickness and Passivation Cleanness** | Multi-angle Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (wavelength range 190 nm to 1000 nm, beam spot diameter <= 1 mm) | 1. Align wafer stage to Si(100) crystal orientation flat/notch. 2. Measure optical parameters Psi and Delta across 49 points in polar mapping configuration. 3. Fit data using Cauchy/Sellmeier optical dispersion model initialized with native SiO2 on bulk Si. 4. Extract effective residual dielectric film thickness across all 49 points. | `Mean residual oxide equivalent thickness must be <= 0.15 nm (equivalent to monolayer sub-oxide/adventitious carbon baseline) with zero points exhibiting residual SiO2 >= 0.30 nm. Total oxide removal uniformity must show 100% strip across the 49-point map.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Heavyweight fluoroelastomer (Viton/Butyl) chemical gloves over inner nitrile gloves (ASTM F739 tested), Chemical-resistant neoprene/PVDF apron with full-length sleeves, Full-face polycarbonate splash shield (ANSI Z87.1) combined with indirect-vent chemical splash goggles, Air-purifying dual-cartridge half-mask respirator fitted with HF/Acid Gas and P100 particulate filters (or continuous positive-pressure air supply hood for bulk preparation), Steel-toe rubber safety boots with acid-resistant gaiters
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Calcium gluconate gel (2.5% USP) must be visibly staged within 1 meter of the wet bench and unexpired. In case of skin exposure: immediately flush with copious running cold water for exactly 60 seconds while removing contaminated PPE, then generously massage 2.5% calcium gluconate gel into the affected area wearing clean nitrile gloves, re-applying every 10 minutes until medical personnel take over. For eye contact: flush immediately at eyewash for >= 15 minutes with sterile 1% calcium gluconate ophthalmic solution or isotonic saline. HF penetrates skin non-dissociated and scavenges systemic Ca2+ and Mg2+, inducing fatal cardiac arrhythmia; emergency medical transport is mandatory for all exposures.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous dedicated polypropylene wet bench wet-scrubber exhaust with slot velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM face velocity at the sash opening), differential pressure interlocked with audio-visual alarm at < 0.20 in-w.g. Exhaust vented exclusively to an active recirculating alkaline fume scrubber (NaOH liquor maintained at pH 9.0-10.5).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent DHF effluent must be plumbed via dedicated double-contained fluoropolymer (PVDF) lines to the fluoride wastewater treatment facility. Automated two-stage neutralization: Stage 1 precipitation with hydrated lime (Calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)2) forming insoluble fluorite (CaF2) at pH 8.0-9.0, followed by coagulant flocculation and clarification to meet strict municipal discharge limit of F- < 15 ppm.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid (Aqueous)** | `7664-39-3` | SEMI Grade 5 (UP-S / PPT) | `0.98% wt (50:1 dilution from 49% stock)` |
| **Ultra-Pure Water (DIW)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type E-1.1 Microelectronics Grade | `99.02% wt (Resistivity 18.2 MOhm-cm at 25C)` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic SC-1 chemical oxide (~1.2 nm thick, saturated with Si-OH silanol groups, particle-depleted)
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophobic, hydrogen-passivated bare silicon (Si(100):2x1-H monohydride/dihydride surface, contact angle >= 75 deg)
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exposure to ambient cleanroom air beyond 30 minutes results in uncontrolled adventitious hydrocarbon adsorption and irregular native oxide regrowth (SiOx), disrupting Deal-Grove linear oxidation kinetics and inducing uncorrectable EOT thickness non-uniformity and high gate leakage.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Complete dissolution and stripping of pre-clean chemical/native silicon dioxide, leaving an atomically clean, hydrogen-terminated, fully hydrophobic Si(100) wafer surface ready for immediate SC-2 metallic strip and thermal gate oxide growth.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-2-1-2-1-01_contact_angle_map.csv`
- [ ] `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-2-1-2-1-02_ellipsometry_residual_oxide_report.pdf`
- [ ] `dhf_wafer_surface_optical_inspection_map.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Mean static deionized water contact angle across 5 inspection sites** | `78.0 deg` | +/- 3.0 deg (Lower specification limit: >= 75.0 deg) | Automated sessile-drop contact angle goniometry with 2.0 uL ultra-pure water droplet |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Post-strip residual equivalent SiO2 thickness** | `0.08 nm` | +0.07 nm / -0.08 nm (Upper specification limit: <= 0.15 nm) | 49-point polar spectroscopic ellipsometry fitted with native SiO2 optical dispersion model |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Surface particle addition count at >= 0.18 um defect size bin** | `0 particles/wafer` | <= 5 particles added across 150mm/200mm wafer surface | Total wafer surface scanning laser inspection system (darkfield scattering) |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Wafer surface achieves complete de-wetting (DI water sheet rolls off instantly with contact angle >= 75.0 deg at all measurement points), residual oxide thickness confirmed <= 0.15 nm, delta particle count <= 5 at 0.18 um, and wafer is loaded into SC-2 chemical bath or nitrogen-purged FOUP/SMIF pod within 10 minutes of drying.

testcases.title: Goniometric Deionized Water Contact Angle Hydrophobic Verification
testcases.instrumentation: Automated Sessile Drop Contact Angle Goniometer with micro-syringe dispenser (accuracy +/- 0.5 deg)
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafer has undergone SC-1 pre-clean, megasonic DI water rinse, 45-second 50:1 DHF strip, quick-dump rinse (QDR), and Marangoni drying within Class 1 cleanroom environment.
testcases.procedure: 1. Transfer wafer directly from dryer to goniometer chamber under filtered N2 purge. 2. Dispense a 2.0 uL droplet of ultra-pure deionized water (resistivity 18.2 MOhm-cm at 25 deg C) onto five standard monitoring sites (Center, North, South, East, West at 10 mm edge exclusion). 3. Capture droplet profile image at 100 ms after stabilization. 4. Calculate static contact angle using Young-Laplace fitting algorithm across all 5 points.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Static DI water contact angle must be >= 75.0 degrees across all 5 test points (confirming uniform H-termination), with within-wafer variation standard deviation sigma <= 2.5 degrees. Contact angle < 70 degrees constitutes failure (residual hydrophilic oxide).

testcases.title: Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Residual Oxide Thickness and Passivation Cleanness
testcases.instrumentation: Multi-angle Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (wavelength range 190 nm to 1000 nm, beam spot diameter <= 1 mm)
testcases.pre_conditions: Tool baseline calibrated against certified Si reference standard. Wafer loaded within 5 minutes post-DHF strip and dry.
testcases.procedure: 1. Align wafer stage to Si(100) crystal orientation flat/notch. 2. Measure optical parameters Psi and Delta across 49 points in polar mapping configuration. 3. Fit data using Cauchy/Sellmeier optical dispersion model initialized with native SiO2 on bulk Si. 4. Extract effective residual dielectric film thickness across all 49 points.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Mean residual oxide equivalent thickness must be <= 0.15 nm (equivalent to monolayer sub-oxide/adventitious carbon baseline) with zero points exhibiting residual SiO2 >= 0.30 nm. Total oxide removal uniformity must show 100% strip across the 49-point map.

ppe_required: Heavyweight fluoroelastomer (Viton/Butyl) chemical gloves over inner nitrile gloves (ASTM F739 tested)
Chemical-resistant neoprene/PVDF apron with full-length sleeves
Full-face polycarbonate splash shield (ANSI Z87.1) combined with indirect-vent chemical splash goggles
Air-purifying dual-cartridge half-mask respirator fitted with HF/Acid Gas and P100 particulate filters (or continuous positive-pressure air supply hood for bulk preparation)
Steel-toe rubber safety boots with acid-resistant gaiters
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: Calcium gluconate gel (2.5% USP) must be visibly staged within 1 meter of the wet bench and unexpired. In case of skin exposure: immediately flush with copious running cold water for exactly 60 seconds while removing contaminated PPE, then generously massage 2.5% calcium gluconate gel into the affected area wearing clean nitrile gloves, re-applying every 10 minutes until medical personnel take over. For eye contact: flush immediately at eyewash for >= 15 minutes with sterile 1% calcium gluconate ophthalmic solution or isotonic saline. HF penetrates skin non-dissociated and scavenges systemic Ca2+ and Mg2+, inducing fatal cardiac arrhythmia; emergency medical transport is mandatory for all exposures.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Continuous dedicated polypropylene wet bench wet-scrubber exhaust with slot velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM face velocity at the sash opening), differential pressure interlocked with audio-visual alarm at < 0.20 in-w.g. q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Hydrophobic, hydrogen-passivated bare silicon (Si(100):2x1-H monohydride/dihydride surface, contact angle >= 75 deg)

expected_result.summary: Complete dissolution and stripping of pre-clean chemical/native silicon dioxide, leaving an atomically clean, hydrogen-terminated, fully hydrophobic Si(100) wafer surface ready for immediate SC-2 metallic strip and thermal gate oxide growth.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Post-strip residual equivalent SiO2 thickness

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-FAB-WET-180-DHF01`  
**Title:** Precision Tooling & Fixturing for Dilute HF Native Oxide Strip and Hydrophobic Surface Transition Verification  
**Hierarchy Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > 180nm Dry Gate Oxide Growth (3.5 nm) > Dry Thermal Oxidation Recipe Execution (850°C–900°C, 3.5 nm SiO₂) > RCA Clean & Pre-Oxidation Surface Conditioning > Dilute HF Oxide Strip and SC-2 Heavy Metal Decontamination Sequence > Dilute HF Native Oxide Strip and Hydrophobic Surface Transition Verification > **Precision Tooling & Fixturing [Mechanical Assembly]**  
**Action Type:** Make  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm / 180nm)

---

### 1. Scope & Objective
This procedure specifies the mechanical assembly, setup, alignment, and execution parameters for the precision fluoropolymer (PTFE/PFA) wafer carrier fixture used during the pre-gate oxidation dilute hydrofluoric acid (DHF/BOE) native oxide strip. It provides direct verification protocols for the chemical hydrophobic transition (H-passivated bare silicon) prior to 850°C–900°C dry gate thermal oxidation (3.5 nm SiO₂ target).

---

### 2. Required Tooling, Fixtures & Safety Equipment
* **Precision Chemical Fixturing:** CNC-machined PFA/PTFE immersion cassette with 25-wafer capacity, slot pitch matching standard 180nm front-end handling, and minimal contact edge-exclusion grips (< 3.0 mm).
* **Wet Bench Immersion Tank:** Recirculating, filtered bath with temperature control maintained at **25°C**.
* **Chemical Safety & First Aid:**
  * Hydrofluoric acid PPE: Acid-resistant neoprene/nitrile double gloves, face shield, and chemical apron.
  * **First Aid Requirement:** Calcium gluconate gel must be present and verified at the bench station at all times (*Source: Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)*).
* **Process Chemicals:**
  * BOE 6:1 formulation: 6 parts 40% NH₄F (Ammonium Fluoride) to 1 part 49% HF (Hydrofluoric Acid) (*Source: Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)*).
  * Wetting surfactant: 0.1% Triton X-100 or Fluorad added to eliminate micro-trench bubble entrapment (*Source: Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)*).
* **Inspection & Metrology:** Deionized water (DIW) cascade overflow rinse tank, optical contact-angle goniometer / optical beading inspection station, and clean dry N₂ blow gun.

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Procedure

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Step 1: PFA/PTFE Fixture Inspection & Bath Prep (25°C)"] --> B["Step 2: Wafer Loading into Precision Edge-Grip Carrier"]
    B --> C["Step 3: Controlled Immersion & Native Oxide Etch (100 nm/min baseline)"]
    C --> D["Step 4: Cascade DI Water Quick Dump Rinse (QDR)"]
    D --> E["Step 5: Surface Dewetting / Hydrophobic Beading Verification"]
    E --> F["Step 6: Controlled N2 Spin/Dry & Transfer to 850°C-900°C Furnace"]
```

#### Step 1: Fixture Inspection and Bath Setup
1. Inspect the PFA/PTFE immersion carrier for micro-cracks, mechanical distortion, or particulate buildup. Verify slot perpendicularity and latching mechanism.
2. Confirm the BOE / Dilute HF bath temperature stabilizes at **25°C** (*Source: Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)*).
3. Verify bath surfactant addition (0.1% Triton X-100 or Fluorad) to ensure complete wetting without bubble entrapment.
4. Verify the physical presence of unexpired calcium gluconate gel at the wet bench operator console.

#### Step 2: Wafer Loading and Edge-Exclusion Alignment
1. Load 180nm DRAM patterned/test wafers into the PTFE cassette with active device surfaces facing the recirculating laminar chemical flow.
2. Ensure edge-gripping contact is restricted strictly to the outer perimeter exclusion zone (< 3.0 mm) to protect active memory cell access regions ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$).

#### Step 3: Controlled Chemical Immersion & Etch Execution
1. Using the automated pneumatic hoist fixture, lower the carrier cassette into the 25°C BOE/DHF bath at a controlled immersion rate of 15–20 mm/s.
2. Agitate vertically with a travel stroke of $\pm 5\text{ mm}$ at 0.5 Hz to maintain uniform etchant replenishment across the wafer array.
3. Maintain etch contact time tailored to clear native oxide (~1.5–2.0 nm) and residual interface oxide based on the 25°C BOE etch rate baseline of **100 nm/minute (1000 Å/min)** (*Source: Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)*).

#### Step 4: Rapid Transfer and DI Water Quench
1. Elevate the fixture smoothly from the etch bath and transfer within < 5 seconds to the Quick Dump Rinse (QDR) / Cascade DI water overflow tank.
2. Execute 4 QDR cycles followed by continuous cascade rinse until bath resistivity reaches $\ge 18.0\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$.

#### Step 5: Hydrophobic Surface Transition Verification
1. Inspect the silicon surface upon carrier withdrawal from the final rinse:
   * **Hydrophilic State (Incomplete Etch / Oxide Present):** Continuous, unbroken liquid water sheet clinging to the wafer face.
   * **Hydrophobic State (Complete Oxide Strip / H-Terminated Si):** Complete, spontaneous liquid dewetting; DI water immediately beads up into discrete droplets and rolls off the active Si surface with zero wetting sheath.
2. For analytical qualification lots, transfer coupon/monitor wafer to the goniometer and record DI water contact angle (target $> 75^\circ$).

#### Step 6: Fixture Spin-Drying & Furnace Staging
1. Transfer the carrier to the automated wafer spin-rinse dryer (SRD) or N₂ marangoni drying station.
2. Immediately seal the dried wafers in an ultra-pure N₂ purged FOUP/pod to prevent room-air native re-oxidation.
3. Transfer the lot to the thermal oxidation queue for immediate 850°C–900°C dry gate oxide growth to deposit the nominal 3.5 nm SiO₂ layer (*Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering*).

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance | Source Reference |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **BOE / DHF Bath Temperature** | $25\text{ °C}$ | $\pm 0.5\text{ °C}$ | *Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)* |
| **Thermally Grown SiO₂ Reference Etch Rate** | $100\text{ nm/min}$ ($1000\text{ \AA/min}$) | $\pm 5\text{ nm/min}$ | *Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)* |
| **Post-Strip Thermal Gate Oxide Physical Thickness** | $3.5\text{ nm}$ | $\pm 0.2\text{ nm}$ | *Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering* |
| **Target Dry Gate Oxidation Processing Temp** | $850\text{ °C to } 900\text{ °C}$ | $\pm 2\text{ °C}$ | *Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering* |

---

### 5. Context Literature Citations
* **Etch Rates, Wetting Agent, and HF Safety:** Sourced directly from *Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)* (BOE 6:1 composition, 100 nm/min etch rate at 25°C, 0.1% Triton X-100 / Fluorad surfactant, and mandatory calcium gluconate gel).
* **Thermal Gate Dielectric Target & Temperature:** Sourced directly from *Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering* (Gate dielectric physical thickness of ~3.5 nm SiO₂, grown via dry oxidation at 850°C–900°C).
* **Active Cell Geometry & Alignment Integrity:** Sourced from *180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench* (Access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The Gen 1 mechanical fixture must interface chemically inert fluoropolymers (PTFE/PFA) with manual or semi-automated wet immersion dip tanks while isolating wafer clamping stress. Gen 1 millimeter-level mechanical alignment tolerances (±0.1 mm) must guarantee zero mechanical chipping or edge exclusion intrusion beyond 3 mm from wafer edge, while ensuring fluidic boundary layer clearance during the rapid de-wetting transition.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Direct exposure to dilute hydrofluoric acid (typically 0.5% to 1.0% DHF or 50:1 H2O:HF) strips native chemical SiO2 (~1.2 nm) and hydrogen-terminates the dangling silicon bonds (Si-H). Fixturing must avoid capillary liquid entrapment at contact points; trapped DHF leads to localized over-etching or uncontrolled micro-droplet residue, inducing surface roughness (>0.2 nm RMS) that fatally degrades 3.5 nm gate oxide breakdown voltage.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Virgin semiconductor-grade PTFE or ultra-pure PFA rod and sheet stock must be procured to machine custom cassettes and dip-fixtures. Metallic fasteners (stainless steel, titanium) or standard nitrile/viton components are strictly forbidden due to severe HF vapor corrosion and trace transition metal contamination (Fe, Cu, Ni > 1e10 atoms/cm2); all threaded fasteners and pins must be machined PFA or PVDF.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Because this tool serves Gen 1 exploratory manual benches prior to automated wet bench integration, the assembly must be machinable using standard workshop CNC/lathe equipment within 5 working days, using off-the-shelf PFA bolts, and yield repeatable hydrophobic dewet verification without requiring an automated contact angle goniometer on the wet line.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Capillary retention of aqueous HF solution at PTFE contact claws causing localized over-etching, edge corrosion, and particulate contamination during wafer transfer.
1. Mechanical micro-cleavage or edge-stress fracturing of the 180nm silicon wafer due to rigid thermal expansion mismatch or excessive clamping torque on PTFE/PFA brackets.
1. Atmospheric re-oxidation or particulate deposition during slow manual transfer from HF bath to deionized water rinse due to suboptimal fixture drainage angles.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-2-1-2-1-1-01` | **Fixturing Hydrophobic Drainage and Fluid Entrapment Clearance Verification** | Calibrated mechanical balance (0.1 mg resolution), digital high-speed macro camera (60 fps), optical inspection microscope (50x-200x) | 1. Secure test wafer into the fixture with standard finger-tight PFA thumbscrews. 2. Fully immerse the fixture and wafer in 1% DHF simulated solution (DI water bath with surfactant) for 60 seconds. 3. Withdraw vertically at a controlled rate of 50 mm/s. 4. Record liquid sheeting behavior and contact-point drainage via 60 fps macro video. 5. Inspect wafer-to-claw interface under 100x optical microscope for trapped meniscus residual droplets within 10 seconds of withdrawal. | `Wafer surface must exhibit uniform de-wetting without liquid pooling; residual fluid meniscus at contact claws must be less than 0.5 mm in radial depth; zero droplet retention on the active area (>3 mm from edge).` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-2-1-2-1-1-02` | **Post-Strip Hydrophobic Surface Transition and Contact Angle Metric** | Session sessile drop contact angle goniometer (or calibrated digital micro-pipette 5 uL with profile imaging software), spectroscopic ellipsometer (Woollam M-2000 or equivalent) | 1. Unload wafer from PFA fixture under Class 100 laminar flow hood. 2. Deposit 5.0 uL ultra-pure DI water droplets at 5 points across the wafer (center and 4 orthogonal points at R=35mm). 3. Capture droplet profiles within 60 seconds to prevent evaporative drift and measure static contact angle. 4. Transfer immediately to spectroscopic ellipsometer to measure residual SiO2 thickness. | `Static contact angle of DI water droplet must exceed 75.0 degrees across all 5 points (indicating complete Si-H termination); residual oxide thickness measured via ellipsometry must be <= 0.20 nm.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Neoprene/Viton heavy-duty chemical-resistant overgloves over double nitrile undergloves, Full-face polycarbonate splash shield with chin protector, Acid-resistant heavy-duty apron (PVDF/PTFE or heavy Neoprene), Chemical safety splash goggles meeting ANSI Z87.1 D3 rating, Closed-toe chemical-resistant boots with acid gaiters
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Immediately flush skin exposure with copious cool water for 2-3 minutes while alerting cleanroom staff. Continuously massage 2.5% calcium gluconate gel onto affected area with gloved hands until medical personnel arrive. In case of eye contact, flush continuously with sterile eye wash or isotonic saline for at least 15 minutes, holding eyelids open. Never delay calcium gluconate treatment.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated acid wet bench with polypropylene/PTFE construction and negative pressure exhaust ducting. Face velocity must maintain 100 ± 10 FPM (0.5 m/s) at sash opening height of 12 inches. Continuous Magnehelic differential pressure monitoring interlocked with wet bench power.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent DHF wet bath must be segregated into dedicated fluoropolymer drain plumbed to a specialized fluoride waste treatment system. Manual carboys must be neutralized by slow addition of technical-grade calcium hydroxide (slaked lime, Ca(OH)2) or calcium chloride (CaCl2) to precipitate insoluble fluorite (CaF2), adjusting pH to 6.5-8.5 prior to certified hazardous disposal.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid** | `7664-39-3` | Semiconductor Grade (VLSI / cleanroom grade) | `0.5% - 1.0% w/w (diluted from 49% stock)` |
| **Deionized Water** | `7732-18-5` | Ultra-pure (UPW, 18.2 MOhm-cm at 25°C) | `99.0% - 99.5% w/w` |
| **Calcium Gluconate Topical Gel** | `18016-24-5` | USP Medical Grade | `2.5% w/w` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `20 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic chemical native oxide (~1.2-1.5 nm SiO2) with trace chemical residues post-SC-1 organic clean.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Fully hydrophobic, clean hydrogen-passivated silicon surface (Si-H mono/di-hydride terminated) with native oxide thickness <= 0.2 nm.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Spontaneous uncontrolled room-temperature native oxide regrowth in ambient air, airborne organic VOC contamination, and loss of hydrogen termination, causing non-uniform dielectric thickness and trap states during subsequent 3.5 nm dry gate oxide furnace growth.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Precision PTFE/PFA wet dip fixture and edge-clamp assembly validated for zero liquid entrapment, complete DHF chemical stripping of native SiO2, and clean hydrophobic surface transition across 100mm wafers for 180nm dry gate oxidation.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `DWG_PFA_DHF_FIXTURE_GEN1_REV_B.pdf`
- [ ] `HYDROPHOBIC_TRANSITION_VERIFICATION_LOG.csv`
- [ ] `POST_ETCH_CONTACT_ANGLE_ELLIPSOMETRY_REPORT.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Static deionized water contact angle across full wafer surface post-strip** | `>= 75.0 deg` | +15.0 deg / -0.0 deg | Sessile drop goniometric profile measurement at 5 orthogonal wafer sites |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Residual interfacial silicon dioxide thickness post-DHF strip** | `<= 0.20 nm` | +0.05 nm / -0.10 nm | Spectroscopic ellipsometry modeling Cauchy layer at 632.8 nm wavelength |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Radial fluid meniscus retention depth at PTFE support claw interface** | `<= 0.50 mm` | +0.20 mm / -0.50 mm | Optical coordinate measuring microscope (100x magnification) immediately post-withdrawal |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Engineering sign-off requires 5 consecutive wafers achieving contact angle >= 75 deg with residual oxide <= 0.2 nm, zero edge micro-cracking verified by 100x optical microscopy, and verified EHS fluoride ventilation and waste interlocks active.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

**Title:** Process Parameter Benchmarking for Dilute HF Native Oxide Strip and Hydrophobic Surface Transition Verification  
**Module:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) — Wet Chemistry / Surface Conditioning  
**Target Node / Generation:** 180nm (Gen 2 µm)  
**Downstream Dependency:** 180nm Dry Gate Oxide Growth (3.5 nm to 4.0 nm at 850°C–900°C)

---

### Process Flow Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Pre-Clean Inspection  │
│      & Bath Prep       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  DHF Oxide Strip Dip   │
│        at 25 C         │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   QDR DI Water Rinse   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Surface Dewet &     │
│  Contact Angle Check   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Surface Conditioning  │
│   for Gate Oxidation   │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Safety Protocol & PPE Verification**
   - Confirm dedicated HF personal protective equipment (heavy neoprene gloves, face shield, chemical apron) is donned.
   - Verify unexpired calcium gluconate gel is stationed directly adjacent to the wet bench.
   - Ensure the wet bench exhaust face velocity is operational and monitored.

2. **Chemical Bath Benchmarking & Thermal Stabilization**
   - Prepare the dilute HF / buffered oxide etch station maintained strictly at $25^\circ\text{C} \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ to lock thermal kinetic drift.
   - Add $0.1\%$ surfactant wetting agent (e.g., Triton X-100 or Fluorad) to ensure complete wetting without bubble entrapment across dense 180nm layout micro-trenches (channel width $W = 220\text{ nm}$, channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$).

3. **Immersion Etch & Native Oxide Strip**
   - Immerse 180nm wafer lot into the dilute HF bath with continuous nitrogen agitation to eliminate mass-transport boundary layer starvation.
   - Time the dip based on the benchmarked thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ etch rate baseline ($\approx 100\text{ nm/min}$ / $1000\text{ \AA/min}$ at $25^\circ\text{C}$) to strip surface native oxide ($1.0\text{--}1.5\text{ nm}$) with controlled $20\text{--}30\%$ overetch, avoiding excessive pitting of the single-crystal silicon substrate.

4. **Quick Dump Rinse (QDR)**
   - Transfer wafer carrier within $\le 5\text{ seconds}$ to the Quick Dump Rinse tank filled with high-purity deionized (DI) water ($> 18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$).
   - Execute 4 dump-and-fill cycles to arrest etching and completely remove fluoride complexes.

5. **Hydrophobic Surface Transition Verification**
   - Perform in-line visual and automated dewetting inspection upon wafer withdrawal from DI water:
     - Bare hydrophilic silicon ($\text{SiO}_2$-terminated) exhibits complete water film sheeting.
     - Fully stripped silicon is hydrogen-terminated ($\text{Si-H}$ passivation) and exhibits instantaneous water roll-off / dewetting (hydrophobic behavior with DI water contact angle $\ge 70^\circ$).
   - Confirm complete hydrophobic transition across the entire active array ($W = 220\text{ nm}$, $L = 180\text{ nm}$ access transistor regions).

6. **Post-Strip Decontamination Queue**
   - Route immediately to SC-2 heavy metal decontamination clean and subsequent dry oxidation furnace queue ($850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$, target thickness $3.5\text{ to }4.0\text{ nm}$) to prevent uncontrolled ambient native oxide regrowth.

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric | Engineering Unit | Measurement Method / Tool |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Bath Temperature** | $25.0 \pm 0.5$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ | Immersion thermocouple / RTD sensor |
| **Baseline Thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ Etch Rate** | $\approx 100$ ($\approx 1000$) | $\text{nm/min}$ ($\text{\AA/min}$) | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry on monitor wafer |
| **Wetting Agent Concentration** | $0.1$ | $\% \text{ (vol)}$ | Precision metered chemical dosing |
| **Surface Dewet Contact Angle** | $\ge 70$ (Hydrophobic) | $\text{degrees } (^\circ)$ | Automated Optical Goniometer / Dewet sensor |
| **Post-Strip Target Dielectric Thickness** | $3.5 \text{ to } 4.0$ | $\text{nm}$ | In-situ / Ex-situ Ellipsometer (post-dry ox) |

---

### Literature Context Citations

- **Etch Chemistry, Wetting Agent, and Safety:** *Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)* — Etch rate of thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ at $25^\circ\text{C}$ is approximately $100\text{ nm/minute}$ ($1000\text{ \AA/min}$). Addition of $0.1\%$ wetting agent (Triton X-100 / Fluorad) eliminates micro-trench bubble entrapment. Safety requirement mandates calcium gluconate gel on site at all times.
- **Topological Layout Constraints:** *180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench* — Unit cell access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$ in $8F^2 / 6F^2$ folded bitline layout.
- **Gate Dielectric Target:** *Deal-Grove Silicon Thermal Oxidation Kinetics in Quartz Tube Furnace* — Dry oxidation regime ($900^\circ\text{C}\text{--}1000^\circ\text{C}$ in pure dry $\text{O}_2$) with target thickness for 180nm gate dielectric specified at $3.5\text{ to }4.0\text{ nm}$ to achieve $E_{\text{bd}} > 10\text{ MV/cm}$ and $D_{\text{it}} < 10^{10}\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{eV}^{-1}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Native oxide removal with dilute HF (DHF 50:1 or 100:1) dictates the starting boundary condition for subsequent 3.5 nm dry gate oxidation. An under-etched surface leaves residual sub-stoichiometric SiOx islands that cause dielectric breakdown voltage (BVox) degradation and local thickness non-uniformities. Conversely, excessive DHF over-etch induces Si surface microroughness (RMS roughness > 0.15 nm), degrading 180nm DRAM access transistor channel mobility and increasing interface trap density (Dit).
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Transitioning from a hydrophilic native chemical oxide (~1.0-1.5 nm) to a fully hydrogen-passivated (Si-H) hydrophobic surface must be verified without aqueous watermark generation. Unbuffered DHF exhibits contact angles > 70° upon completion. Rinsing dynamics are critical: dump-rinser flow velocity and marangoni/IPA dry execution must prevent dissolved oxygen re-oxidation and particle redeposition, keeping residual native oxide below 0.1 nm equivalent oxide thickness prior to oxidation furnace load.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Electronic-grade (SEMI Tier 4 / Grade 1, trace metals < 10 ppt) hydrofluoric acid supply must be tightly controlled. Fluctuations in supply-chain barrel lots or on-tool DHF spiking can cause concentration drift from nominal 0.5% (100:1) to 1.0% (50:1), dramatically shifting strip duration. Local availability of HF-compatible high-purity PFA baths, automated inline conductivity sensors, and dedicated calcium gluconate stocks are mandatory operational bottlenecks in Vietnam fab lines.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Benchmarking DHF parameters directly impacts pre-gate clean throughput and takt time. The strip process itself takes 30-90 seconds, but the strict post-DHF Q-time to furnace insertion (< 60 minutes in air) creates severe logistics coupling between wet bench line 2 and horizontal furnace diffusion banks. Inability to meet Q-time yields scrap batches of product wafers, impacting schedule milestones for the 180nm DRAM tape-out.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Watermark defectivity caused by trapped deionized water droplets on hydrophobic H-passivated silicon during spin/rinse dry, producing localized silicic acid precipitates and pinholes in 3.5 nm gate oxide.
1. Incomplete native oxide removal due to bath HF depletion or insufficient immersion time, resulting in unstripped SiO2 patches and wide EOT variance across 200mm wafers.
1. Excessive surface roughening and pitting from ambient dissolved oxygen in DHF solution catalyzing anisotropic etching along Si(100) atomic step edges.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-2-1-2-1-2-01` | **Automated Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Contact Angle Verification of Native Oxide Strip** | Woollam M-2000 Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (SE) and Krüss DSA100 Automated Optical Goniometer with Sessile Drop System | 1. Measure baseline 49-point wafer map of native oxide thickness on spectroscopic ellipsometer. 2. Immerse wafer cassette into 100:1 DHF bath for targeted benchmark durations (30s, 45s, 60s, 75s, 90s). 3. Transfer immediately to Quick-Dump-Rinse (QDR) with 18.2 MOhm-cm UPW for 3 cycles, followed by IPA vapor dry. 4. Measure post-strip thickness using SE at the identical 49 points. 5. Dispense 2.0 uL ultra-pure DI water droplets at 9 radial locations and record contact angle after 5 seconds stabilization. | `Pass if residual oxide thickness <= 0.08 nm across all 49 points (uniformity 3-sigma < 0.02 nm) and DI water static contact angle >= 75.0° across all measured locations.` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-2-1-2-1-2-02` | **AFM Surface Microroughness and Particle Adder Defectivity Inspection** | Park Systems FX40 Atomic Force Microscope (AFM) and KLA Tencor Surfscan SP2 Unpatterned Surface Inspection System | 1. Perform initial Surfscan SP2 inspection to record incoming baseline particle count (LPD >= 65 nm). 2. Process pilot wafers through optimal DHF strip recipe (established in TC-01) plus 100% over-etch margin (120s exposure). 3. Transfer to QDR and SRD dry under Class 1 laminar flow hood. 4. Execute post-strip SP2 particle scan. 5. Scan 5 points (center, top, bottom, left, right at 5mm edge exclusion) with tapping mode AFM over 1 um x 1 um and 5 um x 5 um fields. | `Pass if surface microroughness Rq (RMS) <= 0.12 nm (1 um x 1 um scan) and total net particle adders (size >= 65 nm) <= 10 counts across entire 200mm wafer surface.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Heavy-duty butyl or neoprene over-gloves (minimum 15 mil thickness) worn over nitrile inner gloves, Chemical-resistant neoprene apron covering chest to knees, Full-face splash shield (ANSI Z87.1 certified) combined with indirect-vent chemical splash goggles, Acid-resistant chemical safety boots with steel toe cap and non-slip soles
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Calcium Gluconate Gel (2.5% USP) must be stored in unexpired, tamper-evident containers within 3 meters of the wet bench. In case of skin exposure: immediately strip contaminated clothing, flood area with cold water for 2 minutes, apply generous amounts of 2.5% calcium gluconate gel, and massage continuously into the skin until medical personnel arrive. In case of ocular exposure: flush immediately in plumbed eyewash with buffered isotonic saline or tempered water for at least 15 minutes while holding eyelids open; do not apply topical gel directly into eyes. Seek immediate emergency tertiary medical care; inform responders of hydrofluoric acid systemic toxicity and hypocalcemia risk.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated acid fume wet bench lip exhaust maintaining face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) across all sash openings; continuous automated static differential pressure monitoring connected to fab scada with acoustic interlock alarms; exhaust ducted through polypropylene/PVDF manifolds directly to dedicated fab wet acid scrubbers.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: All DHF effluent and rinse water must be isolated from general drains and plumbed through double-contained PVDF lines into the dedicated Fluoride Waste Neutralization (FWN) system. Treatment requires stoichiometric precipitation with hydrated lime (calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)2) or calcium chloride (CaCl2) to convert soluble fluoride into insoluble fluorite (CaF2) sludge, followed by coagulant/flocculant sedimentation, maintaining discharge effluent fluoride concentration below 10.0 ppm and pH between 6.5 and 8.5.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid (aqueous solution, DHF precursor)** | `7664-39-3` | SEMI Grade 4 / VLSI electronic grade (trace metals < 100 ppt) | `0.49% - 0.98% wt (diluted 100:1 to 50:1 from 49% stock)` |
| **Ultra-Pure Deionized Water (UPW diluent)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM D5127 Type E-1.2 Electronics Grade (>18.2 MOhm-cm at 25°C) | `99.0% - 99.5% wt` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `60 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic native chemical oxide (0.8 - 1.5 nm SiO2) from pre-diffusion RCA SC-1 clean, water contact angle < 15°.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Fully hydrogen-passivated (Si-H terminated) hydrophobic single-crystal silicon surface, water contact angle >= 75°, native oxide thickness < 0.08 nm.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exposure to ambient air beyond 60 minutes results in spontaneous native oxide regrowth (re-oxidation > 0.3 nm), surface hydrocarbon chemisorption, and airborne boron/phosphorus contamination, resulting in uncontrolled gate oxide EOT shifts, flatband voltage instability (Vfb drift), and premature gate dielectric breakdown in 180nm DRAM transistors.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Benchmarking and recipe validation of the dilute HF native oxide strip process on 200mm Si (100) wafers, confirming complete oxide clearing, uniform hydrogen passivation (water contact angle >= 75°), atomic-level surface smoothness (RMS < 0.12 nm), and integration compatibility with downstream 3.5 nm dry gate oxidation within verified Q-time constraints.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `DHF_Etch_Rate_and_Thickness_Map_Report.csv`
- [ ] `Hydrophobic_Contact_Angle_Characterization_Summary.pdf`
- [ ] `Surface_Roughness_AFM_Topography_Scans.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Residual native oxide thickness post-DHF strip across 49-point wafer map** | `0.05 nm` | <= 0.08 nm maximum at any single point | Multi-angle Spectroscopic Ellipsometry using Cauchy/Tauc-Lorentz optical dispersion model |
| `ASSERT-02` | **DI water static contact angle confirming hydrophobic H-termination** | `78.0 degrees` | >= 75.0 degrees across all 9 radial die zones | Automated goniometer sessile drop method with 2.0 uL UPW droplet size |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Silicon post-strip root-mean-square surface microroughness (Rq)** | `0.10 nm` | <= 0.12 nm (1 um x 1 um scan area) | Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) in non-contact/tapping mode |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Process Engineer and Module Lead signoff upon verifying that 3 consecutive test lots achieve 100% compliance across ASSERT-01 through ASSERT-03 with zero watermark defects, zero HF safety incidents, and demonstrated queue-time stability up to 60 minutes in air and 4 hours in purged N2 FOUPs.
