# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

**Document ID:** `SOP-DIFF-180NM-001`  
**Title:** Quartz Tube RCA-Clean, Bake-Out & MFC Flow Calibration ($N_2/O_2$)  
**Target Node:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip — Thermal Processing & Gate Dielectric Formation  
**Furnace Type:** Horizontal 3-Zone Fused Quartz Tube ($150\text{ mm}$–$200\text{ mm}$ OD, $99.999\%\text{ SiO}_2$)

---

### Process Execution Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Stage 1: Quartz Ware  │
│    RCA Wet Cleaning    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Stage 2: High Purity  │
│       Gas Sweep        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Stage 3: Thermal    │
│      Bake Out and      │
│       Profiling        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Stage 4: MFC Flow    │
│   Calibration N2 and   │
│           O2           │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

## 1. Step-by-Step Procedure

### Stage 1: Quartz Ware RCA Wet Chemical Cleaning
1. **SC-1 (Standard Clean 1) Bath Preparation:**
   - Formulate chemical ratio of $5\text{ parts UPW} : 1\text{ part } 29\%\text{ NH}_4\text{OH} : 1\text{ part } 30\%\text{ H}_2\text{O}_2$ in a high-purity immersion bath.
   - Heat the solution to **$70^\circ\text{C}$ to $75^\circ\text{C}$** with active megasonic agitation at **$1\text{ MHz}$**.
   - Submerge the quartz tube and wafer boat for **$10\text{ minutes}$** to oxidize organics and strip surface micro-particulates via zeta potential repulsion.
2. **Cascade Dump Rinse:**
   - Execute **$5\text{ cycles}$** of Cascade Dump Rinse using $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ Ultra-Pure Water (UPW). Continue rinsing until dump bath resistivity exceeds **$> 16\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$**.
3. **Native Oxide / Surface Etch Strip (Dilute HF):**
   - Immerse quartz ware in dilute hydrofluoric acid ($1:50$ to $1:100\text{ HF}:\text{UPW}$, $0.5\%$ to $1.0\%\text{ HF}$) for **$15\text{ to } 30\text{ seconds}$** at **$22^\circ\text{C}$** until complete hydrophobic dewetting is verified.
   - Perform final cascade UPW rinse and dry thoroughly with filtered hot $N_2$.

### Stage 2: Tube Installation & Inert Gas Sweep
1. **Tube Mounting & Alignment:**
   - Mount the cleaned $99.999\%\text{ SiO}_2$ fused quartz tube into the 3-zone furnace shell (Kanthal-A1 or APM alloy coils across Source, Center, and Load zones).
   - Insert dual Type R/S Platinum-Rhodium thermocouples encased in quartz thermowells into each zone.
2. **Purge Initiation:**
   - Establish an ultra-pure carrier gas sweep ($N_2$, $99.999\%$ purity) via calibrated Mass Flow Controllers (MFC) at **$2.0\text{ to } 5.0\text{ SLPM}$** laminar velocity to prevent ambient back-diffusion. Add $1\text{–}3\%\text{ dry HCl}$ during initial bake-out steps to passivate mobile $\text{Na}^+$ ions and volatilize residual metallic impurities.

### Stage 3: High-Temperature Bake-Out & Thermal Profiling
1. **Ramp-Up Schedule:**
   - Ramp the 3-zone digital PID controller through decoupled loops from idle to bake-out temperatures between **$850^\circ\text{C}$ and $1150^\circ\text{C}$** (up to $1200^\circ\text{C}$ ceiling).
2. **Thermal Flat Zone Stabilization:**
   - Soak at target temperature to desorb entrapped hydroxyl groups and moisture from the fused quartz walls.
   - Fine-tune feedforward PID power trims across Source and Load zones to eliminate convective end-losses and maintain isothermal equilibrium.
3. **Thermal Shock Mitigation:**
   - Restrict quartz boat mechanical push/pull speed to **$< 50\text{ mm/minute}$** during all insertion and withdrawal maneuvers to prevent crystallographic slip dislocations.

### Stage 4: Multi-Point MFC Flow Calibration ($N_2$ / $O_2$)
1. **Zero Point & Span Baseline Calibration:**
   - Check electrical zero point on the thermal mass flow controllers with upstream isolation valves closed.
2. **Multi-Point Flow Verification:**
   - Regulate ultra-pure $N_2$ and dry $O_2$ ($99.999\%$ purity) sequentially across the operating sweep band from **$1.0\text{ SLPM}$ to $5.0\text{ SLPM}$** (specifically calibrating setpoints at $1.0$, $2.0$, $3.5$, and $5.0\text{ SLPM}$).
   - Verify downstream mass displacement to maintain steady-state laminar gas velocity through the tube cross-section without turbulence.

---

```text
     Boat Speed┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒             │

               0.0      18.8     37.5      56.2    75.0 
```

| Parameter Metric | Target Specification | Exact Engineering Units | Verification Instrument |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Center Flat Zone Thermal Uniformity** | $\le \pm 0.5$ across $\ge 300\text{ mm}$ (up to $350\text{ mm}$) | $^\circ\text{C}$ | Profiling Type R/S Pt-Pt/Rh Thermocouple Array |
| **Laminar Process Sweep Flow Rate ($N_2 / O_2$)** | $2.0 \text{ to } 5.0$ (range: $1.0 \text{ to } 5.0$) | $\text{SLPM}$ | Calibrated Digital Thermal MFC Flow Transducer |
| **Wafer Boat Insertion / Withdrawal Speed** | $< 50$ | $\text{mm/minute}$ | Automated Stepper Lead-Screw Boat Loader |
| **RCA Dump Rinse Final Resistivity** | $> 16.0$ (Baseline: $18.2$) | $\text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ | In-Line Resistivity Sensor at Dump Rinse Outlet |

---

## 3. Literature Citations & Physical Constraints

- **Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation:**
  - *Temperature Uniformity:* Must maintain $\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ across central $300\text{ mm}$ boat region ($800^\circ\text{C}\text{–}1150^\circ\text{C}$).
  - *Gas Delivery Dynamics:* MFC-regulated laminar gas sweep between $1.0\text{ and } 5.0\text{ SLPM}$.
  - *Thermal Shock Barrier:* Push/pull speed strictly $< 50\text{ mm/minute}$ to avoid crystallographic slip.
  - *Sensors:* Dual Type R/S Platinum-Rhodium thermocouples in quartz thermowells.
- **Three-Zone Quartz Tube Diffusion Furnace Thermal Profiling & Gas Delivery:**
  - *Furnace Tube Material:* Fused quartz ($150\text{ mm}$ to $200\text{ mm}$ OD, $99.999\%\text{ SiO}_2$).
  - *Zonal Division & Uniformity:* Source, Center, and Load zones maintaining flat profile $\le \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ across $350\text{ mm}$ at $1000^\circ\text{C}\text{ to } 1200^\circ\text{C}$.
  - *Gas Sweep & Purge Chemistry:* Laminar sweep of $2.0\text{ to } 5.0\text{ SLPM}$ ultra-pure $O_2$ ($99.999\%$), $N_2$, and $1\text{–}3\%\text{ dry HCl}$ to inhibit air back-diffusion and volatilize $\text{Na}^+$ ions.
- **RCA Standard Clean SC-1, SC-2, and Native Oxide HF Dip Engineering:**
  - *SC-1 Formulation:* $5\text{ UPW} : 1\text{ NH}_4\text{OH} (29\%) : 1\text{ H}_2\text{O}_2 (30\%)$ at $70^\circ\text{C}\text{–}75^\circ\text{C}$ for $10\text{ minutes}$ with $1\text{ MHz}$ megasonics.
  - *Rinse & Strip Targets:* 5-cycle cascade dump rinse to $> 16\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ (UPW source $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$); $1:50$ to $1:100\text{ HF}$ dip for $15\text{–}30\text{ seconds}$ at $22^\circ\text{C}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Cleaning and baking a process quartz tube introduces severe cross-contamination risks if the auxiliary wet-bench immersion hardware or furnace exhaust lines are not chemically isolated. Wet RCA cleaning of large quartz tubes requires dedicated mega-baths or spray-acid tools with fluoropolymer supports to prevent mechanical stress fractures. Thermal bake-out at 1000°C under continuous ultra-pure N2 purge is essential to desorb moisture, organic residues, and hydroxyl groups (-OH) from the inner quartz wall before exposing it to dry O2 oxidation cycles at 850°C. Furthermore, thermal expansion mismatch between the quartz tube, SiC paddle, and quartz boat must be managed via closed-loop linear push/pull speed (< 50 mm/min) to avoid particle generation from friction.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Growing a 3.5 nm gate oxide for 180nm DRAM transistors requires defect-free, ultra-clean quartz inner surfaces; residual metallic impurities (specifically Na+, Fe, Cu) act as mobile ionic contaminants and surface recombination centers, leading to gate-oxide-integrity (GOI) breakdown and threshold voltage (Vth) drift. RCA SC-1 removes organic traces and particulates via NH4OH/H2O2 micro-etching, while SC-2 (HCl/H2O2) or dilute HF cleans must desorb trace heavy metals without aggressively etching fused silica. If the quartz tube bake-out is incomplete, trace outgassed H2O acts as an unintentional steam oxidation accelerator, throwing off the Deal-Grove linear growth rate regime and resulting in gate oxide thickness overshoot beyond the ±0.1 nm specification. Mass flow controllers (MFC) for N2 and O2 must undergo primary standard in-situ rate-of-rise (RoR) calibration to guarantee stoichiometric reproducibility.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Ultra-pure semiconductor grade reagents (SEMI Grade 5 NH4OH, H2O2, HCl, and 49% electronic HF) face extended procurement lead times in regional supply chains. Synthetic fused silica quartz tubes (GE 214 or equivalent ultra-low alkali quartz) have lead times exceeding 16 to 24 weeks. Sourcing secondary multi-gas digital mass flow controllers (Horiba STEC or Brooks Instrument) with Kalrez/metal seal technology and 316L VCR fittings is critical to prevent ambient atmospheric leakage. Sourcing localized certified calibration standards or portable molbloc/molbox transfer standards must be locked in prior to furnace qualification.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Quartz tube preparation and MFC gas calibration form the gating milestone for the 180nm dry gate oxidation baseline. Any tube breakage during wet RCA immersion handling or thermal shock during high-temperature bake-out stalls the DRAM fab pilot line for multiple months. This work package must strictly enforce a 2-hour queue time between tube wet clean drying and furnace tube installation/bake-out to eliminate airborne particulate adsorption, with continuous RGA (Residual Gas Analyzer) background tracking to confirm dryness before advancing to wafer runs.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal shock fracture or structural micro-cracking of the quartz tube during rapid insertion into the hot furnace or non-uniform cooling after 1000°C bake-out.
1. Mobile alkali ion contamination (Na+, K+) leaching from handling jigs into the quartz inner wall, catastrophically degrading the breakdown field (Ebd < 10 MV/cm) of subsequently grown 3.5 nm gate dielectric films.
1. Moisture retention inside the quartz tube pores resulting in parasitic wet oxidation kinetics, causing gate oxide thickness to exceed the 3.5 nm target by > 15%.

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Heavy-duty Neoprene/Butyl dual-layer chemical immersion gauntlets (18-inch sleeve), Chemical splash apron and full-coverage acid-resistant chemical suit, Full-face transparent polycarbonate splash shield over ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical goggles, Acid-resistant composite-toe boots with metatarsal protection, Thermal aluminized heat-resistant gloves (rated to 600°C) for furnace hot-zone handling
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For Hydrofluoric Acid exposure: Immediate, continuous copious irrigation with running water for 5 minutes followed by vigorous topical massage of 2.5% Calcium Gluconate gel into the affected area, continually reapplying every 15 minutes until emergency medical services arrive. Provide immediate oxygen inhalation for NH4OH vapor inhalation; flush eyes with saline eyewash solution for at least 20 minutes if exposed to SC-1/peroxide chemistry.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Acid/corrosive wet bench must maintain minimum slot face velocity of 100 fpm (0.51 m/s) with dedicated wet acid scrubber exhaust. Furnace tube exhaust must be hard-ducted to a toxic gas scrubbed central ventilation system with automatic N2 back-purge and interlocked differential pressure sensors (< -0.25 inches water column). Ambient O2 deficiency monitors and toxic NH3/HF gas sniffers must be active within 2 meters of the workstation.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent SC-1 (NH4OH/H2O2) must be cooled below 30°C in an agitated equalization tank, followed by controlled acidic neutralization to pH 7-8 prior to biological industrial discharge. Fluoride-bearing effluent (dilute HF rinse) must be segregated into a dedicated Fluoride Waste Treatment system, reacted with hydrated lime (Ca(OH)2) to precipitate insoluble Calcium Fluoride (CaF2), and verified below 10 ppm F- concentration before municipal release.

| **Hydrofluoric Acid** | `7664-39-3` | SEMI Grade 5 (Ultra-low metal) | `0.5% - 1.0% diluted aqueous solution` |
| **Nitrogen Gas (Compressed/Cryogenic)** | `7727-37-9` | Grade 6.0 (99.9999% Electronic Grade) | `100%` |
| **Oxygen Gas (Compressed)** | `7782-44-7` | Grade 6.0 (99.9999% Electronic Grade) | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: As-received raw or re-conditioned fused silica quartz tube with ambient organic dust adsorption, surface hydroxyls, and native micro-particulates.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophobic/trace-oxide clean quartz inner diameter, fully dehydrated (hydroxyl-free), trace metal contamination < 1x10^10 atoms/cm2, hermetically sealed inside the furnace casing under 2.0 SLPM ultra-pure N2 purge at 650°C idle standby.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding the 30-minute cleanroom air exposure window leads to airborne boron, phosphorus, and volatile organic hydrocarbon re-adsorption on the quartz inner tube wall. When subsequently heated to 850°C-1000°C, these contaminants diffuse into the furnace atmosphere and incorporate into the 3.5 nm gate oxide, causing excessive interface trap density (Dit > 5x10^11 eV^-1 cm^-2), abnormal gate leakage currents (Jg > 1 A/cm2 at 1.8V), and degraded channel carrier mobility in the DRAM access transistors.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full RCA wet cleaning, megasonic cascade dump rinse, drying, mechanical installation, 1000°C ultra-pure N2 bake-out, and multi-point primary Rate-of-Rise MFC gas calibration for N2 and O2 process lines are completed and certified. The furnace quartz process tube is verified ultra-clean, thermally conditioned, and hydro-chemically dehydrated, establishing the baseline chamber qualification for 180nm dry gate oxidation.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `TUBE_CLEAN_BAKEOUT_RGA_PROFILE_GEN1.csv`
- [ ] `MFC_N2_O2_ROR_CALIBRATION_CERT_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `QUARTZ_TUBE_INNER_SURFACE_TXRF_INSPECTION.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| `ASSERT-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-2-2-1-1-02` | **MFC N2 and O2 flow accuracy deviation from primary Rate-of-Rise (RoR) volumetric calculation across 0.5-5.0 SLPM operating range** | `0.0` | ±0.5% of full scale | In-situ Rate-of-Rise pressure manometry with calibrated 12.45 L reference volume and MKS Baratron gauge |
| `ASSERT-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-2-2-1-1-03` | **Total surface metallic contamination (Fe, Cu, Ni, Na, K) on inside quartz tube wall post bake-out** | `5.0e9` | < 1.0e10 atoms/cm2 | Vapor Phase Decomposition - Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (VPD-ICPMS) coupon monitor witness wafer |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Sign-off requires 100% completion of the 1000°C 4-hour thermal bake-out with RGA water partial pressure verified < 5.0x10^-9 Torr, certified 5-point MFC calibration reports showing < ±0.5% deviation across both N2 and O2 lines, zero physical quartz defects/dislocations observed under high-intensity inspection, and lead process engineer plus safety officer sign-off on the fab traveler.

testcases.title: MFC N2 and O2 In-Situ Flow Verification via Rate-of-Rise (RoR) Pressure Manometry
testcases.instrumentation: Calibrated Baratron Capacitance Manometer (0-100 Torr, 0.05% accuracy), Calibrated Reference Vacuum Chamber (known volume V = 12.45 L ± 0.02 L), Quartz Furnace Pressure Transducer, High-Speed Precision Data Logger
testcases.pre_conditions: Process quartz furnace tube sealed with blind flange, evacuated to baseline base pressure < 1.0 mTorr using turbomolecular pump; manifold temperature stabilized at 23.0°C ± 0.5°C; MFC supply gas lines pressurized to 30.0 psig ± 0.5 psig with semiconductor-grade N2 (99.9999%) and O2 (99.9999%).
testcases.procedure:
1. Isolate the reference chamber and zero the Baratron capacitance manometer.
2. Command the N2 MFC to a setpoint of 2.000 SLPM (Standard Liters Per Minute) while venting to bypass for 60 seconds to achieve steady-state flow.
3. Actuate pneumatic isolation valve to divert N2 flow directly into the calibrated reference volume; initiate high-resolution pressure data acquisition at 100 Hz for 30.0 seconds.
4. Calculate volumetric mass flow Q = (V / (R * T)) * (dP / dt) converted to standard reference conditions (0°C, 101.325 kPa).
5. Repeat steps 1-4 across 5 setpoints: 0.500, 1.000, 2.000, 3.500, and 5.000 SLPM.
6. Purge chamber with N2 for 10 minutes, evacuate below 1.0 mTorr, and repeat entire sequence for the dry O2 MFC.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Measured flow rate via Rate-of-Rise must match commanded MFC setpoints within ±0.5% of full scale across all setpoints (0.5 to 5.0 SLPM). Flow repeatability across 3 consecutive runs must exhibit RSD < 0.2%.

testcases.title: Quartz Tube High-Temperature Bake-Out and Residual Outgassing Verification via In-Situ RGA
testcases.instrumentation: In-situ Residual Gas Analyzer (RGA, 1-100 amu, Quadrupole Mass Spectrometer with Faraday cup and electron multiplier), Secondary Electron Multiplier (SEM), Quartz-sheathed Type-S Thermocouple Array (3-Zone).
testcases.pre_conditions: Quartz tube installed inside furnace casing, sealed with double Viton/fluorocarbon O-rings and water-cooled end-flanges; continuous ultra-dry N2 purge at 2.0 SLPM; furnace ramped at 5°C/min from 400°C to 1000°C.
testcases.procedure:
1. Maintain furnace multi-zone temperature at 1000°C ± 0.5°C under continuous 2.0 SLPM N2 purge for 4.0 hours.
2. Open the micro-metering sampling valve connecting the furnace exhaust plenum to the turbomolecularly pumped RGA chamber (operational pressure ~2.0 x 10^-6 Torr).
3. Continuously scan partial pressures for amu 18 (H2O), amu 28 (N2/CO), amu 32 (O2), amu 44 (CO2), and hydrocarbons (amu 41, 43, 55, 57).
4. Record partial pressure trends over a 60-minute isothermal hold at 1000°C.
5. Ramp down furnace temperature to standby temperature (650°C) at 3°C/min and record baseline background spectrum.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Partial pressure of water vapor (amu 18) must drop below 5.0 x 10^-9 Torr inside the RGA sampling plenum at 1000°C. Total sum of organic hydrocarbon fragmentation peaks (amu 41, 43, 55, 57) must remain below 1.0 x 10^-10 Torr. Outgassing decay rate must reach steady-state baseline (dP/dt < 1.0 x 10^-11 Torr/min).

Provide immediate oxygen inhalation for NH4OH vapor inhalation; flush eyes with saline eyewash solution for at least 20 minutes if exposed to SC-1/peroxide chemistry.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Acid/corrosive wet bench must maintain minimum slot face velocity of 100 fpm (0.51 m/s) with dedicated wet acid scrubber exhaust. Furnace tube exhaust must be hard-ducted to a toxic gas scrubbed central ventilation system with automatic N2 back-purge and interlocked differential pressure sensors (< -0.25 inches water column). Ambient O2 deficiency monitors and toxic NH3/HF gas sniffers must be active within 2 meters of the workstation.

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Quartz Process Tube RCA-1/RCA-2 Wet Decontamination & Megasonic DI Rinse

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Immersion / Spray    │
│         RCA-1          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Intermediate DI     │
│         Rinse          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   1:50 HF Oxide Etch   │
│          Dip           │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│       RCA-2 Wet        │
│    Decontamination     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│       Megasonic        │
│  High-Purity DI Rinse  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     High-Purity N2     │
│        Blow-Dry        │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **RCA-1 (SC-1) Organic Decontamination & Light Metal Oxidation**:
   - Prepare the SC-1 cleaning mixture in a chemical-duty tank with a volumetric ratio of `5 : 1 : 1` (5 parts Deionized $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, 1 part Ammonium Hydroxide [$29\%\text{ NH}_4\text{OH}$], 1 part Hydrogen Peroxide [$30\%\text{ H}_2\text{O}_2$]).
   - Heat and stabilize the solution at **70°C to 80°C**.
   - Submerge/expose the quartz process tube into the bath for **10 to 15 minutes** to solubilize organic surface films and oxidize light trace metal contaminants.

2. **Intermediate Dump Rinse**:
   - Transfer the quartz process tube immediately into the dump rinse station.
   - Execute a dump rinse cycle using **18.2 MΩ·cm** deionized water for **3 minutes** to wash off residual ammonia and peroxide.

3. **Hydrofluoric Acid (HF) Native Oxide Strip**:
   - Immerse the quartz tube in a **1:50 $\text{HF}:\text{H}_2\text{O}$** dilute solution for **15 to 30 seconds**.
   - Strip the thin native oxide layer until the surface transitions cleanly from hydrophilic to hydrophobic.

4. **RCA-2 (SC-2) Ionic & Heavy Metal Decontamination**:
   - Prepare the SC-2 cleaning mixture with a volumetric ratio of `6 : 1 : 1` (6 parts Deionized $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, 1 part Hydrochloric Acid [$37\%\text{ HCl}$], 1 part Hydrogen Peroxide [$30\%\text{ H}_2\text{O}_2$]).
   - Heat and maintain the bath temperature at **70°C to 80°C**.
   - Expose the quartz tube for **10 minutes** to eliminate alkali ions ($\text{Na}^+$, $\text{K}^+$) and heavy metal contaminants ($\text{Fe}$, $\text{Cu}$, $\text{Ni}$).

5. **Megasonic Deionized Water Final Rinse**:
   - Transfer the tube to the high-purity DI overflow tank with active megasonic transducer assistance.
   - Flush continuously with **18.2 MΩ·cm** DI water until the resistivity reaches steady state.

6. **Drying**:
   - Perform a final drying blow-down using filtered high-purity Nitrogen ($\text{N}_2$) gas.

---

### Target Parameter Metrics

```text

                  │●●●●●●●●●                           │
DI Water (MOhm-cm)┤●●●●●●●●●                           │
                  │■■■■■■■■■■■■                        │
        HF Dip (s)┤■■■■■■■■■■■■                        │
                  │░░░░░░                              │
  RCA-2 Time (min)┤░░░░░░                              │
  RCA-1 Time (min)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                             │
                  │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                             │
RCA-2 Temp (deg C)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
                  │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
RCA-1 Temp (deg C)┤████████████████████████████████████│
                  │████████████████████████████████████│
                  └┬────────┬────────┬───────┬────────┬┘
                  0.0     18.8     37.5    56.2    75.0 
```

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Acceptance Window / Target | Unit | Verification Tool / Sensor |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **RCA-1 (SC-1) Bath Temperature** | `70.0 to 80.0` | °C | In-line chemical bath immersion thermocouple |
| **RCA-2 (SC-2) Bath Temperature** | `70.0 to 80.0` | °C | In-line chemical bath immersion thermocouple |
| **HF Strip Exposure Duration** | `15.0 to 30.0` | s | Automated wet bench pneumatic recipe timer |
| **Rinse DI Water Resistivity** | `18.2` | MΩ·cm | In-line resistivity sensor at rinse tank weir outlet |

---

### Citations & Literature Context
- **Standard RCA-1 and RCA-2 Silicon Wafer Cleaning Procedure**: Provides volumetric bath ratios (`5:1:1` for SC-1; `6:1:1` for SC-2), temperature setpoints (**70°C–80°C**), bath durations (**10–15 min** for SC-1; **10 min** for SC-2), intermediate **3-minute** dump rinse with **18.2 MΩ·cm** DI water, **1:50 HF** strip dip window (**15–30 s**), and final high-purity $\text{N}_2$ dry.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Cleaning a full-length horizontal quartz furnace tube (~2 meters, OD >200 mm) via liquid immersion presents severe structural and geometric challenges. Handling wet quartzware requires specialized hoist fixtures to prevent mechanical shock and point-load fractures. Furthermore, megasonic transducer coupling across curved, 4-6 mm thick quartz walls experiences non-uniform acoustic wave dampening and standing wave hotspots, risking localized cavitation micro-erosion or inadequate particle lift-off along the central hot-zone interior.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For high-quality 3.5 nm dry gate oxide (180nm DRAM node), residual metallic impurities (specifically Fe, Cu, and mobile alkali ions like Na+) must be suppressed below 1E10 atoms/cm2. In RCA-1 (SC-1), high pH and peroxide cause micro-etching of SiO2/fused quartz; if NH4OH concentration or bath temperature exceeds 75°C, surface micro-roughness (RMS >0.2 nm) will increase, degrading oxide dielectric breakdown (TDDB/Ebd). In RCA-2 (SC-2), temperature must remain strictly at 75°C ± 2°C to sustain metal-chloride complexation (e.g., [FeCl6]3-) without excessive H2O2 thermal outgassing.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Electronic-grade UPW (18.2 MOhm-cm at 25°C, TOC <5 ppb) and SEMI Grade 5 chemicals (29% NH4OH, 37% HCl, 30% unstabilized electronic grade H2O2) must be secured. Standard industrial H2O2 often contains tin or phosphate stabilizers that act as catastrophic furnace poisoners. Immersion tanks of this size require over 150-250 L per chemical bath, demanding substantial local inventory buffering and dedicated chemical delivery/drain pumping systems.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Decontamination of large quartz tubes is a critical-path throughput bottleneck. Wet bench footprint, heating cycle latency for 200 L baths (~45-60 min ramp), and dump rinse resistivity recovery times directly throttle furnace tube swap schedules. Clear SOP gate checks and pre-mixed chemical delivery are required to ensure the tube transition into the furnace bake-out stage does not breach thermal queue times.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal shock or mechanical stress fracture of the fused silica quartz process tube during crane-assisted transfer into or out of heated 75°C chemical baths.
1. Stabilizer or metallic cross-contamination from non-SEMI-5 grade H2O2 leading to furnace hot-zone background alkali/metal contamination >1E11 atoms/cm2.
1. Inadequate megasonic displacement and incomplete cascade rinse leaving trace NH4+ or Cl- residues, generating ammonium chloride haze or premature tube devitrification during high-temperature bake-out.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-2-2-1-1-1-01` | **Post-RCA-2 Cascade Dump Rinse Resistivity and Ionic Leach Test** | In-line temperature-compensated resistivity sensor (Thornton/Mettler-Toledo M300 with 0.01 cm-1 cell constant) and ICP-MS (Agilent 8900 Triple Quadrupole). | 1. Submerge quartz tube in cascade overflow DI rinse bath with continuous UPW inflow (30 L/min) and megasonic sweep (1 MHz, 400 W). 2. Monitor effluent UPW resistivity continuously until stabilization across 5 dump cycles. 3. Extract a 50 mL aliquot of final effluent rinse water directly from the interior bore of the quartz tube. 4. Run ICP-MS elemental sweep for Na, K, Fe, and Cu concentrations. | `Effluent UPW resistivity must reach >= 18.0 MOhm-cm at 25°C within 15 minutes; ICP-MS trace metal concentrations in the final tube bore rinse aliquot must be <= 0.05 ppb for Na, K, Fe, and Cu individually.` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-2-2-1-1-1-02` | **Megasonic Surface Particle Count and Zeta-Potential Cleanliness Verification** | Surface Particle Inspection System (KLA-Tencor Surfscan SP2 / wafer witness extraction) and liquid optical particle counter (PMS UltraChem 40 for bath particle analysis). | 1. Position witness wafers within the inner wall diameter of the tube prior to final UPW megasonic overflow rinse. 2. Subject the assembly to 10 minutes of active megasonic agitation at 22°C UPW overflow. 3. Transfer witness wafers directly to Marangoni dry module inside mini-environment. 4. Measure localized defect density and particle additions (bins >= 0.18 um) on witness wafers using laser surface scanning. | `Net particle adder count on witness wafers must be <= 0.05 particles/cm2 for particle sizes >= 0.18 um; zero localized particle clusters or residue streaks detected.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Full-face chemical splash shield conforming to ANSI Z87.1, Heavy-duty Neoprene/Viton chemical-resistant sleeves and gauntlet gloves, Full-body acid/base chemical apron (chem-resistant PTFE/Neoprene), Steel-toe composite EH safety boots with non-slip chemical-resistant soles, Emergency cartridge respirator equipped with multi-gas/vapor/particulate filters (ammonia, acid gases, H2O2 mist)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye exposure: Flush with isotonic eyewash or clean tempered water for minimum 15 minutes, holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmological attention. Skin exposure: Immediately peel contaminated gear and flush affected region with copious water for >= 15 min; apply calcium gluconate gel if cross-contamination with fluorine is suspected, otherwise soothing burn dressing after neutralizing decontam. Inhalation: Relocate victim to fresh air immediately; provide 100% humidified oxygen if breathing is labored; alert emergency medical services.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Wet bench dedicated segmented exhaust: Corrosive acid vapor exhaust line (dedicated PP/PVDF ducting, face velocity >= 0.5 m/s at sash opening) for RCA-2 HCl vapors; separate alkaline/NH3 ammonia exhaust line to prevent solid NH4Cl aerosol salt precipitation in ventilation plenums; continuous differential pressure monitoring across wet hood sashes with interlocked low-exhaust audible/visual alarms.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: RCA-1 alkaline effluent and RCA-2 acidic effluent routed via segregated double-containment drainage lines into automated industrial waste neutralization system (AWN); automated dosing using 20% H2SO4 and 25% NaOH with multi-stage agitation to achieve neutral discharge pH (6.5 - 8.5); peroxide decomposition tank equipped with catalytic manganese dioxide or UV dissociation before public sewer discharge.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Ammonium Hydroxide** | `1336-21-6` | SEMI Tier C / Grade 5 | `28.0% - 30.0% NH3 in H2O` |
| **Hydrogen Peroxide** | `7722-84-1` | SEMI Tier C / Grade 5 (Unstabilized Electronic Grade) | `30.0% - 32.0% aqueous` |
| **Hydrochloric Acid** | `7647-01-0` | SEMI Tier C / Grade 5 | `36.5% - 38.0% aqueous` |
| **Ultra-Pure Water (UPW)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM D5127 Type E-1.2 Electronic Grade | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: As-received or post-machining/welding quartz process tube with potential organic handling residues, ambient dust particles, and atmospheric airborne trace metallics.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic, ultra-clean, atomically passivated quartz surface (OH-terminated silanol groups) devoid of metallic contaminants (<1E10 atoms/cm2), trace organics, and free anions (Cl- <0.05 ppb).
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding ambient air Q-time causes adsorption of airborne volatile organic compounds (VOCs, siloxanes, plasticizers) and cleanroom airborne molecular contaminants (boron, phosphorus, trace amines), leading to gate oxide thinning, breakdown voltage degradation, and fixed charge density shifts in 3.5 nm thermal gate oxide.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full physical, chemical, and megasonic decontamination of the horizontal quartz process tube completed through sequential RCA-1 organic/particle lift-off and RCA-2 ionic desorption cleans, rinsed to 18.2 MOhm-cm resistivity, dried, and safely transferred into the horizontal furnace loading zone within certified Q-time.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `QUARTZ_TUBE_RCA_CLEAN_METROLOGY_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `RINSE_RESISTIVITY_AND_TEMPERATURE_LOG.csv`
- [ ] `SURFSCAN_WITNESS_PARTICLE_DISTRIBUTION.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Final effluent rinse UPW resistivity reaches baseline pure water resistivity.** | `18.2 MOhm-cm` | +0.0, -0.2 MOhm-cm at 25°C | Calibrated in-line high-purity immersion conductivity sensor in effluent overflow cell |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Post-cleaning extractable surface iron (Fe) and sodium (Na) surface contamination density.** | `5.0E+09 atoms/cm2` | <= 1.0E+10 atoms/cm2 | Vapor Phase Decomposition - Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (VPD-ICP-MS) |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Witness wafer particle adders across the entire active internal cleaning envelope.** | `0.02 particles/cm2` | <= 0.05 particles/cm2 for size >= 0.18 um | Laser darkfield surface defect scanning (KLA-Tencor Surfscan) |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 3 quantitative assertions strictly met, chemical bath parameters verified by EHS and QA logs, tube visually inspected under high-intensity collimated halogen inspection light showing zero watermarks or haze, and tube sealed into cleanroom N2-purged transport sleeve with active Q-time countdown under 30 minutes to furnace insertion.

q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Hydrophilic, ultra-clean, atomically passivated quartz surface (OH-terminated silanol groups) devoid of metallic contaminants (<1E10 atoms/cm2), trace organics, and free anions (Cl- <0.05 ppb).
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Exceeding ambient air Q-time causes adsorption of airborne volatile organic compounds (VOCs, siloxanes, plasticizers) and cleanroom airborne molecular contaminants (boron, phosphorus, trace amines), leading to gate oxide thinning, breakdown voltage degradation, and fixed charge density shifts in 3.5 nm thermal gate oxide.

expected_result.summary: Full physical, chemical, and megasonic decontamination of the horizontal quartz process tube completed through sequential RCA-1 organic/particle lift-off and RCA-2 ionic desorption cleans, rinsed to 18.2 MOhm-cm resistivity, dried, and safely transferred into the horizontal furnace loading zone within certified Q-time.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Final effluent rinse UPW resistivity reaches baseline pure water resistivity.
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Calibrated in-line high-purity immersion conductivity sensor in effluent overflow cell

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Post-cleaning extractable surface iron (Fe) and sodium (Na) surface contamination density.
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Vapor Phase Decomposition - Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (VPD-ICP-MS)

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Witness wafer particle adders across the entire active internal cleaning envelope.
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Laser darkfield surface defect scanning (KLA-Tencor Surfscan)

expected_result.signoff_criteria: All 3 quantitative assertions strictly met, chemical bath parameters verified by EHS and QA logs, tube visually inspected under high-intensity collimated halogen inspection light showing zero watermarks or haze, and tube sealed into cleanroom N2-purged transport sleeve with active Q-time countdown under 30 minutes to furnace insertion.

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-DIFF-180-007`
**Title:** High-Temp Quartz Furnace Vacuum Bake-Out & Outgassing Desorption Cycle (1000°C)  
**Process Step:** 180nm Dry Gate Oxide Growth (3.5 nm) > Thermal Oxidation Tube Prep  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (180 nm) | **Action Type:** Buy / Facility Qualification

---

### Process Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Chamber Evacuation &  │
│       Leak Check       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Ramp to 1000C under   │
│       N2/Vacuum        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Isothermal High-Temp  │
│    Desorption Soak     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Controlled Ramp-Down  │
│      to Idle 800C      │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Pre-Check & Quartz Tube Sealing:**
   - Confirm RCA cleaning and drying of the quartz tube and silicon carbide/quartz cantilever boat have concluded.
   - Inspect Type R/Type S Platinum-Rhodium thermocouples in their quartz thermowells across Load, Center, and Source zones.
   - Insert empty quartz boat carrier via the mechanical transfer mechanism at a rate strictly under $50\text{ mm/minute}$ to prevent mechanical stress. Seal furnace end-flange.

2. **Chamber Purge & Vacuum Integrity Check:**
   - Flow ultra-high-purity (UHP) $\text{N}_2$ through the calibrated mass flow controller (MFC) at $1\text{ to }5\text{ SLPM}$ to establish laminar purge flow and displace ambient air.
   - Isolate purge or throttle vacuum line using the mechanical booster roots pump system to verify chamber seal integrity and baseline base pressure.

3. **Multi-Zone Temperature Ramp-Up (to 1000°C):**
   - Initialize triple-loop digital PID controller with feedforward decoupling across Kanthal-A1 / Super Kanthal $\text{MoSi}_2$ heating coils (Load, Center, Source).
   - Ramp tube temperature from idle ($800^\circ\text{C}$) to the peak desorption temperature of $1000^\circ\text{C}$ under continuous laminar $\text{N}_2$ purge ($1\text{ to }5\text{ SLPM}$) at a controlled rate ($\le 5^\circ\text{C/min}$).

4. **Isothermal Bake-Out & Outgassing Desorption Soak:**
   - Dwell at $1000^\circ\text{C}$ for the designated desorption period to thermally outgas residual moisture ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$), hydroxyls, and volatile organic contaminants from the quartz tube inner wall.
   - Ensure dynamic triple-loop PID regulation keeps temperature uniform across the central $300\text{ mm}$ flat zone.

5. **Ramp-Down to Idle State:**
   - Ramp down furnace zones from $1000^\circ\text{C}$ to the idle holding temperature of $800^\circ\text{C}$ to $850^\circ\text{C}$ (prior to dry oxidation recipe introduction).
   - Maintain continuous carrier $\text{N}_2$ laminar flow at $1\text{ to }5\text{ SLPM}$ to prevent back-streaming of atmospheric contaminants.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Inspection / Telemetry Method | Target Specification | Physical Units |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isothermal Flat Zone Uniformity** | Multi-zone Type R/S Platinum-Rhodium Thermocouple profiling | $\pm 0.5$ across $300\text{ mm}$ central boat zone | $^\circ\text{C}$ |
| **Peak Desorption Temperature** | Triple-loop digital PID furnace controller | $1000$ (operational range $800 - 1150$) | $^\circ\text{C}$ |
| **Carrier Gas Laminar Flow Rate** | Calibrated Thermal Mass Flow Controller (MFC) | $1.0\text{ to }5.0$ | $\text{SLPM}$ |
| **Boat Mechanical Travel Speed** | Automated cantilever push/pull motor encoder | $< 50$ | $\text{mm/minute}$ |

---

### 3. Literature Context Citations

- **Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation:**
  - Multi-zone heating (Load, Center, Source with Kanthal-A1 or Super Kanthal $\text{MoSi}_2$ elements) and triple-loop digital PID controller with feedforward decoupling.
  - Temperature uniformity requirement of $\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ across central $300\text{ mm}$ boat region over the $800^\circ\text{C} - 1150^\circ\text{C}$ regime using Type R or S Platinum-Rhodium thermocouples.
  - Laminar carrier gas flow regulated by MFC at $1\text{ to }5\text{ SLPM}$.
  - Wafer boat mechanical push/pull speed limit of $< 50\text{ mm/minute}$ to prevent thermal shock and crystallographic slip dislocations.
- **Deal-Grove Silicon Thermal Oxidation Kinetics in Quartz Tube Furnace:**
  - Dry oxidation regime background conditions ($900^\circ\text{C} - 1000^\circ\text{C}$ dry $\text{O}_2$, target $3.5\text{ to }4.0\text{ nm}$ gate oxide dielectric, $E_{bd} > 10\text{ MV/cm}$, $D_{it} < 10^{10}\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{eV}^{-1}$).
- **Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD) of Silicon Nitride Hard Masks:**
  - Vacuum booster roots pumping systems and vacuum seal integrity considerations.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Maintaining vacuum integrity (< 1e-6 Torr ultimate vacuum or sub-mTorr under roots/turbomolecular pumping) at a sustained 1000°C quartz furnace tube skin temperature introduces significant risks of mechanical creep, quartz ovality deformation, and elastomer O-ring thermal degradation at the vacuum flanges. The thermal isolation collar and water-cooled stainless steel end-flanges must be interlocked with chilled water flow meters (minimum 3.0 LPM per flange, T < 25°C) and multi-loop PID controllers with decoupled feedforward terms to prevent thermal runaway beyond the quartz softening threshold while mitigating 3-zone convective-radiative thermal gradients.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 1000°C under vacuum/purged bake-out, the primary kinetics involve desorbing hydroxyl groups (Si-OH), chemisorbed moisture, and volatile metallic halides (e.g., sodium and iron residues) embedded in the inner quartz wall. If residual moisture is desorbed without continuous dry ultra-high-purity N2 or Ar sweeping (2.0 to 5.0 SLPM), hydroxyl back-diffusion and vapor-phase transport will re-contaminate the quartz process tube, leading to catastrophic degradation of gate oxide fixed charge density (Qss) and interface trap density (Dit > 1e11 cm^-2 eV^-1) during the subsequent 3.5 nm dry gate oxidation recipe.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Ultra-high purity fused quartz tubes (GE 214 or equivalent semiconductor grade, 99.999% SiO2, OH content < 5 ppm) and Type R/S Pt-Pt/Rh thermocouples have lead times exceeding 12 to 16 weeks in Southeast Asia. Frequent high-temperature vacuum bake-out cycles accelerate devitrification into cristobalite if surface alkali contamination is present. A strict inventory of replacement fluoroelastomer/Kalrez perfluoroelastomer O-rings (Viton is unacceptable at flanges operating > 150°C) and ceramic feedthrough spares must be maintained to prevent multi-month fab downtime.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The 1000°C vacuum bake-out and thermal outgassing cycle directly anchors the critical path of the 180nm dry gate oxidation baseline. Schedule slippage during tube qualification or outgassing verification cascades directly into furnace idle time, blocking pilot lot wafer dispatch. The bake-out procedure must be locked to an 8-hour deterministic cycle (2 hr ramp-up at 8°C/min, 4 hr 1000°C soak under high vacuum, 2 hr controlled ramp-down to 600°C standby idle) with automated residual gas analyzer (RGA) data collection to guarantee verifiable milestone sign-off without human delay.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal devitrification and structural collapse/ovality of the fused quartz tube under differential vacuum pressure (> 1 atm net external stress) at 1000°C due to localized alkali metal contamination or exceeded quartz strain point.
1. Flange seal failure and vacuum breach caused by cooling water flow interruption to the stainless steel load/source end-flanges, leading to thermal pyrolysis of Kalrez/fluoroelastomer seals and gross atmospheric air back-streaming.
1. Incomplete outgassing desorption and moisture condensation in exhaust forelines, resulting in high H2O partial pressure (RGA mass-to-charge m/z 18 > 1e-8 Torr) during subsequent 850°C gate oxide growth, shifting target 3.5 nm oxide thickness and threshold voltage.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-2-2-1-1-2-01` | **Quadrupole RGA Residual Gas Outgassing Partial Pressure and Vacuum Integrity Test at 1000°C** | Extorr XT300 Quadrupole Residual Gas Analyzer (RGA) (1-300 amu), Edwards Turbomolecular Pump Station with Dry Scroll Backing Pump, Inficon Bayard-Alpert Pirani/Hot-Ion High Vacuum Gauge. | 1. Evacuate quartz furnace tube from atmospheric pressure to base vacuum (< 5.0e-6 Torr) using dry scroll backing and turbomolecular pump. Record baseline cold RGA mass spectrum from m/z 1 to 100. 2. Initiate multi-zone thermal ramp across Load, Center, and Source zones at 8.0°C/min under active pumping until reaching 1000.0°C. 3. Stabilize furnace at 1000°C ± 0.5°C flat zone for 240 minutes. 4. Continuously log partial pressures of m/z 18 (H2O), m/z 28 (N2/CO), m/z 32 (O2), and m/z 44 (CO2) every 30 seconds. 5. Perform a vacuum rate-of-rise test at minute 230 by isolating the high-vacuum gate valve for exactly 60 seconds and logging pressure change via Hot-Ion gauge. 6. Re-open isolation valve, initiate controlled cooling to 600°C standby under 2.0 SLPM UHP N2 sweep. | `PASS if: (a) At minute 240 of 1000°C soak, RGA partial pressure of H2O (m/z 18) <= 5.0e-9 Torr, (b) RGA partial pressure of total hydrocarbons (sum of m/z 41, 43, 55, 57) <= 1.0e-10 Torr, (c) 60-second isolation leak-up rate at 1000°C <= 1.0e-4 Torr·L/s, and (d) Ultimate base vacuum reaches < 1.0e-6 Torr upon cooling to 600°C. FAIL if any partial pressure or rate-of-rise threshold is exceeded.` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-2-2-1-1-2-02` | **Three-Zone Isothermal Flat-Zone Profiling and Quartz Dimension Drift Verification** | 9-point Gold-standard Profiling Thermocouple Array (NIST-traceable Type S Pt/10% Rh-Pt encased in quartz sheath), Fluke 1586A Super-DAQ Precision Temperature Scanner, Mitutoyo Laser Scan Micrometer (LSM-6902H). | 1. Insert calibrated 9-point Type-S thermocouple quartz profiling wand into the center wafer flat zone (covering 350 mm axial span: 0 mm center, ±50 mm, ±100 mm, ±150 mm, ±175 mm). 2. Allow 30 minutes for thermal equilibration at 1000°C. 3. Log all 9 temperature channels simultaneously at 1 Hz for 15 minutes (900 data points per channel). 4. Calculate spatial thermal uniformity (T_max - T_min) and temporal stability (3-sigma drift over 15 minutes) across the 350 mm flat zone. 5. Following furnace cool-down to ambient, remove quartz tube and measure outer diameter (OD) and circularity across 5 equidistant axial points using the laser scan micrometer. | `PASS if: (a) Center 350 mm flat-zone spatial temperature uniformity <= ±0.50°C at 1000.0°C, (b) Temporal temperature drift <= ±0.20°C across the 15-minute measurement window, and (c) Post-bake quartz tube outer diameter ovality/deviation <= 0.25 mm relative to pre-bake baseline. FAIL if temperature delta exceeds ±0.50°C or quartz deformation exceeds 0.25 mm.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal radiant heat proximity face shield (Gold-coated polycarbonate, EN 166 / ANSI Z87.1 approved), Heavy-duty aluminized Kevlar heat-resistant furnace gloves rated to 1050°C contact temperature, Flame-retardant Nomex cleanroom lab coat / thermal apron, Safety glasses with side shields (ANSI Z87.1+ UV/IR filtering), Closed-toe steel-toe cleanroom ESD safety boots with thermal-insulated soles
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal Burns: Immediately immerse affected area in gentle, cold running potable water for at least 15 minutes; do not apply ice, salves, or ointments; cover with sterile, non-adherent dressing; seek immediate medical emergency evaluation. Cryogenic/Asphyxiation Hazard (N2 Purge): Move victim immediately to fresh air; if breathing has stopped, administer artificial respiration by trained personnel; administer oxygen if breathing is labored; seek immediate hospital transportation.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Vacuum roughing and turbomolecular pump exhausts must be hard-ducted directly to dedicated hazardous semiconductor dry scrubber exhaust ducting with negative static differential pressure (minimum -0.75 in. w.g., face velocity >= 100 FPM at flange enclosures). Ambient room continuous real-time optical/electrochemical O2 deficiency monitoring sensors (setpoint alarm 1 at 19.5% O2, evacuation alarm 2 at 18.0% O2) interlocked with automated N2 gas delivery shutoff solenoid valves.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Vacuum pump oil (if fluorinated Fomblin or hydrocarbon backup oil is used) must be collected in closed UN-certified polyethylene/steel drums as hazardous halogenated/hydrocarbon waste for specialized off-site thermal treatment. Dry scroll vacuum tip-seals and quartz shards must be containerized in labeled puncture-proof hazardous solid waste bins in accordance with regional cleanroom hazardous waste disposal protocols.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Nitrogen (Gas, Ultra-High Purity 99.9999%)** | `7727-37-9` | Grade 6.0 (UHP VLSI/Semiconductor Grade, H2O < 50 ppb, O2 < 50 ppb) | `>= 99.9999% vol` |
| **Oxygen (Gas, Ultra-High Purity 99.9995%)** | `7782-44-7` | Grade 5.5 (UHP Semiconductor Grade, Total Hydrocarbons < 100 ppb) | `>= 99.9995% vol` |
| **Fused Silica / Quartz (Solid tube matrix)** | `60676-86-0` | Semiconductor Synthetic / Fused Quartz Grade GE 214 (99.999% SiO2) | `100% solid` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pre-cleaned quartz process tube following RCA standard sequence (SC-1 organic strip, SC-2 metallic desorption, 50:1 HF oxide de-glaze, 18.2 MOhm·cm megasonic UPW rinse), dried via filtered UHP N2, verified zero particulate contamination (Class 1 cleanroom environment).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Thermally outgassed, dehydrated fused quartz inner wall matrix with depleted surface hydroxyls (Si-OH < 0.1 monolayer), zero volatile organic/metallic residues, sealed under 1.5 atm continuous UHP N2 positive pressure purge at 600°C standby idle.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding allowable queue time before running subsequent 850°C gate oxidation causes airborne moisture and ambient hydrocarbon chemisorption back onto the inner quartz tube surface. During gate oxidation, this desorbs as steam and carbon contaminants, causing uncontrolled moisture-assisted accelerated oxidation, interface roughness (> 0.3 nm RMS), fixed oxide charge spikes (Qss > 5e10 cm^-2), and premature time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB) of the 3.5 nm DRAM gate dielectric.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full high-temperature (1000°C) vacuum bake-out, outgassing desorption, and 3-zone thermal profiling qualification of the horizontal fused quartz oxidation furnace tube. Verifies complete removal of moisture, hydrocarbons, and surface volatile contaminants under continuous high vacuum and UHP N2 sweep, ensuring the furnace tube maintains structural integrity, vacuum leak tightness, and ±0.5°C flat-zone isothermal stability prior to 3.5 nm dry gate oxidation execution.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `FURNACE_TUBE_1000C_VACUUM_BAKEOUT_RGA_SPECTRUM.csv`
- [ ] `THREE_ZONE_1000C_ISOTHERMAL_PROFILE_RUN_LOG.pdf`
- [ ] `QUARTZ_TUBE_POST_BAKEOUT_METROLOGY_SCAN.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Maximum water vapor (H2O, m/z 18) partial pressure at 1000°C bake-out soak termination** | `5.0e-9` | <= 5.0e-9 Torr | Extorr XT300 Quadrupole Residual Gas Analyzer continuous spectrum logging at 1000°C under turbomolecular pumping. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Furnace center flat zone 350 mm spatial temperature uniformity at 1000°C** | `0.0` | <= ±0.50 °C delta across 350 mm axial span | NIST-traceable 9-point Pt/Pt-Rh Type S profiling thermocouple wand scanned at 1 Hz for 15 minutes using precision Super-DAQ. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Vacuum chamber isolation rate-of-rise (leak-up and outgassing rate) at 1000°C** | `5.0e-5` | <= 1.0e-4 Torr·L/s | High-vacuum isolation valve closure for 60 seconds with Inficon Bayard-Alpert Hot-Ion gauge differential pressure recording. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> The furnace bake-out and thermal qualification is approved only when: (1) RGA logs confirm H2O partial pressure <= 5.0e-9 Torr and total hydrocarbons <= 1.0e-10 Torr at 1000°C, (2) Three-zone thermal flat-zone profiling demonstrates spatial uniformity within ±0.50°C across 350 mm for >= 15 continuous minutes, (3) Rate-of-rise leak rate is verified <= 1.0e-4 Torr·L/s at 1000°C, (4) Quartz tube circularity metrology verifies OD deviation <= 0.25 mm with no visual devitrification hazing, and (5) Furnace is sealed under positive UHP N2 flow at 600°C standby idle ready for immediate 3.5 nm dry gate oxide pilot processing.

Cryogenic/Asphyxiation Hazard (N2 Purge): Move victim immediately to fresh air; if breathing has stopped, administer artificial respiration by trained personnel; administer oxygen if breathing is labored; seek immediate hospital transportation.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Vacuum roughing and turbomolecular pump exhausts must be hard-ducted directly to dedicated hazardous semiconductor dry scrubber exhaust ducting with negative static differential pressure (minimum -0.75 in. w.g., face velocity >= 100 FPM at flange enclosures). Ambient room continuous real-time optical/electrochemical O2 deficiency monitoring sensors (setpoint alarm 1 at 19.5% O2, evacuation alarm 2 at 18.0% O2) interlocked with automated N2 gas delivery shutoff solenoid valves.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Vacuum pump oil (if fluorinated Fomblin or hydrocarbon backup oil is used) must be collected in closed UN-certified polyethylene/steel drums as hazardous halogenated/hydrocarbon waste for specialized off-site thermal treatment. Dry scroll vacuum tip-seals and quartz shards must be containerized in labeled puncture-proof hazardous solid waste bins in accordance with regional cleanroom hazardous waste disposal protocols.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Pre-cleaned quartz process tube following RCA standard sequence (SC-1 organic strip, SC-2 metallic desorption, 50:1 HF oxide de-glaze, 18.2 MOhm·cm megasonic UPW rinse), dried via filtered UHP N2, verified zero particulate contamination (Class 1 cleanroom environment).
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Thermally outgassed, dehydrated fused quartz inner wall matrix with depleted surface hydroxyls (Si-OH < 0.1 monolayer), zero volatile organic/metallic residues, sealed under 1.5 atm continuous UHP N2 positive pressure purge at 600°C standby idle.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Exceeding allowable queue time before running subsequent 850°C gate oxidation causes airborne moisture and ambient hydrocarbon chemisorption back onto the inner quartz tube surface. During gate oxidation, this desorbs as steam and carbon contaminants, causing uncontrolled moisture-assisted accelerated oxidation, interface roughness (> 0.3 nm RMS), fixed oxide charge spikes (Qss > 5e10 cm^-2), and premature time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB) of the 3.5 nm DRAM gate dielectric.

expected_result.summary: Full high-temperature (1000°C) vacuum bake-out, outgassing desorption, and 3-zone thermal profiling qualification of the horizontal fused quartz oxidation furnace tube. Verifies complete removal of moisture, hydrocarbons, and surface volatile contaminants under continuous high vacuum and UHP N2 sweep, ensuring the furnace tube maintains structural integrity, vacuum leak tightness, and ±0.5°C flat-zone isothermal stability prior to 3.5 nm dry gate oxidation execution.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Maximum water vapor (H2O, m/z 18) partial pressure at 1000°C bake-out soak termination
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Extorr XT300 Quadrupole Residual Gas Analyzer continuous spectrum logging at 1000°C under turbomolecular pumping.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Furnace center flat zone 350 mm spatial temperature uniformity at 1000°C
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: NIST-traceable 9-point Pt/Pt-Rh Type S profiling thermocouple wand scanned at 1 Hz for 15 minutes using precision Super-DAQ.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Vacuum chamber isolation rate-of-rise (leak-up and outgassing rate) at 1000°C
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: High-vacuum isolation valve closure for 60 seconds with Inficon Bayard-Alpert Hot-Ion gauge differential pressure recording.

expected_result.signoff_criteria: The furnace bake-out and thermal qualification is approved only when: (1) RGA logs confirm H2O partial pressure <= 5.0e-9 Torr and total hydrocarbons <= 1.0e-10 Torr at 1000°C, (2) Three-zone thermal flat-zone profiling demonstrates spatial uniformity within ±0.50°C across 350 mm for >= 15 continuous minutes, (3) Rate-of-rise leak rate is verified <= 1.0e-4 Torr·L/s at 1000°C, (4) Quartz tube circularity metrology verifies OD deviation <= 0.25 mm with no visual devitrification hazing, and (5) Furnace is sealed under positive UHP N2 flow at 600°C standby idle ready for immediate 3.5 nm dry gate oxide pilot processing.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-DIFF-MET-004`
**Title:** Ultra-High Purity N2/O2 Mass Flow Controller (MFC) Dynamic Flow Calibration & Leak Rate Verification  
**Hierarchy Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > 180nm Dry Gate Oxide Growth (3.5 nm) > Dry Thermal Oxidation Recipe Execution (850°C-900°C, 3.5 nm SiO2) > Horizontal Quartz Furnace Dry O2 Oxidation Recipe Execution (850°C, Pure O2/N2 Dilution) > Quartz Furnace Tube Prep, Multi-Zone Thermal Profiling & MFC Gas Calibration (850°C N2/O2) > Quartz Tube RCA-Clean, Bake-Out & MFC Flow Calibration (N2/O2) > Ultra-High Purity N2/O2 Mass Flow Controller (MFC) Dynamic Flow Calibration & Leak Rate Verification  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm / 180nm)  
**Action Type:** Make / Metrology  

---

### 1. Purpose & Scope
This procedure governs dynamic in-situ flow calibration and helium mass spectrometer / pressure rate-of-rise leak verification for Ultra-High Purity (UHP) carrier and process gas Mass Flow Controllers ($\text{N}_2$ purge and ultra-pure $\text{O}_2$) dedicated to the horizontal quartz tube dry gate oxide furnace ($t_{ox} = 3.5\text{--}4.0\text{ nm}$).

---

### 2. Required Equipment & Reference Standards
- NIST-traceable Molbloc/Molbox or dry piston displacement gas calibrator (working range: 0.5 to 10.0 SLPM).
- Portable Helium Mass Spectrometer Leak Detector (sniffing and vacuum hood modes).
- Capacitance Diaphragm Gauge (CDG) manifold (range: 0.1 mTorr to 1000 Torr).
- 316L VCR UHP manifold isolation valves and particulate filters ($0.003\ \mu\text{m}$).

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Procedure

```
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| Step 1: Pre-Calibration Gas Line Purge & Environmental Soak |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| Step 2: External & Internal Seat Leak Rate Verification     |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| Step 3: Multi-Point Dynamic Flow Calibration (1 to 5 SLPM)  |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| Step 4: Step Response & Zero-Stability Drift Verification   |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
```

#### Step 1: Pre-Calibration Gas Line Purge & Environmental Soak
1. Connect the NIST-traceable flow calibrator downstream of the gas delivery panel using electropolished 316L SS VCR lines.
2. Cycle-purge the delivery manifolds 10 times alternating between dry UHP $\text{N}_2$ (99.9999% purity) at 30 psig and turbo-molecular vacuum evacuation ($< 1\times 10^{-3}\text{ Torr}$).
3. Energize the thermal/pressure-based MFC control electronics for at least 60 minutes prior to calibration to achieve internal thermal equilibrium.

#### Step 2: External & Internal Seat Leak Rate Verification
1. **External Boundary Leak Check:** Enclose all MFC body seals, VCR gaskets, and upstream/downstream welds in a flexible helium shroud. Pressurize lines to 30 psig with UHP He and verify external leak rate using the mass spectrometer leak detector.
2. **Internal Shutoff Valve Seat Leakage Check:** Close the MFC integrated shutoff solenoid/piezo valve with upstream line pressurized at 30 psig. Evacuate the downstream test volume to $< 100\text{ mTorr}$, isolate the vacuum pump, and measure downstream pressure rise rate over a 10-minute hold using the high-accuracy CDG.

#### Step 3: Multi-Point Dynamic Flow Calibration (1 to 5 SLPM)
1. Set upstream gas supply pressure to regulated recipe operating pressure (typically 30.0 psig ± 0.5 psig).
2. Command the MFC controller through a 5-point calibration ladder within the validated furnace laminar flow envelope:
   - Point 1: 1.0 SLPM (20% of 5 SLPM full scale)
   - Point 2: 2.0 SLPM (40% of full scale)
   - Point 3: 3.0 SLPM (60% of full scale)
   - Point 4: 4.0 SLPM (80% of full scale)
   - Point 5: 5.0 SLPM (100% of full scale)
3. Allow each setpoint to stabilize for 60 seconds. Record the standard volumetric flow rate ($Q_{std}$ at 0°C, 101.325 kPa) from the primary reference calibrator against the MFC electrical analog/digital feedback signal.
4. Calculate flow error:
   $$\text{Error} (\%) = \frac{Q_{\text{indicated}} - Q_{\text{reference}}}{\text{Full Scale (5 SLPM)}} \times 100$$
5. Perform linear interpolation adjustment in the tool recipe controller if calibration drift exceeds permissible acceptance criteria.

#### Step 4: Step Response & Zero-Stability Drift Verification
1. Command a step transition from 0 to 5.0 SLPM and record the time to reach within ±1.0% of final target value.
2. Command setpoint back to 0.0 SLPM, wait 30 seconds, and measure the zero-flow signal drift over a 15-minute continuous monitoring window.

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Specification | Physical Units | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Calibrated Gas Flow Range** | $1.0\text{ to }5.0$ | $\text{SLPM}$ | NIST-traceable primary flow calibrator |
| **Flow Accuracy across 1–5 SLPM** | $\le \pm 1.0\%$ | $\%$ of Full Scale (5 SLPM) | Multi-point calibration average deviation |
| **MFC Integrated Seat Leak Rate** | $< 1.0 \times 10^{-6}$ | $\text{atm}\cdot\text{cm}^3/\text{sec (scc/sec He)}$ | Pressure rate-of-rise via CDG |
| **External Envelope Leak Rate** | $< 1.0 \times 10^{-9}$ | $\text{atm}\cdot\text{cm}^3/\text{sec (scc/sec He)}$ | Vacuum/shroud He mass spectrometer |
| **Flow Step Settling Time** | $< 2.0$ | $\text{seconds}$ | Step-response tracking (0 to 5 SLPM setpoint) |

---

### 5. Context Citations & Technical Justification
- **Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation:** Direct source for the furnace gas flow dynamics, mandating laminar carrier gas flow ($\text{N}_2$ purge, ultra-pure $\text{O}_2$) regulated by Mass Flow Controllers within the **$1\text{ to }5\text{ SLPM}$** range to preserve uniform gas phase boundary layers without disrupting the isothermal zone.
- **Deal-Grove Silicon Thermal Oxidation Kinetics in Quartz Tube Furnace:** Establishes the dry thermal oxidation process context where gate oxide thickness targets of **$3.5\text{ to }4.0\text{ nm}$** require strictly repeatable, precise delivery of pure dry $\text{O}_2$ to maintain linear rate constant ($k_l = B/A$) stability and minimize interface trap density ($D_{it} < 10^{10}\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ eV}^{-1}$).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Thermal mass flow controller (MFC) calibration curves must be dynamically integrated into the furnace PID automation loop. Non-linear flow response between 1.0 and 5.0 SLPM directly destabilizes boundary-layer thickness across the 350 mm isothermal flat zone, compromising dry O2 partial pressure regulation and Deal-Grove linear oxidation rate constants.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For ultrathin 3.5 nm gate dielectric growth, a ±1.0% error in O2/N2 dilution ratio causes a >0.2 nm shift in oxide thickness, introducing unacceptable threshold voltage (Vth) dispersion and gate leakage variability. Dynamic rate-of-rise (RoR) metrology must decouple gas expansion thermal artifacts from physical leak rates to prevent false-positive hermeticity signoffs.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Ultra-High Purity (UHP) metal-sealed MFC units (316L VIM/VAR electropolished) and dry primary piston provers have 16-24 week procurement lead times. In-situ pressure rate-of-decay and volumetric primary standards must be maintained locally to circumvent Fab shutdown during recalibration intervals.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: MFC dynamic flow verification and helium mass spectrometer leak check represent an irreversible gate before furnace bake-out and 850°C baseline dry oxidation runs. Failure to pass both within scheduled metrology windows cascades into immediate tool downtime for the entire 180nm front-end thermal gate module.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal sensor drift or zero-offset error in the O2 MFC causing uncalibrated excess oxygen partial pressure, leading to uncontrolled rapid initial oxidation and out-of-spec gate oxide thickness (>3.7 nm).
1. VCR fitting seal compromise or internal MFC control-valve seat leakage introducing ambient moisture (>5 ppb H2O) and atmospheric N2/O2 contamination into UHP lines, triggering catastrophic gate oxide interface trap density (Dit > 1e11 eV-1 cm-2).

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-2-2-1-1-3-01` | **MFC Dynamic Flow Accuracy & Linearity Multi-Point Calibration (N2 & O2)** | NIST-traceable Molbloc/Molbox dry gas primary flow calibration system, calibrated downstream quartz pressure transducer, digital flow controller data acquisition interface. | 1. Connect NIST-traceable primary flow standard to downstream manifold of UHP N2 MFC. 2. Command setpoints in 5 discrete steps: 10% (0.5 SLPM), 25% (1.25 SLPM), 50% (2.5 SLPM), 75% (3.75 SLPM), and 100% (5.0 SLPM). 3. Dwell at each step for 180 seconds to reach steady-state thermal equilibrium. 4. Record 60 continuous flow measurements per step at 1 Hz. 5. Repeat sequence for UHP O2 MFC using gas-specific thermal correction factor (CF). 6. Compute linearity deviation, zero drift, and full-scale error across all setpoints. | `Flow rate setpoint accuracy within ± 0.5% of full scale (FS) across 1.0 to 5.0 SLPM; flow repeatability <= 0.2% FS; zero-offset drift <= 0.1% FS after 180s stabilization.` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-2-2-1-1-3-02` | **MFC In-Line Hermeticity and Helium Mass Spectrometer Leak Rate Verification** | Pfeiffer ASM 340 High-Sensitivity Helium Leak Detector, UHP manifold turbo-molecular pumping station, 1/4-inch VCR metal gasket test caps, calibrated He permeation standard (leak rate: 1.0e-9 mbar·L/s). | 1. Connect helium leak detector to downstream port of MFC assembly. 2. Establish high-vacuum baseline test mode (pressure < 1.0e-4 mbar). 3. Measure background He signal until stable below 1.0e-10 mbar·L/s. 4. Hood test: Enclose MFC body, VCR fittings, and inlet/outlet connections inside plastic bagging filled with 99.999% pure He for 180 seconds. 5. Sniffer/probe test: Direct high-purity He jet (10 sccm) precisely around VCR gland welds, body seals, and valve actuator bonnet. 6. Internal seat leak test: Close MFC valve via software (setpoint 0.0 SLPM), pressurize upstream with He at 30 psig, and monitor downstream leak rate for 300 seconds. | `Total external envelope helium leak rate < 1.0e-9 mbar·L/s; internal valve seat cross-leakage < 1.0e-7 mbar·L/s under 30 psig differential pressure.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom-grade nitrile gloves (double gloving), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Cryogenic/thermal gloves during high-pressure connection torqueing, Flame-retardant cleanroom lab coat
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Asphyxiation Hazard (N2/He): Immediately remove victim to fresh air. If breathing is labored, administer medical oxygen by trained personnel. If breathing ceases, initiate artificial respiration and CPR immediately; contact emergency medical services. Oxygen Enrichment Hazard (O2): Flush victim skin/clothing with water; remove non-flameproof clothing immediately to prevent flash-fire ignition. No chemical antidote required.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated cleanroom gas cabinet toxic/inert exhaust operating at constant negative static pressure (-0.5 to -1.0 in. w.g.); minimum duct face velocity >= 200 FPM; continuous inline O2 deficiency and enrichment room sensors (alarm thresholds: low at 19.5% O2, high at 23.5% O2).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Inert venting of dry N2 and He via dedicated scrubbed process exhaust lines; UHP O2 purged to atmosphere through high-dilution exhaust ducting isolated from hydrocarbon and solvent vapor streams.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Nitrogen (Ultra-High Purity Gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Grade 6.0 (99.9999%) | `100%` |
| **Oxygen (Ultra-High Purity Gas)** | `7782-44-7` | Grade 5.5 (99.9995%) | `100%` |
| **Helium (Leak Detection Gas)** | `7440-59-7` | Grade 5.0 (99.999%) | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Electropolished 316L VIM/VAR internal gas-contact surfaces (Ra <= 5 micro-inch / 0.13 um), ultrasonically solvent-cleaned, helium leak-tight, and pre-baked at 120°C under UHP N2 purge.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Moisture-passivated (< 5 ppb H2O), hermetically sealed, dynamically calibrated internal manifold isolated under 15 psig UHP N2 positive pressure blanket.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Atmospheric moisture and airborne molecular contamination (AMC) back-streaming into open gas delivery lines forms hydrated native silanols and transition metal oxides on inner tube walls, degrading 3.5 nm dry gate oxide breakdown field (Ebd < 10 MV/cm) and causing uncontrolled initial growth transients.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full 5-point NIST-traceable dynamic calibration of N2 and O2 mass flow controllers verified across the 1.0 to 5.0 SLPM range, accompanied by helium mass spectrometer leak envelope verification confirming complete hermeticity of all process gas delivery lines prior to furnace tube bake-out.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `mfc_n2_o2_dynamic_calibration_curves.csv`
- [ ] `helium_leak_detector_qualification_report.pdf`
- [ ] `mfc_step_response_and_zero_drift_telemetry.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **MFC steady-state dynamic flow error across 1.0 to 5.0 SLPM setpoints** | `0.0% FS` | <= ±0.5% FS | Downstream comparison against NIST-traceable Molbloc/Molbox dry gas primary piston prover standard. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Total external envelope helium leak rate for MFC and VCR manifold joints** | `< 1.0e-10 mbar*L/s` | <= 1.0e-9 mbar*L/s | Hard vacuum hood and sniffing mode using Pfeiffer ASM 340 Helium Mass Spectrometer Leak Detector. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **MFC internal control valve shutoff seat bypass leak rate under 30 psig supply pressure** | `0.0 sccm` | <= 1.0e-7 mbar*L/s | Downstream pressure rate-of-rise measurement into calibrated isolated vacuum chamber. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Both N2 and O2 MFCs exhibit full-scale accuracy <= ±0.5% across all 5 test points, envelope leak rate verified <= 1.0e-9 mbar·L/s He, internal seat leakage verified <= 1.0e-7 mbar·L/s He, and UHP line moisture verified < 5 ppb H2O with signed engineering metrology approval.
