nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## RCA-1 (SC-1) and RCA-2 (SC-2) Chemical Bath Preparation and Organic/Metallic Decontamination

**Task Hierarchy:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > 180nm Dry Gate Oxide Growth (3.5 nm) > Pre-Oxidation RCA Clean and Passivation  
**Action Type:** Make | **Generation:** Gen 2 (µm)

---

### Process Flow

```text
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│  RCA-1 Clean 70-80C  │
│                      │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│   Dump Rinse 18.2    │
│       MOhm-cm        │
│                      │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│  HF 1:50 Dip 15-30s  │
│                      │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│  RCA-2 Clean 70-80C  │
│                      │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│   Final Rinse & N2   │
│       Blow-Dry       │
│                      │
└──────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **RCA-1 (Standard Clean 1 / SC-1) Formulation & Bath Preparation**:
   - In a chemical wet-bench quartz or Teflon tank, blend deionized water, ammonium hydroxide, and hydrogen peroxide in a **5 : 1 : 1** volumetric ratio:
     - 5 parts ultra-pure deionized water ($\text{DI H}_2\text{O}$, $\ge 18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$).
     - 1 part Ammonium Hydroxide ($\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$, $29\%$).
     - 1 part Hydrogen Peroxide ($\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$, $30\%$).
   - Heat the chemical bath to **$70^\circ\text{C} - 80^\circ\text{C}$**.

2. **RCA-1 Organic & Particle Decontamination**:
   - Immerse silicon wafer cassettes into the RCA-1 bath at **$70^\circ\text{C} - 80^\circ\text{C}$** for **$10 - 15\text{ minutes}$** to oxidize and dissolve organic surface contamination and light trace metals.

3. **Intermediate Quick Dump Rinse (QDR)**:
   - Transfer wafers into a dump rinse tank filled with **$18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$** DI water; cycle for **$3\text{ minutes}$** until baseline resistivity is recovered.

4. **Intermediate Native Oxide Strip (HF Dip)**:
   - Submerge wafers in a dilute **$1:50\text{ HF}:\text{H}_2\text{O}$** solution for **$15 - 30\text{ seconds}$** to strip chemically grown/native surface oxide until the surface exhibits complete hydrophobicity (dewetting).
   - Follow immediately with a DI water cascade rinse.

5. **RCA-2 (Standard Clean 2 / SC-2) Formulation & Bath Preparation**:
   - In a separate clean quartz immersion bath, prepare the acidic bath in a **$6 : 1 : 1$** volumetric ratio:
     - 6 parts ultra-pure deionized water ($\text{DI H}_2\text{O}$).
     - 1 part Hydrochloric Acid ($\text{HCl}$, $37\%$).
     - 1 part Hydrogen Peroxide ($\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$, $30\%$).
   - Heat the chemical solution to **$70^\circ\text{C} - 80^\circ\text{C}$**.

6. **RCA-2 Heavy & Alkali Metal Stripping**:
   - Immerse wafers into the heated RCA-2 solution at **$70^\circ\text{C} - 80^\circ\text{C}$** for **$10\text{ minutes}$** to solubilize and desorb alkali ionic contamination ($\text{Na}^+, \text{K}^+$) and transition/heavy metallic traces ($\text{Fe, Cu, Ni}$).

7. **Final Rinse & Spin/Drying**:
   - Transfer wafers through an ultra-pure DI rinse until effluent reaches **$18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$**.
   - Dry immediately utilizing high-purity filtered Nitrogen ($\text{N}_2$) blow-dry or spin-rinse dryer.

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Range | Physical Unit | Measurement Tool / Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **RCA-1 (SC-1) Bath Temperature** | $75.0$ | $70.0 - 80.0$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ | Integrated Pt-100 / Teflon thermocouple probe |
| **RCA-1 Immersion Duration** | $12.5$ | $10.0 - 15.0$ | $\text{min}$ | Wet bench robotic recipe timer |
| **Intermediate Rinse Water Resistivity** | $18.2$ | $\ge 18.2$ | $\text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ | In-line conductivity / resistivity sensor |
| **1:50 HF Dip Etch Duration** | $22.5$ | $15.0 - 30.0$ | $\text{s}$ | Automated pneumatic arm process timer |
| **RCA-2 (SC-2) Bath Temperature** | $75.0$ | $70.0 - 80.0$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ | Tank quartz-sheathed temperature sensor |
| **RCA-2 Immersion Duration** | $10.0$ | $10.0$ | $\text{min}$ | Wet bench process controller timer |

---

### Literature Citations
- **Source: Standard RCA-1 and RCA-2 Silicon Wafer Cleaning Procedure**:
  - *RCA-1 formulation ($5:1:1\text{ DI H}_2\text{O} : 29\%\text{ NH}_4\text{OH} : 30\%\text{ H}_2\text{O}_2$), operational temperature ($70^\circ\text{C}-80^\circ\text{C}$ for $10-15\text{ min}$), $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ dump rinse ($3\text{ min}$), $1:50\text{ HF}$ native oxide strip ($15-30\text{ s}$), RCA-2 formulation ($6:1:1\text{ DI H}_2\text{O} : 37\%\text{ HCl} : 30\%\text{ H}_2\text{O}_2$), operational temperature ($70^\circ\text{C}-80^\circ\text{C}$ for $10\text{ min}$), and high-purity $\text{N}_2$ blow-dry.*

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Maintaining strict thermal bath control (75°C ± 2°C) while managing continuous H2O2 catalytic and thermal decomposition requires an automated chemical replenishment schedule or bath lifetime capping at 4 hours max. Without real-time bath concentration monitoring or strict bath expiration timers, the peroxide-to-ammonia ratio drifts, accelerating silicon micro-roughening in SC-1 and impairing the subsequent 3.5 nm ultra-thin gate oxide breakdown field (E_bd).
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: SC-1 chemistry (5:1:1 UPW:NH4OH:H2O2) must be precisely balanced: excessive NH4OH or depleted H2O2 dramatically increases surface etching and roughness (RMS > 0.15 nm), degrading inversion layer channel mobility and gate oxide integrity in 180nm DRAM access transistors. In SC-2 (6:1:1 UPW:HCl:H2O2), failure to complex transition metals (Fe, Cu, Ni) below 1E10 atoms/cm² creates mid-gap states and gate dielectric weak spots, leading to excessive leakage currents in the peripheral analog and bitline sense circuitry.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Electronic/Semiconductor grade chemicals (SEMI Tier 1 / Grade 5 or SEMI-C12) are mandatory for NH4OH, HCl, and unstabilized H2O2; standard reagent grade contains trace ppm levels of iron and mobile sodium that will contaminate the RCA wet bench quartz tanks and carry over directly into the horizontal oxidation furnace quartz tube.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: RCA clean steps require synchronized operator batching with the pre-oxidation HF-dip bench and the horizontal diffusion furnace loading sequence. Idle time post-cleaning prior to HF passivation and thermal oxidation must be strictly metered under strict Q-time tracking to prevent queue hold-ups and batch scrap.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal and catalytic depletion of H2O2 in the SC-1 bath shifting the chemical equilibrium toward pure alkaline silicon etching, producing severe surface pitting and gate oxide punch-through.
1. Inadequate intermediate dump rinse resistivity (< 18.0 MOhm-cm) causing alkaline drag-out from SC-1 into the acidic SC-2 bath, neutralizing the HCl chelating environment and causing precipitation of insoluble transition metal hydroxides.
1. Excessive exposure time or temperature runaway (> 80°C) during SC-1 causing silicon surface micro-roughness exceeding 0.18 nm RMS, deteriorating Deal-Grove linear oxidation kinetics and 3.5 nm oxide dielectric uniformity.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-2-2-2-1-1-01` | **Post-SC-1 and SC-2 Surface Metallic Trace Contamination Assessment via TXRF** | Total Reflection X-Ray Fluorescence Spectrometer (TXRF, Rigaku TXRF 3760 or equivalent calibrated with multi-element silicon wafer standards) | 1. Load processed wafer into TXRF automated chamber under Class 1 mini-environment. 2. Align glancing incidence angle at 0.05° to achieve total external reflection. 3. Measure X-ray fluorescence spectrum across a 9-point radial map (center, R/2, R-5mm edge exclusion) targeting Fe, Cu, Ni, and Zn peaks with 1000s live integration time per point. 4. Calculate surface areal density in atoms/cm². | `Surface concentrations across all 9 points must meet: Fe < 1.0E10 atoms/cm², Cu < 5.0E9 atoms/cm², Ni < 5.0E9 atoms/cm², and Zn < 1.0E10 atoms/cm².` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-2-2-2-1-1-02` | **Post-SC-1 Surface Micro-Roughness and Particle Density Verification** | Atomic Force Microscope (AFM, Bruker Dimension Icon in Tapping Mode) and Laser Surface Particle Scanner (KLA-Tencor Surfscan SP2 or equivalent at 65nm threshold) | 1. Run wafer through KLA Surfscan to count light point defects (LPD) ≥ 65 nm with a 3 mm edge exclusion. 2. Transfer wafer to AFM. 3. Scan 5 distinct 2 µm x 2 µm locations across center and 4 orthogonal peripheral sites at 0.5 Hz scan rate. 4. Extract root-mean-square roughness (Rq / RMS) from flattened topography maps. | `Surface Particle Density: Total LPD (≥ 65 nm) < 20 particles/wafer. Surface Micro-roughness: RMS micro-roughness ≤ 0.12 nm across all 5 measured sites.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Chemical-resistant neoprene/Viton dual-layer wet bench gloves with extended cuffs, Full-face polycarbonate chemical splash shield over ANSI Z87.1 safety glasses, Heavy-duty chemical apron (acid/alkali resistant PTFE/PVDF or rubber), Cleanroom-compatible steel-toe chemical protective boots with safety gaiters
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin contact: Immediately flush affected area with copiously flowing water from safety shower for minimum 15 minutes while stripping contaminated clothing. For eye exposure: Hold eyelids open and flush with clean emergency eye-wash water for at least 15 minutes; seek urgent ophthalmologist review. Inhalation of ammonia or hydrochloric fumes: Relocate victim to fresh outdoor air immediately, administer medical oxygen if breathing is labored, and obtain prompt emergency medical services.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Wet chemical bench dedicated lip exhaust slots providing continuous face velocity of ≥ 0.5 m/s (100 FPM). Fume collection separated into distinct acid exhaust (for HCl) and alkaline/corrosive exhaust (for NH3 fumes) connected to dedicated wet scrubbers to prevent reactive ammonium chloride (NH4Cl) particulate deposition in ducting.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: SC-1 alkaline effluent and SC-2 acid waste must be segregated into independent chemical drain networks. SC-2 waste is routed to the automated Acid Waste Neutralization (AWN) system adjusting pH to 6.5-8.5 using 10% NaOH prior to discharge. SC-1 alkaline waste is directed to basic equalization sumps neutralized with dilute sulfuric acid. Spent concentrated peroxide mixtures must undergo controlled catalytic thermal dissipation to prevent exothermic runaway or pressure buildup in collection tanks.

| **Ultrapure Water (UPW)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM D5127 Type E-1 (TOC < 1 ppb, Resistivity 18.2 MOhm-cm @ 25°C) | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic or contaminated silicon surface exhibiting native chemical oxide (0.8-1.5 nm) with organic airborne hydrocarbons, particulates, and baseline metallic ionic contaminants.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic silicon surface terminated with an ultra-clean, chemically grown passivating thin chemical oxide (0.6-0.8 nm SiO2) free of metallic impurities and organic carbon residues.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding queue time allows cleanroom airborne volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and moisture to chemisorb onto the chemically active oxide surface, creating carbon traps and nucleation defects that distort 3.5 nm gate oxide thickness uniformity and induce early breakdown (TDDB) during furnace oxidation.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful bath preparation and wafer chemical clean execution across SC-1 (5:1:1 UPW:NH4OH:H2O2 @ 75°C) and SC-2 (6:1:1 UPW:HCl:H2O2 @ 75°C) followed by thorough Quick Dump Rinsing (18.2 MOhm-cm) and N2 drying, yielding cleanroom-verified, particle-free, transition-metal-free silicon surfaces ready for subsequent gate-quality native oxide HF strip and thermal oxidation.

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Dilute HF (1:50) Oxide Strip and Hydrogen-Terminated Surface Passivation Dip

**Hierarchy Context**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (`DRAM Foundation VN`) > 180nm Dry Gate Oxide Growth (3.5 nm) > RCA Clean and Pre-Oxidation Surface Passivation with HF Last Etch > Dilute HF (1:50) Oxide Strip and Hydrogen-Terminated Surface Passivation Dip  
**Action Type**: Make  
**Technology Node**: 180nm (Gen 2)

---

### Process Architecture Workflow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["RCA Clean Output (Post SC-1 & SC-2)"] --> B["Dilute HF (1:50) Immersion Tank (20°C - 25°C)"]
    B --> C["Native / Chemical SiO2 Strip (Selective vs Si3N4)"]
    C --> D["Hydrophobic Hydrogen-Terminated (Si-H) Passivation"]
    D --> E["Quick Dump Rinse (QDR) to 18 MOhm·cm"]
    E --> F["Surface Tension / Marangoni N2 Spin Dry"]
    F --> G["Immediate Load to 850°C Gate Oxidation Furnace"]
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Bath Preparation & Temperature Stabilization**:
   - Prepare a 1:50 volumetric dilution using semiconductor-grade 49% hydrofluoric acid ($1\text{ part HF (49\%)} : 50\text{ parts UPW}$).
   - Verify recirculation and bath temperature stabilization at $22.0^\circ\text{C} \pm 1.0^\circ\text{C}$ in a PVDF/PTFE wet bench tank.

2. **Cassette Transfer & Pre-Wetting**:
   - Transfer wafer batch directly from the downstream RCA clean (post-SC-2 / megasonic rinse) into the process tank manipulator arm.
   - Lower the cassette into the DHF bath at a controlled immersion velocity ($15\text{ mm/s}$) to eliminate air entrapment on high-aspect DRAM micro-topologies.

3. **Oxide Etch & Surface Depassivation**:
   - Submerge wafers for $60\text{ to }90\text{ s}$ to strip native/chemical silicon oxide ($\sim 1.0\text{--}1.5\text{ nm}$).
   - Etch proceeds according to: $\text{SiO}_2 + 6\text{HF} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{SiF}_6 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
   - Ensure preservation of underlying silicon nitride masks (nitride etch rate remains $< 0.5\text{ nm/min}$).

4. **Hydrogen Termination & Dewet Verification**:
   - Allow final surface fluorine desorption and surface replacement with monohydride/dihydride bonds ($\text{Si-H}$ passivation), rendering bare silicon channel areas entirely hydrophobic.
   - Confirm complete dewet ("sheeting off" of aqueous solution) upon wafer edge emergence.

5. **Quick Dump Rinse (QDR) & Marangoni Dry**:
   - Transfer within $< 5\text{ s}$ to the ambient Quick Dump Rinse (QDR) tank to arrest etching.
   - Cycle 4 dump/fill sequences with ultra-pure water (UPW) until bath resistivity reaches $\ge 18.0\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$.
   - Transfer to a surface-tension Marangoni dry or N2-purged spin rinse dryer (SRD) at $2000\text{ RPM}$ with heated filtered $\text{N}_2$ ($> 99.9999\%$ purity).

6. **Queue-Time (Q-Time) Enforcement**:
   - Transfer the passivated cassette in an enclosed, nitrogen-purged SMIF pod / wafer carrier directly to the horizontal quartz gate oxidation furnace tube.

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Specification | Tolerance / Limits | Measurement Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Silicon Nitride Etch Loss** | $< 0.5\text{ nm/min}$ | $\le 0.5\text{ nm/min}$ maximum | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry on $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ monitor wafer |
| **QDR Rinse End-Point Resistivity** | $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ | $\ge 18.0\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ | In-line conductance/resistivity probe |
| **Pre-Oxidation Queue Time (Q-Time)** | $\le 60\text{ min}$ | $\le 120\text{ min}$ hard interlock abort | Automated MES lot tracking timestamp to 850°C furnace load |
| **Post-Strip Oxide Residual** | $0.0\text{ nm}$ (Hydrophobic dewet) | Native oxide $< 0.2\text{ nm}$ | In-line X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS) / Ellipsometry |

---

### Verified Literature Context Citations

- **Deal-Grove Silicon Thermal Oxidation Kinetics in Quartz Tube Furnace**: Validates the requirement of an oxide-free, passivated starting interface to execute thin-regime ($x_0 \ll A/2$) linear rate oxidation at $850^\circ\text{C}$ targeting $3.5\text{ to }4.0\text{ nm}$ gate oxide with minimal interface trap density ($D_{it} < 10^{10}\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ eV}^{-1}$) and breakdown field $E_{bd} > 10\text{ MV/cm}$.
- **Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD) of Silicon Nitride Hard Masks**: Confirms etch selectivity and boundary conditions where stoichiometric $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ hard mask exhibits extreme resistance to dilute/concentrated HF and BOE with an etch rate $< 0.5\text{ nm/min}$ (selective preservation of LOCOS and capacitor nitride barriers).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: In the 180nm DRAM integration flow, this 1:50 DHF strip directly sets the pre-gate oxide interface prior to 3.5 nm dry gate oxidation. Using dilute unbuffered HF (1:50 DIW:HF 49%, ~1.0 wt% HF) rather than BOE (which incorporates NH4F) is essential to avoid ionic ammonium/nitrogen contamination on the bare silicon channel. However, unbuffered DHF exhibits a rapid depletion gradient across 150mm/200mm batch carriers; bath agitation and recirculating filtration with constant chemical spiked replenishment or single-wafer spray delivery must be enforced to avoid within-wafer native oxide clearance non-uniformity.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: The primary objective is complete chemical/native oxide dissolution with complete Si-H monohydride/dihydride/trihydride passivation. The etch rate of chemical oxide in 1:50 DHF at 22°C is ~2.5 to 3.0 nm/min, requiring a 60–90 second dip to clear a ~1.2 nm RCA SC-2 chemical oxide with 100% overetch. Overexposure beyond 120 seconds induces atomic surface roughening (RMS > 0.15 nm) via OH- attack at step edges, directly degrading gate oxide breakdown field (Ebd) and carrier mobility in 180nm peripheral and array access transistors.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Electronic-grade Hydrofluoric Acid (SEMI Tier 4 / Grade 5, low trace metal <10 ppt for Fe, Cu, Ni, Ca) and ultra-pure water (UPW, 18.2 MOhm·cm, TOC < 1 ppb) are mission-critical. Uncontrolled fluoropolymer tubing or wetted PFA/PVDF vessel outgassing can leach trace metals directly into the acidic bath, causing catastrophic pre-gate heavy metal surface contamination.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Strict physical staging must couple this wet bench directly to the dry oxidation furnace loading bay. Any bottleneck in queue management will cause uncontrollable native oxide regrowth in cleanroom ambient, invalidating downstream 3.5 nm thermal oxide thickness targets and inflating gate oxide thickness standard deviations across the lot.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Incomplete chemical oxide removal due to bath HF depletion, leaving residual Si-O bonds, causing local gate oxide thickness variations and anomalous interface trap density (Dit > 5e10 eV-1 cm-2).
1. Pinhole microroughening from prolonged HF immersion or dissolved O2 micro-corrosion, degrading gate oxide dielectric breakdown voltage (BVox) and time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB) margins.
1. Excessive Q-time exposure (>30 min) in cleanroom air before furnace load, driving uncontrolled, non-stoichiometric native sub-oxide regrowth and airborne volatile organic carbon (VOC) condensation.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-2-2-2-1-2-01` | **Contact Angle Hydrophobicity and Native Oxide Clearance Verification** | Automated Sessile Drop Goniometer with de-aerated UPW micro-syringe and Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (SE) | 1. Submerge wafer carrier into 1:50 DHF bath for precisely 75 seconds with vertical megasonic or fluid oscillation. 2. Transfer immediately to quick-dump rinse (QDR) tank; execute 4 dump cycles with 18.2 MOhm UPW. 3. Spin rinse dry under heated N2 blanket (<0.1 ppm O2). 4. Within 5 minutes, dispense 3.0 uL UPW droplet at 5 sites (center, 4 edges at 5mm edge exclusion) and measure dynamic contact angle. 5. Perform 9-point spectroscopic ellipsometry to detect residual oxide film. | `DI water static contact angle must be >= 75 degrees across all 5 test sites (demonstrating uniform hydrogen termination), and measured residual oxide thickness by SE must be <= 0.05 nm (nominal zero/bare Si interface).` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-2-2-2-1-2-02` | **Post-Strip Surface Micro-Roughness and Trace Metallic Contamination Test** | Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) in tapping mode and Total Reflection X-Ray Fluorescence (TXRF) | 1. Perform 1:50 DHF etch for 75 seconds followed by QDR and SRD on prime 150mm p-type <100> monitor wafer. 2. Mount wafer in AFM under anti-vibration enclosure; scan three 1.0 um x 1.0 um fields within the active die coordinate zone. 3. Extract root-mean-square roughness (Rq / RMS). 4. Transfer wafer under sealed N2 pod to TXRF stage; integrate 1000s scan per site at center, mid-radius, and edge. | `Surface roughness RMS must be <= 0.12 nm (delta RMS <= 0.03 nm relative to incoming pre-clean baseline). Surface trace metal concentrations (Fe, Ni, Cu, Zn) measured by TXRF must each be < 5.0e9 atoms/cm2.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Fluoropolymer/Butyl rubber chemical apron and chemical-resistant sleeves, Heavyweight butyl/neoprene outer gloves over double Nitrile inner gloves (tested for HF permeation), Full-face polycarbonate chemical splash shield with ANSI Z87.1 splash goggles underneath, Acid-resistant composite toe chemical safety boots
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Hydrofluoric acid causes severe, deep-tissue liquefactive necrosis and life-threatening systemic hypocalcemia. In case of skin exposure: Immediately flood contact area with cold safety shower for minimum 2 minutes, continuously removing contaminated clothing. Immediately massage 2.5% Calcium Gluconate USP topical gel into the skin using gloved hands until pain subsides; repeat application every 15 minutes. For eye splash: Flush with sterile saline/water for 15 minutes and immediately apply 1.0% calcium gluconate eye solution if trained medical staff is present. Mandatory immediate emergency medical evacuation (EMS) for all exposures regardless of apparent initial pain.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous lip-exhaust and rear plenum face velocity maintained at 100 - 120 FPM (0.51 - 0.61 m/s) with dedicated fluoropolymer-lined wet acid scrubber ducting. Interlocked differential pressure sensor set to trigger audible alarm and disable bath immersion arms if face velocity drops below 80 FPM.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent DHF bath must drain strictly via dedicated fluoride-bearing waste drain line (FW) separate from standard acid-waste neutralization (AWN). Waste must undergo precipitation with excess Calcium Hydroxide (Ca(OH)2) or Calcium Chloride (CaCl2) to precipitate insoluble Calcium Fluoride (CaF2 sludge), buffering discharge effluent to pH 6.5 - 8.5 with total fluoride concentration <= 10 ppm.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid (Electronic/VLSI Grade)** | `7664-39-3` | SEMI Tier 4 / Grade 5 | `0.98 - 1.05 wt% (from 49% stock diluted 1:50 with UPW)` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic chemical oxide (1.0 - 1.3 nm) with trace metallic/organic surface impurities stripped by standard SC-1 / SC-2 RCA sequence.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophobic, atomically smooth hydrogen-terminated (Si-H) surface with zero native oxide and sub-monolayer hydrocarbon exposure.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding queue time results in uncontrolled native SiO2 island re-nucleation (0.2 - 0.4 nm), airborne boron/organic contamination, and interfacial defect density escalation, causing gross deviation from the nominal 3.5 nm Deal-Grove dry gate oxide target.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful complete dissolution of chemical oxide and establishment of a stable, hydrophobic, hydrogen-passivated silicon surface meeting class 1/ISO 3 cleanroom integrity without microroughening, staged immediately for 3.5 nm dry gate oxidation.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `DHF_Strip_Passivation_Inspection_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `Ellipsometry_Oxide_Thickness_PrePost.csv`
- [ ] `AFM_Surface_Roughness_Scan_3Sites.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Residual oxide thickness post-DHF 1:50 dip and dry** | `0.00 nm` | +0.05 nm | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry (9-point map on monitor wafer) |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Static contact angle of de-aerated UPW droplet** | `78.0 degrees` | +/- 3.0 degrees | Optical Goniometry (5-point measurement per wafer) |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Post-strip surface micro-roughness RMS (Rq)** | `0.10 nm` | +0.02 nm / -0.00 nm | Atomic Force Microscopy (1 um x 1 um scan window) |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All monitor wafers demonstrate <= 0.05 nm residual oxide, contact angle >= 75 degrees, surface roughness RMS <= 0.12 nm, zero visual staining or drying residue under high-intensity collimated inspection light, and physical transfer into the horizontal furnace N2-purged load-lock within <= 30 minutes of spin-rinse completion.

critics.systems_engineer: In the 180nm DRAM integration flow, this 1:50 DHF strip directly sets the pre-gate oxide interface prior to 3.5 nm dry gate oxidation. Using dilute unbuffered HF (1:50 DIW:HF 49%, ~1.0 wt% HF) rather than BOE (which incorporates NH4F) is essential to avoid ionic ammonium/nitrogen contamination on the bare silicon channel. However, unbuffered DHF exhibits a rapid depletion gradient across 150mm/200mm batch carriers; bath agitation and recirculating filtration with constant chemical spiked replenishment or single-wafer spray delivery must be enforced to avoid within-wafer native oxide clearance non-uniformity.
critics.domain_expert: The primary objective is complete chemical/native oxide dissolution with complete Si-H monohydride/dihydride/trihydride passivation. The etch rate of chemical oxide in 1:50 DHF at 22°C is ~2.5 to 3.0 nm/min, requiring a 60–90 second dip to clear a ~1.2 nm RCA SC-2 chemical oxide with 100% overetch. Overexposure beyond 120 seconds induces atomic surface roughening (RMS > 0.15 nm) via OH- attack at step edges, directly degrading gate oxide breakdown field (Ebd) and carrier mobility in 180nm peripheral and array access transistors.
critics.supply_chain: Electronic-grade Hydrofluoric Acid (SEMI Tier 4 / Grade 5, low trace metal <10 ppt for Fe, Cu, Ni, Ca) and ultra-pure water (UPW, 18.2 MOhm·cm, TOC < 1 ppb) are mission-critical. Uncontrolled fluoropolymer tubing or wetted PFA/PVDF vessel outgassing can leach trace metals directly into the acidic bath, causing catastrophic pre-gate heavy metal surface contamination.
critics.laya_pm: Strict physical staging must couple this wet bench directly to the dry oxidation furnace loading bay. Any bottleneck in queue management will cause uncontrollable native oxide regrowth in cleanroom ambient, invalidating downstream 3.5 nm thermal oxide thickness targets and inflating gate oxide thickness standard deviations across the lot.
critical_failure_modes: Incomplete chemical oxide removal due to bath HF depletion, leaving residual Si-O bonds, causing local gate oxide thickness variations and anomalous interface trap density (Dit > 5e10 eV-1 cm-2).
Pinhole microroughening from prolonged HF immersion or dissolved O2 micro-corrosion, degrading gate oxide dielectric breakdown voltage (BVox) and time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB) margins.
Excessive Q-time exposure (>30 min) in cleanroom air before furnace load, driving uncontrolled, non-stoichiometric native sub-oxide regrowth and airborne volatile organic carbon (VOC) condensation.

ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: Hydrofluoric acid causes severe, deep-tissue liquefactive necrosis and life-threatening systemic hypocalcemia. In case of skin exposure: Immediately flood contact area with cold safety shower for minimum 2 minutes, continuously removing contaminated clothing. Immediately massage 2.5% Calcium Gluconate USP topical gel into the skin using gloved hands until pain subsides; repeat application every 15 minutes. For eye splash: Flush with sterile saline/water for 15 minutes and immediately apply 1.0% calcium gluconate eye solution if trained medical staff is present. nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: SOP-MET-PREOX-001
**Title:** Pre-Oxidation Surface Hydrophobicity, Particle Inspection, and Native Oxide Ellipsometry Verification  
**Hierarchy Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > 180nm Dry Gate Oxide Growth (3.5 nm) > Thermal Oxidation Execution (850°C Dilute Dry $O_2/N_2$) > RCA Clean & HF-Last Etch > Pre-Oxidation Metrology Verification  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (180 nm node)  
**Action Type:** Make / Metrology Verification  

---

### 1. Scope & Objective
This SOP establishes the procedural protocol for post-RCA/HF-last metrology verification on bare silicon wafers prior to horizontal quartz furnace 3.5 nm dry gate oxide growth. Metrology inspects surface passivation completeness (hydrogen termination / hydrophobicity), airborne defect particle count, and residual native oxide thickness via spectroscopic ellipsometry to guarantee Deal-Grove thermal oxidation kinetic repeatability and gate dielectric integrity ($E_{bd} > 10\text{ MV/cm}$, $D_{it} < 10^{10}\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ eV}^{-1}$).

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

```text
  [Step 1: Hydrophobicity] ---> [Step 2: Ellipsometry] ---> [Step 3: Particle Scan] ---> [Gate Furnace Queue]
     DI Water Contact Angle       Native Oxide Thickness      Defect Density (<0.2 µm)       Q-Time < 2.0 hrs
```

#### Step 1: Surface Passivation & Hydrophobicity Assessment
1. Transfer cassette from the post-RCA/HF-last spin-rinse dryer (SRD) directly to the automated sessile-drop contact angle goniometer under an ISO Class 1 mini-environment.
2. Dispense a $1.0\ \mu\text{L}$ droplet of ultra-pure deionized (DI) water (resistivity $\ge 18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$) onto 5 standard test sites (Center, Top, Bottom, Left, Right; $10\text{ mm}$ edge exclusion).
3. Measure static water contact angle ($\theta_c$) within 15 seconds of dispense.
4. **Verification:** Confirm complete hydrogen termination ($\text{Si-H}$) indicated by non-wetting hydrophobic behavior ($\theta_c \ge 75^\circ$). If $\theta_c < 70^\circ$, surface hydroxyl groups ($\text{Si-OH}$) or re-oxidation is present; reject lot to re-clean.

#### Step 2: Spectroscopic Ellipsometry for Native Oxide Thickness
1. Load the pilot/monitor wafer onto the automated spectroscopic ellipsometer stage.
2. Align laser beam ($\lambda = 632.8\text{ nm}$ He-Ne or broadband $250\text{–}800\text{ nm}$) at an incidence angle of $70.0^\circ$.
3. Acquire $\Psi$ (amplitude ratio) and $\Delta$ (phase difference) across a 9-point radial map.
4. Apply the optical dispersion model: $\text{Single-layer SiO}_2$ on $\text{c-Si}$ substrate (refractive index $n_{\text{SiO}_2} \approx 1.46$).
5. Measure native oxide thickness ($t_{\text{native}}$). Ensure baseline native oxide is $\le 0.5\text{ nm}$ before furnace entry so total gate dielectric target ($3.5\text{ nm}$) is controlled strictly by the subsequent 850°C–900°C dry oxidation step.

#### Step 3: Laser Surface Particle & Defect Scanning
1. Transfer wafer to the unpatterned surface defect inspection system (darkfield laser scattering).
2. Execute full-surface scan with calibration set for defect bin sizes $\ge 0.18\ \mu\text{m}$ (critical dimension threshold for 180nm technology node).
3. Record total defect particle count and map spatial density across the wafer ($5\text{ mm}$ edge exclusion).
4. Verify total particle count remains within acceptable cleanroom threshold.

#### Step 4: Q-Time Staging to Furnace
1. Tag wafer lot with completion timestamp.
2. Transport lot in an ultra-clean nitrogen-purged FOUP/SMIF pod to the horizontal quartz tube furnace loading bay.
3. Enforce hard Queue-Time (Q-time) limit ($\le 2.0\text{ hours}$) from HF-last etch completion to furnace dry $O_2$ push at 850°C to inhibit uncontrolled native oxide regrowth.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Limit | Measurement Tool / Unit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **DI Water Contact Angle ($\theta_c$)** | $\ge 75.0^\circ$ | $\ge 70.0^\circ$ min (uniform hydrophobic) | Automated Goniometer ($^\circ$, degrees) |
| **Residual Native Oxide Thickness ($t_{\text{native}}$)** | $\le 0.30\text{ nm}$ | $\le 0.50\text{ nm}$ max | Spectroscopic Ellipsometer ($\text{nm}$) |
| **Particle Defect Count (size $\ge 0.18\ \mu\text{m}$)** | $< 10\text{ ea/wafer}$ | $\le 15\text{ ea/wafer}$ max | Darkfield Laser Defect Scanner ($\text{count/wafer}$) |
| **Furnace Transfer Queue Time ($t_{\text{queue}}$)** | $< 60\text{ min}$ | $\le 120\text{ min}$ ($2.0\text{ hr}$) max | CIM / MES Track-In Timer ($\text{minutes}$) |

---

### 4. Context & Source Citations
- **Deal-Grove Silicon Thermal Oxidation Kinetics in Quartz Tube Furnace:**
  - Guides pre-oxidation surface preparation to maintain uniform interface reaction kinetics ($x_0 \ll A/2$, rate limited by $k_l = B/A$).
  - Mandates native oxide suppression ($t_{\text{native}} \le 0.5\text{ nm}$) to meet the gate oxide thickness target of $3.5\text{ to }4.0\text{ nm}$ grown at $850^\circ\text{C}\text{–}900^\circ\text{C}$ in dry $O_2$, ensuring high dielectric breakdown field ($E_{bd} > 10\text{ MV/cm}$) and low interface trap density ($D_{it} < 10^{10}\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{ eV}^{-1}$).
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering:**
  - Establishes the 180nm physical integration parameters (wordline/bitline pitch $360\text{–}400\text{ nm}$, transistor gate dielectric target $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ physical thickness $\text{SiO}_2$) and defect sensitivity scale for 1T1C cells.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Pre-oxidation metrology represents an active Q-time bottleneck between wet bench HF-last clean and the 850°C horizontal oxidation furnace. Measuring native oxide regrowth and particle count consumes critical budget against the 30-minute cleanroom air exposure window. Automated cassette handling and rapid 5-point ellipsometry mapping must execute within an allocated 8-minute cycle, or the wafer lot risks uncontrolled native oxide thickening (>0.3 nm), which distorts the ultra-thin 3.5 nm target gate dielectric capacitance-equivalent thickness (CET).
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Spectroscopic ellipsometry on hydrogen-terminated Si (100) requires caution regarding optical dispersion models: assuming a standard bulk SiO2 Cauchy or Sellmeier model without fitting for surface roughness and sub-oxide (SiOx) intermediate layers introduces up to 0.4 nm systematic error on sub-nanometer native oxide layers. Furthermore, contact angle goniometry for hydrophobicity verification cannot be performed directly on active device product die due to droplet residue contamination; sacrificial edge-exclusion zones or dedicated pilot wafers must be utilized.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Single-wavelength laser ellipsometers (e.g. HeNe 632.8 nm) provide high-throughput delta-psi extraction, but lack the spectral resolution needed to decouple surface roughness from native oxide at sub-0.5 nm thickness. Calibrated spectroscopic ellipsometer sources (Xe arc / deuterium-halogen) and replacement optics require long procurement lead times in Vietnam; calibration standard wafers (1.5 nm and 100 nm thermally grown SiO2 on Si) must be sourced with traceable NIST certification.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Wafers queueing at the metrology station directly compress production velocity for the 180nm DRAM test vehicle lot. If laser surface particle scanning (LSPS) flags exceed defect excursion thresholds, a deterministic protocol must rapidly trigger an HF re-dip rather than idling the horizontal quartz furnace dry O2 boat load. Clear go/no-go interlocks must be logged digitally in the MES before wafer transfer into the load lock.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Uncontrolled native oxide regrowth exceeding 0.3 nm during metrology delay, resulting in target 3.5 nm gate oxide thickness overshoot and reduced accumulation capacitance (Cox).
1. Laser surface particle scanner contamination transfer via dirty end-effector or vacuum chuck contact, causing pinholes and premature dielectric breakdown (TDDB) in planar MOSCAP gates.
1. Incomplete hydrogen termination (hydrophilic water break failure) leading to non-uniform dry thermal oxidation kinetics across the 150mm/200mm wafer surface.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-2-2-2-1-3-01` | **Spectroscopic Ellipsometry 9-Point Native Oxide Thickness & Refractive Index Verification** | Variable Angle Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (VASE, spectral range 250 nm - 850 nm, incident angle 70°) | 1. Load p-type (100) test wafer onto clean vacuum chuck. 2. Align wafer notch/flat and focus optical probe. 3. Acquire Delta and Psi spectra across 250-850 nm at 9 standard locations (center, 4 mid-radius at 0.5R, 4 outer-edge at 0.9R). 4. Fit acquired optical spectra using Si(substrate)/native SiO2/ambient optical model. 5. Record native oxide thickness (t_nat) and goodness of fit (MSE). | `Average native oxide thickness t_nat <= 0.30 nm across all 9 measurement sites; mean square error MSE < 2.5; 9-point thickness non-uniformity (1-sigma) <= 0.05 nm.` |
| `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-2-2-2-1-3-02` | **Laser Surface Particle Inspection and Hydrophobic Water Break Contact Angle Check** | Darkfield Laser Surface Particle Scanner (LSPS, 488 nm laser, sensitivity >= 0.18 um) and Automated Optical Contact Angle Goniometer | 1. Transfer wafer to laser surface particle scanner; perform 100% full-surface darkfield scan with 3 mm edge exclusion. 2. Count and bin particle defects >= 0.18 um. 3. Transfer sacrificial witness wafer to contact angle goniometer. 4. Dispense 2.0 uL droplet of 18.2 MOhm*cm deionized water onto 3 wafer peripheral locations. 5. Capture droplet silhouette and calculate static contact angle using Young-Laplace fitting. | `Total defect count for particles >= 0.18 um is <= 15 defects per 150 mm wafer (defect density < 0.085 defects/cm2); static DI water contact angle >= 72.0° confirming hydrophobic Si-H surface termination.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom clean-suit (antistatic Tyvek coverall, hood, and boot covers), Nitrile gloves (double-gloved, cleanroom certified), Laser safety goggles certified for 488 nm and 632.8 nm Class 3B/4 beams, UV-absorbing safety glasses
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Ensure 2.5% calcium gluconate gel is accessible within 10 seconds of metrology station in case of residual HF contact from cassette handles. In case of skin exposure, flush with cold water for 2 minutes, apply calcium gluconate gel liberally, and seek emergency medical evaluation. In case of laser beam eye exposure, immediately shut off optical source and transfer personnel to an ophthalmologist.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Cleanroom laminar air flow velocity 0.45 m/s +/- 20% downflow; dedicated local exhaust ventilation on goniometer droplet disposal station with minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Goniometer droplet wipe-off textiles and sample water droplets collected in designated acid-compatible fluoropolymer waste receptacles; residual acid water drain plumbed directly into the facility Acid Waste Neutralization (AWN) system maintained at pH 6.5 - 8.5 with calcium hydroxide slurry.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Deionized Water (Ultrapure 18.2 MOhm*cm)** | `7732-18-5` | SEMI Grade C-12 | `100%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (Ultra-High Purity Purge Gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Electronic Grade 6.0 | `>= 99.9999%` |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid (trace residual vapor from wet bench transfer)** | `7664-39-3` | Electronic / VLSI Grade | `<= 0.5% (prior bath)` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophobic, hydrogen-passivated (Si-H) single-crystal silicon surface immediately following 0.5% dilute HF dip and spin-rinse drying.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Particle-verified, native oxide thickness-validated (< 0.3 nm), hydrophobic Si-H surface staged inside N2-purged FOUP/SMIF pod ready for furnace boat push.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding queue time allows atmospheric oxygen and moisture adsorption to nucleate uncontrolled native oxide islands (t_nat > 0.4 nm) and airborne molecular contamination (organic hydrocarbons), causing variable initial oxidation rates, interface trap density (Dit) spikes above 5e10 eV-1 cm-2, and gate dielectric pinhole leakage.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful metrology qualification verifies that the silicon surface is clean, fully hydrogen-terminated, low-defect, and exhibits native oxide thickness below 0.30 nm, authorizing lot dispatch into the 850°C horizontal quartz dry oxidation tube for 3.5 nm gate dielectric growth.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `PRE_OX_ELLIPSOMETRY_9PT_MAP.csv`
- [ ] `PRE_OX_PARTICLE_SCAN_DEFECT_MAP.tiff`
- [ ] `PRE_OX_METROLOGY_SIGNOFF_REPORT.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Mean native oxide thickness measured across 9 wafer points** | `0.20 nm` | +/- 0.10 nm (Max <= 0.30 nm) | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Delta-Psi regression fitting against Si/SiO2 model |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Darkfield particle defect count at >= 0.18 um optical threshold** | `5 defects/wafer` | +/- 10 defects (Max <= 15 defects/wafer) | Full-wafer darkfield laser scattering surface inspection |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Static contact angle of ultrapure DI water droplet on sacrificial witness surface** | `75.0 deg` | >= 72.0 deg | Sessile drop optical goniometry with Young-Laplace profile fit |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 9 ellipsometry sites measure t_nat <= 0.30 nm with MSE < 2.5, particle count >= 0.18 um is <= 15 defects per 150 mm wafer, static contact angle is >= 72.0°, total elapsed Q-time from HF dry is <= 12 minutes, and MES lot status is digitally flagged 'PASS_DISPATCH_TO_DRY_OX_FURNACE'.

testcases.title: Laser Surface Particle Inspection and Hydrophobic Water Break Contact Angle Check
testcases.instrumentation: Darkfield Laser Surface Particle Scanner (LSPS, 488 nm laser, sensitivity >= 0.18 um) and Automated Optical Contact Angle Goniometer
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafer dried in spin-rinse dryer with ultra-pure N2 (>99.9999%); Class 100 laminar flow hood; inspection station calibrated with 200 nm PSL (polystyrene latex) spheres.
testcases.procedure: 1. Transfer wafer to laser surface particle scanner; perform 100% full-surface darkfield scan with 3 mm edge exclusion. 2. Count and bin particle defects >= 0.18 um. 3. Transfer sacrificial witness wafer to contact angle goniometer. 4. Dispense 2.0 uL droplet of 18.2 MOhm*cm deionized water onto 3 wafer peripheral locations. 5. Capture droplet silhouette and calculate static contact angle using Young-Laplace fitting.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Total defect count for particles >= 0.18 um is <= 15 defects per 150 mm wafer (defect density < 0.085 defects/cm2); static DI water contact angle >= 72.0° confirming hydrophobic Si-H surface termination.

ppe_required: Class 100 cleanroom clean-suit (antistatic Tyvek coverall, hood, and boot covers)
Nitrile gloves (double-gloved, cleanroom certified)
Laser safety goggles certified for 488 nm and 632.8 nm Class 3B/4 beams
UV-absorbing safety glasses

cas_chemicals.name: Hydrofluoric Acid (trace residual vapor from wet bench transfer)

ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: Ensure 2.5% calcium gluconate gel is accessible within 10 seconds of metrology station in case of residual HF contact from cassette handles. In case of skin exposure, flush with cold water for 2 minutes, apply calcium gluconate gel liberally, and seek emergency medical evaluation. In case of laser beam eye exposure, immediately shut off optical source and transfer personnel to an ophthalmologist.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Cleanroom laminar air flow velocity 0.45 m/s +/- 20% downflow; dedicated local exhaust ventilation on goniometer droplet disposal station with minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM).
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Goniometer droplet wipe-off textiles and sample water droplets collected in designated acid-compatible fluoropolymer waste receptacles; residual acid water drain plumbed directly into the facility Acid Waste Neutralization (AWN) system maintained at pH 6.5 - 8.5 with calcium hydroxide slurry.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Hydrophobic, hydrogen-passivated (Si-H) single-crystal silicon surface immediately following 0.5% dilute HF dip and spin-rinse drying.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Particle-verified, native oxide thickness-validated (< 0.3 nm), hydrophobic Si-H surface staged inside N2-purged FOUP/SMIF pod ready for furnace boat push.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Exceeding queue time allows atmospheric oxygen and moisture adsorption to nucleate uncontrolled native oxide islands (t_nat > 0.4 nm) and airborne molecular contamination (organic hydrocarbons), causing variable initial oxidation rates, interface trap density (Dit) spikes above 5e10 eV-1 cm-2, and gate dielectric pinhole leakage.

expected_result.summary: Successful metrology qualification verifies that the silicon surface is clean, fully hydrogen-terminated, low-defect, and exhibits native oxide thickness below 0.30 nm, authorizing lot dispatch into the 850°C horizontal quartz dry oxidation tube for 3.5 nm gate dielectric growth.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Mean native oxide thickness measured across 9 wafer points
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Delta-Psi regression fitting against Si/SiO2 model

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Darkfield particle defect count at >= 0.18 um optical threshold
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Full-wafer darkfield laser scattering surface inspection

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Static contact angle of ultrapure DI water droplet on sacrificial witness surface
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Sessile drop optical goniometry with Young-Laplace profile fit

expected_result.signoff_criteria: All 9 ellipsometry sites measure t_nat <= 0.30 nm with MSE < 2.5, particle count >= 0.18 um is <= 15 defects per 150 mm wafer, static contact angle is >= 72.0°, total elapsed Q-time from HF dry is <= 12 minutes, and MES lot status is digitally flagged 'PASS_DISPATCH_TO_DRY_OX_FURNACE'.

nodes.label: Horizontal Quartz Furnace 3.5nm Dilute O2/N2 Thermal Oxidation Run at 850°C
nodes.primary_metric: Sub-milestone of Horizontal Quartz Furnace 3.5nm Gate Oxide Growth Recipe Execution (850°C Dilute Dry O2/N2)
nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) ## Title: Horizontal Quartz Furnace 3.5nm Dilute $\text{O}_2/\text{N}_2$ Thermal Oxidation Run at 850°C **Process Hierarchy:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > 180nm Dry Gate Oxide Growth (3.5 nm) > Dry Thermal Oxidation Recipe Execution (850°C–900°C, 3.5 nm $\text{SiO}_2$) > Horizontal Quartz Furnace Dry $\text{O}_2$ Oxidation Recipe Execution (850°C, Pure $\text{O}_2/\text{N}_2$ Dilution) > Horizontal Quartz Furnace 3.5nm Gate Oxide Growth Recipe Execution (850°C Dilute Dry $\text{O}_2/\text{N}_2$) **Action Type:** Make **Target Dielectric Layer:** High-density Dry Gate Dielectric ($\text{SiO}_2$), Target $t_{\text{ox}} = 3.5\text{ nm}$ --- ### 1. Process Flowchart ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Step 1: Idle & Thermal Stabilization
850°C across 3 Zones, N2 @ 2.0–5.0 SLPM"] --> B["Step 2: Wafer Boat Insertion
Load into 350 mm Flat Zone in N2 ambient"] B --> C["Step 3: Thermal Equilibration
Dwell at 850°C until uniformity ≤ ±0.5°C"] C --> D["Step 4: Oxidation Cycle
Switch to O2/N2 Dilution Sweep, Run 22 min"] D --> E["Step 5: Post-Oxidation N2 Purge
Cut O2, Purge N2 @ 2.0–5.0 SLPM"] E --> F["Step 6: Wafer Boat Unload & Metrology
Cool down and transfer to Ellipsometry"] ``` --- ### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure 1. **Pre-Run Furnace Verification & Thermal Profile Stabilization:** - Verify the fused quartz process tube (99.999% $\text{SiO}_2$, 150 mm to 200 mm OD) is purged under ultra-pure $\text{N}_2$ sweep. - Set the 3-zone digital PID temperature controllers (Source, Center, Load zones monitored via dual Type-R/S Pt-Pt/Rh thermocouples) to a setpoint of **850°C**. - Establish laminar carrier purge using calibrated Mass Flow Controllers (MFC) supplying ultra-pure $\text{N}_2$ at **2.0 to 5.0 SLPM** to prevent ambient back-diffusion. - Confirm temperature stabilization in the middle **350 mm Center Flat Zone** to within **$\le \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$**. 2. **Wafer Loading & Dwell:** - Load pre-cleaned (100) Si wafer boat into the 350 mm center flat zone under continuous $\text{N}_2$ blanket sweep (**2.0 to 5.0 SLPM**). - Allow a thermal recovery dwell period until all 3 zones equilibrate to **850°C $\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$**. 3. **Oxidation Gas Introduction & Growth:** - Transition MFC gas delivery to introduce high-purity dry $\text{O}_2$ (99.999% purity) with $\text{N}_2$ dilution, maintaining total laminar flow at **2.0 to 5.0 SLPM** (optionally including 1–3% dry HCl for mobile $\text{Na}^+$ ion and metallic gettering). - Execute the oxidation step at **850°C** for a recipe duration of **22 minutes** (operating in the linear-parabolic initial thin oxide regime where parabolic rate constant $B = 0.0031\,\mu\text{m}^2/\text{hr}$ and linear rate constant $B/A = 0.018\,\mu\text{m}/\text{hr}$). 4. **Oxidation Termination & Post-Oxidation Purge:** - Shut off the $\text{O}_2$ (and HCl) MFC valves immediately upon reaching 22 minutes. - Sweep the quartz tube with ultra-pure $\text{N}_2$ at **2.0 to 5.0 SLPM** to completely clear residual oxidants from the tube. 5. **Unload & Transfer:** - Slowly withdraw the quartz boat from the furnace center flat zone into the load zone under positive $\text{N}_2$ purge flow. - Cool to handling temperature and transfer wafers to spectroscopic ellipsometry for dielectric thickness validation. --- ### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria | Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Limit | Measurement Method / Tool | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Gate Oxide Physical Thickness ($t_{\text{ox}}$)** | $3.5\text{ nm}$ | $\pm 0.2\text{ nm}$ ($3.3\text{ nm} - 3.7\text{ nm}$) | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry | | **Center Flat Zone Thermal Uniformity** | $850^\circ\text{C}$ | $\le \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ across $350\text{ mm}$ length | Dual Type-R/S Thermocouple Array | | **Dielectric Breakdown Field ($E_{\text{bd}}$)** | $> 10\text{ MV/cm}$ | Minimum threshold: $10\text{ MV/cm}$ | Fast Voltage Ramp / C-V / I-V Probe | | **Interface Trap Density ($D_{\text{it}}$)** | $< 10^{10}\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{eV}^{-1}$ | Maximum threshold: $10^{10}\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{eV}^{-1}$ | High-Frequency / Quasi-Static C-V | --- ### 4. Verified Literature References 1. **Deal-Grove Silicon Thermal Oxidation Kinetics in Quartz Tube Furnace:** - Governed by $x_0^2 + A x_0 = B(t + \tau)$. - Validates dry oxidation targets for 180nm gate dielectric: $3.5\text{ to }4.0\text{ nm}$, dielectric breakdown $E_{\text{bd}} > 10\text{ MV/cm}$, and interface trap density $D_{\text{it}} < 10^{10}\text{ cm}^{-2}\text{eV}^{-1}$. 2. **Three-Zone Quartz Tube Diffusion Furnace Thermal Profiling & Gas Delivery:** - 3-zone configuration (Source, Center, Load) with dual Type-R/S Pt-Pt/Rh thermocouples. - Fused quartz process tube outer diameter 150mm–200mm (99.999% $\text{SiO}_2$). - Middle 350 mm flat zone uniformity requirement: $\le \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$. - MFC gas flow range: 2.0 to 5.0 SLPM laminar gas sweep; 1–3% dry HCl capability. 3. **Deal-Grove Silicon Oxidation Kinetic Coefficients & Gate Oxide Thickness:** - Rate constants for (100) Si at 850°C in dry $\text{O}_2$: $B = 0.0031\,\mu\text{m}^2/\text{hr}$, $B/A = 0.018\,\mu\text{m}/\text{hr}$. - Recipe benchmark: 850°C dry oxidation for 22 minutes yields physical thickness $t_{\text{ox}} = 3.5\text{ nm} \pm 0.2\text{ nm}$. --- ### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA) - **Systems Engineer Critic**: Thermal profiling across the 350 mm flat zone in horizontal configurations exhibits convective thermal updraft and longitudinal temperature drops during push/pull boat sequences. Even with triple-loop digital PID feedforward decoupling and dual Type-R thermocouples per zone, boat cantilever insertion speed must be locked strictly below 50 mm/min to prevent axial thermal shock (dT/dt > 10°C/min) and maintain an isothermal zone within ±0.5°C at 850°C. Furthermore, laminar gas sweep velocity (MFC delivery at 2.0-5.0 SLPM) must be continuously dynamically balanced against furnace tube door exhaust throttling to suppress ambient oxygen back-diffusion without creating local Venturi cooling at the load-end wafers. - **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 850°C with dilute O2/N2 (typically 10% O2 in N2 carrier), Deal-Grove linear oxidation rate constants (B/A) dominate the ultra-thin 3.5 nm regime where initial non-linear rapid oxidation kinetics occur. Initial chemisorption and space-charge effects can cause rapid oxide growth within the first 60 seconds; hence, gas switching latency from N2 stabilization purge to dilute O2/N2 must have a transit response under 3 seconds to avoid uncontrolled initial interface growth. Addition of 1-2% trans-1,2-dichloroethylene (DCE) or dry HCl is essential for passivating mobile sodium (Na+) ions and suppressing stacking faults, but chloride incorporation must not degrade the interface trap density (Dit <= 2E10 eV^-1 cm^-2). - **Supply Chain Critic**: Fused quartz process tubes (99.999% purity) and recrystallized silicon carbide (SiC) wafer boats have lead times of 16-24 weeks from precision quartz fabricators. High-purity process gas delivery manifolds require point-of-use gas purifiers to guarantee 99.9999% (6N) purity for N2 and O2, as trace moisture (> 50 ppb H2O) unpredictably doubles the oxidation rate and severely degrades thickness target control across 25-wafer lots. Local supply chain alternatives in Vietnam must establish secondary sourcing for certified ultra-high-purity (UHP) gas cylinders and quartzware welding services to mitigate downtime risk. - **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Targeting 3.5 nm gate oxide thickness with ±0.15 nm 3-sigma tolerance requires strict coordination between pre-diffusion RCA-2/HF dip and furnace loading. Unscheduled delay between cleanroom bays causes uncontrolled native oxide regrowths that exhaust the error budget. Establishing an automated run-to-run (R2R) APC (Advanced Process Control) feedback loop between post-ox spectroscopic ellipsometry and furnace recipe hold-time parameters is critical to achieving production yield milestones for the 180nm open-source DRAM peripheral FETs. **Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**: 1. Uncontrolled native oxide regrowth (> 0.6 nm) prior to furnace push due to breached Q-time post-DHF clean, causing aggregate physical thickness to exceed the 3.65 nm upper specification limit and inducing threshold voltage (Vth) shift in 180nm peripheral transistors. 1. Crystallographic slip dislocations along <110> planes generated by excessive boat insertion speed (> 50 mm/min) or center-to-edge thermal gradients exceeding 2.0°C/cm, inducing junction leakage in DRAM access transistors. 1. Back-diffusion of atmospheric oxygen or moisture through the exhaust flange during the N2 thermal stabilization and ramp-down phases, resulting in premature or asymmetric parasitic oxidation across load-zone wafers. ### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench) | Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-2-2-2-2-01` | **Gate Oxide Physical Thickness and Multi-Site Within-Wafer Uniformity Verification** | Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (SOPRA / Woollam M-2000 multi-wavelength 190-1000 nm, 70° incidence angle, Cauchy dielectric model for thin SiO2 on Si) | 1. Ramp furnace center zone from 650°C idle to 850°C at 5°C/min under 4.0 SLPM UHP N2 sweep. 2. Stabilize thermal profile across 3-zone thermocouples for 20 minutes (verify <= ±0.5°C deviation). 3. Switch mass flow controller to process gas mix: 0.4 SLPM O2 + 3.6 SLPM N2 (10% dilute O2) at 850°C for exactly 14.5 minutes. 4. Flush tube with 5.0 SLPM pure UHP N2 for 10 minutes; ramp down to 650°C at 3°C/min. 5. Pull cantilever boat at 30 mm/min. 6. Transfer 3 monitor wafers (Load, Center, Source) to spectroscopic ellipsometer and execute standard 49-point polar map per wafer (5 mm edge exclusion). | `Wafer center physical thickness target = 3.50 nm. Center wafer mean thickness must be within [3.35 nm, 3.65 nm]. 49-point within-wafer thickness standard deviation (1-sigma) <= 0.08 nm (< 2.5%). Across-boat wafer-to-wafer thickness range (Max - Min) <= 0.15 nm.` | | `TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-2-2-2-2-02` | **MOS Capacitor Interface Trap Density (Dit) and Breakdown Field (Ebd) Extraction** | Automated Mercury Probe (Hg-probe) or Evaporated Al Gate C-V/I-V System with Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Analyzer and LCR meter (1 kHz to 1 MHz high-frequency and quasi-static C-V) | 1. Place wafer on chuck under N2 dry purge enclosure (RH < 5%). 2. Lower mercury capillary contact or probe dot array (contact area = 1.0E-3 cm^2). 3. Measure High-Frequency (1 MHz) and Quasi-Static C-V curves from -3.0 V to +3.0 V at 50 mV/s sweep rate. 4. Extract flat-band voltage (Vfb), equivalent oxide thickness (EOT), and interface trap density (Dit) using the High-Low Frequency (Castagne-Vapaille) method near midgap. 5. Perform ramped voltage stress (I-V) up to dielectric breakdown to determine breakdown electric field (Ebd). | `Interface trap density at midgap Dit <= 2.0E10 eV^-1 cm^-2. Flat-band voltage shift |delta-Vfb| <= 50 mV relative to theoretical work function. Dielectric breakdown electric field Ebd >= 11.5 MV/cm at J_leak = 1.0 mA/cm^2 across >= 95% of tested sites.` | ### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes - **Hazard Classification**: `High` - **Mandatory PPE**: Level B high-temperature heat-resistant aluminized Kevlar furnace gloves (rated >= 500°C contact), Polycarbonate full-face shield over ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/IR side-shield safety glasses, Nomex flame-resistant cleanroom lab coat / bunny suit, Chemical-resistant nitrile under-gloves with fluoroelastomer outer gloves for maintenance handling, Safety shoes with non-conductive, heat-resistant soles - **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal Burns: Immediately flush affected area with sterile cold water for at least 20 minutes; do not apply ice directly or peel away adhered clothing; apply dry sterile non-adhesive dressing and transfer to hospital burn unit. Cryogenic/Asphyxiation Hazard: Remove victim to fresh air immediately; if breathing has stopped, administer artificial respiration and supplemental oxygen by trained medical personnel. If anhydrous HCl exposure occurs: Flush skin/eyes immediately with copious water for 15 minutes while stripping contaminated clothing; for eye contact, irrigate with buffered isotonic saline and obtain immediate ophthalmologic care. - **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous negative pressure tube exhaust scavenging with certified static differential pressure >= 1.2 inches water column (-300 Pa). Redundant toxic/pyrophoric gas monitoring sensors at gas cabinets and tube scavenger shroud integrated into automated Emergency Gas Shutoff (EGS). Cleanroom ballroom airflow maintained at ISO Class 5 (Class 100) laminar downflow with minimum 70 air changes per hour. - **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Tube exhaust routed directly to point-of-use wet acid scrubber (packed bed column with aqueous 5-10% NaOH recirculating liquor) to neutralize halogen/acid effluents (pH regulated between 7.5 and 8.5) before municipal effluent discharge. Nitrogen sweep and dilute O2 process off-gas passed through demisters to eliminate thermal condensate droplets prior to building HVAC vent stack release. **Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**: | Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Oxygen (Compressed Gas / Cryogenic Liquid)** | `7782-44-7` | VLSI / Semiconductor Grade 5.5 | `>= 99.9995%` | | **Nitrogen (Compressed Gas / Cryogenic Liquid)** | `7727-37-9` | Electronic Grade 6.0 | `>= 99.9999%` | | **Hydrogen Chloride (Anhydrous, if used for tube pre-clean/chlorination)** | `7647-01-0` | Electronic Grade 4.5 | `>= 99.995%` | | **Silicon Dioxide (Vitreous Quartz Dust / Scavenger particulate)** | `60676-86-0` | Technical Grade | `100%` | ### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints - **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours` - **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophobic, hydrogen-terminated silicon (100) surface following dilute HF (0.5% DHF) etch, rinse to 18.2 MOhm-cm resistivity, and Marangoni/IPA dry (surface oxide <= 0.15 nm, contact angle > 75°). - **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Stoichiometric, defect-free, amorphous silicon dioxide (SiO2) dielectric thin film with smooth interface morphology (root-mean-square surface roughness Rq <= 0.12 nm) and dangling bonds passivated. - **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding allowable air Q-time causes uncontrolled native oxide growth (0.5-0.8 nm) and airborne organic/airborne molecular contamination (AMC) adsorption, resulting in uncorrectable gate oxide thickness over-target errors (> 3.8 nm), increased interface trap density (Dit > 5E10 eV^-1 cm^-2), and pinhole-induced early gate dielectric breakdown. ### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done) **Exit Objective Summary**: > Execution of horizontal quartz furnace recipe growing 3.50 nm ± 0.15 nm high-quality gate thermal oxide on 200mm p-type silicon wafers at 850°C using a 10% O2 / 90% N2 dilute oxidation cycle. Process achieves within-wafer thickness standard deviation <= 0.08 nm, across-boat range <= 0.15 nm, midgap Dit <= 2.0E10 eV^-1 cm^-2, and breakdown field >= 11.5 MV/cm, fully validated by spectroscopic ellipsometry and MOS C-V characterization. **Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**: - [ ] `RUN_850C_3P5NM_THERMAL_PROFILE_PID_LOG.csv` - [ ] `GATE_OX_3P5NM_49PT_ELLIPSOMETRY_MAP.pdf` - [ ] `MOSCAP_CV_IV_DIT_BREAKDOWN_REPORT.tiff` **Quantitative Completion Assertions**: | Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `ASSERT-01` | **Center wafer gate oxide physical thickness measured across 49 points via spectroscopic ellipsometry** | `3.50 nm` | ±0.15 nm (3.35 nm - 3.65 nm) | Multi-wavelength (190-1000 nm) spectroscopic ellipsometry using Cauchy dielectric model | | `ASSERT-02` | **Center-zone flat zone temperature uniformity over 350 mm boat length at 850°C steady state** | `850.0°C` | ±0.50°C | Calibrated profile thermocouple rake logged at 1 Hz across Load, Center, and Source zones | | `ASSERT-03` | **MOS capacitor interface trap density (Dit) at midgap after forming gas anneal** | `1.5E10 eV^-1 cm^-2` | <= 2.0E10 eV^-1 cm^-2 | High-Low Frequency C-V (Castagne-Vapaille method) at 1 MHz and Quasi-static sweep | **Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**: > All 3 monitor wafers (Load, Center, Source) pass 49-point ellipsometry thickness specifications (mean 3.50 ± 0.15 nm, 1-sigma <= 0.08 nm), furnace datalog confirms isothermal stability (850.0 ± 0.5°C) throughout process gas delivery, and extracted Dit satisfies <= 2.0E10 eV^-1 cm^-2 with zero observed crystallographic slip lines on edge wafers under high-intensity collimated inspection light.

testcases.title: Gate Oxide Physical Thickness and Multi-Site Within-Wafer Uniformity Verification
testcases.instrumentation: Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (SOPRA / Woollam M-2000 multi-wavelength 190-1000 nm, 70° incidence angle, Cauchy dielectric model for thin SiO2 on Si)
testcases.pre_conditions: 200mm p-type (100) Si monitor wafers (resistivity 1-10 ohm-cm) processed through standard RCA-1, SC-2, and 0.5% DHF clean (surface contact angle > 75°); elapsed Q-time in N2 storage < 15 minutes prior to load at 650°C idle temperature.
testcases.procedure: 1. Ramp furnace center zone from 650°C idle to 850°C at 5°C/min under 4.0 SLPM UHP N2 sweep. 2. Stabilize thermal profile across 3-zone thermocouples for 20 minutes (verify <= ±0.5°C deviation). 3. Switch mass flow controller to process gas mix: 0.4 SLPM O2 + 3.6 SLPM N2 (10% dilute O2) at 850°C for exactly 14.5 minutes. 4. Flush tube with 5.0 SLPM pure UHP N2 for 10 minutes; ramp down to 650°C at 3°C/min. 5. Pull cantilever boat at 30 mm/min. 6. Transfer 3 monitor wafers (Load, Center, Source) to spectroscopic ellipsometer and execute standard 49-point polar map per wafer (5 mm edge exclusion).
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Wafer center physical thickness target = 3.50 nm. Center wafer mean thickness must be within [3.35 nm, 3.65 nm]. 49-point within-wafer thickness standard deviation (1-sigma) <= 0.08 nm (< 2.5%). Across-boat wafer-to-wafer thickness range (Max - Min) <= 0.15 nm.

testcases.title: MOS Capacitor Interface Trap Density (Dit) and Breakdown Field (Ebd) Extraction
testcases.instrumentation: Automated Mercury Probe (Hg-probe) or Evaporated Al Gate C-V/I-V System with Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Analyzer and LCR meter (1 kHz to 1 MHz high-frequency and quasi-static C-V)
testcases.pre_conditions: Oxidized monitor wafer from TC-DEAL-GROVE-DRY-OX-2-2-2-2-01 subjected to post-oxidation forming gas anneal (FGA) at 420°C in 10% H2/90% N2 for 30 minutes; back-side native oxide stripped with buffered oxide etch and metallized with 100 nm Al.
testcases.procedure: 1. Place wafer on chuck under N2 dry purge enclosure (RH < 5%). 2. Lower mercury capillary contact or probe dot array (contact area = 1.0E-3 cm^2). 3. Measure High-Frequency (1 MHz) and Quasi-Static C-V curves from -3.0 V to +3.0 V at 50 mV/s sweep rate. 4. Extract flat-band voltage (Vfb), equivalent oxide thickness (EOT), and interface trap density (Dit) using the High-Low Frequency (Castagne-Vapaille) method near midgap. 5. Perform ramped voltage stress (I-V) up to dielectric breakdown to determine breakdown electric field (Ebd).
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Interface trap density at midgap Dit <= 2.0E10 eV^-1 cm^-2. Flat-band voltage shift |delta-Vfb| <= 50 mV relative to theoretical work function. Dielectric breakdown electric field Ebd >= 11.5 MV/cm at J_leak = 1.0 mA/cm^2 across >= 95% of tested sites.

ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: Thermal Burns: Immediately flush affected area with sterile cold water for at least 20 minutes; do not apply ice directly or peel away adhered clothing; apply dry sterile non-adhesive dressing and transfer to hospital burn unit. Cryogenic/Asphyxiation Hazard: Remove victim to fresh air immediately; if breathing has stopped, administer artificial respiration and supplemental oxygen by trained medical personnel. If anhydrous HCl exposure occurs: Flush skin/eyes immediately with copious water for 15 minutes while stripping contaminated clothing; for eye contact, irrigate with buffered isotonic saline and obtain immediate ophthalmologic care.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Continuous negative pressure tube exhaust scavenging with certified static differential pressure >= 1.2 inches water column (-300 Pa). Redundant toxic/pyrophoric gas monitoring sensors at gas cabinets and tube scavenger shroud integrated into automated Emergency Gas Shutoff (EGS). Cleanroom ballroom airflow maintained at ISO Class 5 (Class 100) laminar downflow with minimum 70 air changes per hour.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Tube exhaust routed directly to point-of-use wet acid scrubber (packed bed column with aqueous 5-10% NaOH recirculating liquor) to neutralize halogen/acid effluents (pH regulated between 7.5 and 8.5) before municipal effluent discharge. Nitrogen sweep and dilute O2 process off-gas passed through demisters to eliminate thermal condensate droplets prior to building HVAC vent stack release.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Hydrophobic, hydrogen-terminated silicon (100) surface following dilute HF (0.5% DHF) etch, rinse to 18.2 MOhm-cm resistivity, and Marangoni/IPA dry (surface oxide <= 0.15 nm, contact angle > 75°).
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Stoichiometric, defect-free, amorphous silicon dioxide (SiO2) dielectric thin film with smooth interface morphology (root-mean-square surface roughness Rq <= 0.12 nm) and dangling bonds passivated.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Exceeding allowable air Q-time causes uncontrolled native oxide growth (0.5-0.8 nm) and airborne organic/airborne molecular contamination (AMC) adsorption, resulting in uncorrectable gate oxide thickness over-target errors (> 3.8 nm), increased interface trap density (Dit > 5E10 eV^-1 cm^-2), and pinhole-induced early gate dielectric breakdown.

expected_result.summary: Execution of horizontal quartz furnace recipe growing 3.50 nm ± 0.15 nm high-quality gate thermal oxide on 200mm p-type silicon wafers at 850°C using a 10% O2 / 90% N2 dilute oxidation cycle. Process achieves within-wafer thickness standard deviation <= 0.08 nm, across-boat range <= 0.15 nm, midgap Dit <= 2.0E10 eV^-1 cm^-2, and breakdown field >= 11.5 MV/cm, fully validated by spectroscopic ellipsometry and MOS C-V characterization.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Center wafer gate oxide physical thickness measured across 49 points via spectroscopic ellipsometry
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Multi-wavelength (190-1000 nm) spectroscopic ellipsometry using Cauchy dielectric model

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Center-zone flat zone temperature uniformity over 350 mm boat length at 850°C steady state
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Calibrated profile thermocouple rake logged at 1 Hz across Load, Center, and Source zones

quantitative_assertions.assertion: MOS capacitor interface trap density (Dit) at midgap after forming gas anneal
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: High-Low Frequency C-V (Castagne-Vapaille method) at 1 MHz and Quasi-static sweep

expected_result.signoff_criteria: All 3 monitor wafers (Load, Center, Source) pass 49-point ellipsometry thickness specifications (mean 3.50 ± 0.15 nm, 1-sigma <= 0.08 nm), furnace datalog confirms isothermal stability (850.0 ± 0.5°C) throughout process gas delivery, and extracted Dit satisfies <= 2.0E10 eV^-1 cm^-2 with zero observed crystallographic slip lines on edge wafers under high-intensity collimated inspection light.
